a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: And we have a roll program.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You have good thrust on all five engines.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: And we have a pitch program.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode One Bravo.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Booster Systems Engineer reports to Flight Director that S-IC stage [is] looking good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Everything looks perfect down here.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Looks cleared up here, Gordo. [Long pause.]

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, the altimeter is six zero.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Going through maximum dynamic pressure at this time.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Okay. 1:32. Program looks good, Dave. Out at 11 miles.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Good shot. Two and a half g.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 9 [nautical] miles [16.6 km] downrange, 13 - 14.5 [nautical] miles [24 - 26.8 km] height.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode One Charlie.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, we're at 3g's. Stand by for inboard.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Each of the five S-IC engines [are] gulping 3 tons of fuel [means propellant] per second.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, 10 seconds to staging. Hang on.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Flight Dynamics reports Go for staging.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. You have good thrust on the S-II. All five are good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Good show. We'll go on time.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Roger. We confirm the Skirt Sep. You're Mode II.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Coming up on 10,000 feet per second [3,000 m/s] mark. Down range 131 [nautical miles, 243 km], altitude 66 [nautical miles, 122 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Just - looks just about a hundred feet per second [30 m/s] down on the H-dot, but everything else looks fine.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, I got the big fireball going by at staging. I don't know whether you saw it or not. That beauty really goes.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. At 4 [minutes], the guidance has converged. The CMC is Go and everything looks good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo. Looks good up here. [Long pause.]

a15_0000013.speaker: Irwin
a15_0000013.text: Man, I got the Moon in my window.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Thrusters are stable; the ball's stable.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: We're at a V I of 11,000 and right on the money.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Good show. Let me check here at 4:30 just to make sure.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: That sucker's right on - right on.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Little high on altitude. I bet you they're going to give you the [garble] here in a minute.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Now at 35 per cent of the velocity needed to orbit. Downrange 190 [nautical] miles [352 km]. Altitude 79 [nautical miles, 146 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Five minutes. Everything looks nominal. You're Go.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo; thank you. Looks good up here. Got a smooth ride so far.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 40 percent of velocity needed [to achieve orbit].

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 271 [nautical miles, 501 km] altitude 88 [nautical miles, 163 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: See, we're getting just a little teeny bounce. You feel it now?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, be watching for the S-IVB for COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Times are nominal. The level sense arm will be 8 plus 34, and S-II cut-off at 9 plus 09. Over.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Predicting nominal shutdown on the S-II stage.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: And stand by for S-IVB to COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Mark. You have S-IVB to COI now.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Roger. S-IVB to COI. [Long pause.] [To Irwin:] Jim?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, we're right - right down the line.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Coming up on 15,000 V I , 260 H-dot. That's right where we ought to be, and that gives us an SCS COI.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay. Keep your eye up for S-IVB to orbit.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 380 [nautical] miles [704 km] downrange, altitude 94.5 [nautical miles, 175.0 km], velocity 15,000 feet per second [4,572 m/s].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for S-IVB to orbit capability.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 479 [nautical] miles, [887 km], altitude 96 [nautical] miles, [178 km], now approaching 65 per cent of velocity needed for orbit. The velocity now, 16,700 feet per second [5,090 metres per second]. Official time of lift-off [9 hours] 34 minutes, 00 seconds .79. [Eastern Daylight Time]

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Feels like we get a little vibration out of that thing.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Well, it seems to be pretty steady though.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: We're about 1.7g, somewhere around there. Okay, 10 seconds to inboard.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: V I 's 18,000 [fps, 5,486 m/s]. [Garble] We're at 96 [nautical] miles [178 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Downrange 660 [nautical] miles [1,222 km], altitude 95 [nautical] miles [176 km], velocity 78 per cent velocity required for orbit.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, about 10 seconds to PU shift.

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Didn't even feel it. There it goes, 8:03.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. 15, Houston. Go ahead. Say again, 15?

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Houston, 15. We didn't call. You got something?

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You've had PU shift, and the thrust looks good.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: You've had level sense arm now?

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Stand by for Mode IV capability.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Mark. You have Mode IV now.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Booster reports thrust okay on the S-IVB stage.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. You've had - you have good thrust on the S-IVB.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 960 [nautical] miles [1,778 km] downrange, 94.7 [nautical miles, 175.4 km] altitude. Velocity 23,230 [feet per second, 7,081 m/s].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. Everything's looking perfect. Predicted [S-IVB engine] cut-off time [is] 11 plus 37. Over.

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: 1,281 [nautical] miles [2,372 km] downrange, 93.4 [nautical miles, 173.0 km] altitude, 97 percent of velocity - 98 percent of velocity required. [Current velocity is] 25,143 feet per second [7,664 m/s].

a15_0000013.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0000013.text: Booster confirms the S-IVB has shutdown.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Houston. [SPS engine] Gimbal Motors are Off, and the S-IVB oxidizer is 40 [psi, 276 kPa], and the fuel's about 31 [psi, 214 kPa].

a15_0000013.speaker: Worden
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo. We got ourselves in a 93.7 [nautical miles, 173.5 km] by 88.9 [nautical miles, 164.6 km, orbit]; [engine] shutdown [was] on a V I [inertial velocity] of plus 25595 [fps, 7,801 m/s]; H dot, plus 00008 [fps, 2.4 m/s], altitude plus 00932 [93.2 nautical miles, 172.6 km].

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. IU shows you in a 92.5 by 91.5 [nautical mile orbit, 171.3 by 169.5 km]. Radar confirms that. And the booster is safed.

a15_0000013.speaker: Scott
a15_0000013.text: Okay, Gordo; good job. That was a very smooth ride all the way.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. The booster is configured for orbit. Over.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: 15, Houston. I have your Z torquing angle.

a15_0000013.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0000013.text: Minus decimal 1 degrees. One tenth of a degree, minus.

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: Okay. Have you got the torquing angle?

a15_0001610.speaker: Worden
a15_0001610.text: Mm-hum. Okay, we could do the SM RCS monitoring check and the CM...

a15_0001610.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0001610.text: We've had Loss Of Signal through Bermuda. About a minute out of Canary Islands. To recap a moment, the measured orbital... here is a call now to the crew.

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: Okay. The S-IVB tank pressures are - about 41 [psi] on the oxidizer and about 21 [psi] on the fuel.

a15_0001610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0001610.text: I know we're over the [garble] but [garble] Indian Ocean should be.

a15_0001610.speaker: Scott
a15_0001610.text: And it looks like the S-IVB is tracking very nicely.

a15_0001610.speaker: Worden
a15_0001610.text: I - I guess I hadn't really - hadn't - myself thought we wouldn't be - it wouldn't be visibly this fast.

a15_0001610.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0001610.text: Apollo 15 [is] in a 92.5 by 91.5 nautical mile [171.3 by 169.5 km] Earth orbit. 1 [nautical] mile [1.85 km] out of perfectly circular. Communications through the Canary Island tracking station for about 4 minutes and 11 seconds total pass time.

a15_0001610.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0001610.text: Coming up on Loss Of Signal through Canaries.

a15_0002113.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0002113.text: 15, Houston. About 35 seconds to LOS [Loss Of Signal], and we have nothing further for you. We'll see you at Carnarvon, as shown on the checklist, at 52 [minutes GET]. Over.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I'm going to do a fuel cell purge check here, Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0002113.text: Flight Dynamics Officer reports that the data coming from the Canary Islands tracking station confirms the initial measurements of the Earth parking orbit, and we're expecting to acquire Apollo 15 again over the Carnarvon, Australia, tracking station at 52 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, about 30 minutes from now. And at 22 minutes, 13 seconds Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Do you want to get - get going down there?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Try and clean some of this stuff off, too.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: You can take mine and stick it in there, too.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: With that indicator out, I can't confirm an H 2 purge on fuel cell 2.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Can't you get the - get the H 2 ...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Hmm. Better discuss that with them next time we...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Well, shall we gently step along?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Do you want R-12 out now, Jim? Anything Flight-Data-File-wise that you need now?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I'm just going to stick these cards here in the compartment then, and...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Dave. Do you want to swing over and get the SM RCS monitoring check? Or do you want me to get that?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Here. I can just read it to you.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: SM RCS Propellant talkback, eight, gray.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Whoops, stand by; we got one - one barber pole right down - we got B Propellant - barber pole. That was probably a mistake. We open it, and it's gray.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: You want to make a note?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: B Secondary Propellant - B Sec Propellant was barber pole, and it reset to gray.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Okay. SM RCS Indicator, Helium Tank Temp.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: RCS Indicator selector to A through D. Give me Package Temp, Helium Pressure - all four.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Let me get calibrated here. You want - That's in temperatures only, huh?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: No, I want Temp, Pressure, [garble] Pressure, and Helium Tank Temp.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, your Manifold Pressure's too low.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: The Manifold Pressure on D is a little low, about 2.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Its lower - lower limit is, accord - 192.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Oh, okay, I'll give you one - Well, shoot, [garble]...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: You can't read it. Okay. CM RCS monitoring check.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: CM RCS Propellant talkback, two, gray.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: RCS Indicator, switch to CM 1 and 2.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. CM 1 - I'm waiting - Okay, you want...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Helium Temp, Pressure and Manifold Pressure.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Two; I'm looking at 70, 4000, and about 90.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Okay. I'm going to do a Caution and Warning operational check here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: We're going to get a Master Alarm here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, you're down in the LEB, Al?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, can you get the strut unlocked while you're getting those?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: I'm getting them right - I'm getting them right now.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: I'm just now beginning to understand what went on.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Are you still working on that, Al?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Drinking Water Supply valve, On.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. See if I can get to it here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Quit having a good time and go to work. [Laughter.]

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. CB: COAS/Tunnel Lighting, Main B, closed.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Get your big foot out of the way.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Unstow helmet bags, accessory bags, and tool E.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. David, the helmet bags - Let's see, they're behind you, aren't they?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Yes, they're - I got to get those stupid things.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: They're in U-4 - or U-1. Tool E is in L-2.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Yes. I'll get it. I don't know what this little thing is here, [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, I'm going to switch around and get that window cover.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Let's see, where the heck is tool E? [Garble]. Here it is.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: [Laughter.] I didn't see the - the decal on the light over here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Yes. "This vehicle will not be placed in motion until all seat belts are properly fastened. By order of the Chief of Staff, USAF."

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: It would sure be easy to knock some switches here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. It sure would be. Okay, that's a thing we got to watch pretty close, huh?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: I - I might get you to get that window shade, Al, if - if you have a chance.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: I know where it is - it's just hard for me to get over to one of them - [garble] below it...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Is it in with the other window shade?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: I can get it, it's right in here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: We want to put that in here so we don't get sunburned.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Now, let's see. You want to do that Emergency Cabin Pressure thing?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Yes, let me - I've got a - I'm confirming normal suit and cabin pressure.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Be very careful of that Lexan, because I - I'm going to need to take some pictures through it.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Make sure you get everything tied down when you get through using it, because we got one more little g-level thing to go through here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Helmets and access - helmet bags and accessory bags.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. The Lexan shade is on.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: And grab the TSBs while you're there, too. Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Jim. I guess we could do the...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Where are the TSBs, Al? They're not up here. They're down in one of those other things.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: In U-1 - I was looking in U-2?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Let's see. The O 2 flow is high.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Oh, it - it just dropped down.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: What's - what's the cabin pressure? We still got the waste stowage vent...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Well, it was just high for a little bit.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Cabin Pressure - Emergency Cabin Pressure valve to Both, Al.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Emergency Cabin Pressure going to Both.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: And Suit Circuit Return Value, Open, Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. We can - I got the window cover on. We can remove helmet and gloves and stow in PGA bag.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Don't we - don't we do a check first?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: No, we don't. That Main Reg[ulator] check's on the next page.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: As long as you're in position though, Al, let's do it.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Main Reg B valve, closed.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Push To Test pushbutton, push for O 2 Flow increase.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Main Reg B valve, Open.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Push To Test pushbutton, push for O 2 Flow increase.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Main Reg A valve, Open.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Emergency Cabin Pressure, select to Both.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: So, we - you want to take off helmets and gloves now?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Let's get into our little home. Shall we do it?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: The accessory bags inside here, Dave?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: And let's see what kind of label you got on yours today. Jim, you got an R - for you today.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: R, C, and L. Guess we can keep track of that.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: It's so pretty out here, Dave, I'd almost settle for an Earth-orbit mission.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Well, you'll get one, maybe someday. Who knows?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Boy. Sure doesn't take much to scratch these helmets.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Let's see, what have we got going, just the suit fans?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: It's so quiet, it's kind of eerie...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. We got to snap these things [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. We're supposed to try to keep them up there where we can get them [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: You give me a hand here, will you?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Oh, what a joy! [Laughter.] Oh, what a joy!

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Let's see. If you're going to do that, hand me the checklist...

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. What do we - what do we need, Dave? Why don't you read it out to me now? [Garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Assemble and mount in the left-hand window [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Left hand [garble]. Okay, [garble] need to get out of here [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Dave, When you get a chance, you want to monitor Secondary Accumulator Quantity.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Now - do you want to get the Hasselblad out?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Mag M. Oh, it is crossed out?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: [Garble] EL. Oh, okay. Spotmeter. Stow in the LMP TSB. I guess you better get the TSBs out [garble]...

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: And the TSBs are up behind Jim.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Yes. They're behind you, Jim.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Guess that's all we need out of here for now. [Garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Boy, you really get a Coriolis effect by looking at that [garble] in here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Yes; that's why I say, just go slow, because it will all go away here in a few hours. Won't even notice it. [Garble]...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: [Garble] always felt we'd parted some company, didn't you?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: No, but it's nice to just go slow.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Are you ready for some TSBs?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes, you need yours most of all.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes, because you need to put these two cameras in it.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. You want to hand me the camera, Al?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Jim, that's the - Yes, here you go.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Is that for my UV work?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Your EL with magazine M in it.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Okay. And here's your spotmeter.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Got it? Okay. I'll get the TV camera out.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay, I'm going to do the - Dave, are you ready for that leak...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. If you'll - put the Secondary Glycol To Rad valve, Normal, for 30 seconds.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Yes, it's right up in front of you there, Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Oh, thank you. Jimmy? Can you reach here?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: No. And it's starting to get dark.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Really? I've got to get going on the P52.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I can't get that, Jim, until Al closes the door there.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: I'll do this ECS Postinsertion Configuration.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Glycol Reservoir Bypass valve to Open.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: And the Prim quantity, let me check it - 25 to 50 at - It's good.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Al, let's - Can you reach the Prim Accumulator Fill valve?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Here, Jim, can you reach the cable? [Garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: You working on that one, Dave?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Can you get to it there, Dave?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Haven't yet; No. Can you get to it?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Well, what do you need? Primary Accum?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes, sure. Which way do you want it?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Well, it was the Primary Accumulator Fill valve...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Put it On. I'll tell when to - put it back...

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, it's Off. Is that all?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Why don't you get the secondary while you're there? Jim, do you have that?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Secondary Glycol To Rad valve, Normal, Al, if you're in that position. Let me know when you - when you get it in Normal.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes, I can't quite reach that.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Can you get it there, or...

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: If you'll wait a minute, I'll be able to get it.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: I can get it. Thank you.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Let me know when you get it to Normal.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Jim. Here are the lines to the TV.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Wish I had a place to set that thing.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. How long you want this thing in Normal?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Oh, I'll give you a hack here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Dave, can I hand you the monitor over there?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Let me - Let's see, I got ECS Rad Flow Control to Power; Prim Glycol To Rad valve, Normal.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: I got that. ECS Rad Flow Control, Power.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. You've got Prim Glycol To Rad valve, Normal...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: ECS Rad talkback is gray. Glycol Evap Temp In, going Auto.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, who can give me a checklist so I can do these optics?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Potable Water Heater to Main A. Okay. ECS Postinsertion Configuration complete.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: What else you got on there, Jim? Oh, the TSBs.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Yes, do you want a TSB?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: I'll get them out. Do you want to put one up on the...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I've got an EPS monitoring check here; secondary glycol loop check, and we've got the cameras out already.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Al, you want to check that?

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: I'm going to go through a secondary glycol loop check here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: See that little - see that funny little switch they put on here?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: I've got a pocket down here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: I got a pocket, no sweat, I just don't want to forget it and have it floating around.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Optics eyepieces are in, G/N Optics Power going on. Optics Zero, Off, then Zero. Okay.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay, that's 15 seconds. The Optics Zero, Off - Mode, Manual. [Garble]. Here we go.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Who gave you permission to write [garble] out here? [Garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Okay, old PICAPAR, let's see what you can do.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Boy, at night, you might - might as well be in the simulator [laughter].

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Yes, except for the physiological change.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Yes. Okay, the EPS monitoring check is complete, Dave.

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: Except for the battery relay bus read-out down there in Systems Test meter 5-B.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. It doesn't look too good [garble] down in there.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Did - did you do your fuel cell purge check, or [garble]...

a15_0002113.speaker: Irwin
a15_0002113.text: No, I couldn't do the H 2 .

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Let's see how we did. [Cleared throat.]

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. I'll tell you what I'd like to do here [garble] the pass.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Check out the RCS real quick.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Go back to zero, and I think I have to get the optics back out. Right? Did you stow the optics, Jim?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay. Here, do you want to torque at 40? What do we torque at rendezvous?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Yes, did - did you stow the optics eyepiece, Jim?

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Okay. You got the numbers written down?

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Okay, Al, and you might - Why don't you come up here and let me show you what the jets look like when we fire the [garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Oh, okay. Yes. Let me - let me check out a quick star here.

a15_0002113.speaker: Scott
a15_0002113.text: Well, we got to do - I want to do this before AOS.

a15_0002113.speaker: Worden
a15_0002113.text: Well, let me climb up here. [Garble].

a15_0002113.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0002113.text: This is Apollo Control; 50 minutes, 34 seconds Ground Elapsed Time in the mission of Apollo 15. Now approaching the Carnarvon, Australia tracking station. We're [going to have] about a 6½ minute pass over that station. [We are] halfway through the first Earth parking orbit. Next time they pass over Carnarvon or over [the] Australian subcontinent, the crew of Apollo 15 will be preparing for the Translunar Injection maneuver, [in] which the spacecraft and S-IVB stage will break out of Earth parking orbit and begin the 3-day journey to the Moon. Actually the targeting will be toward where

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Okay. It's - it's good.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Okay. You can probably look out my window.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Saw a flash? You did? Couldn't hear it - I didn't hear it. Huh, I'll be darned!

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Yes. Saw a flash, but I didn't hear it. Gosh, I used to hear them all the time. Huh!

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: You know, it's amazing what [garble] outside that window [garble].

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: That's because you got your [garble] lights on in here.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: Okay, the secondary glycol loop check's complete.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Rog. Houston, 15. You're loud and clear.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: Okay the insertion [and system] checks are coming along very nicely. We're down through [item] 21 in the checklist. And the cameras are out, and Al's completed his alignment.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: And I only got one comment [that] Jim's got for you.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: Houston - Houston, 15. On the H 2 purge, fuel cell 2, I cannot confirm [the H 2 flow rate] since I had no - no read-out of a flow indication, or a caution and warning associated with that flow.

a15_0005034.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005034.text: And, if you'd like, I could do it any time, and perhaps you could confirm it.

a15_0005034.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005034.text: This is Houston. We're unable to help you on confirming that purge down here, Jim.

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: Gordo, this is Al. I've got the numbers on the P52 for you.

a15_0005034.speaker: Worden
a15_0005034.text: Okay. [I] used stars 33 and 41. Noun 05 was plus 000.01 and the torquing angles were minus 00.019, plus 00.021, minus 00.061, and they were torqued out at 50 minutes.

a15_0005034.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005034.text: Roger. Copied. And the torquing angles are minus 00.019, plus 00.021, and a minus 00.061. Over.

a15_0005034.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0005034.text: This is Apollo Control. Cabin pressure aboard Apollo 15 [is] holding at 5.7 pounds per square inch [39.3 kPa]. Heart rates for Scott, Worden, and Irwin, respectively, are 70, 83 and 88.

a15_0005034.speaker: Scott
a15_0005034.text: And, Houston, one other comment. Apparently sometime during launch, the RCS-B secondary propellant isolation valve closed, and we recycled it and got a gray talkback.

a15_0005755.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005755.text: Apollo 15, Houston. About 15 seconds to LOS. Estimating [contact with the] United States at 1:30 [GET].

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Al, my doggone checklist says Mag M ought to be on here for the UV.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes ... better get two of these...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: You want to put that on there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. I don't know what we're going to do with this thing. I guess Jim has to hold this during TLI. Or something like that.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Why - why can't I put it on the bracket?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Man, that was some fantastic ride! Gaa!

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Something you're not likely to forget for a while.

a15_0005755.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0005755.text: And we've had Loss Of Signal through the Carnarvon, Australia tracking station. We're standing by now for the post-launch press conference at press site 39 at Kennedy Space Center. And at 59 hours, 22 minutes [means 59 minutes, 22 seconds] Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control."

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: And when you get a chance, Al, I need the - the UV bracket.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: The UV bracket, and the UV ..., and the UV lenses.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Am I supposed to be ... you, Al?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Camera checkout. Can I have the ... up here, Jim?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay, Al. Where'd it go? Let me trade you. Hold the lens for me. While you're holding the lens - If you'll hold that, I'll get you the bracket.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Could you put this - here, I guess - can you put this lens away? Up there, or do you want me to keep it up here?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: ... You'll - you'll need it if you take any color pictures ... lots of ... already. What's the matter, Davy?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: (Laughter) You got to have the pyro arm circuit breakers in to turn the RCS command on.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: We're going to keep you honest.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay, where do you want it?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. Pitch, roll; roll, pitch. Good ...

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Let me know when you all are...

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: ...ready for your TSBs, and I'll hand them to you.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Okay. Hey, you can give me mine, Jim. He's taking yours.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Then when you get a change...

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: ... but the University of Michigan was well represented.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. Couple of little calling cards here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: You know, I keep going up to the top of the vehicle.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: That's exactly right. We did that for 10 days and never figured out why.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Al, I'm going to give you the ... to put back up there.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: So we don't lose track, here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: That's the name of the game for the next 12 days, gang. Put it back.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Okay. Let's see, Al. Do you have the...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: What? The TV lens? Where's the TV?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: ... back here and see if I can bump into it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Do you have the right settings on it? Want me to read them to you?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: I don't know why we've been putting that TV up so early_

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Just to get it out of the way.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay. We want ALC to peak. And f/44.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Guess we - we might as well leave the - the lens cover on until we're ready to use it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Dave, did you do - do that SCS attitude reference - reference check?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: ... f-stop, 30, and the focus at - at infinity...

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: I'll take those. I guess it doesn't really matter...

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Okay, Jim, if you want to stick that in the -

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Hey, Jim. You got the SPS monitoring check all right? ECS monitoring check? EPS?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes. I've taken care of all those checks, Davy. [Garble] come up to the - docking probe.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Okay, Jimmy, you're all hooked up.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay. If I can just get my bracket in here. Pointed in the right dir...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Do we need anything else out of A-1, before I close it?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: When you get a chance, Al, out of R-12, I think I need that - probably need - [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Just like that cardboard - for the window.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: You - you want - you want to pull R-12 out?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes, that whole brack - that temporary sto - that bracket? Yes. Yes, I think I'll probably stow the cardboard in there.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay. We really don't have a place to put this if you got the TV up [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: That's what you got a Flight Plan volume for.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: What do we have in there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Flight Plan, Malfunctions, and all that jazz is in there.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: The card - is my cardboard window shade in there, or something else?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Probably [garble] supposed to be with the cue cards.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: I don't know. Our Flight Data File boxes up here, they're almost empty.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Maybe they just happened to fall open.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: No, there's just very little in here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: That's all we need, is that Flight Plan. I talked to Ted Guillory [garble] all we really need. Up there is Volume I?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. I've already [garble] all through these containers,

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Well, we got all our data - got all that...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: It just doesn't take up a whole container. All those checklists ...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: You need Mag N. (Cleared throat) Okay, coming up.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Where are the rest of the cue cards?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: I think we got the [garble] in the pocket.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Yes, man. [Garble] seems like it can be just a hell of a [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Yes, let me - get my coffee here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Did you finish that check, Dave?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes, the attitude reference check is complete.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay, coming down to ORDEAL, David.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Oh! [Garble] can't - we can't do this - [garble] I can see [garble] hoses [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: I just got my hoses [garble] If you - if you can...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Well, this is going to be a backroom brawl.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: [Garble] get myself hooked up on everything here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Hey, Al, if you get a chance on this - Did you find my cardboard window covering?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Which part of the Data Card Kit?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Here, let me look some more.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. I don't even see where the cue-card part of the Data Card Kit is.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay. I guess I don't need it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: [Coughing.] Hey, you know, I got your meal, Al?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Hey, I think I'm pretty well caught up with the UV photography here.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Goody, goody. Read over the procedures.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Want me to read them to you?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: No, why don't you read them to yourself?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: I - I - Did you get the - Oh, you're looking for the cue cards, is that right?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Yes, I'm just trying to get them all sorted out.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Just a second, Jim, and I'll get it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: I can reach it. Have to push these back - Watch your foot!

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Man, you hit my foot; it really...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: I don't think we need the Data Card Kit out right now.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: May- maybe we could - Is there a good place to stow this down there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Uh, I - I think you'd be better off if you stuck it right back in the window pouch, there.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Is this just for this pass, Jim?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: ...that's probably true. The next pass is at about [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes, I'll have the cardboard up for it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: I guess we could put - we put that back up before we do TLI, don't we?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay, you guys, let that thing be - let it be.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Come on up here and look at this. [Garble] switches.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay; all right. All right, have you got - have you got [garble] This is unreal to watch.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: You've got to watch this, boy. This is one of the beauties that few people ever...

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Just watch it, there. Watch this for a few minutes...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Look at that. You can see lightning. Looks like streaks of lightning around there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: See the little light thing out there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Oh, yes. I didn't see that.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Ooo, like - Oh, that - that's fantastic.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Hey, you're right! That's got to be.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Sure it's a sat - satellite, not a - a planet?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Huh, I guess it is a planet. It's sure bright, though, isn't it?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: It's sure bright, but it's a planet.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Is it going to be black like this all the way out?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: By golly, it's getting bright and early.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: That Earth is a big mother.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes, it looks pretty big, but I think it's probably going to be small.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: [Cough] Yes, that must be a planet, Dave, because...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: ...it's staying in inertial, and we're going Orb Rate now.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Yes. [Garble]. Let's see, I'm going to start getting up around [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Too much trouble for me to get - for you to get [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Looks like Aquarius coming up back there.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. How about your rendezvous window, Jim?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: [Garble]. You think you need a [garble] there, Jim?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: I've got it, man. It shouldn't.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: I couldn't prove it to you.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: I've got to get that [garble] to dock.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Which reminds me, I've got my own docking checklist.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: What's the matter with this other one?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Well, the one - the one I found, it's the one that doesn't have any, you know, any references in it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: You never got the other one changed?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: There ain't no way I could do that.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Hand controller, not a [garble] control. Okay.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: What do we have to do?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Where are we stowing the tape?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: We should be stowing it back where it goes.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Here's the tape, Al. Where are you putting it, down there ?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Are you ready for the UV, Jim?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: I - I guess - I guess I might as well wait until then.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes, I think you should. Let's do everything right on the money.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: When do we shut it off? Do you shut it off ...?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Do you want to wait until we get...

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: ...AOS before we do the docking probe, don't you?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Do you want to go through it now?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay, CB Docking Probe, two, close. Two, verify.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Docking Probe Extend/Release to Extend/Release until full probe extension.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Okay, here it goes. You've got it, man.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Pretty good. Okay, got a barber pole to gray.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Okay. Docking Probe Extend/Release to Retract. Talkback gray.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: There are a lot of clouds out there, huh?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Hey, Al, you got the - the Hasselblad down there?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Yes, it's in the TSB. The Hassel - Well, the Hasselblad's set up for the UV window.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: ... the pad. You got your updates. Pyro Arm ...

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Hey, now, do you have the TLI card in your pocket?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: No use in finding mine. I did look.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Oh, yes? You get a better ... (laughter).

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: You carried my lunch; I carried your card.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Well, I got a ... here ... a little culture.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: When we get past this cloud bank, I think I might take some of these UV pictures.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: They want some clouds for the UV.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Yes, I know. But I didn't want...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: What are you all looking at out there? Can you tell?

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: You mean what part of the world?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: No - about where the camera's pointing .... They didn't care what time, but we need to correlate it ....

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Hey, look. There's ... out there, I think.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: I'll take some UV pictures of it.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Except I don't think we know the right time...

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: Oh, you can see some of that pattern...

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Hey, yes. We know where it is.

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: This thing is really, really weird.

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: ...I didn't even notice the S-IVB flashes, but you can see them now.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Well, let's see. I guess somebody's got to be ready to copy pads.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Jim, I guess you're going to be busy with the...

a15_0005755.speaker: Irwin
a15_0005755.text: No, no, I'll be doing that. It won't take long to do this.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: All right. I'll get the pyro arm check when we get the comm back.

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Al, why don't you get the...?

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Why don't you get this thing...?

a15_0005755.speaker: Worden
a15_0005755.text: Do you - do you want me to [garble] the [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: Yes. Yes, I've already scratched mine [garble].

a15_0005755.speaker: Scott
a15_0005755.text: The glycol pump? Get the glycol pump?

a15_0005755.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005755.text: Would you put the - You're loud and clear, Dave. Would you put the IU Uptel to Accept, please?

a15_0005755.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0005755.text: Okay; we're going to update the IU Nav vector based on tracking at Carnarvon. We'll have you leave that in Accept all the way through the [United] States pass. When we get a better track here across the States, we'll update it again - before the end. Over.

a15_0005755.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0005755.text: This is Apollo Control. We join the conversation in progress with Apollo 15 through Goldstone.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; will do. And we're down through 27 on the checklist. The docking probe is out. Looks good. And standing by for a sequence arm and a logic check when you're ready.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. We can do that now. [Pause.] Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Logic one, On, now. Logic two, On, now. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Logics are good. You're Go for pyro arm.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; and we had one other little one [an anomaly]. At about an hour [GET], we noticed that the primary and secondary propellant isolation valves on Quad Delta were barber pole. We cycled the switch, and they are now gray. And the RCS checks okay.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. [Pause.] I have a TLI plus 90 and lift-off plus 8 abort PADs, when you're ready.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Can you stand by one, please, Gordo?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Gordo. I'm ready for the TLI [means TLI plus 90] PAD.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. This is the TLI plus 90 abort PAD, Jim.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: TLI plus 90, SPS/G&N; Noun 47 is 66938; minus 0.52, plus 1.90; GET for ignition is 004:19:56.99; Noun 81, minus 0425.4, plus 0000.1, plus 4921.7; attitude, 180, 166, 002; H A is N/A [not applicable], H P , plus 0021.0; 4940.1, 6:34, 4920.8. Sextant star is 40, 079.5, 35.9; boresight star, N/A; Noun 61, plus 16.04, minus 030.00; 1099.0, 34492; GET for 05g, 017:43:58; GDC Align stars are Deneb and Vega; 112, 128, 356; no ullage. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We're not reading you. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Houston; there is a breakup - breakup in the VHF, and Jim lost some of the first part of the transmission. Could you go through it again?

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, just what do you need?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: We have Noun 47 through roll, pitch and yaw.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Jim. Noun 47 is 66938; minus 0.52, plus 1.90; Noun 33, 004:19:56.99; Noun 81, minus 0425.4, plus 0000.1, minus 4921.7 - correction on Delta-V Z is a plus 4921.7; roll, pitch, and yaw are 180, 166, 002. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay, Jim, your readback's correct. Lift-off plus 8 PAD is 008:00, 6076, minus 175, 027:06. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. And I'll have the TLI PAD when you're ready for that one. [Pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: All right. Go ahead. I'm ready for the TLI PAD.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Time base 6 predict 2:40:23; attitude for TLI, 180, 045, 001; burn time 5:55; 10401.1, 35599; Sep attitude, 359, 077, 320; extraction attitude, 301, 257, 040. R2 align, 045.0, 038.0; ORDEAL start, 56:45; Yaw 001; ejection time 4:16:00. Go ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. A little static on two readbacks. Read back Yaw for extraction and R2 align, please?

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. We have a question regarding the primary and secondary isolation valve. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: We're wondering if you happened to just notice them [as] barber pole at one hour [GET], or did you notice them close at one hour? Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Ah, no. We just noticed that they were closed at an hour, But apparently in the shuffle here, somebody probably bumped the one switch which would do it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. You don't - you can't tie them to any other action or event there then? Is that right?

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. [Could you put] IU Uptel to Block? We have put in a second IU Nav[igation] vector, based on Stateside data.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. We'd like P00 and Accept.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: P00 and Accept. You've got it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: 15, Houston. IU Uptel [means CM Uptel] to Block. You have a new state vector now.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Roger. CM Uptel going to Block.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Roger. My mistake. Also have a short update for your TLI checklist ORDEAL angles because of the slight performance difference in the S-IVB. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay. On the launch checklist, page L2-30, bottom of the page. Tell me when you have it. [Pause.]

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: At 56 minutes, slew FDAI number 1 to pitch equals 17 degrees rather than 16; and, at the top of the next page, ensure FDAI number 1 pitch equal 14 degrees rather than 13. Over.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Roger. Copied. 17 degrees instead of 16, and 14 instead of the 13.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Okay; then on the next page, 2-32 at 59:55, change 7 degrees to 8 degrees, ensure FDAI number 1 pitch equal 8 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: One more on the cue card for TLI down slightly below the middle, the long cue card that the CDR uses at 54 minutes. The 24 degrees should be changed to 25 degrees. "Ordeal 300/Lunar, 25 degrees.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: And then there will be a 1 degree difference on the rest of the ORDEAL numbers.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay; looks like they all fit.

a15_0012929.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0012929.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We're about to LOS. Nothing further. We'll see you at Carnarvon at 2:25 GET.

a15_0012929.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0012929.text: This is Apollo Control. Apparently, we have had Loss Of Signal through the Vanguard tracking ship in mid-Atlantic. During that pass over the United States, the numbers for the upcoming Translunar Injection maneuver was passed up - were passed up to the crew. This maneuver, slightly over an hour from now, [is] planned at 2 hours, 50 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The burn, lasting 5 minutes, 55 seconds with the S-IVB third stage, will place the spacecraft into a trajectory toward the Moon. It will increase the velocity by some 10,414 feet per second (actually 10,401.1 fps [3,170.3 m/s]). The meas

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Well, I checked the Delta-V on the EMS; and, I guess, you might as well just hold on until we get all the way around here - until we get the ... again. There's nothing else really to do.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay. You got EDS Power, On, up?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: You want me to hold off?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Really not much more to check. GDC align; I'll wait until we get a little bit farther down the road to do that.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Where is my kitchen timer, Al?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Yes, I guess I ought to put it to use when I start cycling on the cryo fans here shortly. You know, we - actually, we have plenty of time. I could put that 105 lens on again and take a colored picture.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: ... there's a requirement to do it.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Good idea, Why not do it?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: It's - it's not the same place, but -

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Yes, yes - Well, there's no - no - If you want to take a color picture, they - what they want is a color picture to back up the scene you're seeing in the UV. So, if you can't get a color picture of that area, there's no sense taking it. But you might go ahead and take some pictures with the 80 millimeter. There's nothing wrong with that. On the...

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Have you got the Update Book out, Jim?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Did you log - you didn't log the UV pictures in here, did you?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Oh, on - in the photo procedures here ...

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: No, we want to log them on the - on the ...

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Photo Log - 70 millimeter, Mag N, was it?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: (Laughter) Yes, I reckon. How's old Davy?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Oh, we're muttering along, flying across the sea.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Do you have yourself strapped in the seat there, Dave ?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Yes. I do that most of the time, I think.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: It's a lot more comfortable. ... relative position.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Because, otherwise, you're fighting the panel all the time.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Not nearly as loud at 5 psi.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Get your lifevest put away, Jim?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Can't get it quite as tight as ...

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Where would you keep the Update Book?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: R-3 is a pretty handy place for all those books up there.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Is there a snap up there?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: I think I see it now.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Ah, it'll be dark pretty soon. We'll get to see the never-never land. There's no horizon.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: We got to have some place to put the ...

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Well, we could unhook it. Maybe - -

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Matter of fact, why don't we get everything stowed for TLI? ... couple helmets - Why don't you put it down in the LEB somewhere, and we'll just leave them there until after TLI - -

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Let's - let's just leave them until we get docked and start getting up into the tunnel...

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Could just stick these PGA bags in there.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Whoops! Did I do it again?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: You're pretty consistent down there, Al.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: I can't imagine you did that twice in a row.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: The emergency cabin regulator check book.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: We're getting a good check at that, Al.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Are we going to eat before TLI?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Okay, give me your helmet back there, Dave, and I'll stash it away.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Yes, it does. Yes, you see never-never land out there?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Yes. No - no horizon at all.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Let's just take a look at this [garble]. Sort of interesting.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Boy, that's - Look at that planet, how orange it is out there, Dave? Directly ahead.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Yes, it is. isn't it? How come we saw the same planet in the sunlight, Jim? Huh? Tell me that.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Oh, you're - you're still saying it's a satellite, huh?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Well, I - I don't know what I'm saying now, because you convinced me it's a planet. But now, it's in the same position it was...

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: ...when we had sunrise as we go into sunset. So that tells me something.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Two hours 10 minutes and 7 seconds. Turn the lights out. [Garble] never-never [garble]. Now I can put the COAS on it. And for the COAS, [garble]. It's right on it. It's depressed - just about 18 degrees. [Garble]. Here we are. Here we are at Orb-rate. Time's going to be 10 - 2:10. Okay, I'm going to mark it. [Garble]. Get a writing pad. Two hours and 11 minutes exactly.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Mark. Two hours and 11 minutes. COAS is on - 7 degrees depressed below our image - our attitude towards the Earth.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: Well, you know, that's got to be Saturn. Saturn is over by Scorpio.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay, let's see. We got everything stowed now?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Anybody want to eat anything now?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: I'm going to wait until we get everything squared away after docking.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Okay. Is your suit dry today, Jim?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Well, you haven't smelled too much urine, have you?

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Okay, it must have worked then.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Well, I'll tell you, I used it three or four times [garble]. (laughter).

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Yes. Three times before launch and once in orbit.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: I really drank the Gatorade yesterday.

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Twenty-six minutes to go before ignition.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: You want to wait until we get AOS and then start through it?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Getting ready to go to sleep?

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: No, lot of work to do [garble].

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: I've been feeling a little more full in the head all the time.

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: You mean it gets more and more?

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: Well, for - it's up - everybody's a little different. For me, it gets a little more and more after the first - like 7 or 8 hours. And then it stabilizes, and you don't even notice it after the first night. I didn't. Ever - everybody's a little different. Your - your body adjusts - adjusts to the whole thing.

a15_0012929.speaker: Worden
a15_0012929.text: [Garble] feel tired quicker because we don't have anything to push against. Seems like ...

a15_0012929.speaker: Scott
a15_0012929.text: No, I didn't feel any muscle fatigue [garble]. Well, Jim, why don't we go through this thing now? We're going to be [garble].

a15_0012929.speaker: Irwin
a15_0012929.text: Perform EMS Delta-V test and null bias check.

a15_0022400.speaker: Worden
a15_0022400.text: Well, the seat's kind of tight right underneath there.

a15_0022400.speaker: Worden
a15_0022400.text: Just passed through the ...; we're in good shape.

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: This is Apollo Control; 2 hours, 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. We've just had acquisition [of signal] through the Carnarvon station and Gordon Fullerton [is] giving them a call at this time.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: All right, Houston; [Apollo] 15 here. [You are reading] 5 by [5].

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Houston, 15. We're down to the middle of the TLI Prep [on page L2-29] , and everything's in order.

a15_0022400.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0022400.text: We're showing the Manual Attitude switches in Rate... [correcting himself] in Min Impulse, and we recommend Rate Command.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Roger. Rate Command. And the pyros are armed.

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: Flight Director Gerry Griffin [is] preparing to poll his flight controllers, here in the Mission Control room, for Go/No-Go, which shows in the Flight Plan, to be passed up through one of the [ARIA] aircraft in the mid-Pacific. However, it looks like the Go/No-Go signal will be voiced up to the crew just prior to the Loss Of Signal here at Carnarvon. 22 minutes - Mark, 22 minutes to ignition for Translunar Injection.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: And the S-IVB oxidizer looks like about 36 [psi]. The fuel looks like about 19 [psi].

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: We've had Loss Of Signal at Carnarvon. However we will leave the circuit up live for the relays through the aircraft in mid-Pacific - relay through the Guam station, for any continuing conversation with the crew of Apollo 15. 17 minutes, 35 seconds to ignition for Translunar Injection. The S-IVB with the Apollo 15 spacecraft now weigh around 103,000 pounds - as you were - 309,630 pounds [140,448 kg]. After the burn is complete the spacecraft [mass] will have shrunk to 103 thousand pounds approximately [46,700 kg approx.]. After Translunar Injection burn, velocity will rise from the present 25,

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: About 20 minutes after burn cut-off, the S-IVB will maneuver to the separation attitude, and at 3 hours, 20 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, the Apollo 15 spacecraft will separate and do a turn-around maneuver and prepare to dock with the Lunar Module, which is housed in the spacecraft/LM adapter atop the S-IVB stage. The four panels will shed away. The spacecraft, after docking with the Lunar Module, is ejected from the S-IVB stage. The Lunar Module landing gear struts are attached at the knee joints to fittings inside the Spacecraft/Lunar Module [Adapter] or SLA as it is called in acronisms - ac

a15_0022400.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0022400.text: We've had Acquisition Of Signal with the first ARIA aircraft. During the docking - separation and docking maneuver, we should have a live color television picture from the Command Module Westinghouse television camera.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Mm-hmm, Don't bump your head on those lights ...

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: Put your head back here in that little old cubbyhole.

a15_0022400.speaker: Scott
a15_0022400.text: ... it's daylight. Think we can see this pretty burn ?

a15_0022400.speaker: Irwin
a15_0022400.text: Okay. We're standing by for time base 6.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Burn time - 5:55. And, when you get the shutdown, you got a 2-second thruster V I . Right?

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... degrees per second rate. The first one is at 59. Make sure you got that. 45 degrees pitch and yaw.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... degrees per second roll. The S-IVB guidance function ... Okay.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Do we have Hawaii all the way through the burn?

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: No, we haven't .... No, we have...

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: No. We have LOS at 49:52 for ... minutes.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: No, we get them back at 2:55.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Yes, well, we tried it the other day.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: If you did, you can change your Delta-V ... 20 feet per second.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: I bet you it's from the S-IVB.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: We're down to 5 on the cabin.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: When we get ready to dock, and the cabin's up to 5 pounds.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: I thought we were supposed to leave some pressure for that.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Right after Waste Stowage Vent, Closed.

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston through ARIA. Over. [No answer.]

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: You don't have the S-band squelch on, do you?

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Yes, yes, I thought it was...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: ... we ought to be able to get that ...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Oh, that's pretty - that is loud. Isn't it?

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston through ARIA. Over.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Rog, Houston, 15. You're about 1 by 1 through ARIA. [i.e. very poor.]

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Roger. You're about 3 by [3]; clear enough to understand.

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: He said we're clear enough ..., I think.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Roger. We have somebody else on the loop with us, too.

a15_0023212.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0023212.text: Coming up on 10 minutes to TLI ignition. Mark, 10 minutes.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: It's a familiar sound, and I can't remember what I - what it is.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: You can't change the frequency there. You might hook up...

a15_0023212.speaker: Worden
a15_0023212.text: Why don't we hook up the speakers, and let's do some checking...

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: We have the S-II Sep light?

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: The Uplink Activity light went out.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Very well. It should come on now. Come on, baby.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Okay. ORDEAL FDAI 1 to Orb-rate; 2 to Inertial.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: Okay, Houston. It looks like we have a slow repress start. We're up to about 22 to 23 on the fuel pressure.

a15_0023212.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0023212.text: Roger, Dave. You're just barely readable. Understand you're getting a normal Repress. We're - It looks good down here.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: Uptelemetry, CM and IU, both to Block.

a15_0023212.speaker: Irwin
a15_0023212.text: What - what was that on repress that you ... normal?

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: It's - it's just something that's a little slow in here.

a15_0023212.speaker: Scott
a15_0023212.text: It's normally quite fast. ... At 54 minutes, we want to be at 25 degrees.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay; at 56, slew FDAI 1 to Pitch at 17.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Okay; at 56:45, it should be 14 degrees.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Plot boards here in Mission Control Center on the center screen are being set up now to monitor the Translunar Injection burn. Some 5 minutes, 43 seconds away from ignition. Should be in about a minute and a half acquired by the second ARIA spacecraft - [correcting himself] aircraft in mid-Pacific. BOOSTER reports that the tanks in S-IVB stage have been pressurized.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Apollo 15, Houston through ARIA number 2. Over.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. You're way down in the static, but I can hear you transmit. Over.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. We'll pick you up at the keyhole.

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Why don't they have a picture like that in the simulator?

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: TVC Servo - SCS TVC Servo Power 1 to AC 1/Main A.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: This is Apollo Control. There was some doubt in the BOOSTER Engineer's mind that the engine bell of the S-IVB J-2 engine had been properly chilled down from the data that he got through the ARIA 1 aircraft. However, his new data coming in through ARIA 2 has confirmed that the chilldown procedure prior to start has been accomplished as scheduled. Some 2 minutes, 15 seconds away from TLI ignition. Continuing to standby as we approach acquisition at Hawaii in some 2 minutes from now. Still standing by through the ARIA 2 aircraft. Communications through ARIA 2 have been somewhat scratchy - almost

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: Tape Recorder's going High Bit Rate.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Put it in between the camera, Al. No, don't force it.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Can you get it up there?

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Looking at ignition time of 2 hours, 50 minutes, 1 second Ground Elapsed Time. Cut-off at 2 hours, 55 minutes, 54 seconds. Total spacecraft velocity at cut-off should be 35,608.7 feet per second [10,853.5 m/s]. Coming up on 20 seconds. Mark, 20 seconds to TLI ignition.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston; we're showing good thrust. [Long pause.]

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Velocity building up. Now 26,270, 26,347 feet per second [8,007, 8,031 m/s]. Resulting apogee building up, now 679 [nautical] miles [1,258 km], 706 [1,308]: clicking over very rapidly.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Load's about a half a g. ORDEAL ... should be tracking with it.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Well, it had a little surge right at this ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. S-IVB pressure is 40 [psi for the LOX tank] and 30 [psi for the fuel tank] and we had a little surge at about one minute.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger. That was PU shift and that looks - the thrust looks good.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Velocity continuing to build, 26,700 feet per second [8,140 m/s]; resulting apogee 1,661 [nautical miles, 3,076 km].

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: You feel a very slight amount of bumping ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Coming up on 30 thousand... [PAO is interrupted by Dave Scott]

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Houston, 15. And we're about halfway through. Pressures are steady at 40 [psi] and 30 [psi] and ORDEAL is tracking right on through.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: Roger, 15. At 3 minutes, it looks completely nominal to us.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Coming up on 30,000 feet per second - Mark. 30,000 feet per second [9,144 m/s]. Resulting apogee, 4,685 nautical miles [8,677 km].

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: My countdown's going to be off probably 2 seconds here. Let's start my watch and ... it again. I want to be sure the engines ... start.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: You can feel it, can't you?

a15_0024404.speaker: Irwin
a15_0024404.text: I get the little surge before the bang.

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: Pressure's looking good. ORDEAL's tracking. A quarter g - a half g ...

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay, Houston. We have about a minute to go. We're tracking 39 and 30 on the pressures and ORDEAL's about zero.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: That should be on for cut-off.

a15_0024404.speaker: Fullerton
a15_0024404.text: 15, Houston. We're estimating cut-off about 4 seconds earlier than the PAD time.

a15_0024404.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0024404.text: Velocity rapidly approaching TLI cut-off speed.

a15_0024404.speaker: Worden
a15_0024404.text: I'll give you a countdown to 55.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
a15_0024404.text: Okay. Al, get the data there.

a15_0024404.speaker: Scott
