a15_0325100.text: Well. It looks to me like it's about - we started out at about 95 percent and we're down to about 90 percent.

a15_0325100.speaker: Worden
a15_0325100.text: Okay. I'm going to put some of those cameras away here. We don't need the pictures any more here, right?

a15_0325100.speaker: Worden
a15_0325100.text: Okay, Dave. Dave, you want to - stash that just for now, and -

a15_0325100.speaker: Scott
a15_0325100.text: Oh, it'll be a long time.

a15_0330525.speaker: Henize
a15_0330525.text: 15, this is Houston. We're anxious to know down here if you've checked the LM/CM Delta-P. [Pause.]

a15_0330525.speaker: Scott
a15_0330525.text: Not yet, Karl. We will though.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston, 15.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. The LM/CM Delta-P is now plus .8 [psi, 5.5 kPa], and I guess - there's no need to do the Tunnel Vent Valve, is there, at this stage? Looks to us like we can go ahead and bring the pressure back up - equalize the Delta-P before we get into the tunnel.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. We would like to go to Vent on the Tunnel Vent Valve until the Delta-P is - is greater than 2.7.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. We'll do that. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Dave, we'd like for you to tell us when the Delta-P gets to 2.7 [psi], and stop there. The basic problem here is, we want to dump the residual atmosphere out of the LM in order to put in good fresh oxygen before we have you climb in. We're sort of up against the time line now...

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. That's what we...

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Righto.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. That - that's what we figured, Karl, [garble].

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Good; okay. Don't - don't go below 2.7 Delta-P there.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Rog.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston. We're at 2.7 on the Delta-P on tunnel vent.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. Say again.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Roger. We're at 2.7 on the Delta-P on the tunnel vent. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. The number that we need now [for the LM/CM Delta-P], since the [CM] cabin [pressure] went up, is; we need a Delta-P of 3.1 [psi]. We have to vent the tunnel.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Delta-P at 3.1. [Garble]. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, we'd like Omni Bravo.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Yeah, Rog. Omni Bravo. And what was your last, after you said you wanted 3.1 on the LM tunnel vent?

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by on that one. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. To keep our records straight here, we're anxious for you to bring the tunnel down until we have a Delta-P of 3.1. [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Rog, Houston. That's in work, and we're up to 2.9 [psi].

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, this is Houston. There's a couple of read-outs we'd like to get, when you have time. First of all, we'd like to get the PRD read-outs for all three of you. And we'd also like to have the magazine numbers used for the sextant photography and for the UV photography.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay. Those are as - magazines are as per Flight Plan, and we'll get you the PRD's when we can get down into our suits. We'll get them before the day is out.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Dave. And, incidentally, can you give us any sort of report on that number 5 window? [Pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: [The window] looks clear.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: We copy. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay, Houston. The Delta-P is hanging right in at about: 2.9 to 3.0. I'd suggest we pressed on, huh? [Long pause.]

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: Stand by on that, Dave.

a15_0331328.speaker: Henize
a15_0331328.text: 15, This Houston. Time is not too critical. We'd like to let it vent a little longer. Try to get 3.1 [psi on the gauge]. If we don't reach it in about 5 minutes, we'll probably go ahead.

a15_0331328.speaker: Scott
a15_0331328.text: Okay; understand.

a15_0332929.speaker: Henize
a15_0332929.text: 15, Houston. That's excellent. I guess we can go ahead with pressure - pressurizing the LM.

a15_0332929.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0332929.text: This is Apollo Control at 33 hours, 33 minutes. The Apollo 15 crew has picked up some time in the Flight Plan. We're unable to determine at the moment whether the TV will be precisely on schedule. However, Flight Director Milt Windler says that it could be, and if there is a delay he believes it will be less than 10 minutes - less than a 10-minute delay. Apollo 15 now 127,861 nautical miles [236,798 km] from Earth, traveling at a velocity of 4,427 feet per second [1,349 m/s].

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: 15, this is Houston. Can you tell us how the pressurization is going?

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Oh, we're all squared away, and the probe's coming out. [Pause.]

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: Roger. And - if you could give us the high-gain angles [in the Flight Plan] there, we'd like to get that going.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Okay, Houston. The probe is out, and it worked very smoothly.

a15_0334126.speaker: Worden
a15_0334126.text: Okay. Here it is. Jettison, Jim.

a15_0334126.speaker: Irwin
a15_0334126.text: I've got the drogue here, Al, if you can get the TV between my legs.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: I got the probe, Jim. Let's see, you take the jettison bag. I want to put the probe over here by the hatch.

a15_0334126.speaker: Irwin
a15_0334126.text: Okay, I've got the Jett bag.

a15_0334126.speaker: Henize
a15_0334126.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Narrow Beam, please. [Pause.]

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Not yet, Jim. We're not going anywhere yet. There. Okay, now -

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: It seems to me that - the best thing - Give Jim back that TV. I think we can probably put his drogue also under the couch.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Well, that's too crowded, but I think under - under here.

a15_0334126.speaker: Scott
a15_0334126.text: Let's see how we might make out. Okay, watch your suit.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. Whenever you have a chance up there, we're interested in seeing some TV.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Rog, Houston. We thought we'd get the tunnel cleared out because, with all that extra gear in the Command Module, it's sort of tough to find a place to stow everything. And the TV is - right now, sort of in the way. So we'll try and get to you as soon as we can.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: It's a new world in this Command Module, with all these extra box - boxes and everything.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Roger. We had an AC Bus 2 light and a Main Bus B Undervolt. Voltage looks good, and AC Bus 2 looks good. Reading 28.5 volts on Main Bus B and AC Bus 2 looks good. [At] about that time, we had a loss of S-band. I don't know whether it was coincidental or not.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. We saw some of those problems here on the ground, too. And we would like to get back on the High Gain [Antenna], if you would reacquire.

a15_0334622.speaker: Worden
a15_0334622.text: Auto's fine for what we're doing.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Okay, Houston. You should have the [signal from the] High Gain [Antenna, HGA] now.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: Roger, 15. Give us Narrow Beam, please.

a15_0334622.speaker: Scott
a15_0334622.text: Okay, Houston, the LMP is in the LM.

a15_0334622.speaker: Henize
a15_0334622.text: 15, this is Houston. Could you give us a description of any actions you took when you had that electrical glitch? [Long pause.]

a15_0334622.speaker: Worden
a15_0334622.text: Karl, Jim just reset both [electrical buses] and they - everything seems to be okay now. He checked the voltages, and they were fine.

a15_0334622.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0334622.text: We're getting a black and white picture now. It should be coming up color soon.

a15_0335605.speaker: Worden
a15_0335605.text: Hey, Karl, [are] you getting anything in on the TV?

a15_0335605.speaker: Henize
a15_0335605.text: Negative, we have no signal yet. [Voice in background: "It's coming, it's coming."] Pardon me; something is just now coming down.

a15_0335605.speaker: Worden
a15_0335605.text: Okay, fine. I'm over in the LM with them, and they're just going through the checklist.

a15_0335839.speaker: Henize
a15_0335839.text: 15, this is Houston. We're getting a reasonably good TV signal from you. And, we have about four procedure changes connected with the ASA [Abort Sensor Assembly] heater circuit breaker coming up at about 34:30 in your time line, and we'd like your choice as to whether I read it up to you as a block, or whether you want us to read it to you step by step when the time comes. [Long pause.]

a15_0335839.speaker: Worden
a15_0335839.text: Houston, 15. Hey, Karl, how about waiting until Jim and Dave get on comm, and then read up the procedure.

a15_0335839.speaker: Worden
a15_0335839.text: If that's satisfactory, let's do it that way.

a15_0335839.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0335839.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 1 minute. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin are going through a LM checklist to ensure that all the switch settings in the LM are the same as they were prelaunch; that they have not somehow changed position since launch.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Go ahead, Houston; 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, when you had the S-band loss back there a few minutes ago, we think the problem was basically on the ground. And, when you lost uplink, it's - it's likely that your High Gain Antenna slewed against the limits; and we wonder if there was any circuit breaker resetting required to get you back up?

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, Karl, stand by one, and I'll find out. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Negative, Houston. No circuit breakers are reset.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Very good. [Pause.] And, Al, we're getting a real good picture down here.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, Karl.

a15_0340408.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0340408.text: The conversations since the start of the TV have been between CapCom Karl Henize and Command Module Pilot Al Worden. Major Worden reporting that Dave Scott and Jim Irwin are not on the air/ground communications while they are completing the checklist.

a15_0340408.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0340408.text: You can get brief glimpses of Dave Scott from time to time on the left. His head coming into view now. Checking part of the Environmental Control System now.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, the TV picture is beautiful, and we're going to give that cameraman an honorary union card. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: That cameraman's got too many hands busy to answer you right now, Karl.

a15_0340408.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0340408.text: We're getting a look at Jim Irwin now.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Okay, give us a time hack, would you Karl, please? GET. [Pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Roger. We're counting up to 34 hours, 11 minutes and 50 seconds. 4, 3, 2, 1...

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Mark. [Long pause.]

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Rog. If you're ready, Dave and Jim are ready to activate the comm now.

a15_0340408.speaker: Henize
a15_0340408.text: Roger. Did you get that time hack okay.

a15_0340408.speaker: Worden
a15_0340408.text: Yes, sir, sure did. Thank you.

a15_0340408.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0340408.text: That picture's coming from 129,473 nautical miles [239,784 km] in space.

a15_0341613.speaker: Worden
a15_0341613.text: Roger, Karl. You guys ready to start a comm check now? [Long pause.]

a15_0341613.speaker: Henize
a15_0341613.text: Roger. We're ready down here for a comm check.

a15_0341613.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0341613.text: That looked like Al Worden coming through the tunnel there.

a15_0342237.speaker: Crewmember
a15_0342237.text: [Garble]. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Endeavour reading you 5 square in Duplex B. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. I got your message loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Go ahead.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Rog, Karl. Jim's been calling you on S-band.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Sorry about that. They're just telling me here that we do have some problems, and we need to stand by for a few more minutes.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay; understand. Stand by for a few minutes before we try again.

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: [The] problem is with the tracking station at Goldstone. It's expected to be cleared up very shortly.

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: Goldstone's ready now.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston, and we're all set up for the voice check. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, Houston is now configured to go along with you on the voice check. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston - Houston, this is Endeavour. It - apparently Falcon is reading you five square, but you're not reading him.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: That's correct, I've had no messages from Falcon.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, he has been calling you, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Karl. What are you receiving? Are you getting any low bit rate [data] from the - from the LM - from the Falcon?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: That's affirmative.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: You are? Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Endeavour. Be advised Falcon's going high bit rate, we'll give you another call.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Endeavour again. Apparently Falcon's still reading you, but you're not reading him. How do you pick him up with high bit rate? [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, Houston is getting the high bit rate data okay, and we'd like to have you hold this present configuration while we think a bit.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Karl.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Aren't those pretty?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Say again.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Aren't those pretty little things?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Oh boy. Navy blue, yet. Colorful. Too bad they don't work very well.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: [Garble] had them watch you configure the camera.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: You do?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Yeah. That might be embarrassing.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Really?

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Because you might not get it con - Should be back over on the right-hand side. Oh my! You had it last, Al, when you were cleaning up the - screens. I put it in that compartment there, Al, just above the emergency medical kit - compartment above the emergency medicikinal [sic] kit.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: 15, this is Houston. We're reading you on Vox.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: [Ha, ha] Hot on Vox. ...

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay. Down Voice Back-up...

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, they would - hot mike.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Good, I'm glad you're reading us, Fi - Houston, finally. [Pause.] Are we coming through loud and clear now, Karl?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. You're coming through loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Okay. I guess while we're in this position, we ought to go back to low [bit rate].

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: We've got...

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: We ought to go back to low bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. Dave, we're reading you loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: [Garble] you want to go back? [Pause.] Okay; back to low bit rate. Let's try that.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Yeah. [The] camera's configured, Dave.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Except for the Mag. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay; we're on low bit rate. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, how do you read Falcon on low bit rate?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, Houston is reading you loud and clear on low bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Roger. We read you the same.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay; let's go back Biomed, Right and High bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Okay. High and Right. [Pause.] Houston, This is Falcon on high bit rate, with Biomed, Right. How do you read?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. We're writing - we're reading you loud and clear.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: We're reading you the same. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Falcon again. Biomed, Right and Low bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. We're reading you loud and clear on Biomed, Right, and low bit rate.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, we're not reading Falcon at the present time, and we've had loss of signal.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, Endeavour. Roger; understand. And I wonder if you just got that last piece on the TV there. It was a piece of gray tape with some glass on it that came out of the tapemeter.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: We're getting a very good picture of it, thank you.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Rog.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Falcon. How do you read?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Houston. Reading you loud and clear. How us? [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, we caught the first part of your transmission, and then you were cut out.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. Falcon, this is Houston. How do you read us?

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Read you loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Houston. We're in PCM High. How do you read?

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. Houston is reading you loud and clear. And did I understand PCM High?

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: That's affirm. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, this is Falcon. Standing by for a voice and range check. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. We're ready for step 8. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Houston, we're configured for step 8.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. We're reading you loud and clear. How us?

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: The picture is Dave Scott, the voice is Jim Irwin.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: ED Voltage reading 37 on both.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. We copy that.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Irwin
a15_0342237.text: Go ahead Houston, Falcon.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger. We'd like to tell you that the initial problem with and - with the S-band was a ground problem, and it looks as though all of the comm checks are Go. And, we would like to ask if our VHF uplink was okay. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay, VHF A and B both checked out, with Endeavour, loud and clear. And since we don't have anything other than the sequence camera to check out here, we're going to check that out and then powerdown and take care of the rest of the housekeeping without the power. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger, Falcon. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, this is Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Be advised that we have - had an excellent TV show here, and that you can secure it, as you like. And I'd like to remind you that we have a - an update to the LM Contingency Checklist that we need to make before you leave - leave the LM.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Okay, we'll take that over in the Command Module, Karl. We'll go ahead and power the LM down now and clean up the housekeeping, and see you on the other side. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, stand by. We're interested in the OPS checkout.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Rog. We can give you that from the Command Module.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Roger.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: We'll do all the housekeeping. We'll just give you the report from Endeavour. [Pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Falcon, that all sounds good, and only one other mat - matter, and that's the docking index angle as you go back through.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Rog. We checked that. It was plus .1.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: Hey, Houston, correction. That's a minus .1.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Correction received.

a15_0342237.speaker: Scott
a15_0342237.text: It's so close to zero it's hard to tell.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Endeavour, this is Houston.

a15_0342237.speaker: Worden
a15_0342237.text: Okay, Karl. I'll go ahead and secure the TV now.

a15_0342237.speaker: Henize
a15_0342237.text: Very good.

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 49 minutes. That television transmission duration was 49 minutes, 6 seconds. The broken glass on the tapemeter will not be a constraint to the mission. The tapemeter is the instrument on the Lunar Module that shows altitude and altitude-rate during the landing sequence; and range and range-rate during the rendezvous sequence.

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: This is Apollo Control at 34 hours, 54 minutes. TELMU, the flight controller who monitors the Lunar Module Electrical Power System, got a good look at Falcon's batteries on telemetry while the Lunar Module was powered up. Reports that the battery condition is excellent.

a15_0342237.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0342237.text: This is Apollo Control at 35 hours, 3 minutes. Apollo 15 now 131,660 nautical miles [243,834 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,314 feet per second [1,315 m/s].

a15_0351036.speaker: Worden
a15_0351036.text: Okay, Karl. I've got the OPS checkout numbers for you if you want them.

a15_0351036.speaker: Worden
a15_0351036.text: Okay. Commander's OPS had a source pressure of 5,800 [psi, 40,000 kPa], 5,800, And a regulated pressure of 3.8 [psi, 26.2 kPa]. And the LMP's source pressure was 5,800, and regulator pressure was 3.85 [psi, 26.5 kPa].

a15_0351036.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0351036.text: That was Al Worden giving that report.

a15_0351036.speaker: Henize
a15_0351036.text: And, 15, when Jim has a couple of minutes, we'd like to ask a few questions about the High Gain Antenna.

a15_0351036.speaker: Worden
a15_0351036.text: Okay; he's off the headset right now, Karl. I'll get him as soon as I can.

a15_0351036.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0351036.text: This is Apollo Control at 35 hours, 35 minutes. Apollo 15 is 132,936 nautical miles [246,197 km] from Earth, traveling at a velocity of 4,278 feet per second [1,304 m/s]. We'll continue to stay up live, monitoring for any air/ground conversation.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Hi, Karl. Hey, listen; we're start - going to start up PTC here pretty soon. Do you want to update which RCS jets you want me to use? [Pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Stand by on that, Al.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay. I'll go ahead and do the Verb 49 maneuver and start damping rates.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Negative, Al. We want to stand by in this attitude.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Oh, okay.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: We - we are thinking real hard down here about your AC glitch and its possible connection to the loss of comm. [Pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Whenever Jim is available, we'd be pleased to ask a couple of questions.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Roger, Karl. You have to stand by on that. He's finishing up over in the LM right now.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Al, if you are looking for a job, I could read you up a flyby PAD.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay, Karl. [I'll] be a moment.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay, Houston; this is 15. Go ahead with the PAD, Karl.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Roger. Purpose is flyby, SPS/G&N; 66655; plus 1.24, minus 0.11; 073:30:56.80; plus 0257.2, plus 0230.9, minus 0314.9; 331, 109, 079; NA [meaning not applicable], plus 0020.8; 0467.6, 1:11, 0463.0; sextant star is 02, 148.5, 26.4; boresight star is NA; latitude, plus 13.32, minus 174.04; 1098.7, 36170; 170:59:57. GDC Align stars, Vega and Deneb; 209; 009; 349. No ullage. Comments. The burn is SPS docked. Number 2, use onboard preferred REFSMMAT, because of yaw gimbal angle. Number 3, LM weight is 36220. And that's all. [Long pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Roger; understand. Purpose is flyby, that's SPS/G&N; and PAD's as follows: 66655; plus 1.24, minus 0.11; 073:30:56.80; plus 0257.2, plus 0230.9, minus 0314.9; 331, 109, 079; and the next is NA; and I missed a couple in there. Picking up at sextant star would be 02, 148.5, 26.4; boresight star is NA; latitude is plus 13.32, longitude, minus 174.04; 1098.7, 36170; 170:59:57. Vega and Deneb are set stars; with angles of 209; 009; and 349. No ullage. And the SPS docked burn, use a preferred REFSMMAT because of the yaw gimbal angle, and the LM weight is 33260.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: The LM weight is 36220. [Pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay, Karl. Understand; 36220.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: That's correct. And down in Noun 44, H P is plus 0020.8, Delta-V T , 0467.6, burn time, 1:11, Delta-V C , 0463.0. [Pause.]

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Roger, Karl; understand. H A is NA, H P is plus 0020.8; Delta-V T is 0467.6, with a burn time of 1:11. Delta-V C , 0463.0.

a15_0361633.speaker: Henize
a15_0361633.text: Roger. That's all correct.

a15_0361633.speaker: Worden
a15_0361633.text: Okay.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Houston, this is - Endeavour. [Long pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Houston, this is Apollo 15. Over.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: 15, this is Houston. [Pause.] This is Houston; go ahead.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Yes, Karl, this is Jim, I'm back in and on comm. As far as that AC and main bus undervolt [are concerned], I have not much more to add than what I said before. Do you have any other questions?

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Roger. Stand by just about 30 seconds, and we'll come up with a couple.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Go ahead, Karl.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Jim, we've been doing a lot of thinking about that AC glitch down here, and - the coincidence of time - makes us guess that there was a connection with that power loss, but we don't see how. We'd like to start off with a couple of questions. The first one is, when you - reacquired on the High Gain Antenna, did you possibly notice that the High Gain angles were different from what you'd set on the knobs?

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Yes; as a matter of fact, they were.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Okay.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: I - I did nothing up here to reacquire on the - the High Gain [Antenna]. It came back automatically.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Okay; that's interesting information. Were there any talkbacks noted - changing state at the time of the glitch?

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: No change that I noticed.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Okay. Was anyone in the tunnel at the time of the glitch? [Pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Say again about the tunnel, Karl.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Was anyone in the tunnel at the time of the glitch? [Pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Stand by.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Okay, Karl. Al was in the tunnel, but there were no electrical connections being made at the time.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Roger. I - I guess a follow up question then - and you've probably answered it - is, was there any unusual activity associated with the tunnel umbilicals?

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Don't think so - we don't think so, Karl, not at that time.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Okay. And another question on this line is, what was and what is the position of the LM power 1 Main B and 2 Main B circuit breakers on panel 5?

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: They're both in [that is, they are Closed].

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Okay. If you have some minutes to spare up there, we'd like to go through a cockpit check for open circuit breakers connected with Main [bus] B and AC [bus] 2, on the theory that whatever happened might have blown a circuit breaker that wasn't obvious to you.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Okay. I'll - I'll do that now.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: We suggest - that - well, you know, this - figures 3-1 and 3-2 are a good guide to that for the normally open circuit breakers.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: I'll check all circuit breakers. [Long pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Jim, I've got the diagrams down here, if there's anything I can do to help you.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Okay; we'll look around.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Karl, this is Jim.

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Go ahead.

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Roger. On [panel] 226, under Lighting, Numerics/Integral, LEB [Lower Equipment Bay] AC 2 has been popped, or I believe it's popped, I would think it'd normally be closed now. [Long pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Henize
a15_0362950.text: Roger, Jim. We confirm that that is normally closed. [Pause.]

a15_0362950.speaker: Irwin
a15_0362950.text: Okay; it looks like it might be the problem.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: 15, This is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Go ahead, Karl.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: When you're through checking the circuit breakers, we have a little procedure we'd like to go through here as a - as a further check.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Okay. Did you want me to continue checking? I figured after I - Stand by.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Yes. I thought you checked them all, Jim. Sure. Check them all. Sure.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Roger, Jim. We - we'd like to have a - a complete check there, and don't - don't reset that circuit breaker, incidentally.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: I understand.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Not yet.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: ... do this?

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Okay. TV.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: ... That's over ...

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Yes, when I read it out to you. Not before.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Oh, yes.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Okay, Karl. I've checked all circuit breakers, and that's the only one that seems to be out of [the proper] configuration.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Okay; very good. What we're going to do, Jim, is to drop the uplink and see what happens. And just to clarify the communications glitch that we had, the ground station lost the power amplifier, and we lost uplink to you. There was apparently no loss of downlink. So what we want to do now is to - is to drop the uplink and see if it creates the same glitches that - as you got on the AC bus that time. In view of your circuit breaker being out, we don't think there's a connection, but we'd just like to have this final confirmation. And...

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Okay; we're standing by.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: ...to start the procedure here, we'd like to just double check that you - that the dials for the High Gain Antenna are setting at Pitch, minus 30; Yaw, 276.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Yes, that's correct.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Roger. And verify that we have...

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Yaw - yaw is really...

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Go ahead.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Yes, we're in Track, Auto.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: We - we'd like to have Auto and Narrow [beam width].

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Yaw is... [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Just let it go for a while. It's black and it's black and it's black.

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Pitch is minus 30, Yaw is 270, and Track is Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: You can stop that one someplace.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Okay.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Roger, Jim. And what we're going to do now is to drop uplink for 20 seconds, and you are to read out and record the High Gain Antenna dials and any changes that occur there. Then we'll bring up the uplink; and, at that time, we want you to require - reacquire High Gain Antenna on - on Auto, Narrow. Okay?

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: Okay. Right now the Yaw indicator [for the HGA] is reading about 280. [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: What does your dial say? [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: The dial is 280. The thumbwheel is 270.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: That's okay. And are you ready for us to drop the uplink? [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: [Faint] Yes, go ahead. [Pause.] Yes, go ahead.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Okay. We'll be dropping - dropping the uplink for 20 seconds. Here we go.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read?

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: This is 15. I read you loud and clear.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Roger. Did you observe anything special up there?

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Well, nothing other than the - the Pitch went to zero, and the Yaw decreased just very slightly. And, of course, when you reacquired, it went back to Pitch went back to 30. [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: That's right ....

a15_0364948.speaker: Worden
a15_0364948.text: Take this here ....

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: We copy.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Get it off?

a15_0364948.speaker: Worden
a15_0364948.text: Yes, I ... turn this PRD in.

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Get the PRD out of there while you're at it.

a15_0364948.speaker: Worden
a15_0364948.text: Out of - where is it?

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: It's in the pocket with yours, ... It's in your cuff - by your - top of your right hand. Ah, I got it.

a15_0364948.speaker: Worden
a15_0364948.text: Oh, okay ....

a15_0364948.speaker: Scott
a15_0364948.text: Is this PAD you copied down, Al, is that - the next midcourse, huh?

a15_0364948.speaker: Worden
a15_0364948.text: No. That's a flyby PAD.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: 15, this is Houston. That's enough troubleshooting, and we're ready to go to PTC now. And we'd like to have you use the A and D quads for damping. And use the B and D quads for spin up. And we'd like to confirm that we are using a spin rate of .375 [degrees per second] this time. [Pause.]

a15_0364948.speaker: Irwin
a15_0364948.text: We copied all that, Karl. A and D for damping, B and D for spin up. And .375 for the rate.

a15_0364948.speaker: Henize
a15_0364948.text: Roger.

a15_0364948.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0364948.text: This is Apollo Control; 37 hours, 4 minutes. Apollo 15 now 136,611 nautical miles [253,003 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,173 feet per second [1,272 m/s]. We'll attempt to - to recap and summarize what we've been doing here for the last hour or so and some of these tests we've been running. The Goldstone tracking station lost a power amplifier affecting a transmitter. We had a temporary loss of data. At the same time on the Command Module, an AC bus voltage alarm occurred. We've been running some tests to see whether there was any connection between the mishap at the tracking station and the alar

a15_0364948.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0364948.text: This is Apollo Control at 37 hours, 9 minutes. The flight controllers who monitor Lunar Module systems have been reporting to Flight Director Milton Windler on the status of these systems as they were observed by telemetry during the LM activation period. They all appear to be in good shape. The batteries look good, the Descent Propulsion System parameters are normal. The LM Reaction Control System parameters all normal. The supercritical helium pressure is good. That's the pressurization [system] for the Descent Propulsion System.

a15_0370902.speaker: Henize
a15_0370902.text: 15, this is Houston. Your rates look low enough to go into spin-up, if all of your vents have been closed.

a15_0370902.speaker: Scott
a15_0370902.text: Okay, Karl. I think we got everything closed, and we'll go ahead and spin her up.

a15_0370902.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0370902.text: This is Apollo Control. This spin-up will establish the Passive Thermal Control mode for the rest period. Spacecraft will be rotated at a rate...

a15_0370902.speaker: Henize
a15_0370902.text: 15, could you please confirm that you're on Omni Bravo. [Pause.]

a15_0370902.speaker: Scott
a15_0370902.text: That's affirm, Karl. We're on Omni Bravo.

a15_0370902.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0370902.text: The desired rotation rate for PTC is 3 tenths of a degree per second.

a15_0372007.speaker: Henize
a15_0372007.text: 15, this is Houston. We have a read-out down here that A-1 jet is on. Could you confirm that? And if it is on, let's turn it off. [Pause.]

a15_0372007.speaker: Worden
a15_0372007.text: Roger, Houston; 15. Your read-out is correct and it's now off. Sorry, Karl, I overlooked that one.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: 15, this is Houston. Your spin-up is looking very good to us, and when you have a couple of minutes to listen, we have a brief status report to send up to you. [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Scott
a15_0372341.text: Okay; go ahead, Houston. We're standing by.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Okay. In regards to your range-rate tapemeter - That is normally sealed in a helium atmosphere at 15 psi [103 kPa], and with that outer glass broken, this seal is broken and the meter is now operating in zero to 5 psi [34 kPa] in an oxygen environment. We don't know that this has any effect on it, but Grumman is doing tests to show whether or not its okay. Concerning the SPS...

a15_0372341.speaker: Scott
a15_0372341.text: [Garble.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Yes, go ahead.

a15_0372341.speaker: Scott
a15_0372341.text: I was just going to say, it'd be interesting to hear what they find out.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Roger, we'll let you know. Concerning the SPS, we're still reviewing the LOI [Lunar Orbit Insertion] procedures that we'll use, but it's probable that we'll want to start automatically on bank B and bring on [bank] A five seconds later, using the circuit breaker and then turning it off at 6 minutes and finishing up the burn on bank B. Its probable that the other burns, except for TEI, will be done on bank B only. Any comments on that?

a15_0372341.speaker: Scott
a15_0372341.text: No, that's just about what we were thinking too, Karl.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Okay. In the LM, the batteries and the SHe [Supercritical Helium] look in perfect shape. And concerning the lighting circuit breaker problem: we're still getting in the data in down here, and we'll review the situation with you tomorrow. We see no problem with the High Gain Antenna. And other than your - and other than your crew status report, and your onboard read-outs, that just about wraps up the evening. We'd still like to have your PRD read-outs, and I guess we have a battery charge in progress that will need to be cut off.

a15_0372341.speaker: Scott
a15_0372341.text: Okay, Karl; we'll finish up the rest of the items here and bring you up to date on all the read-outs, and - sorry about the PRDs, but since [garble] the suits [garble] tonight.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Okay. No problem on that. And I have a - I have the update to LM Contingency Checklist, and if you want to take it this evening, I can give it to you; otherwise, it can be put off until tomorrow. [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Okay, stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: [Garble] Karl, [garble] copy notes you have [garble, probably the LM] Contingency Checklist.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: 15, this is Houston. I heard you trying to come through but we were noisy just then. Hold off just a minute.

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Reading you better now; go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: 15, this is Houston. [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: 15, this is Houston. I'm reading you loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: You're loud and clear.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Roger. Did I understand that you were ready for the LM Flight Plan - Contingency Checklist update?

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Yes, I am, Karl. [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Roger. On page 1-1, down under "Power Transfer and RCS Heater Activation."

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Go ahead.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: At the end of step 2, add the following line: "Circuit breaker 16, Stabilization/Control. ASA, Close." [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Okay; I copy that.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Roger. On page 1-7, under "AGS activation." [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Okay?

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: I was standing by.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Add before step 1: "Verify ASA circuit breaker - has been Closed for 10 minutes. [Long pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Roger. Understand before step 1, "Verify ASA circuit breaker's been Closed for 10 minutes."

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Roger. The next one is page 2-5. [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: And on that circuit breaker configuration, in the second row down, put a black dot under the ASA circuit breaker. [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Okay; I understand.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: And on page 2-13. Under "AGS activation and Self Test" add before step 1: "Verify ASA circuit breaker - has been Closed for 10 minutes." [Pause.]

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Okay; I copied all of that.

a15_0372341.speaker: Henize
a15_0372341.text: Very good. That's all of the update.

a15_0372341.speaker: Irwin
a15_0372341.text: Okay; thank you, Karl.

a15_0372341.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0372341.text: This is Apollo Control at 38 hours, 1 minute. Apollo 15 now 138,871 nautical miles [257,189 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,110 feet per second [1,253 m/s]. Guidance, Navigation and Control Officer says it looks like a good PTC has been set up by Apollo 15. All indications point to that fact. However he wants to watch it a little while longer to make sure that we're in the proper rotation. Took three attempts last night to - to get the desired rotation. However, historically, we've had problems the first night in setting up Passive Thermal Control mode.

a15_0372341.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0372341.text: This is Apollo Control at 38 hours, 27 minutes. Apollo 15 is 139,914 nautical miles [259,120 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,082 feet per second [1,244 m/s]. Apollo 15 will reach the halfway point, in time, to lunar orbit at 39 hours, 17 minutes, 21.7 seconds. At that time, distance from Earth will be 141,860 nautical miles [262,724 km] and it will be 86,864 nautical miles [160,872 km] from the Moon.

a15_0383715.speaker: Henize
a15_0383715.text: 15, this is Houston. How are you enjoying dinner?

a15_0383715.speaker: Henize
a15_0383715.text: Great, glad to hear it. Hey, we'd like to ask a question about that glass breakage in the LM. Did it shatter into little bits or just a few big hunks? How well do you think you got it cleaned up? [Pause.]

a15_0383715.speaker: Scott
a15_0383715.text: Oh, I think we probably got about - maybe 50, 60 percent of what was broken, and it was broken into - some pieces on the order of three-quarters to an inch and other little millimeter type pieces.

a15_0383715.speaker: Henize
a15_0383715.text: Okay. I guess that gives us a picture of the situation. We're somewhat concerned about that having drifted into equipment or - yeah, into equipment. [Pause.]

a15_0383715.speaker: Scott
a15_0383715.text: Okay. Well we looked around and picked up what we could with [sticky] tape, and we took the vacuum cleaner over and ran it for quite a while to try and pull up what we could.

a15_0383715.speaker: Scott
a15_0383715.text: We don't have any idea why it broke. It didn't look like there was anything in the ISA [Interim Stowage Assembly] which could have done that to the - just the face of that meter. The ISA had mostly soft equipment. It was pretty well padded.

a15_0383715.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0383715.text: This is Apollo Control at 38 hours, 47 minutes. GNC [Guidance, Navigation and Control officer] says the Passive Thermal Control has been established satisfactorily on the first try tonight. So, we'll not need another attempt to do that. Apollo 15 is 140,707 nautical miles [260,589 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,060 feet per second [1,237 m/s]. Crew should be going through the presleep checklist very shortly now. Rest period scheduled to start at 39 hours. We'll continue to stand by live for the final air/ground transmissions of the day.

a15_0385351.speaker: Henize
a15_0385351.text: 15, this is Houston. We're ready to terminate the charge on Bat A now.

a15_0385351.speaker: Scott
a15_0385351.text: Roger. Terminate charge on Bat A.

a15_0385351.speaker: Henize
a15_0385351.text: And incidentally, we see a - an off-nominal drain on Bat A, and we'd like to verify that the Pitch 1 and the Yaw 1 circuit breakers on panel 8 are Open. If not, we'd like to Open them. [Pause.]

a15_0385351.speaker: Scott
a15_0385351.text: Okay. Standby. [Pause.] Circuit breakers are verified Open.

a15_0385351.speaker: Henize
a15_0385351.text: Thank you. And, let's leave them Open.

a15_0385351.speaker: Henize
a15_0385351.text: 15, this is - 15, this is Houston. I want to correct a false impression I gave you. We don't see any off-nominal drain on battery A.

a15_0385351.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0385351.text: This is Apollo Control at 39 hours, 15 minutes. Flight Director Glynn Lunney and his team of flight controllers are now preparing to take over in the Mission Control Room, relieving...

a15_0391546.speaker: Scott
a15_0391546.text: Okay. We have our presleep checklist when you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15_0391546.speaker: Scott
a15_0391546.text: Okay. Crew status report, everybody's in good shape. No medication today. The onboard read-outs: Bat C, 37 [volts]; Pyro Bat A, 37.2; B, 37.2; RCS A, 90 [per cent propellant remaining]; B, 89; C, 91; and D, 89. The [H 2 cryo] fans are being cycled now. The water has been chlorinated. All the valves are closed. We're getting ready to pump up the cabin. And we'll give you an E-memory dump whenever you are ready. [Pause.]

a15_0391546.speaker: Scott
a15_0391546.text: And one more thing, we've - I've got the PRDs for you.

a15_0391546.speaker: Scott
a15_0391546.text: Okay. CDR is 23020, the CMP is 5008, and the LMP is 8008. [Pause.]

a15_0391546.speaker: Henize
a15_0391546.text: Thank you, Dave. And incidentally, if you'd like to get rid of that biomed harness, you can change off now, you know.

a15_0391546.speaker: Scott
a15_0391546.text: Oh, that should work, right now.

a15_0391546.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0391546.text: This is Apollo Control. We're estimating the change of shift news conference for 12:15 am Central Daylight Time in the briefing room at the news center. Apollo 15 now 141,903 nautical miles [262,804 km] from Earth. Velocity; 4,028 feet per second [1,228 m/s].

a15_0392341.speaker: Henize
a15_0392341.text: 15, this is Houston. We're ready for the E-memory dump.

a15_0392341.speaker: Henize
a15_0392341.text: And, Dave, a - we - our telemetry says that the optics power is still on, and I'd like to remind you to turn it off.

a15_0392341.speaker: Scott
a15_0392341.text: Yeah, but we just got that off.

a15_0392341.speaker: Scott
a15_0392341.text: Well, Karl, does your telemetry tell you it's on or off now?

a15_0392341.speaker: Henize
a15_0392341.text: They were just telling me that - hey, it was off about the time that I called you.

a15_0392341.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0392341.text: This is Apollo Control at 39 hours, 38 minutes. We've completed the shift handover here in Mission Control. At the moment Flight Director Glynn Lunney is reviewing the status of the mission with each of his flight controllers. Our capsule communicator on this shift will be astronaut Robert Parker. A change of shift press briefing is scheduled to begin shortly in the MSC news center auditorium. Although we haven't said goodnight to the crew yet, we don't expect a great deal of conversation with them. Should we receive any communications between - with the crew during the briefing, we'll tape re

a15_0395711.speaker: Parker
a15_0395711.text: Roger. Guys, before you go to sleep, I'd like to have the mode - S-band Normal Mode - switch Voice to Off, please.

a15_0395711.speaker: Scott
a15_0395711.text: S-band Normal Mode Voice - switch Voice to Off. Is that it?

a15_0395711.speaker: Parker
a15_0395711.text: Roger. And, unless you guys have something else, we're going to let you go to sleep now.

a15_0490300.speaker: Allen
a15_0490300.text: Good morning, Apollo 15; this is Houston. Do you read? Over. [No answer.

a15_0490300.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0490300.text: Seems the voice subcarrier is not up yet to the spacecraft. [We're] waiting for the network to be completely set up to handle the two-way communications. Meanwhile, some distance and velocity numbers: Apollo 15 now 163,140 nautical miles [302,135 km] out from Earth; velocity now 3,499 feet per second [1,066 m/s]. We'll leave up the air/ground circuit live until the crew does respond.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: Good morning, Apollo 15; this is Houston. Are you awake yet? Over. [Pause.]

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: Good morning, Houston; this is 15. Reading you loud and clear there, Joe. Good morning.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: Good morning, Alfredo. It sounds like you had a good night's sleep. We're standing by for crew status.

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: Okay, Joe; we certainly did have a nice sleep, and we think your tracking data must be right, the Moon's getting bigger out the window.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: Roger, Al. At least our direction is right.

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: [It] appears that way. [Pause.] And, Joe, this is Al. We'll give you a status report here in about 5 minutes, when we get organized.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: That sounds good, Alfredo. And if you'd like, I'm standing by down here with a PAO [Public Affairs Office] Gold Bugle Morning News, if you'd like to hear some? [Long pause.]

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: Joe, can you stand by for a minute on that. We wouldn't want our LMP to miss it.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: No, I agree; he should be aware of it. I'll stand by.

a15_0490943.speaker: Irwin
a15_0490943.text: Joe, Jim's awake here now. Ready to listen.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: Okay, Apollo 15. This is your friendly news reporter with the morning news. Apparently the Houston Post reported, yesterday, that the Falcon's checkout went smoothly, and the mission is proceeding on schedule. The inside pages show drawings of how you will deploy the Lunar Roving Vehicle. They didn't tell us anything I think we don't already know so I won't go into the details of the drawings. In national news - Now, we may be use - losing communications now; I'll stand by a minute. [Long pause.]

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: Rog, Joe; we're back with you.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: All right. Moving right along, now, in national news, Secretary of Labor Hodgson has asked the United Transportation Union and the rail industry to put their dispute before a neutral panel for settlement. The U.S. Senate will vote today on an amendment to delay a federally guaranteed loan to Lockheed. The vote is expected to be very close. In local news, a Texas animal health commission employee said that he thinks that the Harris County vaccination program against sleeping sickness is almost at an end. I don't know if they're going to institute preflight quarantine on the animals or not. And

a15_0490943.speaker: Worden
a15_0490943.text: Okay, Joe. Thank you very much for the weather and the news this morning.

a15_0490943.speaker: Allen
a15_0490943.text: Okay, Al. And I have a CSM consumables update and a number of other things, when you're ready to listen to them. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Worden
a15_0491940.text: Houston, this is 15. We are ready to copy the consumables update [garble].

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Al, stand by. We're not receiving you clearly.

a15_0491940.speaker: Worden
a15_0491940.text: Okay. We'll stand by.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Rog; it's very weak, and severe noise in the background, 15. We're standing by for better comm.

a15_0491940.speaker: Worden
a15_0491940.text: We understand.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Al, this is Houston. The noise seems to have quieted down again. Why don't we give it another try?

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, Joe. Would you like to copy our consumables and then you can pass up S-band. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Okay.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, RCS [quad A], 90 [per cent remaining], [B,] 89, [C,] 90 and [D,] 89. On H 2 [tank 1], 92 [per cent remaining], [tank 2,] 90, [tank 3,] 70. O 2 [tank 1], 90 [per cent remaining], [tank 2,] 90 and [tank 3,] 85. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Roger, Jim. We copy all that. Let me give you a set of figures here. They agree very closely to what you've read to us. At GET 48 plus 00; the RCS total was 87 [per cent remaining]; and then Quad A, 86, 87, 86, 87. H 2 tank, 92, 92, 70. O 2 tank, 90, 92, 85. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, I copied all those. [Pause.] As far as sleep, Dave figures 8 hours and two segments; Al was 8 hours for two; and I figure I got 9 hours in about three segments.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Roger; we copy that. Sounds like that's the most sleep you've had in several months. Out of curiosity, since we're coming up on this eye-flash experiment, I wonder if any of you has noticed any of the flashes yet?

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Yes, we've noticed them both nights, Joe.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Okay; I guess we'll talk more about that a little later on. I have a number of other things to read up to you, in whatever order you'd like. They include a fairly extensive Flight Plan update; nothing profound but it will require some - certain amount of writing, and then a few miscellaneous questions which we'd like to ask you. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Ok - okay; I guess I can start on the - these Flight Plan bits. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Okay, Jim. And are you the recording secretary this morning? [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Yes. [Long pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Okay, Jim. Before we start, did you get the radiation dosimeter readings for us? [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: We reported them last night. Do you want them again this morning?

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Apparently, we'd like them again the - this - this morning on the schedule.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay; stand by.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, Joe. I have a radiation report for you.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, radiation. On Dave, it's 23023; Al, 25009; and mine is 08010. [Pause.]

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: We copy those, Jim; thank you. And normally, I guess, we'd like to have those in the postsleep period as opposed to presleep, which is when we got them yesterday. I guess it's in the checklist that way.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, we'll - okay, we'll normally do it that way.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Okay; fine, and I'm ready to start with the Flight Plan update. When you're set up to copy up there, I'll start at about 54:50.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay, let me get 54:50.

a15_0491940.speaker: Allen
a15_0491940.text: Fine, Jim. And we're coming up on a Omni switch. When we're on the new antenna, I'll start to read. You might want also your LM Activation Checklist handy because we'll be using it later on.

a15_0491940.speaker: Irwin
a15_0491940.text: Okay.

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Houston, how do you read 15?

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Jim, you're loud and clear, and we're ready down here if you are.

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay. I'm at 54:50 on the Flight Plan.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Okay. Before I start into it step by step, let me just say that it's basically - the - the change is basically moving some of the items around in time, and there's not many changes in procedures involved. The one main thing is, we're going to ask you to go into - into the LM a little early, I guess, earlier then you had planned. And we're going to also request that you give us enough - you bring enough of the telemetry online so we look at the - can look at the LM batteries. And there's no particular reason we want to do this today - nothing that we suspect is wrong - but rather, apparently, t

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay, I'm ready Joe. And we understand.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Okay; 54:50, [add] the step "If LM/CM Delta-P less than 2.7 psid [pounds per square inch, differential], LM Tunnel Vent valve, panel 12, vent until Delta-P greater than 2.7 psid." [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay. I have "If LM/CM Delta-P is less than 2.7 psid, LM Tunnel Vent valve on panel 12, vent until Delta-P greater than 2.7 psid." [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: That's correct. Now turn one page to 55 [hours] plus 15 [minutes in the Flight Plan]. [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay; I'm there.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Okay. Insert "Stop PTC [Passive Thermal Control] at roll 50 degrees. High Gain Antenna angles: Pitch, minus 48; Yaw, plus 82." [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Roger. "At 55:15, stop PTC roll 50 degrees; High Gain Antenna: Pitch, minus 48; Yaw, plus 82."

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: That's correct. Now, turn back several pages to 3-54 please. And that's the "Cycle film in Pan and Map Cameras" page - procedures page. [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay; I have it.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Okay. Down near the bottom, delete the line "SM Sector 1, SM/AC Power, Off." And add in its place "Map Camera on" - that should read "Map Camera on Standby/talkback gray." Over.

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay; understand. Delete "SM Sector 1 SM/AC Power off," and add "Mapping Camera on to Standby/talkback gray."

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: That's correct. Now, turn back to 55 plus 50, and there's a long series of deleted activities that will follow. These - [are] all because we're not going to do a midcourse [correction] 3, as you're well aware. And I'll call them out line by line, and they'll carry through for - I guess about a page and a half here. At 55:00 [means 55:50].

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Delete "P30 External Delta-V" and "V49 Maneuver to PAD Burn Att[itude]." Turn the page. [Pause.] Jim, I apparently made a mistake on that. That should have been at 55:50. I think you're at the right - the right place. Continuing on over to 50...

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Yes; I got it.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Rog. Continuing to 56 plus 00, delete the next seven lines up to the 2 lines which you should leave in "O 2 Fuel Cell Purge" and "Waste Water Dump." [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay; I have that.

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Okay. Continuing - continue deleting the lines below that, down to 57 plus 00. [Long pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay. So the only two actions we have on that page, 56 hours, is the "O 2 Fuel Cell Purge" and the "Waste Water Dump."

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: That's affirm. [Pause.] Now, once again backing up to the time, 55 plus 50. [Pause.] That should read "Verb 49 Maneuver to LM Checkout Attitude." [Pause.] And that attitude is "305, 090, 000." High Gain angle: "Pitch, minus 30; Yaw, 276." [Pause.]

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay. "Verb 49 Maneuver to LM Checkout Attitude" at 55:50; the attitude "305, 090, and 000; High Gain: Pitch, minus 30; and Yaw, 276."

a15_0493144.speaker: Allen
a15_0493144.text: Readback's correct, Jim. I'll stand by until we get another Omni[-directional antenna] change.

a15_0493144.speaker: Irwin
a15_0493144.text: Okay.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: 15, Houston. Our comm's quieted down again, and I'll continue if you're ready.

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. I'm ready, Joe.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Roger, Jim. At 56 plus 50, start "CSM Systems Checklist, IVT to LM," and this is an item that's moved up from 57:20, by the way. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay, at 56:50, start "CSM checklist, IVT to LM."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct, and you're to start that checklist from the beginning. And at 57 plus 00, you move the CSM PTC procedures to completion of our LM battery checkout. And I guess that's an item for Al. [Long Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand. I'll move all that there for the PTC until after we complete the battery checkout.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct, and that should come around 57 plus 50 or perhaps a little later. But, once again, not time critical. We're coming up on 57 plus 30. And, if you'll take out your LM Activation Checklist, page 1-1 , please. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; I have it.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay. And this is to start at 57 plus 30. Perhaps you should put a mark in your time line, but then on - on the checklist from page 1-1, delete "Comm carrier, CWG connector." [Pause.] Delete step 2. Delete step 5. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. On 1-1, I delete "Comm carrier, CWG connector;" step 2; and step 5.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's affirm. Do page 1-13. And if you'll turn to that, [pause] do 1-13 except in step 2. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: In step 2, delete "VHF B Transmitter, Close; VHF A Receiver, Close; CDR Audio, Close." And add the instruction "CB 11, ECS Cabin Fan, Close." [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Joe. On 1-13, under step 2, [I've] to delete "VHF B Transmitter, Close; VHF A Receiver, Close; Commander Audio, Close." And add "CB 11, ECS Cabin Fan, Close."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct, Jim. Do page 1-14, except in step 5. Delete "VHF A Transmitter, Close; VHF B Receiver, Close;" and delete step 6. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. On 1-14, we'll do all that. Under step 5, we'll delete "VHF A Transmitter, Close; VHF B Receiver, Close;" and want to delete step 6.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Readback's correct, and add step 7. Your comm S-band configuration is "PM, Secondary, Primary, Off; PCM, Off/Reset, Off, and High." [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. The S-band configuration is "PM, Secondary, Primary, Off; PCM Off/Reset, Off, and High."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct. We'll want you to stay in that configuration for 15 minutes while we take the data. After that time, do page 1-18 and 1-19 . [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Understand, [we are] to stay in that configuration for 15 minutes, then do 1-18 and 1-19.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. Sounding fine. Now, back into your time line. At 57 plus 45, proceed with LM housekeeping. And we've got some words here on the housekeeping. I'll read them to you, and I guess - Copy down whatever you think you haven't done yet. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand. At 57:45. We're to proceed with LM housekeeping, and go ahead with the - your steps, Joe. I'll note them down.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay. Vacuum [the] Cabin Fan filter. And as a subgroup under this, you unsnap netting around Cabin Fan filter. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Then you vacuum the filter. [Pause.] But do not scrub bristles of the vacuum cleaner over the surface of filter. [Pause.] Then, you remove the remaining particles on [the] Cabin Fan filter with sticky tape, using care not to dislodge [the] filter material. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Then, you remove the particles on the inlet screen of the vacuum cleaner with sticky tape; and, finally, replace the netting. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: And, Jim, that's the end of that procedure. Our comm's starting to fade out on us, so we may not be able to copy you. Hopefully, you're copying us clearly still.

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Yes, we are, Joe. I got that [garble]. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. And just an added note on that. As you're well aware, we're interested in cleaning up as many of those flying glass particles as we can, which is primarily the reason for - for this procedure. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Yeah; we quite agree, Joe.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay. At the time, 57 plus 45, the steps "S-band Aux, TV to Science, Pan Camera Power to On," and then, in parenthesis "for five minutes/Off." [Pause.] And finally, "S-band Aux, TV to Off." [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Joe. At 57:45, understand [that] you want the "S-band Aux, TV to Science." Then I missed the information after - after that, and then, finally, the last one was "S-band Aux, TV to Off." [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. What we're interested in here is looking at the Pan Camera temperature. And the center step, the one you missed, reads "Pan Camera Power to On for five minutes and then Off." [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand. "Pan Camera Power to On for five minutes and then to Off."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct. At 57 plus 50, "CSM proceed with PTC activation." [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. At 57:50, "CSM proceed with PTC activation."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Roger. And turning over a page to 60 hours. After the step, "S-band Aux, TV, Off," add "Pan Camera Self Test to Off." And...

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Stand by, Joe. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Joe, do you read me now?

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. Reading you loud and clear.

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: That last information you gave me on S-band Aux, TV. I add that - I added that in at 57:45. [Pause.] Is that correct?

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Jim, no; negative. Turn over the page to 60 hours, 60 plus 00. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; I have 60 hours. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Joe. I'm at 60 hours.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. This is a new step completely at 60 hours. We did say something at 57:45. I'll come back to that in a minute to make sure that's straightened around. But at 60 hours, after the step in the Flight Plan, S-band Aux, TV to Off, add 2 steps. And they are "Pan Camera, Self Test to Off" [pause] and "Map Camera On, to Off." Over.

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand. Two steps there after "S-band Aux, TV, Off." "Pan Camera, Self Test, Off" and "Pan [means Map] Camera On, to Off." [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That sounds - that sounds good, Jim. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Let's go back to 57:45. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. At 57:45, the three steps you added in there should be "S-band Aux, TV to Science; Pan Camera Power, On for 5 minutes and then Off; and S-band Aux, TV, Off."

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand that. I guess I got a little confused there, Joe, when you said turn the page, and you turn several pages to get to 60 hours. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: I think you caught me in that. I guess I did. Sorry. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. I'm ready to go on to the next one, Joe.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Jim. That completes the Flight Plan update, and you should know by now that you have to take me for what I mean, not for what I say. [Pause.] I do have...

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: We do.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Rog. I do have a note, which you can put down in the margin or wherever, and it involves subsequent P23 sightings if required. [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: And the note is "Reduce trunnion to less than 10 degrees before zeroing optics." [Pause.] And then, "Always do optics calibration after optics zero in P23." [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay, Joe. For subsequent P23 sightings, we're to reduce the trunnion to less than 10 degrees before zeroing optics, and always do the optics cal[ibration] after the optics zero in P23.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's exactly right, Jim. And that is all I have on my Flight Plan update. I guess we've got an afterthought here. I'll get with you in a minute. I do have some other questions which I'd like to ask, but let me give you this addition while you have the Flight Plan there on your lap. And it involves the time 56 plus 20. I'll stand by [for] when you're there. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay. I'm at 57 - 56:20.

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: Okay. The step is "Direct O 2 , Open until cabin pressure equals 5.7 psia." [Pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay; understand. At 56:20, "Direct O 2 , Open until cabin pressure equals 5.7 psia [pounds per square inch absolute, i.e. relative to a vacuum]."

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: That's correct. [Long pause.]

a15_0494248.speaker: Allen
a15_0494248.text: And, Jim. I'm going to wait until the comm gets a little better before I continue on here. Be a - a minute or so.

a15_0494248.speaker: Irwin
a15_0494248.text: Okay.

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: Jim, we've got about 3 or 4 small questions for you. Your choice whether you'd like to talk about them now or proceed on with the light flash experiment.

a15_0500553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0500553.text: No. We're going to delay that light flash experiment anyway until we get cleaned up here and have breakfast. So you can ask - ask the questions. We'll be thinking about it while we're cleaning up.

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: Okay. That sounds good. Our first one: we noted a very small load change on battery bus A yesterday, several minutes prior to your SPS burn, and we're trying to - to chase down what may have caused this. We suspect that you may have - have closed two circuit breakers that should have been closed and just are curious to know if you did close them, or if, when you looked to verify them, they were already closed. And, the circuit breakers in question are the SPS Pitch 1 and Yaw 1 circuit breakers that feed Bat A. [Pause.]

a15_0500553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0500553.text: Okay. We - we closed those per checklist, Joe.

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: Jim, I understand you closed them for the checklist. By that do you mean that you - when you looked at them, you found them open and closed them? [Long pause.]

a15_0500553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0500553.text: Okay. That's affirm[ative], Joe. They were open, and we closed them per the checklist.

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: Okay. The guys in the back room here psyched that out pretty well, I guess. Thank you. That - I guess that was a question mostly of academic interest. Al, the circuit breaker in the Lower Equipment Bay, AC2, is still out as you're well aware, and it affects a number of EL [electroluminescent: digital displays extensively used in the CSM and LM, and the predecessors to todays LEDs and liquid crystal displays] and DSKY lights and so on, and we'll want to talk to you later on today about this. It should be no problem in any way, but we do want to talk about - discuss [the] ramifications of the -

a15_0500553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0500553.text: Okay, Joe. On that - on that valve on [panel] 377. It was in Bypass, and Dave just cycled it to - cycled it to Normal and then back to Bypass.

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: Okay, Jim. Thank you. [Pause.] And that's all we have down here for the time being. I've been reading the Apollo 15 status report that's put out every two hours. What's normally several pages, is just a page today.
