And - with very few words on it, the most prominent one being the word nominal, the meaning of which I'm going to look up as soon as I get off this shift. [Pause.]

a15_0500553.speaker: Allen
a15_0500553.text: And, Jim, unless you have any questions, why don't you proceed on with a comfortable breakfast, and we'll be standing by for a callout of when your ready to continue.

a15_0500553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0500553.text: This is Apollo Control; 50 hours, 18 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The crew of Apollo 15 presently preparing breakfast aboard spacecraft Endeavour . Unstowing all the items for space breakfast. Very lengthy Flight Plan update [was] read up to the crew by spacecraft communicator Joe Allen. The crew said they would be back to Allen to discuss the day's activities after they've had breakfast. [They] also mentioned that they preferred to delay the Visual Light Flash Phenomenon Experiment, which is shown in the Flight Plan at 50 hours Ground Elapsed Time. This particular experiment will be delayed.

a15_0500553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0500553.text: This is Apollo Control at 51 hours, 8 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 15 now 167,260 nautical miles [309,765 km] out from Earth. Velocity; 3,405 feet per second [1,038 m/s]. Like most men at breakfast, they're probably reading the morning paper because they're sure not saying anything. We expect to hear from the crew of Apollo 15 after they tidy up following the breakfast meal. As mentioned earlier, the Visual Light Flash Phenomenon Experiment has been delayed by the crew. It was originally scheduled for 50 hours. There's nothing time critical about when they do this. Requires all three of

a15_0512302.speaker: Scott
a15_0512302.text: Okay, Houston. We're getting ready to do the light flash experiment, and we'd like to run the tape recorder so we can get the voice marks on it, if that won't interfere with any of your [garble].

a15_0512302.speaker: Allen
a15_0512302.text: Okay, Dave. Stand by. I'll inquire.

a15_0512302.speaker: Allen
a15_0512302.text: Roger. In answer to your question on the DSE, we'll handle the DSE from down here when we start the eye flash experiment. We do have a - a request of you before you start the experiment, though. We don't have the necessary oxygen purity in the LM yet that we think that we're going to need for the surface EVAs several days from now. And - consequently, we want you to start to vent the LM once again. We're going to drain it out and fill it with oxygen again later on today. So, if you would please, turn the Tunnel Vent valve to the Vent position before we start the eye flash.

a15_0512302.speaker: Scott
a15_0512302.text: Okay, Houston. And we'll take a couple of minutes here and run a hatch integrity check and make sure it's all fixed up, and we'll be with you in about 5 [minutes].

a15_0513601.speaker: Scott
a15_0513601.text: Okay, Houston; 15. The Tunnel [garble] the hatch looks good, we're willing to start the experiment.

a15_0513601.speaker: Allen
a15_0513601.text: Okay, Dave. We're standing by. And I could give you a few reminders on the experiment here, if you'd like them.

a15_0513601.speaker: Allen
a15_0513601.text: Rog. We're just interested - in primarily a mark from each of the three of you when you notice a - a flash. And then, you might indicate who it is calling it out and then a description, as you see it: position, color, etc., etc. And - if - any - if another one of you notices one in the meantime during the description, call 'Mark' and that one then takes precedent [means priority]. Over.

a15_0513601.speaker: Scott
a15_0513601.text: Okay. That's about the way we talked it over, Joe. We're all set. Thank you.

a15_0513601.speaker: Allen
a15_0513601.text: And, Dave, we'll be standing by for when...

a15_0513601.speaker: Scott
a15_0513601.text: Okay. If you'll start the tape recorder, we'll start.

a15_0513601.speaker: Allen
a15_0513601.text: Roger, Dave. And just wanted to make sure you - you understood that we'd also prefer the mark on real time comm, as well. [Pause.]

a15_0514330.speaker: Allen
a15_0514330.text: Roger, Dave. Since I've hadn't heard anything, I'll assume you haven't noticed anything yet. And I'm assuming, also, that you are wearing your eyemasks.

a15_0514330.speaker: Scott
a15_0514330.text: [Garble, probably: We get the] message, Joe, and the window shades are up [i.e. closed], and the cabin is dark.

a15_0514616.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0514616.text: And Lunar Module Pilot Jim Irwin has seen a light flash...

a15_0514616.speaker: Allen
a15_0514616.text: And, Al, any sensation other than just a flash?

a15_0514616.speaker: Allen
a15_0514616.text: Rog, Dave. And is it a - just a pinpoint, or a streak, or what?

a15_0514616.speaker: Scott
a15_0514616.text: All coming on the DSE, Joe.

a15_0514616.speaker: Scott
a15_0514616.text: We can give you that, but it might get confusing. [Long pause.]

a15_0514616.speaker: Scott
a15_0514616.text: Houston, so far we've all seen just point sources of light, rather than streaks.

a15_0514616.speaker: Allen
a15_0514616.text: Okay, Dave. And some of us are a bit...

a15_0514616.speaker: Allen
a15_0514616.text: 15, this is Houston. If you see something significantly different from the point source, we'd like a real-time voice description of it, as well as a DSE recorded.

a15_0514616.speaker: Scott
a15_0514616.text: Okay, Houston. Fine. It's just that when we're trying to talk back and forth with the time delay, it's going to get confusing on the comm for us to try and record... Mark CDR.

a15_0514616.speaker: Irwin
a15_0514616.text: Mark LMP. And this one did have a - a streak nature to it. Like it went from 8 o'clock over to the plus X position.

a15_0521439.speaker: Allen
a15_0521439.text: 15, this is Houston. Are you still with us?

a15_0521840.speaker: Allen
a15_0521840.text: 15, Houston. Are you still with us?

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Mark CMP.

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR.

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR.

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Mark CMP. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger, Al. And we're coming up on about 10 minutes remaining.

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Mark LMP. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Mark CDR. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay, Houston. We've got 60 minutes up here. How's your clock look? [Pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Dave. We're coming up on 60 minutes here too. And I've - I think that's certainly an adequate period. A couple of quick questions, though. Could you describe for us briefly your positions in the spacecraft during this time?

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay. We've got it - several comments for you, Joe. Let us un - uncouple here, and we'll talk to you for a while about this.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay. Houston, 15. I guess - we realize the interest behind this and the significance of the thing and - and we'll each try and describe what we saw in the way of the flashes. And I think - because of the randomnum - randomness of the flashes, it was probably better to let us go ahead and work out the events on the DSE. And I think, also, you'll find on the DSE, when you review the tape, that we've come up with a little scheme to give you some quantitative data, which may or not - may not be the best. And if you have any suggestions on future tests or how we can make it a little better for you

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger, Dave. Loud and clear.

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay, I guess - as far as my impressions, I would say 90 per cent of them were what I'd call a point source of light. And to give you perhaps an analogy, you might picture yourself sitting high in the stands of the - of the Ice Capades with the arena darkened and some single figure on the - on the ice, like Peggy Fleming, doing a nice thing. And you look across at the other side of the - the dark arena and somebody shoots a flashbulb out of their Instamatic or something, and that would be what I'd call a - a typical flash of intensity 5 on a scale 1 to 5, and we tried to sort these out relativ

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay, let Al give you his impressions.

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Okay, Joe. I guess I didn't see the same thing that Dave did - and - talking about the intensity, I guess that's a very subjective thing. But I guess the analogy with the flashbulb [garble] was pretty good for the brighter intensities, and it seems like there was - there was one flash maybe that was of [garble] an intensity in the majority of the [garble].

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Hey, Al - Stand - Al, stand by. Stand by.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Al, we're starting to lose you because we're changing our Omnis now. Could you stand by a second, and I'll give you a call back.

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Okay, Joe.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: 15, while you're standing by waiting for the Omni to come around where we can read you more clearly - Dave, that was a very, very nice description of the flashes. Of course, we're very pleased with the - apparently, the intensity values that you put on the - on the DSE. And I think our comm - comm is starting to improve here, Al, so I'll be standing by for your continued description.

a15_0522600.speaker: Worden
a15_0522600.text: Okay, Joe. I guess in addition to - to what's been said already, most of the light flashes seem to be of the order of flashcubes or maybe starbursts that you've seen in the summertime. I saw very few streaks or radial paths of light. They all seem to be just point sources of light, and - and I guess that's really about all I've got to add, Joe; I'll - I'll see if Jim's got something.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger.

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Joe, I just have one comment, [garble] that's on the tape. And that is, just after the timing [garble] ended, we were taking - about to take our masks off, I had one - very brilliant streak. [Garble]...

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Stand by - stand by.

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: ...[garble] at nine o'clock...

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Jim, stand by a second. Our comm's starting to drop out again, and it may be a partial problem with your microphone position. Stand by just a second though, please. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Okay, Jim. We have comm again. Proceed on.

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Roger. I wanted to comment on one brilliant streak that I had just after the timing period had ended, and I was about - I was in the process of taking the mask off, and there was a brilliant streak, intensity 5, that went from the 9 o'clock position - through 12 o'clock - and out the 3 o'clock.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger, Jim. We copy that. And could you tell us which eye that one was in?

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Well, it seemed like it went from the left eye to the right eye.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Okay; very interesting. Endeavour, the Principal Investigators on this, Dick Benson and Larry Pinsky, have followed it closely and are quite pleased, I think, with the data you've given us; they'll be looking at the DSE information in detail and may have a - some definite procedure changes to give to you later, based on the information you've given us so far. And I guess as far as we're concerned, we have no more questions.

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Okay; fine, Joe. We'll be standing by and I - I guess another thing that - that you've picked up - interesting thing, is that the - the flashes are quite easily located relative to either eye or the position within either eye, which I think we found rather interesting.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: That's remarkable, Dave. Right; thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: 15, when you get squared away there, we'll be looking for - your starting to charge battery B, battery Bravo.

a15_0522600.speaker: Scott
a15_0522600.text: Rog. Understand. And I might add one more comment that - in discussing that - that last one [meaning Dave's last statement], why, Jim didn't quite have that impression of localization within each eye, although Al and I both do.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Jim, this is Houston again. I have a small addition to your Flight Plan update which I can give you whenever convenient for you.

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Okay; stand by.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger; whenever convenient, Jim. No hurry on it at all.

a15_0522600.speaker: Irwin
a15_0522600.text: Battery charge B is in process.

a15_0522600.speaker: Allen
a15_0522600.text: Roger.

a15_0524557.speaker: Irwin
a15_0524557.text: Okay, Joe. I'm ready to copy these additional comments you have for the Flight Plan.

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: Roger, Jim. The first one is at 53 hours exactly, and it's just a note for you information. [Pause.]

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: Roger. In the left-hand side of the Flight Plan there, the "lift off time [if required]." Note that it is not required in this case so we don't have to worry about that. The - second change - is possibly not a change: at 60 hours, six zero hours, I wanted to double check your readback of the addition which I gave to you earlier. And it should read, at 60 hours: "Pan Camera Self Test, Off," and "Map Camera On, to Off." [I] wanted to double check that last step.

a15_0524557.speaker: Irwin
a15_0524557.text: Roger. I have both of those, Joe, and they occur after the [line which says] "S-band Aux TV, Off."

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: Okay; thank you very much, Jim. The third change is an addition to the LM Activation Checklist changes which I gave you earlier.

a15_0524557.speaker: Irwin
a15_0524557.text: Is it in the Activation Checklist or is it in the Flight Plan?

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: I think you copied it in the LM Activation Checklist on page 1-13.

a15_0524557.speaker: Irwin
a15_0524557.text: Okay. I'm on 1-13 of the Activation Checklist.

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: Okay, Jim. After the addition on that page, which read, "Circuit breaker 11, ECS Cabin Fan, Closed," add: "Circuit breaker 11, EPS: DC Bus Volt, Closed." [Pause.]

a15_0524557.speaker: Irwin
a15_0524557.text: Okay; copy: "CB 11, EPS: DC Bus Volt, Closed."

a15_0524557.speaker: Allen
a15_0524557.text: Okay, Jim. That's it from down here [in Mission Control] for a while.

a15_0525751.speaker: Allen
a15_0525751.text: Roger; Dave. The next time one of you floats past the LM/CM Delta-P gauge, could you get a readout for us please.

a15_0530131.speaker: Allen
a15_0530131.text: Apollo 15, go to P00 and Accept, please, for a clock sync update.

a15_0530131.speaker: Scott
a15_0530131.text: Rog. We're within about - 1200 to the mission timer. [Pause.]

a15_0530131.speaker: Allen
a15_0530131.text: Sounds pretty good to me. [Long pause.]

a15_0530131.speaker: Scott
a15_0530131.text: Rog. I guess I should have said 12 centiseconds.

a15_0530838.speaker: Allen
a15_0530838.text: 15, Houston. Requesting Block on the Up TM [uplink telemetry].

a15_0530838.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0530838.text: This is Apollo Control. 53 hours, 15 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Distance and velocity [are] now 171,365 nautical miles [317,367 km] from Earth; velocity, 3,315 feet per second [1,010 m/s]. Apollo 15 air to ground communications still live. This is Apollo Control.

a15_0531500.speaker: Scott
a15_0531500.text: Okay. On the way. Thank you.

a15_0535611.speaker: Worden
a15_0535611.text: Hey, Joe, I just did a Delta-V and null bias check if you want to copy some numbers.

a15_0535611.speaker: Worden
a15_0535611.text: Okay, the Delta-V check was - test was satisfactory. It was a residual minus 21.0 [fps] in ten seconds, and the null bias was .8 feet in 100 seconds.

a15_0535611.speaker: Allen
a15_0535611.text: Okay, Al. We copy. Thank you.

a15_0535611.speaker: Allen
a15_0535611.text: Roger. Will you be starting into your lunch break now?

a15_0535611.speaker: Allen
a15_0535611.text: Okay. That sounds like a good idea. [Long pause.]

a15_0535611.speaker: Allen
a15_0535611.text: 15, Houston. If anyone by chance floats past the LM/CM Delta-P gauge, we'd like another read-out.

a15_0535611.speaker: Worden
a15_0535611.text: Okay, Joe. We'll get that for you.

a15_0541228.speaker: Allen
a15_0541228.text: Roger, Al. Would you tell Jim, please, that I've got a - a change Echo to his LM Activation Checklist, when he finishes with lunch and wants to copy it down. No hurry on it, but I don't want to forget it.

a15_0542249.speaker: Allen
a15_0542249.text: Roger. The next time somebody goes down into the kitchen to mix up some food, could you read the Delta-P gauge for us, please. [Pause.]

a15_0542249.speaker: Allen
a15_0542249.text: Rog, Dave. As luck would have it, we lost our comm just as we got the Delta-P number from you. We copied 1.9. Verify that for us, please. And, also, would you make sure that the valve is still in the Vent position.

a15_0542249.speaker: Scott
a15_0542249.text: Roger. I checked that. It[the valve]'s [position is] LM Tunnel Vent and it's, well - 1.9 to 2 - pretty close.

a15_0542249.speaker: Allen
a15_0542249.text: Okay, Dave. Thank you. Just leave it in that position.

a15_0542833.speaker: Allen
a15_0542833.text: 15, this is Houston. We have a further question about that LM Tunnel Vent valve.

a15_0542833.speaker: Allen
a15_0542833.text: Roger, Dave. We should have had a much greater drop in pressure - during the - the time between these two readings. We want to confirm that you went to the Delta-P position to read the meter this second time. Over.

a15_0542833.speaker: Scott
a15_0542833.text: Oh, no. I thought you just wanted the reading in the Vent position.

a15_0542833.speaker: Allen
a15_0542833.text: No, sir. Apparently we have to go over to Delta-P, get a reading, and then go - return to the Vent position.

a15_0542833.speaker: Scott
a15_0542833.text: Yeah, that's absolutely correct, Joe. Thank you. We'll do that.

a15_0542833.speaker: Scott
a15_0542833.text: Okay. In the LM/CM Delta-P [position] - it's 2.9 [psi], and then back to LM Tunnel Vent it's 3.5 [psi].

a15_0542833.speaker: Allen
a15_0542833.text: Okay, Dave. We copy that. Sounds so much better.

a15_0542833.speaker: Scott
a15_0542833.text: Yes, it sure does, doesn't it.

a15_0542833.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0542833.text: This is Apollo Control at 54 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 15 still in Passive Thermal Control, or bar-b-cue mode, in which they roll about the longitudinal axis to stabilize the thermal response or heating on the spacecraft. [They are] scheduled to leave Passive Thermal Control shortly after 55 hours Ground Elapsed Time and prepare for the LM checkout and housekeeping. Present distance from Earth, 174,203 nautical miles [322,623 km]. Velocity; 3,254 feet per second [992 m/s]. Air to ground circuit with the crew still up live at 54:45; this is Apollo Control.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Houston, this is 15.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Roger, 15; go ahead.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Joe, I understand you have another change to the Activation Checklist.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Roger, Jim, I had to change Echo for you. I'm up to change Foxtrot already, if you're ready to copy.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: I'm ready to copy, Joe

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Okay. Nothing very profound here. It - it has to do with the LM housekeeping/cleaning procedures I read to you at 57 plus 45. And the procedures which I read were basically a cleaning of the vacuum Cabin Fan filter. And it involved unsnapping a netting around the Cabin Fan filter, running the vacuum cleaner over it, and finally replacing that netting. And we've had second thoughts about that entire procedure down here - mainly, because the netting is in too cramped an area to get to comfortably - it takes a long time to take the netting off and replace it, and the - the procedure is, actually,

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Ah, yes, you're clear so far. Do you still want us to turn the cabin fan on?

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Roger, Jim. In fact, the procedure now reads like this. Before you begin the LM Activation Checklist and you're entering the LM, we want you to vacuum all the LM accessible areas such as Velcro, places like that, where dirt and particularly glass particles have accumulated. Then, when you've cleaned it to your satisfaction, tape the vacuum cleaner to the [ascent] engine cover. Let it run while you're doing the rest of the housekeeping activities. Over.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Okay; I understand, Joe.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Okay, Jim. And then, finally when you're through with the housekeeping activities, clean the vacuum cleaner inlet screen with sticky tape. We think you'll probably find glass particles there which you can remove conveniently with the sticky tape. [Pause.]

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Okay; I copy.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Okay, Jim. That's all I had for you really.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Joe, this is 15 again.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Go ahead.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Roger. Did you confirm that you still want us to turn the cabin fan on?

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: That's correct. We - we confirm that. We want the cabin fan turned on.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Okay. And assume if we - if we should see any glass on the cabin fan filter, then I suppose we should try to get down there with tape and clean it off. [Pause.]

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Roger, Jim. That's right. It just - we do not now want you to unsnap the netting around that cabin fan filter, in spite of what we told you earlier. It still might be possible to clean that area with sticky tape - without unsnapping the netting, though.

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Okay; I understand.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Basically, as - I know you understand. We - we just want as much of the glass in the LM cleaned up as you can find. [Pause.]

a15_0550236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0550236.text: Okay. I think we cleaned it up pretty well yesterday, but we'll do it again.

a15_0550236.speaker: Allen
a15_0550236.text: Roger. Just look around. It may not take much at all to take it.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Houston. Apol... [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Yes, Houston. Go ahead.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: I was informed that you called. Did you call?

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Roger. We were wondering if you've got the High Gain angles for us...

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Stand by.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Yeah, we called you. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Houston, Apollo 15. [Pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay. We are ready to cycle the cameras, now, if you've got some High Gain [Antenna] angles for us.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Stand by on the High Gain angles. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Roger, 15. Your High Gain angles are Pitch, minus 75; Yaw, plus 36.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay; understand. Pitch, minus 75; and yaw, plus 346 [sic].

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Plus 36. Affirmative. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay; tell you what, Houston, we'll go back to 50 degrees roll and pick up the UV for you. Do it there. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, this is Houston...

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: And, Houston, 15. Did you copy the P52?

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Roger. We got your torquing angles. Thank you. And they say down here that you don't need to roll at the present time. We'd just as soon save the propellant.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Well, we'll pick it up at the 50-degree mark, when we come around.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Okay; that'll be fine.

a15_0552009.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0552009.text: This is Apollo Control. Maroon team Flight Director Milt Windler now taking over from Gerry Griffin. Going around the room talking to the various console positions. Being brought up to speed on what the next 8 hours' activities will be. Meanwhile, Apollo 15 is now 175,450 nautical miles [324,933 kilometres] from Earth. Velocity [is] now 3,227 feet per second [984 m/s] relative to Earth. Before too long the displays here in the Control Center should go to Moon reference data. They'll have a crossing into the lunar sphere of influence at about 63 hours, 52 minutes. This is an arbitrary figure, b

a15_0552009.speaker: Irwin
a15_0552009.text: Okay, Houston. We've got you on the High Gain [Antenna] now, and we'll check our circuit breakers, be ready to cycle the cameras when you're ready

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: We copy, 15.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay, Houston; 15. If you've got telemetry, we'll cycle the film on your cue. [Pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Roger. Stand by, 15.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, this is Houston. Before we cycle the cameras, we need to stop [the] PTC [mode]. You can either do that immediately - or else go through the - go through the 50-degree roll and use the angle[s] that are in your Flight Plan. That's your choice.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Oh, we'll just press on to 50 degrees, and stop there. We thought you could pick it up on the way around.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: That'll be fine. Thank you.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Houston, Apollo 15.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, this is Houston. Go ahead.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay. I'm taking a look at our attitude for the UV photos. We see we need a roll of 153 [degrees], and your update today gave us a roll of 050 degrees. And, it seems like we probably ought to stop the roll at 153, and just skip that 050 degree attitude so we can save the maneuver.

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: 15, the High Gain won't be available to us at the angle 153. [Pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: And, Houston; 15. For future reference, I - I guess we are to understand that you cannot do the camera cycling while we're in PTC, even though you have High Gain. Is that correct? [Long pause.]

a15_0552009.speaker: Henize
a15_0552009.text: Dave, there are pros and cons to that. We could do it if we finessed it just right. But since it's difficult, and we have to stop rolling anyhow, it's better to stop the roll this time.

a15_0552009.speaker: Scott
a15_0552009.text: Well, that - that's true. We're just trying to save you a maneuver. We [have] got to stop the roll and then start the roll again to get back to another spot. But, we'll go that way.

a15_0552009.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0552009.text: This is Apollo Control at 55 hours, 36 minutes. We're estimating the change of shift news conference in the News Center for 10 minutes from now, about 4:20 pm Central Daylight Time. Change of shift news conference approximately 4:20 pm.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay, Houston; Apollo 15. Standing by for the Map and Pan Camera, On, on your cue. [Pause.]

a15_0553649.speaker: Henize
a15_0553649.text: Roger, 15. We have a good High Gain lock on, and we're Go for the cycling of the cameras. [Long pause.]

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Roger, Houston. We're standing by for your cue to cycle the Map and Pan Cameras.

a15_0553649.speaker: Henize
a15_0553649.text: Roger. We are ready to cycle the Man and Pan - the - the pan and mapping cameras. Go ahead.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay. The Man and Pap [sic] cameras are coming up now.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay, Jim. How do you cycle those?

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay. Map Camera on to On for 2 minutes and then Off, and I'll set the camera.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: The clock is running. Pan Camera Self Test to on (up). Talkback barber pole, to five frames, and then gray.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: And then five. Then you do five frames.

a15_0553649.speaker: Worden
a15_0553649.text: ... he doesn't. I think you - you'll - you'll see at 5 - about 5 seconds - and then gray.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Did it go barber pole when you put it - put it on?

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Oh, I see, Al. It does five frames automatically, and then it automatically goes gray.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Good. Pan Camera Self Test to Heaters.

a15_0553649.speaker: Worden
a15_0553649.text: We still don't know whether it - what - anything about the craters.

a15_0553649.speaker: Irwin
a15_0553649.text: Okay, Pan Camera Self Test going to Heaters.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay. After mapping camera - Oh, wait a minute. Stand by for the bell.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: And when the bell rings, you want to go Mapping Camera to Off.

a15_0553649.speaker: Irwin
a15_0553649.text: Too bad they didn't put this panel over on Al's side.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: I think it'd been a lot easier for him during the flight - or during the...

a15_0553649.speaker: Irwin
a15_0553649.text: Yes. Yes, it would have, too.

a15_0553649.speaker: Irwin
a15_0553649.text: Didn't have any room for it ...

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Well, they probably - the wire ... probably were all built for this, you know.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Map Camera, Off. Okay, and then for 1 minute, we time the Mapping Camera, Off. And after it's been Off for 1 minute, Map Camera goes - the Map Camera, On, goes to Standby, and we should get a gray talkback. And the clock is running.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: You have another 49 maneuver, or you want to recoup -

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Oh, oh, it says - Well, you get the idea that the - Let's see - it says secure the high gain antenna.

a15_0553649.speaker: Scott
a15_0553649.text: Okay, Jim. Map Camera, On, to Standby.

a15_0554330.speaker: Scott
a15_0554330.text: Houston, Apollo 15. That completes the Man and Pap Camera operation. And if you're through, we'll secure the High Gain and maneuver to the UV attitude. [Pause.]

a15_0554330.speaker: Henize
a15_0554330.text: Okay. You're Go to maneuver to UV photo attitude.

a15_0554330.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0554330.text: This is Apollo Control at 55 hours, 45 minutes. The change of shift news conference is ready to begin. We'll take the air/ground off the release line and tape for later replay.

a15_0554703.speaker: Henize
a15_0554703.text: We wonder if you can give us an estimate of how long it takes between removing the Lexan shade and getting the cardboard shade back into the window, when you go into the UV experiment. We need something rough to, say, plus or minus 30 seconds.

a15_0554703.speaker: Scott
a15_0554703.text: Karl, this is 15. Looks like you just barely got started when we - when we lost the S-band. How about saying that over again, please.

a15_0554703.speaker: Henize
a15_0554703.text: Roger. We'd like to have an estimate of how much time it takes between removal of the Lexan shade, and installation of the cardboard shade, when you go into the UV experiment. Something rough to, say, plus or minus 30 seconds.

a15_0554703.speaker: Scott
a15_0554703.text: Karl, we've kept the cardboard in the window up to now. We've had no need to put in the Lexan, so we can't give you the number right now.

a15_0554703.speaker: Scott
a15_0554703.text: But we will - the next time we change it, [we'll] keep it in mind, and we'll give you the [garble].

a15_0554703.speaker: Henize
a15_0554703.text: Okay. We'd like to have an estimate on that, when you get a chance.

a15_0555749.speaker: Worden
a15_0555749.text: Okay, Karl. We're through with the UV photos, and the window number 5 is still clear.

a15_0555749.speaker: Henize
a15_0555749.text: Thank you very much for the report.

a15_0555749.speaker: Henize
a15_0555749.text: 15, this is Houston. You can terminate the charge - charging of battery Bravo. And, when you have a moment, we'd like to get a read-out on the LM/CM Delta-P. And, in about 20 seconds, we're going to have a handover and a loss of comm for 1 minute.

a15_0555749.speaker: Scott
a15_0555749.text: Okay, Karl. We're terminating battery B charge now.

a15_0560845.speaker: Henize
a15_0560845.text: 15, we'd like to have Omni Charlie, please. [No answer.] [Pause.]

a15_0560845.speaker: Henize
a15_0560845.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_0561349.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0561349.text: This is Apollo Control at 56 hours, 18 minutes. Apollo 15 now 177,110 nautical miles [328,007 km] from Earth. Velocity; 3,193 feet per second [973 m/s]. We accumulated 3 minutes, 37 seconds in tape during the news conference. We'll play that for you now.

a15_0561349.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0561349.text: We're back live on air to ground now. To clarify a couple of points in the Flight Plan update read to the crew late in the last shift. The start of the CSM's Systems Checklist for the intravehicular transfer [IVT] to the Lunar Module has been moved up from 57 hours, 20 minutes to 56 hours, 50 minutes. The actual IVT to the LM by the LMP and the spacecraft Commander has been moved up from 58 hours, 10 minutes to 57 hours, 30 minutes. This will not prohibit, however, the LMP and the CDR transferring into the LM earlier if they're ready to go earlier. At 56 hours, 23 minutes; this is Mission Cont

a15_0562545.speaker: Henize
a15_0562545.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_0562545.speaker: Henize
a15_0562545.text: 15, this is Houston. Are you reading us? [No answer.]

a15_0562545.speaker: Henize
a15_0562545.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read?

a15_0562545.speaker: Scott
a15_0562545.text: Yeah; Rog, Houston. We're 5 by. Our LM/CM Delta-P is off scale high. And I wonder if you're happy with the depress of the LM, and may we get on with repressurizing it and go to our housekeeping. [Pause.]

a15_0562545.speaker: Henize
a15_0562545.text: Roger, 15. You have a Go to proceed.

a15_0562545.speaker: Henize
a15_0562545.text: And, Al, can you tell us how the - the shade on window 5 - how the hole is being blocked. Do you have the Lexan over it, or do you have the camera in there? [Pause.]

a15_0562545.speaker: Scott
a15_0562545.text: Okay. We have the cardboard on it and the metal shade behind that. [Pause.]

a15_0562545.speaker: Scott
a15_0562545.text: We've been keeping the metal shade on that window to try and keep the temperature in the cabin down a little bit. When the Sun's coming in the windows, it warms things up pretty well.

a15_0562545.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0562545.text: This is Apollo Control at 56 hours, 31 minutes. The Guidance, Navigation, and Control Officer reports the Command Module and Lunar Module cabin pressures are now equalized.

a15_0563133.speaker: Henize
a15_0563133.text: 15, this is Houston. If you would go to a 5-degree med - deadband, they say down here we might save a little bit of propellant.

a15_0564531.speaker: Henize
a15_0564531.text: 15, this is Houston. If you've got a little cry - Cryo Press light up there - we see that down here, and that's expected at the moment.

a15_0564531.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0564531.text: This is Apollo Control at 56 hours, 52 minutes. Apollo 15 is 178,180 nautical miles [329,989 km] from Earth. Velocity; 3,171 feet per second [967 m/s]. Crew is busy now, making preparations to enter the Lunar Module. We'll continue to stand by live for any air/ground.

a15_0564531.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0564531.text: This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 2 minutes. Telemetry shows power on the LM now and we've just had acquisition of LM data on telemetry now.

a15_0570212.speaker: Worden
a15_0570212.text: Roger, Houston. [The] Falcon's all set up for data [telemetry to Earth], and want to know if you're getting it.

a15_0570212.speaker: Henize
a15_0570212.text: Roger. We're getting data from Falcon.

a15_0570212.speaker: Worden
a15_0570212.text: Okay. If you'll let me know - when you've gotten enough data from Falcon, then I can tell Jim to power that down.

a15_0570212.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0570212.text: That's Al Worden communicating from the Endeavour to CapCom Karl Henize.

a15_0570212.speaker: Henize
a15_0570212.text: 15, this is Houston. The batteries and the SHe all look to be in excellent shape, and we're ready to secure the instrumentation. They can go ahead to page 1-18.

a15_0570212.speaker: Worden
a15_0570212.text: Rog. Understand, Houston. We go on to 1-18. Thank you, sir. [Long pause.]

a15_0570212.speaker: Henize
a15_0570212.text: 15, Houston. Is it possible to get the ED bat[tery] readings?

a15_0570212.speaker: Worden
a15_0570212.text: Houston, the ED batteries are reading 37 on both.

a15_0570212.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0570212.text: This is Apollo Control. SHe is a synchronym [means acronym] for supercritical helium, which is used to pressurize the descent propulsion tanks on the Lunar Module.

a15_0572643.speaker: Henize
a15_0572643.text: 15, this is Houston. Would you please put O 2 Heaters 1, 2, and 3 all to Auto.

a15_0572643.speaker: Worden
a15_0572643.text: Rog, Karl. O 2 Heaters 1, 2, and 3, all Auto.

a15_0573442.speaker: Worden
a15_0573442.text: Rog, Karl. Looks like the - the LM checkout's coming along pretty good. We've checked out all the batteries now. When do you want us to start in the PTC? [Long pause.]

a15_0573442.speaker: Henize
a15_0573442.text: Rog, Al. We - we want to get a few minutes, about 5 minutes of SIM bay data there at - it's 15:45 in your Flight Plan, and then we're - then we can go into PTC.

a15_0573442.speaker: Worden
a15_0573442.text: Okay, Karl. If you're ready, we'll give you the SIM Bay data, now.

a15_0573442.speaker: Henize
a15_0573442.text: Hang on just 1 or 2 minutes. We're not completely set up down here.

a15_0574042.speaker: Henize
a15_0574042.text: Al, we're ready for the SIM bay data.

a15_0574042.speaker: Henize
a15_0574042.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have you turn O 2 Heaters 1 and 2, Off at this time and leave number 3 on Auto.

a15_0574042.speaker: Worden
a15_0574042.text: Okay, Houston. Coming Off with 1 and 2 and leaving 3 in Auto.

a15_0574042.speaker: Henize
a15_0574042.text: 15, this is Houston. We have enough SIM bay data and you can terminate that procedure, and we're ready, then, to go into PTC, and we would like - [RCS quads] Alpha and Delta for damping and Bravo and Delta for spin-up. [Pause.]

a15_0574042.speaker: Worden
a15_0574042.text: Okay, Houston; 15. Understand you've got enough SIM bay data so we'll turn it off. Going into PTC and using Alpha and Delta for damping and Bravo and Delta for spin-up.

a15_0574042.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0574042.text: This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 48 minutes. Command Module Pilot Al Worden will spin-up the spacecraft now to reestablish Passive Thermal Control mode. It'll take some time to determine whether we've achieved the proper rate of 3 tenths of a degree per second. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin will remain in the Lunar Module performing their housekeeping chores while Al Worden establishes PTC. We don't expect to hear from the spacecraft Commander or the Lunar Module Pilot until they do return to the Command Module. At 57 hours, 49 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_0575646.speaker: Henize
a15_0575646.text: 15, this is Houston. How are we coming along on closing up the LM?

a15_0575646.speaker: Worden
a15_0575646.text: Houston, 15. We're coming along, taking our time doing it, Karl, while we're getting going on [the] PTC [mode].

a15_0575646.speaker: Worden
a15_0575646.text: And we'll be a few more minutes - stabilizing the rates here for the PTC 'til we get all the dumps done.

a15_0575646.speaker: Henize
a15_0575646.text: Roger. And be advised that we're prepared to read up a fairly extensive revision to the SPS burns, and we'd like for you guys to - let us know when you're ready to - discuss it and copy it.

a15_0575646.speaker: Worden
a15_0575646.text: Okay, Karl. It'll be a while yet.

a15_0575646.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0575646.text: This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 57 minutes. Apollo 15 [is] now 180,124 nautical miles [333,589 km] from Earth. Velocity; 3,131 feet per second [954 m/s].

a15_0581235.speaker: Worden
a15_0581235.text: Okay, Karl. How do the [rotation] rates look to you now? [Pause.]

a15_0581235.speaker: Henize
a15_0581235.text: Okay. They - Okay, Al; they look good to us, and you can go ahead and spin her up.

a15_0581503.speaker: Henize
a15_0581503.text: 15. We'd like to have Omni Bravo, please.

a15_0581503.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0581503.text: This is Apollo Control at 58 hours, 43 minutes. Apollo 15 isnow 181,521 nautical miles [336,176 km] away from the Earth. Velocity; 3,103 feet per second [946 m/s]. We'll continue to stand by live to monitor any air/ground.

a15_0585340.speaker: Henize
a15_0585340.text: Al, this is Houston. Could we have High Gain, Manual and Wide.

a15_0585340.speaker: Henize
a15_0585340.text: We don't want to bring it up. We simply want to select Manual and Wide.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Houston, Apollo 15. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Henize
a15_0585711.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Rog. We're all up on the comm and ready to talk about the SPS.

a15_0585711.speaker: Henize
a15_0585711.text: Roger, Al. Dick Gordon's here and he's been involved in hashing all of this out, and I'd like to have him read it up to you and argue with you about it.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: I'll do that. Go ahead, Richard. [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Hello, Dave. No argument; what are you doing way out there?

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Oh, we're just sort of checking out the old LM...

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: ...taking a look at the pretty scenery.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Listen, we've been, as you might guess, been talking a great deal about P40 procedures, and we do have some changes to talk to you about and if you've got your G&N Dictionary [sic] handy and page 5-1 where the P40 thrusting goes, I'd like to go ahead and go through it and discuss it with you.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay, let's pull it out, Dick. [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We've got 5-1 out. Go.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay, Dave. Right below the "Verify the SIM Powerdown" line there, I'd like for you to insert two lines. "Circuit breakers, SPS Pilot valves, two of them, Open," and that should be a "Verify." [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. "CB SPS Pilot valve, two, Open; Verify."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: And then the next line would be "Circuit breakers EPS [Electrical Power System], Group 5, two of them, Closed; Verify." [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. CB EPS, Group 5, two, Closed, Verify.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Right there in the same column, underneath "Test Caution and Warning lamps," insert "EMS Function, Off; Verify."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Beneath "Test Caution and Warning lamps," "EMS Function, Off; Verify."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Roger. Then the next line would be "Circuit breakers, EMS Main A and B, two of them, Closed." [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. "CB EMS A and B, both, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay, Dave, That'll finish up that page. The next comment's on page 5-2, where it starts in with a TVC [Thrust Vector Control] check and prep, second line, "Circuit breakers, SPS 10, vice 12, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay; understand. "CB SPS 10, vice 12, Closed," and those are the two pilot valves?

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: That's affirmative. Okay. Page 5-3 at the two minute point - 58 with 2 minutes in parentheses - I'd like for you to scratch the line that says "Delta-V thrust A paren[thesis] B, Normal" and substitute "Circuit breaker, SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. "CB SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Closed," instead of the "Delta-V Thrust A and B to Normal."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: We got an Omni...

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Go ahead; we got it.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: ...Okay; we got an Omni switch; just hang on. [Pause.] Okay, Dave. The - the next one is on page 5-4 and it's an insert, where you get the flashing 99, below the line that says "Pro at TFI [Time From Ignition] greater than zero seconds," insert "Delta-V Thrust A and B, two of them, to Normal," and we'll come back and discuss that in a minute.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay, Dave. Did you get that? "Delta-V Thrust A and B, two of them, to Normal" right after the Pro at the flashing 99.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: No, we - we lost you on the comm there, Dick. At minus 2 minutes, and we verified that we scratched the "Delta-V Thrust A or B, to Normal," and substituted "CB SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Closed." That's the last we heard from you.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. On page 5-4. I was just talking about that line where you get the flashing 99, and the line that says "Pro at TFI greater than zero seconds." Under that line, insert "Delta-V Thrust A and B, two of them, to Normal," and I'm sure we'll want to discuss this in a little bit.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Yeah, it sounds like it. Okay. After "Auto Ignition, Pro at TFI greater than 7 - greater than zero seconds," insert "Delta-V Thrust" - Did you mean A or B or do you mean A and B, Normal.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: I mean - I mean at this time A and B, and we'll talk about different burns on this very subject a little later.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. A and B, Normal.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Down in the next paragraph where it's got the 06 40 and the emergency procedures for the flashing 97 40 for the SPS thrust fail, scratch the line that reads "Delta-V Thrust B paren[thesis] A, Normal," and insert "Circuit breaker, SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Closed." [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Stand by one.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. On the flashing 97, scratch "Delta-V Thrust B paren[thesis] A, Normal," and insert "CB SPS Pilot Valve B, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: That was SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Closed.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: That right?

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: That was Main A, Closed, Dave.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Main - Rog. Sorry about that, Main A, Closed; right.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. What we're saying - if you don't get an ignition on [bank] B, we want you to go ahead and use [bank] A.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. The next change is at 3 seconds. Scratch the line that says "Delta-V Thrust B paren[thesis] A, Normal," and insert "Circuit breaker SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. At 3 seconds, scratch "Delta-V Thrust B, A, Normal," and insert "CBS - CB SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Closed."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. In the bottom of the page, this is applicable to LOI only. And at 6 minutes into the burn, we want the line "Circuit breakers, SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Open."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. At 6 minutes into the burn, "SPS Pilot Valve Main A, Open."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. And then a note there for Jim. At that point, we do - we no longer want any PUGS manipulation for fuel valves.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay; understand. No PUGS after 6 minutes.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We'll talk about the reason for that in a second. I've got one more line [to add] in your P40 checklist, and then we can discuss some things. It's on page 5-5, it's in the cleanup column there, about halfway - no, almost to the "Pro" underneath the line that reads "Circuit breakers SPS Pitch 1 and Yaw 1, Open," insert "Circuit breakers SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Open."

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Beneath "CB SPS Pitch 1, Yaw 1, Open," insert "CB SPS Pilot Valve Main B, Open."

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. That cleans up the - the checklist items. Take the easy one first. And the reason we want to - to secure bank A during the LOI burn at 6 minutes is so we can get a handle on the single bank performance, and we anticipate making all of the other burns with the good bank, bank B, with the exception of TEI [Trans-Earth Injection]. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay; that makes sense.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. And I guess the - the other things we might talk about just - just briefly is that the procedures that we just gave to you are for LOI. For midcourse 4 and DOI [Descent Orbit Insertion], we'll use the same procedures, but we'll do it on bank B only, single bank burn; we'll use the good bank. And we won't do anything with the Pilot Valve for Main A or the Delta-V Thrust A. We'll just go ahead and do these procedures, but not use bank A at all. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay; understand. We'll use dual bank for LOI and TEI, and all other burns will be on bank B only, with no manipulation of the Delta-V Thrust A switch.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. And after we do our LOI and DOI, we should have some real good visibility into [that is: understanding of] bank B; and for Al's planning, when he's up there by himself for the Circ[ularization] and plane change burns, we'll use normal procedures. The old procedures Delta-V Thrust B, Normal at T IG minus 2 minutes, with the exception that we will make those burns [using a] single bank, and we will not attempt to use bank A. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Oh, okay. Well, then, we - we've got three groups and when Al solos, he's going to use single bank B just like he's always done with the circuit breakers with CB SPS Pilot Valve B in at the beginning of the procedures. Is that right?

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: That's correct. And for TEI, the only change we'll probably make is the procedure we just passed. We'll probably let bank A - we'll probably leave bank A in the burn until we get down to about 5 seconds to go, and the reason for this - if something happens to the banks then, we're within our RCS capability for midcourses. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. I guess - Okay; we - we can press on here, but we'll probably talk it over with you before each burn anyway, too.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Yes, I'm sure we will. And I guess the thing to talk about now is our reasoning, our thought processes on having you proceed at 5 seconds, and then having Al throw on both the Delta-V Thrust switches right after that. And let me go through it, and let you think about it then. The reason we want to do that now - even though we do have a great deal of confidence in bank B - but the SPS Engine Thrust light - we have no visibility into that system as long as that light is on. And, if for some reason, since we do have this suspect system here in A, we don't want to take the chance with B. And when

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. That sounds like you been doing some good deep thinking on it all. That fits pretty well, Dick.

a15_0585711.speaker: Henize
a15_0585711.text: Okay, Dave. We'll let you guys think about those - Hang on.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: 15, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: 15, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: 15, Houston.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We've got signal strength back, also, Dick. Go ahead.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay, Dave. I guess we might talk about MCC 4 [Mid-Course Correction number 4] just a little bit. We haven't really gone into this...

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: ...too deeply. We haven't gone into MCC 4 too deeply yet. Right now, it looks like it's a Delta-V of about, oh, 4.2 [feet per second, 1.3 m/s], and our intentions are at this moment to make that single bank burn with bank Bravo. And if something happens there, we're looking at possibly finishing that up with - with RCS. But we're not definite on that, and just wanted you kind of have a feel for it.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay; that makes sense. I guess we've got one point here, and looking at the post-ignition sequence on the LOI burn. In order to monitor start transients and retain Al's capability to take over in case we have a gimbal hardover at start or something like that, perhaps it might be better to push that circuit breaker, the SPS Pilot Valve Main A, closed, as soon as we get ignition. And then that would enable Al to get back over in the THC in case he's got a problem there. How about that?

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We did discuss that little bit down here about that time. We felt that we'd like to have the - the engine stable out - stabilize out to [be under full] guidance [control] and the engine on bank B before he even goes over and tries to get that Pilot Valve circuit breaker in. That will give us visibility on - on the DSE dump on how bank B is performing.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Then why don't we move it down sometime past 3 seconds, a little later. How would that fit you?

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Well, we discussed that one too, and 5 seconds was used. What would you like? [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Well, 5 seconds sounds a tad better than 3, and it gives - gives us a chance to get stable in here, and gives Al a chance to take a look at what kind of start transients we've got.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Dave, I guess our discussion around here - We had proposed 5 [seconds] at one time, and it was a change to your normal procedures of putting the other bank on, so I guess it's really your choice in this regard; 5 seconds is just as good as 3. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Yeah, okay. Well, [laughter] Al made the point that it's all changed anyway, because normally I bring on bank - the second bank in 3 seconds, and he doesn't have to worry about it. He's concentrating on the start transients and everything. So it's a complete change at any rate, and I think it might be a tad better to go to the 5 seconds with Al on the circuit breaker.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay; that sounds good to us. Yeah, Dave; the point's being made that it can be even longer than that, if you really feel like you need it. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Well, we'll shoot for 5 seconds and if Al feels uncomfortable about the start transients and wants to hang on to the T-handle, I think that ought to be his option.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: I couldn't agree more.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. Karl's got some things here, I guess, on the LEB lighting and stuff, and my question to Al is how he wants to handle the timing if he doesn't have that LEB timer for P24's and those good things that he's doing. [Pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: He's thinking. Just a minute.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We don't need an answer now. Karl's got some things on - on that. We can use this as a discussion period, I guess.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Dave, I'm going to go get dinner. We'll talk to you later.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Oh, okay. Thanks a lot, Dick; appreciate it.

a15_0585711.speaker: Gordon
a15_0585711.text: Okay. We'll be looking at you.

a15_0585711.speaker: Scott
a15_0585711.text: Good.

a15_0585711.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0585711.text: This is Apollo Control at 59 hours, 20 minutes. That was astronaut Dick Gordon, Commander of the back-up crew for Apollo 15, passing up to Dave Scott changes in procedures for the Service Propulsion System maneuvers. The P40 checklist he referred to; P40 is the SPS thrusting program in the computer.

a15_0592339.speaker: Scott
a15_0592339.text: Okay; we're standing by for the rest of the comments you may have on the circuit breaker, et al .

a15_0592339.speaker: Henize
a15_0592339.text: Roger. We'll be with you in just a couple of minutes.

a15_0592339.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0592339.text: This is Apollo Control. It appears that Dave Scott and Jim Irwin spent about 2 hours in the Lunar Module. We copied the start of LM data as 57 hours, 2 minutes, and the first call from Dave Scott back in the Command Module came at 58 hours, 57 minutes. We'll continue to stand by live for more air to ground. CapCom Karl Henize is waiting to pass up some more information to the crew shortly. At 59 hours, 26 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: 15, this is Houston.

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Houston, 15; go.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Just a quick note on the - on the circuit breaker on the illumination, and then a procedure that might clarify a couple of things for us. First of all, there's a - a number of numeric and electroluminescent lights that are out, but we won't go into all of that. The main thing is the panel 122 DSKY down there [in the LEB]. The - As far as we can see at the moment, there is some possibility that we still have illumination on your status lights on that DSKY, and if we go through a small procedures here, we may find out whether or not there will be illumination on this. Stand by.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: 15, this is Houston. Are you reading. [No answer.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: 15, this is Houston. [No answer.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: 15, This is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Go ahead, Karl.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Right. Back to our lighting circuit breaker. Let me emphasize two main points to start with. I guess, under no circumstances, do we want to close that circuit breaker. And a second - problem is a - a - a second point is that we don't want to change the Integral Lighting, or the Numerics lighting rheostats on panel 100. Let's leave them just as they are. And then there's the - there is a possibility due to the fact that there is a very low amperage shunt going around that circuit breaker, there is a possibility that we do have lights on the DSKY status lights; that is, the Uplink Activity light

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Okay. Go ahead, Karl; we'll take a look at it.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Okay. First of all, on panel 100, again making sure that we do not change the Numerics and Integral lighting switches [means rheostats], can you tell us the position of those two switches, those two - rheostats?

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Okay, we'll tape them into [the] position they are right now. [Long pause.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Go ahead. [Pause.] 15, this is Houston. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Okay, Houston. We just did a little checkout for your LEB DSKY, and the key release light doesn't work - for one - does not work.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Roger. I guess you are a couple of steps ahead of us there. Can you tell us the position of - of the Numerics knob over on panel 100?

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: About 2 o'clock. [Pause.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Roger, I guess that's - that's one of our weak points. If - if that switch had - if that knob had been over close to full Bright, we had some chance of getting enough energy into those lights to make them work, but in that position, that's probably not possible. And we should leave things as they are.

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Well - well, I - I'm not sure those Integral lighting rheostats have not been moved since the circuit breaker popped. I guess if you want to, we could run it over to full Bright, or I guess you probably prefer to leave it as it is, and if so, we'll give up on the status lights.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: The word at the present time is let's leave them just as they are, Dave.

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Okay. We'll put a piece of tape across so that we don't accidentally run into them.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: That's all we have on that subject, 15. You probably know as well as we, what lights you're missing up there. We could give you a list if you would like.

a15_0593354.speaker: Scott
a15_0593354.text: Oh, no. We've got a good handle on it, Karl. Thank you.

a15_0593354.speaker: Henize
a15_0593354.text: Roger.

a15_0594802.speaker: Henize
a15_0594802.text: I've got one small comment for you, and then a small update to the Flight Plan. First of all, they've init - they've gone through a very thorough test on the range-rate [tape]meter and how it operates under those pressures and in that pure oxygen atmosphere, and so far as we can see at the present time, there's no problem whatever in its operation, but we'll continue that test. In the Flight Plan at 60 hours on the - on the SIM bay procedure to get some data from the cameras there, I have a small change, if you have the Flight Plan out. [Pause.]

a15_0594802.speaker: Henize
a15_0594802.text: Right. That procedure should go in this order. First, the "S-band AUX, TV to Science," as is already there. Then the "Pan Camera Power, On for 5 minutes, and then Off." After the power goes off, wait for a MSFN cue [i.e. a cue from Mission Control via the MSFN] because we want to pick up some data in that - in that state as well. After you get a MSFN cue, then we go to the "Pan Camera, Self Test, Off," the "Mapping Camera, On switch to Off," and then the "S-band Auxiliary, TV, Off," in that order. And we're going to need the High Gain Antenna for this job. And we're going to have a Pitch, minu

a15_0594802.speaker: Irwin
a15_0594802.text: Okay. We copied all that. [Long pause.]

a15_0594802.speaker: Henize
a15_0594802.text: Roger. And when we come close to the right time, let us know when you're ready to start, and then we'll let you know when we're ready.

a15_0594802.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0594802.text: Those last few exchanges have been with Jim Irwin.

a15_0594802.speaker: Irwin
a15_0594802.text: Karl, this is 15. We're ready to do that now, or whenever you're ready. [Long pause.]

a15_0594802.speaker: Henize
a15_0594802.text: 15, we copied. And stand by; within 1 or 2 minutes, we'll be able to give you a Go.

a15_0595406.speaker: Henize
a15_0595406.text: 15, this is Houston. It looks like we have a 2 to 3 minute wait yet.

a15_0595722.speaker: Henize
a15_0595722.text: 15, this is Houston. You're Go to turn on the Pan Camera telemetry. We need to bring up the High Gain Antenna first and then turn on the Pan Camera telemetry.

a15_0595722.speaker: Irwin
a15_0595722.text: Pan Camera Power is on now.

a15_0600157.speaker: Henize
a15_0600157.text: 15, this is Houston. We're ready for the "Pan Camera Power switch, to Off."

a15_0600157.speaker: Scott
a15_0600157.text: Oh, very well. Pan Camera Power is coming Off. [Pause.]

a15_0600157.speaker: Irwin
a15_0600157.text: Pan Camera Power is Off. [Long pause.]

a15_0600157.speaker: Henize
a15_0600157.text: 15, Houston. You can proceed with the rest of that procedure.

a15_0600157.speaker: Henize
a15_0600157.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Omni Bravo.

a15_0600157.speaker: Henize
a15_0600157.text: At your convenience, give - give us the Wide Beam on the High Gain Antenna. And the system down here says that your PTC is excellent. In fact, it's one of the best they've ever seen.

a15_0600157.speaker: Scott
a15_0600157.text: Oh, very good. Okay; you want High Gain [Antenna], Wide Beam, huh?

a15_0600157.speaker: Henize
a15_0600157.text: We - we don't want to bring up High Gain; we just want to select Wide and Manual.

a15_0600157.speaker: Scott
a15_0600157.text: Oh, okay. Okay, we - we['ll] do that.

a15_0600157.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0600157.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 15 now 184,029 nautical miles [340,821 km] from Earth. Velocity; 3,055 feet per second [931 m/s]. The recent discussion on the circuit breaker and the lighting in the Command Module, that is the circuit breaker that popped open last night. The DSKY they were referring to - the lighting in the DSKY - is the display and keyboard in the computer in the lower equipment bay. The DSKY on the main panel in the Command Module is not affected.

a15_0600157.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0600157.text: The crew apparently found nothing amiss in the Lunar Module during this latest visit. The Flight Plan calls for negative reporting, that is, if something is different from the normal, they will report it, otherwise they will not. They haven't reported anything concerning the Lunar Module housekeeping. We did monitor, by telemetry, the LM systems for a period of 5 minutes, early - right soon after the crew had gone into the LM. All the LM Flight Controllers reported the systems looked very good. At 60 hours, 11 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_0603411.speaker: Henize
a15_0603411.text: 15, this is Houston. How are we set for the Bistatic Radar Frequency Check? [Long pause.]

a15_0603411.speaker: Scott
a15_0603411.text: Karl, we're just about ready for it.

a15_0603411.speaker: Henize
a15_0603411.text: Okay; we're about ready down here, too. Let us know when you're Go. [Pause.]

a15_0603411.speaker: Scott
a15_0603411.text: Houston, this is 15. We're all configured up here.

a15_0603411.speaker: Henize
a15_0603411.text: Roger. We copy, and stand by. [Pause.] 15, we're turning off the uplink now.

a15_0604323.speaker: Henize
a15_0604323.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_0604323.speaker: Henize
a15_0604323.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_0604323.speaker: Henize
a15_0604323.text: Good; it sounds like we've got our uplink going again. That next bit down there about ground cue, it'll be about 20 minutes before we get - get down to that.

a15_0604323.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0604323.text: This is Apollo Control at 60 hours, 49 minutes. Apollo 15 now 185,078 nautical miles [342,764 km] from Earth. Velocity; 3,035 feet per second [925 m/s].

a15_0610358.speaker: Henize
a15_0610358.text: I guess we've got all the data we need down here. You can go ahead and turn the VHF off.

a15_0610736.speaker: Henize
a15_0610736.text: Looks like a very quiet night tonight. About the only question we've got for you at the present time is your assessment of the glass clean-up. How did it go? [Pause.]

a15_0610736.speaker: Scott
a15_0610736.text: Well, we got a - a few more pieces just by looking around over there. Some of the smaller like - oh, I guess the largest piece we found was about a centimeter or so, and the vacuum cleaner picked up a bunch of small chips. I guess - In total, we may have 60, 70 percent of the portion that broke, and I think we've really picked up all that is practical at this stage.

a15_0610736.speaker: Henize
a15_0610736.text: Roger. Any special places this stuff seems to collect that you can tell? [Pause.]

a15_0610736.speaker: Scott
a15_0610736.text: I think, initially, we found most of it was - up near the COAS [Crew Optical Alignment Sight] mount and behind the panel on the left side - near - near the forward part of the window. We found several - several larger pieces there and also one large piece just above the data file, which was about an inch long or so. The small pieces seem to have been drifting all about.

a15_0610736.speaker: Henize
a15_0610736.text: And 15, we didn't forget your state vector. It's just that the one you've got on board is very good. We don't need - we feel we don't need an update.

a15_0610736.speaker: Henize
a15_0610736.text: Just polishing off a hamburger and French fries down here. What's on the menu up there tonight?

a15_0610736.speaker: Scott
a15_0610736.text: Oh, stand by a minute, Karl.

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Hey, Houston, 15.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Can you give an - give us an estimate of how many drips per second it is?

a15_0611236.speaker: Irwin
a15_0611236.text: Yeah, it's a - it's a pretty good flow right now. Drips per second, it's hard to measure; it's a whole ball of water right around that valve right now.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Rog... [Pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: What we need is a check valve that we can close or get to, to isolate that port, if we can get one.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Dave, I - I had a problem when I chlorinated on launch day. And, when I first took the valve off, I had about what you've got - quite a strong flow. The cap - the cap stops it from flowing when you put it back on, and after I chlorinated, the flow decreased down to a very slow drip, say once a minute.

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Oh, this is a big run, Karl, and the cap is on tight, and it - you can almost feel something flowing beneath the cap.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Okay, stand by. Lots of people [are] thinking down here now.

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: [Garble]. [Long pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Houston, 15. It seems to be leaking from behind that panel there, right behind where the waste tank servicing valve is, and the potable tank inlet - and it's accumulating at a pretty good rate.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: We copy.

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Hey, Houston; 15. Got any suggestions yet? We need to isolate this thing pretty quick.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: In - just a minute. [Long pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: What was... [Long pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: 15, this is Houston. Our recommendation is that on [panel] 351, you turn the Water and Glycol Tanks Pressure, Regulator, Off. On [panel] 352, turn the Potable Tank Inlet, Off. [Pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Okay. Potable Tank Inlet is now closed, and say again the other one.

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Up on panel 351, Water and Glycol Tanks Pressure, Regulator, Off. [Long pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: Okay, Water and Glycol Tanks Pressure, Regulator is Off. [Long pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: 15, Houston. That should - that should have taken the pressure off of the Potable Water Tank; is it helping the situation any?

a15_0611236.speaker: Scott
a15_0611236.text: No, it's still leaking, Karl; pretty good rate. [Pause.]

a15_0611236.speaker: Henize
a15_0611236.text: Roger; stand by.

a15_0612257.speaker: Scott
a15_0612257.text: Houston, [it] looks like maybe we ought to start dumping out of the waste [water tank] so we can dump out of the potable tanks. It's still leaking and we've got everything but the check valve between the Potable Tank and the chlorine nozzle isolated. [Long pause.]

a15_0612257.speaker: Henize
a15_0612257.text: We copy, Dave. No comments yet. Stand by.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, Houston. We note the pressure in your tank coming down. In the meantime, we suspect that the [pause] we suspect that the fitting there on your chlorine injector outlet is loose, and we have - we have a procedure here for tightening it up.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay; give it, quick.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Roger. We need tool number 3 and tool number W out of the toolkit.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay; 3 and W out of the toolkit.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Right; put - put number 3 in the tool W ratchet, and insuit - sert tool 3 in the hex opening in the chlorine injector port.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay. That's - that looks like where it's probably leaking. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: And, once we have the number 3 tool in the hex opening, it should go in about a quarter of an inch to really engage. It also says "use caution when inserting the tool because it comes in contact with a rubber diaphragm." [Pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: We've agreed down here it's a good idea to take the water gun to fill up a food bag or something of that sort.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Once you've got tool number 3 well engaged in that injection port, turn it about a quarter turn.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay, Houston. It looks like that did it.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Wonderful. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Nice to have the quick response you guys have down there.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Well, you'll never believe it, but after we had the leakage on the morning of the 26th [launch day], somebody sat down and wrote up a special procedure, just in case.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Well, that was good thinking because we about had a small flood up here.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, Houston. We're looking now at the best procedure for getting the water system operating again. In the meantime, we trust you have your hands full of water up there.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Oh yeah. All we have to do now is hang out a few towels to dry, but it looks like we're in good shape.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Very good. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, Houston. We'd like for you to turn the Regulator back on, on panel 351.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay. Regulator coming back on.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, Houston. Is everything looking all right on the leak now?

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Yeah; it looks okay. That fitting there that we tightened up went somewhere between - 180 - 270 degrees of turn. And that - that was where the water was coming from, and it looks like it's secure now.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: We copy.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Hey, Karl. We just ran a little check with our slide rule here, and it was something like 3,000 drips per minute.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Okay guy...; glad to hear that good news. I - I guess up there you don't get drips, do you; that's an interesting fact.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Okay, Dave. We're ready to open the Inlet valve to the Potable Water Tank.

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Okay; Potable Water Inlet coming open.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Incidentally, Dick [Gordon] was over at Lurton's [Dave's wife] and they called up to say "Hey, it's about time you take a bath up there."

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Well, we were sort of discussing that a little earlier tonight anyway. And, as a result, well, I guess we all got cleaned up.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Good enough. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: And, Houston, with the fitting secure now and everything ship-shape, what do you think about proceeding ahead with the chlorination. [Pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: Okay, Dave. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, this is Houston. The word here is to go ahead. [Long pause.]

a15_0612539.speaker: Scott
a15_0612539.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0612539.speaker: Henize
a15_0612539.text: 15, this is Houston. Are - are we in comm[unication] now?
