But we will use our spare - spare film judiciously for the kind of things you hear us talk about that you'd like pictures of.

a15_0800132.speaker: Henize
a15_0800132.text: 15, this is Houston. Joe just came up from below to tell us that Farouk and company are ecstatic about what you've told them so far and that all of the SIM bay experiments are looking to be in excellent shape.

a15_0800132.speaker: Scott
a15_0800132.text: Okay. Thank you, Karl. That's good news.

a15_0800132.text: This is Apollo Control at 80 hours, 4 minutes.

a15_0800402.speaker: Mission Control

In the transmission a few minutes ago the - the 'Joe' referred to is Dr. Joe Allen, a scientist-astronaut, who is the Mission Scientist for the Apollo 15 crew on this mission. The Farouk to whom Karl Henize made reference is Farouk El-Baz, a geologist who has had a great deal to do with the training of the crew. And we're 15 minutes away from Loss Of Signal on this first revolution of the Moon.

a15_0800402.text: This is Apollo Control at 80 hours, 8 minutes. We show Apollo 15's present altitude as 92 nautical miles, velocity 5,316 feet per second.

a15_0801607.speaker: Scott
a15_0801607.text: Okay, Houston; understand. Swirls on Crisium, 3-photo convergent stereo, f/8 1/250th with the 250.

a15_0801607.text: Roger. And Al, you wanted us to remind you about your helmet and gloves when you take shots of Ingenuity this time around. [Pause.]

a15_0801607.text: Okay. Thank you, Karl. We will.

a15_0801607.speaker: Scott

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: You - you're not lis...

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Oh - Oh, okay. Waste water...

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes. You're not paying attention to me again, Jim.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: ...25 percent.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Okay.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: He closed it.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: You're right. Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: You wanted me to confirm that it had been closed.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes, right.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: I don't see a drop anymore.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: [Garble].

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Okay. [Garble].

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Huh?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Can't see that ridge you were talking about, Dave.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: You're going across it. Right where the terminator comes out. No, that's the horizon. Okay. I'm [Garble]. Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Isn't that a good boy, Al?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Hey, Jim, here's this little vent.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Okay.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Worden
a15_0802019.text: Jim, I don't see [garble].

a15_0802019.speaker: Worden
a15_0802019.text: I see. That's - Ingenuity over there on the...

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Hey, Jim, what did you do with those tissues that were over here? Remember?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: I didn't use any of them, Dave.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: No, but - there wasn't any of those little...

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Those medium [garble]?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: What?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: The very subdued rille that runs aro - perpendicular to the mountain? Oh, I see what you mean. Along the edge of the - Is that on the edge of [garble]? Of Ingenuity, huh?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: I can keep you posted here about - You take - you take photos until about 49 here.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: This must be Gagarin coming up.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Think I have better luck holding the map backwards.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: That's Gagarin we're over, huh?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Do you know what Keyhole looks like? Geeze. That's the kind of thing that would be good to explore.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: There's that neat one with the very white ejecta pattern - out at 1 o'clock.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Do you want to [garble] the window?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: I think we better get this - all the windows down.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes. I think we better leave. You know you don't have to get them all, Al. [Garble].

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Oh, yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: [Garble] might be Auto.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Hey, Jim?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: You got your sunglasses?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Not quite, Al. Did you just pass me some sunglasses, Dave?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Okay.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: I think they're yours. Aren't they?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: You can see that - see the canyons on it?

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Find Keyhole, Al? Good.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: What's distinctive about Keyhole?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Oh, really?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: I can sure see a lot - lot of blocks around this one coming up. A lot of blocks on the rim. And a slump on the - the west side of it.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Okay, the next one is target number 7, Al. It's The Bright One.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: That's...

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: The one with slump blocks in the center of it?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: The one we're just coming up on, huh?

a15_0802019.speaker: Worden
a15_0802019.text: Yes. That's it. Yes, that's Dooze [?]. Bright One. Yes, that's the one we want to get a - complete - We want two pictures of the ejecta pattern all the way along through there.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Yes, there's King over there.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Hey, Jim?

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Yes.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Hey, Jim, [garble] take care of that little map. That's the only one we got - you and I.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Yes, I understand.

a15_0802019.speaker: Scott
a15_0802019.text: Take good care of it.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: No, we have another set - Well, the only one of the little ones. Yes, you're right. Don't ask for [garble], huh?

a15_0802019.speaker: Worden
a15_0802019.text: By golly, old Bright Crater is a bright one, too. It's got good ray pattern. Glass all over.

a15_0802019.speaker: Irwin
a15_0802019.text: Geesh.

a15_0810000.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0810000.text: This is Apollo Control. Dr. Gary Latham, the principal investigator on the Passive Seismic Experiments on the lunar surface will hold a news conference in the Apollo News Center briefing room in about 5 minutes to discuss the S-IVB impact seismic signals received a short while ago. To repeat, Dr. Gary Latham will hold a news conference in the Apollo News Center briefing room in about 5 minutes to discuss the seismic signals received from the Apollo 15 S-IVB impact.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Okay, let's see. Let's try to get this Rooster Tail.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: The next target you have is Ibn Yunus.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes, but I'm going to try and see if I can get a shot of the Rooster Tail here if I can.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: That won't go anywhere.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: [Garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: You what, Jim?

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: [Garble] Ibn Yunus ought to be coming up on the left side here shortly.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes. Should be.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: Oh, look at the Earth come up - Earthrise. [Garble] all day, we ought to look at that [garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Oh, yes.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: [Garble] you don't [garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Yes.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: Golly.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: That ought to be good for a picture, huh?

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Oh, yes. Be better when you're [garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes. I got part of the LM in the way there.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Let me see here - let me - Yell if you see the Rooster Tail.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: I'm not sure what the Rooster Tail looks like, Al.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: That's that little secluded - dome on a - on a ca - on a small crater that Farouk was showing us the other day.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: Yes, I think there's one...

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: That a...

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: ...coming up here - that...

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: It should be quite obvious if you see it.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: Well, there's kind of an occluded area to the west.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: It looks - it looks very much like a rooster tail.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: [Garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: See the one coming up, Dave, ... in the occluded area - to the west?

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Is that the one [garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes, I think it's very fresh.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: Should it be right on track?

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes. Right underneath.

a15_0810200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0810200.text: [Garble]. There's one underneath us. Big rille and [garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Could that be it - the one we're just coming up on, Al?

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes. That's it. Must be it.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: [Garble] a shot of it here.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes.

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: There's Babcock out there.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Hey, Al, can I do a Verb 62 in this P20 or will it kick it back out?

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: No. It'll keep it in.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Maybe I ought to get up there and do one ...

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Yes. It should. It should work.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: [Garble].

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Fifteen and 12.

a15_0810200.speaker: Scott
a15_0810200.text: Fifteen and 12?

a15_0810200.speaker: Worden
a15_0810200.text: Uh-huh.

a15_0810200.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0810200.text: This is Apollo Control at 81 hours, 2 minutes. We're a minute away from Acquisition Of Signal time for Apollo 15 on its second revolution of the Moon. We'll stand by live now for first words on this rev.

a15_0810200.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0810200.text: We do have a signal, we'll wait until we have good antenna strength to attempt to talk to the crew.

a15_0811131.speaker: Scott
a15_0811131.text: Rog, Houston. Looks like we're getting locked up now.

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Okay, Houston, 15.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Go ahead, 15. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Okay, Karl. While I got a minute here waiting on Crisium to show up, I'll give you a run down on what we've done so far.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Go ahead.

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Okay; we got the strips of photos of the Sea of Ingenuity - or Ingenii - and took a look at the light colored swirls in the bottom of the mare. I couldn't tell - no elevation associated with those light-colored swirls, and they're very distinct when you look at them at this angle. Also - looked at the - at the area just adjacent to Ingenii; there is a very definite valley that cuts through the edge of the wall there, and with what looks like a rille in the bottom [AS15-91-12374] , what's been described as Vallis Alpha Reed - I guess it is kind of unique; it's the only one we've seen on the bac

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Roger, sounds like you did it up brown.

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Well, it does look - sometimes brown, sometimes gray, Karl. But we'll see when we get back.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Hey, let's keep those colors straight, fellows.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, we can take High Gain [Antenna] to Auto now.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, we need to go back to Reacq - on the High Gain. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: Rog. Reacq.

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0811515.speaker: Worden
a15_0811515.text: Okay, Karl. Just a couple of general observations on Crisium while we're coming up on it. Proclus coming up from the east is really spectacular. You can very distinctly see the - the difference in the - in the color or the albedo in the excluded zone of Proclus, and as you are coming up across Crisium with Proclus ahead, you can see the ray pattern very distinct - extending out across Crisium - and follow the ray patterns almost as far as you like. And the excluded zone in the - in the ray pattern is just very distinct at this point.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Excellent. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: And, Houston, from this angle looking at Proclus about a crater diameter out to maybe a diameter and a half or so, you can see many small bright fresh craters, which appear to be in the general direction of a ray, like part of the ejecta blanket.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Roger, Dave. You mean to say that these small bright craters seem to be clearly related to the ejecta blanket. Is that correct?

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: That's the impression I get. They occur within a diameter to a diameter and a half of Proclus and - they're about the same brightness as the inner walls of Proclus and they're small - just small craters. I don't see any - Yes, I do see one which you might call a loop, which would suggest secondaries. They just seem to lie in the general direction of the rays of the ejecta from Proclus.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: We copy.

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: They're sort of localized to one area which is - probably - yeah, on the - on the western side of Proclus, northwest side.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: We copy that. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Do you - do these small, bright craters have more or less a uniform size or do they come in varied sizes? [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: I'd say - Karl, this is Jim - I'd say they're various sizes.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Okay.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: It is - I - I guess it depends, Karl, on - what do you mean by sizes. There are various sizes within a certain sorting. They - they seem to be fairly well sorted within one range, but within that range, there is a distribution. And they're all much, much smaller than Proclus.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Okay, we copy.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, this is Houston. If you'll give us Accept, we'll send up a - a state vector and a target load. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Roger. You have it.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: And, 15, we don't require a PIPA bias check at this time. And I have a terminator photo PAD when you're ready to copy.

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Okay. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: And I'm ready for the terminator photo PAD, Karl.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Roger. The T start is 81:44:10, and there's a note here that the PCM cable may not reach to window 3. And if it doesn't, go ahead and run on the intervalometer alone. And this pertains to all future photography in window 3. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Roger. We understand. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, we'd like to go to Auto again [on the High Gain Antenna], and go directly from Reacq to Auto without a pause.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: You're in Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: The High Gain looks good this time; thank you.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, Houston. When you can copy, I have both a DOI [Descent Orbit Insertion] PAD and a TEI-5.

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Stand by one, Karl.

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Okay. I'm ready to copy the PAD.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: Roger. DOI; SPS/G&N; 39800, plus 1.68, minus 0.55; 082:39:48.29; minus 0208.4, minus 0048.0, plus 0002.0; 000, 283, 347; 0058.4, plus 0009.2; 0213.9, 0:24.5, Delta-V C is 0208.4; 33, 144.2, 35.7; the rest is NA. Set stars, Vega and Deneb; 288, 340, 346. Ullage is 4 quads, 15 seconds - 15 seconds.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: And the computer is yours. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Okay, Karl, if you're ready, here's the readback for the DOI PAD. SPS/G&N; 39800, plus 1.68, minus 0.55; 082:39:48.29; minus 0208.4, minus 0048.0, plus 0002.0; 000, 283, 347; 0058.4, plus 0009.2; 0213.9, 0:24.5, 0208.4; 33, 144.2, 35.7; Vega and Deneb; 288, 340, 346; 4 quads, 15 seconds.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: That's all correct. And your next is a TEI-5 PAD. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: All right, go ahead.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: TEI-5, SPS/G&N; 38206; plus 0.58, plus 1.01; 088:25:47.09; plus 2864.3, minus 1227.7, minus 0317.0; 180, 091, 338; the rest is NA. Set stars, Vega and Deneb; 288, 340, 346. 4 jets, 12 seconds. This - Comments are that the burn is undocked and it assumes DOI [has taken place]. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Irwin
a15_0811515.text: Okay. TEI-5 readback. SPS/G&N; 38206; plus 0.58, plus 1.01; 088:25:47.09; plus 2864.3, minus 1227.7, minus 0317.0; 180, 091, 338; Vega and Deneb; 288, 340, 346; 4 jet, 12 seconds. Undocked and assumes DOI.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: That's all correct. [Long pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0811515.text: This is Apollo Control at 81 hours, 37 minutes. CapCom Karl Henize has just read up the information on the Descent Orbit Insertion burn to the crew.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: Apollo 15.

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: Okay, as a quick review here, DOI is a single bank burn on B, with nominal procedures, with the exception of having the A Pilot Valve open. [Pause.]

a15_0811515.speaker: Henize
a15_0811515.text: That's affirmative, and if we have no ignition, we'll postpone the burn [for) a rev.

a15_0811515.speaker: Scott
a15_0811515.text: Roger; understand.

a15_0811515.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0811515.text: This is Apollo Control. Ignition time for the DOI burn; 82 hours, 39 minutes, 48 seconds; Delta-V, 213.9 feet per second; duration of the burn, 24.5 seconds. The resulting orbit targeted for 58.4 by 9.2 nautical miles [108.2 by 17.0 km]. Again, this burn will be done behind the Moon while we're not in contact, as was the Lunar Orbit Insertion burn. We'll continue to stand by live to monitor air and ground.

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: 15, this is Houston. We're showing a low voltage on the battery relay bus down here. We think it's just a matter of instrumentation, but there's a couple of procedures we'd like to run through here to check it out. [Long pause.]

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: Okay; first of all, we'd like read - have an onboard read-out of the battery relay bus voltage, which is B-5 on the test meter.

a15_0814100.speaker: Irwin
a15_0814100.text: Okay, Dave moved the - stand by. Dave wiggled the selector to the right - That's on B and the position that backs the B position and now we're reading 3.5.

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: Roger. And we just recovered our read-out of - We got a good voltage reading down here now.

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: Okay; thank you. We'll think on that for a while and everything looks - everything looks fairly normal.

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: 15, we have only one more question on that problem. And can you tell us what position you were in before you went to 5-B on the test meter.

a15_0814100.speaker: Irwin
a15_0814100.text: B was selected, Karl, but Dave moved the selector out of - just barely out of B and back into the B position to obtain the higher reading.

a15_0814100.speaker: Henize
a15_0814100.text: Roger. And what about the numerical side; was it in 5?

a15_0814739.speaker: Henize
a15_0814739.text: 15, this is Houston. And I have a map update for rev 3. [Long pause.]

a15_0814739.speaker: Scott
a15_0814739.text: Okay; go with the map update for rev 3.

a15_0814739.speaker: Henize
a15_0814739.text: Roger. And while you're on that page [of the Flight Plan], I have information for the landmark J-1 observation.

a15_0814739.speaker: Henize
a15_0814739.text: T-Hor [time when J-1 is on the spacecraft's horizon] is 8 - 83:39:33; TCA [Time of Closest Approach] minus 20 [seconds], 83:41:25. [Pause.]

a15_0814739.speaker: Scott
a15_0814739.text: Okay, understand. T-Horizon at 83:39:33; TCA minus 20, 83:41:25.

a15_0815520.speaker: Henize
a15_0815520.text: It's our understanding that we'd agreed that you'd send down magazine numbers and final frame numbers on each pass on this photography, and if you're in agreement with that, we'd like to have the magazine and frame number on the orbital photography and also on the terminator photography.

a15_0830900.speaker: Scott
a15_0830900.text: Nothing to change it over here at all. Nothing to change it, Al, [garble] that we could use.

a15_0830900.speaker: Worden
a15_0830900.text: How about a - Let's see, what kind of [garble] we use. 25.958?

a15_0830900.speaker: Worden
a15_0830900.text: Yes, and you got [garble]. Five point [garble] here. [Garble].

a15_0830900.speaker: Worden
a15_0830900.text: [Garble]. And - I'm going to push these back in.

a15_0830900.speaker: Scott
a15_0830900.text: [Garble] to be all set up with your G&C Checklist [garble] GDC Align.

a15_0830900.speaker: Scott
a15_0830900.text: I get that initial downhill impression. We're supposed to be [garble].

a15_0830900.speaker: Scott
a15_0830900.text: There it was, whatever it was.

a15_0830900.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0830900.text: We have AOS on the Command Module.

a15_0831509.speaker: Scott
a15_0831509.text: Did you get this [garble] on, Jim?

a15_0831509.speaker: Irwin
a15_0831509.text: Yes, but I never could tell [garble], when it went on.

a15_0831509.speaker: Scott
a15_0831509.text: Hello, Houston, Apollo 15. The Falcon is on its perch.

a15_0831509.speaker: Henize
a15_0831509.text: Good to hear you coming around that corner. How do things look?

a15_0831509.speaker: Scott
a15_0831509.text: Okay. Burn status report. Burn was on time. The burn time was about 24.0 - about half a second shorter than predicted. There was no trim; residuals were plus .6 [fps], plus .0, minus .1; Delta-V C , minus 4.4; fuel 29 - 29.25 [per cent of full]; and the oxidizer was 29.55; unbalance, 100 increase. [Pause.]

a15_0831509.speaker: Henize
a15_0831509.text: Thank you, Dave. We copy all that. [Pause.]

a15_0831509.speaker: Henize
a15_0831509.text: Hey, that's an interesting astrophysical observation.

a15_0831509.speaker: Scott
a15_0831509.text: And, Houston, 15. The G&N [Guidance and Navigation computer] had us in a 58.4 by 10.0 [nautical mile, 108.2 by 18.5 km orbit].

a15_0832114.speaker: Scott
a15_0832114.text: Houston, 15. We're in an attitude now in which we cannot see the surface. But our initial impressions after the burn, when we could see the surface, is that we were rolling in on a high-angle pass.

a15_0832114.speaker: Scott
a15_0832114.text: And, Al just added, we were.

a15_0832114.speaker: Henize
a15_0832114.text: 15, this is Houston. You're Stay in the DOI orbit, and we have an orbit for you of 58.8 by 9.5 [nautical miles, 108.9 by 17.6 km].

a15_0832114.speaker: Scott
a15_0832114.text: Very good, Houston. 58.8 - 9.5 and we're Stay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0832114.speaker: Henize
a15_0832114.text: 15. You have a Go to proceed to the landmark observation attitude.

a15_0832114.speaker: Henize
a15_0832114.text: And would you please give us Auto on the High Gain [Antenna]?

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: Okay, Houston, 15. We've got a little bit of visual - visibility now, and we're down in Crisium. [Pause.]

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: And it looks like we have enough altitude to get up over the [mountains on the] western rim!

a15_0832954.speaker: Henize
a15_0832954.text: You know, I sure hope so. [Long pause.]

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: But it sure looks like we're looking up at some of those fellows [the mountains] down there.

a15_0832954.speaker: Henize
a15_0832954.text: That must be sort of exciting, skimming along down there over the waves.

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: That's a mild word for it. [Pause.]

a15_0832954.speaker: Henize
a15_0832954.text: Hey, can you see anything more about those sw - swirls? Anything...

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: No, we're too close. And right now I've just finally picked out the rim of Proclus, and we're just about level, altitude-wise, with the - the rim of Proclus. I cannot see down into it. I can see just a tad of the southern wall. I guess we're just north of it. I can see some large blocks on the outer walls.

a15_0832954.speaker: Scott
a15_0832954.text: But I'd say we're definitely at an altitude even with the top of the rim of Proclus.

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Okay, Houston, we're coming up on the edge of Serenitatis now and I can look out and see a rille that runs parallel with the eastern edge. We're taking some pictures.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Roger, I suspect that's Littrow Rille. [Long pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: And after Littrow Rille, you should be coming up on le Monnier. Do you have much chance of seeing down at that angle? [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Scott
a15_0833610.text: I doubt it, Karl. At this attitude for the landmark tracking, the windows are almost out of it. Jim's got some visibility out window 5.

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Karl, we just passed the wrinkle ridges about a quarter of the way across Serenitatis, and the - there is a - definitely a topographic high in the middle of the wrinkled portions. [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Roger, 15, we copy. [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Are those ridges smooth, or do they show signs of lots of cracks in them?

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: I was impressed with the smoothness of the - the raised portion.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Okay. I'm taking several pictures of the wrinkled ridges that run roughly north and south in Serenitatis.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Excellent, Jim.

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: In the one we just passed over, there were some vertical fractures, definite vertical relief, in the smooth portion of the raised wrinkled ridge. The fractures were also running north and south.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Roger, Jim. We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Karl, just a spectacular view as we glide across the Sea of Serenity, and I'm taking a picture now of a sinuous rille out to the north.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Roger, Jim.

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Okay. We're approaching the mountains now on the western side of Serenitatis. At this point, there's a wrinkle ridge running to the - the northwest. [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Worden
a15_0833610.text: Karl, this is Al.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Go ahead Al.

a15_0833610.speaker: Worden
a15_0833610.text: Okay, Karl. I just finished the observation on J-1, and everything looked fine from my standpoint. [I] could track it very smoothly. And in fact, I took a couple of marks on it, if anyone's interested.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Very good, and we have them down here.

a15_0833610.speaker: Worden
a15_0833610.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: We were sitting down here wondering how you were ever going to find that little bugger. No trouble, huh? [Pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Worden
a15_0833610.text: Not that much trouble, Karl.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Very good.

a15_0833610.speaker: Worden
a15_0833610.text: Seemed like there was plenty of time waiting on it. [Long pause.]

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: 15, does it look like you are going to clear the mountain range ahead?

a15_0833610.speaker: Irwin
a15_0833610.text: Karl, we've all got our eyes closed. We're pulling our feet up.

a15_0833610.speaker: Henize
a15_0833610.text: Open your eyes. That's like going to the Grand Canyon and not looking.

a15_0834715.speaker: Henize
a15_0834715.text: 15, This is Houston. I have the camera photo PADs.

a15_0834715.speaker: Scott
a15_0834715.text: Okay, stand by. We're just noticing the cabin temp here, and also that the outlet temp is up to about - the glycol about - outlet temp's up to about 70[° Fahrenheit]. [Long pause.]

a15_0834715.speaker: Henize
a15_0834715.text: We copy, and EECOM says that's normal and they're on their way down now.

a15_0834715.speaker: Irwin
a15_0834715.text: And, Karl, I'm ready to copy the - the Map Camera PAD.

a15_0834715.speaker: Henize
a15_0834715.text: Roger. They're in the Flight Plan at 84:32 and 84:39. Mapping Camera: T-start, 84:42:23; T-stop 84:54:14. The Pan Camera times are the same as the Mapping Camera's times and we would like to change a shutter speed at 84:24. Instead of 125th, we want 1/250th at 84:24.

a15_0834715.speaker: Irwin
a15_0834715.text: Okay. Understand 84:24. We'll change to F 250 [means 1/250] rather than 125; and on the Map PAD, it's 84:42:23 and 84:54:14, and the Pan Camera PAD's the same.

a15_0835508.speaker: Worden
a15_0835508.text: Okay, let me talk to Karl here for a minute.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Okay, Karl. Got a few numbers for you on the [boom] extension times. We started the whole thing off at 84:06:30, and got the covers open, the Mapping Camera extended, and the extension was about 3 minutes instead of 4. Then we deployed the Gamma-ray and the Mass Spec. booms for barber pole plus 2 seconds [to release the tiedowns]. The Gamma-ray turned barber pole after 6 seconds, and Mass Spec. turned barber pole immediately. And I was suspicious of the Mass Spec., so we tried it again and got the same results. Turned the X-ray, On, at 84:15:10 and the Laser Altimeter, On, at 84:15:30.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Looks like that stuff's working fine. Tch, tch.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: That's it. Verify DSE tape motion at 84:20, and then we get the cameras ready for terminator photos.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Pan camera, we go - we already got our terminator photos. Did you get - Let's see, we want mag R. That's this mag here.

a15_0841532.speaker: Scott
a15_0841532.text: With the Hasselblad? You got the Hasselblad over there?

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Yes. And, let's see, we want the Hasselblad 80 millimeter, intervalometer--

a15_0841532.speaker: Scott
a15_0841532.text: Let's see, intervalometer's down there, Jim, in the - Let's see - It's in the camera - It's right in front of the camera compartment.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Okay. What do you want to do now, get the Hasselblad?

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: Well, the way to do that is just to play it straight from now on.

a15_0841532.speaker: Worden
a15_0841532.text: [Garble] I need somebody to take care of me.

a15_0841825.speaker: Henize
a15_0841825.text: 15, This is Houston. Would you verify that the X-ray is On? [Pause.]

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: If [garble] orders, I can get it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Man, that's really good and stuck!

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: I'm going to order pork and scalloped potatoes; I don't whether you do or not, but I am.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Okay, f - 2.8, 1/250th, and infinity. Take six frames. Okay. Right out of this window here. And we're going to get the pan camera going in there, too.

a15_0841825.speaker: Henize
a15_0841825.text: 15, this is Houston. All systems are looking good down here, and until we tell you otherwise, all the AOS's are as in your Flight Plan.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: We both like to hear that.

a15_0841825.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0841825.text: This is Apollo Control at 84 hours, 21 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal as Apollo 15 turns the corner to go behind the Moon. We'll acquire on the 4th revolution at 85 hours, 8 minutes, 47 seconds, and as you heard in that last [but one] exchange, the scientific instrument bay, the SIM bay is in business now. At 84 hours, 21 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Now, I'm going to show you how I'm going to handle this stuff here. Well, it looks like we just lost them. (Cleared throat).

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: That won't be the same from now on.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Yes. Because we're in SIM bay attitude now.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: That's the stowed position only. It - it's minus 5 and 25 for Reacq when we come around the other side.

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: I'll tell you, this Moon flying could be fun.

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: I said, "This Moon flying could be fun."

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Hey, listen, Al, we got to get the pan camera going here, right?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Yes. T - T-start is the big time, and everything's hinged around T-start, so I take that time and punch it into P30 (cleared throat). And just load Noun 33 to that time.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Yes, I'm going to do it like that on all of them. Now, when you come up on a thing like that, EL says T-start minus 1:40 -

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Well, it's right on the DSKY there.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: And the Mapping Camera, Image Motion, On. Talkback barber pole 3 to 5 seconds, then gray. That can be done anytime; that's not important. EL Off at T-start; Mapping Camera, On, at T-start; Pan Camera, Operate, at T-start. Jesus, they got all kinds of things going on here at T-start. Motion Increase - talkback barber pole plus 2 steps. I better do that mapping-camera thing.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: You got 18 minutes [garble] - If you'll take the EL, and all you got to do is - point the - point the Hasselblad straight down and start the intervalometer going, and start it at - at - at minus 1:40 on the clock and stop it as zero.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: And it would be much appreciated.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Jim, is my spoon up there somewhere? Spoon. Yes, it should be back in there.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: [Laughter] No, I'm not. I just didn't want to get in your way, believe it or not.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Ah, let's see; yes, we're ready to go over here; 84:24; at about 84:33, we better do all that business. In the meantime, grab a bite. What are we having?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: You know, I don't know why it is, every night at this time, my nose gets stuffy.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Every night, my - my nose starts getting stuffy along about this time, and then it cleans up after a bit.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Yes, give me another squirt of hot juice there - when you get a chance.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Hey, Jim, you know what I do tomorrow?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Let's go shoot a landing. I'm ready. I'm ready to put that baby right in there, right now. I haven't had a TV flight in months.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Yes, sir, you better. You'll lose you [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: 0ooh, that one's stretched. Pork and scalloped potatoes!

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: [Laughter.] Yes, you - you know, it really works - works just fine if you - if you pop it and just keep pulling.

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: [Garble] I think, the first thing I'm going to do when we get back?

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: Have a beautiful night in Tahiti.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Hey, you're on, buddy. You're on - you're on! [Garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: No, really. You ought to really think about it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Hey, you know what they tell you when you get to the [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: [Garble]. They got up a special menu; it has everything that you want on it. You can eat steak and eggs [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: You don't [garble] scrambled eggs, do you, Jim?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: You've been away too long, Jim!

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Is that all we get to eat?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: We ought to be about through with that food locker.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: [Garble] pictures. Do we just take them from straight down?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: [Garble] you want to [garble]. You - you got that [garble]?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: These will be the LM. You got all of them?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: And right at - the start of the [garble]. You want to start looking out the window, window 4. [Garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: And then you want to [garble] off [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: That's right. Switch them back in stereo now?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: You know, that feels funny to look down.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: What's wrong, Jim. [Garble] doing the dishes?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: I got mine right over to here.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Looks to me like we're roll.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Is - is this picture supposed to be an oblique?

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: It's not a - a vertical picture.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Yes. Okay. I see where we are. Okay. [Garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Yes, but I - I seem to have it located myself here.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: I don't [garble], but it's dark in here.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Nassau Bay was in the dark, I'm sorry to say.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: I want to take one more for good measure...

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: ...but now it's getting in an area where you're getting something.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Okay, let me turn this over here on the - Let me put this back under here - the bracket; it's a good place for it to be.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: But that's a - that's a good place for it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Yes. Good idea. Run them back in here.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Give me a lunch pack, and I'll eat it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: You want me to move? You want to get over here?

a15_0841825.speaker: Irwin
a15_0841825.text: Give me a spoon [garble]. You got something for those?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: No wonder you never lose it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: One thing you're going to learn how to do is fly upside down.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Yes. Yes. You'll be able to fly right-side up.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: Now I can see a bunch of [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Okay. Let me go to the movie.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: No, by golly, there are lineaments down there all over the place, going - Well, northeast - Yes, northeast, southwest. See it? Right up on the ridge. Right along all the [garble], by golly. Look at that.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: What? Right here. Look out the center window, right down this way. We'll be parking right over - right over the grid.

a15_0841825.speaker: Worden
a15_0841825.text: You mean right over the - the ridge here? Right along the lunar [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: As long as you [garble] having a - the ground track that changes every rev, you're never going to get tired of looking at new things. You know, you'll have something new to look at the whole way.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: You know, I about had meatballs all over the place.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: What are you waiting for 2 minutes from now?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: You want me to get the mass spec and do what?

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Well, I was just thinking about that. I think what we need to do - is - You might take a little bath [Garble]. By golly, let's go do some around the Moon [garble].

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: I figure we're far enough ahead - now. You can stop it - if you want to, you know, to live it up. Really live it up. Get clean, fresh...

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: Oh, look at - look at the one coming up, Al. Look at the debris in the bottom of that crater and over at the side there. Look at that!

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: It's got a big [garble] on the side.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: [Garble]. Check The Bright One? Boy, look at the junk coming out of it.

a15_0841825.speaker: Scott
a15_0841825.text: See this one wall here - how it's completely collapsed, straight down, and a bunch - bunch of little benches go down even farther - towards the bottom.

a15_0841825.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0841825.text: This is Apollo Control at 85 hours, 8 minutes. We're about 20 seconds away from Acquisition Of Signal. We'll stand by.

a15_0850821.speaker: Scott
a15_0850821.text: Hello, Houston. 15. Five by [five, meaning 'reading you loud and clear.']

a15_0850821.speaker: Henize
a15_0850821.text: Roger. Like to remind you to configure the DSE as per the Flight Plan.

a15_0850821.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0850821.text: This is Apollo Control. We're getting good data both from spacecraft systems and from the SIM bay.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Say when we get down to the presleep checklist here in about 50 minutes or so, I wonder if you might give us your best guess on the probability of a DOI trim tomorrow.

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Okay. We'll work on that information.

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Dave, we can give you a pretty good guess at that now. It seems to be unlikely that we're going to need a DOI trim. I've got a couple of trajectory numbers here if you'd like to copy them.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Yeah, it'd be interesting. Go ahead.

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Our tracking data tells us that your current orbit is 58.2 by 9.1 [nautical miles, 107.7 by 16.8 km]. And, tomorrow morning at wakeup time, it'll be 58.6 by 8.7 [nautical miles, 108.5 by 16.1 km]. [Pause.]

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Okay; that looks pretty fair. How about the - the out-of-plane or the cross track?

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Dave, our out-of-plane data looks like about 2/10ths of a [nautical] mile [0.37 km] at PDI [Powered Descent Initiation] time.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Okay; that sounds pretty good. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: 15, we'd like High Gain [Antenna] to Auto, please.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Roger. Hign Gain to Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Dave, thinking about trajectories, you probably noticed the out-of-plane part of the DOI [burn]. They're telling me here that you burned a perfect LOI, but the state vector they gave you was slightly in error. So, they got rid of - they - they made corrections for that during DOI so that we're standing pretty close to perfect now.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Okay. I got to admit we did have some question about that [out-of-plane component] but figured you all had it in hand, as you usually do.

a15_0851305.speaker: Henize
a15_0851305.text: Roger. Between a perfect crew in orbit up there and a perfect crew down here, we're doing pretty good so far. Knock on wood.

a15_0851305.speaker: Scott
a15_0851305.text: Yeah. We got a few miles to cover though.

a15_0852036.speaker: Worden
a15_0852036.text: Okay, Karl. Guess I should bring you up to date on a couple of things here. Everything went as planned on the - on the [far-side] terminator photos. The Pan Camera and the Mapping Camera pass started on time and stopped on time. Turn - Got the Mass Spec. boom deployed and Gamma-ray boom deployed; the Mass Spec. deployed in 2 minutes, 20 seconds; and the Gamma-ray deployed in 2 minutes, 28 seconds. Got the Ion Source, On [means Standby], and the Logic Power, Off, at 85:05. And that brings you up to date.

a15_0852036.speaker: Henize
a15_0852036.text: Beautiful, Al. Sounds like all of that nice equipment is working real nice for us.

a15_0852036.speaker: Worden
a15_0852036.text: Sure does, Karl. Be interested in what kind of data you're getting down there on it. [Pause.]

a15_0852036.speaker: Henize
a15_0852036.text: OSO's [Orbital Science Officer's] two-word summary of it is that we're getting "beautiful data". Incidentally, Al, if - if you'd like sometime, let us have, say - 12 to 24 hours operation, would you like to have a summary sometime tomorrow on some of the details?

a15_0852036.speaker: Worden
a15_0852036.text: Yes, listen. Skip it tomorrow; and, maybe day after tomorrow, we'll get a summary on that. I'll be kind of interested in how it goes myself.

a15_0852520.speaker: Worden
a15_0852520.text: Roger, Karl. For your information, you can see both of the - both of the booms at full extension out of window 5.

a15_0852520.speaker: Henize
a15_0852520.text: Hey, we're glad to hear that.

a15_0852520.speaker: Worden
a15_0852520.text: Yeah; they sure do look pretty sitting out there.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to have you hold off on putting the Mass Spec. Experiment switch to Standby, and we'd like to have the Discriminator, Low. [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Worden
a15_0853420.text: Roger, Karl. We'll hold off till you - cue us, and going Discriminator, Low, now.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Thank you, Al.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: 15, this is Houston. If you'll give us Accept, we'll send up a new state vector. [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Worden
a15_0853420.text: Roger, Houston. You've got it.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: And, - and if you've finished with dinner up there, and somebody can copy, I have a TEI-12 PAD.

a15_0853420.speaker: Worden
a15_0853420.text: Okay. Stand by a minute, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: Houston, we're making a low pass over the Apennines [mountains], and they're really something.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Roger. [Pause.] Do they look like any terrestrial mountains you've ever seen? [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: No. [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: How about the slopes? Are they generally steeper than you expect, or shallower than you expect on something like the Tetons? [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: Say again, Karl. I'm sorry; we were discussing the rille at that time - Hadley, that is.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Roger. I - I was just trying to get a better feel for how the mountains look. Are there - are they more - more craggy and rougher than something like the Tetons or do they give you some other appearance?

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: No. As a matter of fact, from this altitude, even though we're low, they appear to be smooth and rounded. There aren't any jagged peaks that we can see. And even though they're cratered, and rough in texture on a small scale, they really don't look anything like the Alps or the San Juan's or any of the other familiar ranges we know.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Roger. Is there anything that looks like bare rock on them. [Pause.]

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: I think we can see some boulders, but there are no apparent jagged peaks that we can tell or that we can see from this - this particular altitude yet, although some of the - the shadows look fairly sharp.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Roger.

a15_0853420.speaker: Irwin
a15_0853420.text: And, Karl, speaking of shadows, there seems to be enough light being reflected off the sides of the mountains around to supply some light down on the landing site. And the rille is quite distinctive as we pass right over it.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: Beautiful. That must be an eerie sight in a half-light.

a15_0853420.speaker: Irwin
a15_0853420.text: Well, it was, sort of.

a15_0853420.speaker: Henize
a15_0853420.text: And, 15, you can have your computer back.

a15_0853420.speaker: Scott
a15_0853420.text: Roger.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: 15, this is Houston. [Long pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read.

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Loud and clear, Houston.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: Roger. We've finished picking up data on the Mass Spectrometer. Leave the discriminator as it is, and we're ready to go to put the Experiment [switch] in Standby now. [Pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Understand; you're ready to put the Mass Spec. in Standby.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: Roger. And then you can start to put the blunt end forward, anytime you care to.

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Roger; we're maneuvering now.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: 15, this is Houston. Dave, the Surgeon would like to have a special reading of the PRD [Personal Radiation Dosimeter] from you tonight. Your reading last night was not in agreement with the other two crew members and they'd like to get another data point on you.

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Okay. We copy, Karl. We'll give you all three readings.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: Roger. They'll accept them gladly.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: 15, this is Houston. Whenever you can copy, I have the TEI-12 PAD.

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Stand by, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Okay, Karl. I'm ready to copy TEI-12.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: Roger. TEI-12, SPS G&N; 38110; plus 0.58, plus 1.00; 101:36:08.38; plus 2845.0, minus 0380.2, minus 0063.8; 180, 107, 354; the rest is NA; 4-jet ullage for 12 seconds. And this assumes the burn undocked and no circular burn, and the GET of landing is 196 hours at MPL.

a15_0854321.speaker: Irwin
a15_0854321.text: Okay. TEI-12 readback: SPS/G&N 38110; plus 0.58, plus 1.00; 101:36:08.38; plus 2845.0, minus 0380.2, minus 0063.8; 180, 107, 354; 4 jets for 12 seconds. Undocked, no circular burn. Assumes landing at 196 GET at the MPL.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: That's all correct. [Long pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: 15, we need the mode switch in Auto please. [Long pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Worden
a15_0854321.text: Houston, 15. What - what switch you talking about, Karl? [Pause.]

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: That's the CMC Mode switch. I guess we need to get into Auto before we can execute this maneuver.

a15_0854321.speaker: Scott
a15_0854321.text: That's affirmative. And I'll go into Auto as soon as I complete the 40 degrees roll.

a15_0854321.speaker: Henize
a15_0854321.text: Roger.

a15_0855507.speaker: Henize
a15_0855507.text: 15, Houston. On the Mass Spectrometer operations down there at 59 minutes, we'd like to have you keep the Discriminator, Low, as it is now. And, as the Ion Source goes On, we would like to have you pause in the Off position until you get our cue. [Pause.]

a15_0855507.speaker: Worden
a15_0855507.text: Roger; understand. You want the Discriminator left in Low, and want us to pause in Off on the Ion Source on your cue.

a15_0855507.speaker: Henize
a15_0855507.text: Roger. And I - I - think you know that we'd probably - that we - we don't want to go into those operations until we have got into the correct attitude.

a15_0855809.speaker: Henize
a15_0855809.text: Couple of special notes on the hardware. First of all, on - on the Systems Test Meter - we don't fully understand why that switch did funny things for us, and we have some back in - the fairly extensive tests going on down here still trying to understand it. And we suggest that you leave the meter in the 5-B position until we do get some handle on what happened there.

a15_0855809.speaker: Henize
a15_0855809.text: Okay. And I just heard the word that, if you really need it, go ahead and use it, but if you don't have a strong reason for moving it, leave it as it is. And on - We're - we're observing the radiator temperature - occasionally cycling above 80 degrees. This is out of limits, and we don't really have a good solution for this at the present time. We could think about turning on the evaporator, but that would foul up the Mass Spectrometer, and we'd rather not do that. The only things that it's - that the high temperature would be bothering are the IMU PIPAs [Pulse Integrating Pendulous Accelerome

a15_0855809.speaker: Irwin
a15_0855809.text: Houston, this is 15 with some onboard read-outs for you and PRD's.

a15_0855809.speaker: Irwin
a15_0855809.text: Roger. Bat C is 37 [volts]; pyros A and B are both 37.5 [volts]; RCS 83, 82, 82 and 83 [per cent]. The PRD readings; 23072, 25014, and 08016. [Long pause.]

a15_0855809.speaker: Henize
a15_0855809.text: Roger, 15. We copy all that. [Long pause.]

a15_0855809.speaker: Irwin
a15_0855809.text: Houston, this is 15. The Ion Source is Off, and we're standing by for your word. [Pause.]

a15_0855809.speaker: Henize
a15_0855809.text: 15, this is Houston. Let's continue standing by on that Ion Source switch. We'd like to get all the way into attitude before we go into the On position.

a15_0860757.speaker: Henize
a15_0860757.text: 15, this is Houston. We're ready for the E-memory dump.

a15_0860757.speaker: Henize
a15_0860757.text: And, 15, we're ready now for the Ion Source switch, On.

a15_0861029.speaker: Irwin
a15_0861029.text: Houston, 15. We're going to configure communications for sleep. [Long pause.]

a15_0861029.speaker: Henize
a15_0861029.text: 15, Houston. Could you hold off on that until just after LOS.

a15_0861029.speaker: Henize
a15_0861029.text: Okay, 15. Our last worry seems to be cleared up down here. We've got nothing more to bother you with, and all we can do is wish you a good night's sleep.

a15_0861029.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0861029.text: This is Apollo Control at 86 hours, 13 minutes. We have lost the signal now on revolution 4. We've said 'good night' to the crew. Don't expect to talk to them until morning. The voice carrier has been turned off. We'll take this line down now at 86 hours, 14 minutes. We're estimating the change of shift news conference for 11:15 pm Central Daylight Time in the News Center briefing room. Flight Director Gene Kranz is preparing to relieve Milt Windler and his Flight Controller team. At 86 hours, 14 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_0932957.speaker: Parker
a15_0932957.text: Good morning, Jim. We're waking up you [sic] a little early to tell you a few things before you go around the corner because you only have four minutes in the old Flight Plan. So, if you guys are awake and ready to listen, I'll give you a few words. [Pause.]

a15_0932957.speaker: Parker
a15_0932957.text: Okay. At the moment - Okay, one short one. We'd like you to go High Gain Antenna to Auto so we don't lose you just before you go around the corner there.

a15_0932957.speaker: Parker
a15_0932957.text: ...And at the moment, [Apollo] 15, you're sitting in a 58.8- by 7.6-[nautical mile, 108.8- by 14.1-km] orbit; and, at PDI [Powered Descent Initiation], we're extrapolating you to approximately 33,000 feet [10,000 metres]. This is with a plus or minus 9,000 feet [2,750 metres] on top of it, due primarily to the uncertainty of the RLS [Radius of the Landing Site from the centre of the Moon]. Because of this, we're pretty well decided we're going to do a DOI [Descent Orbit Insertion] trim, but we're holding a decision on that until after we get the [tracking] data for this pass, which we'll proce

a15_0932957.speaker: Irwin
a15_0932957.text: Okay. Copied all that. And no medication.

a15_0932957.speaker: Parker
a15_0932957.text: Copy. And we have a [CSM] consumable update for you as of 93:30. RCS [Reaction Control System] total was 75 [per cent remaining], quad Alpha, 76; Bravo, 75; Charlie, 74; Delta, 77; hydrogen 2, tank 1, 84 [per cent]; [tank] 2, 81; and [tank] 3, 54; oxygen 2, tank 1, 82; tank 2, 86; tank 3, 68. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0934441.speaker: Parker
a15_0934441.text: And, Apollo 15, Houston. You're looking good going around the horn. Systems all look good. At your convenience, while you're down the SIM bay area there, we'd like also the Mass Spec[trometer] Discriminator to High. Over.

a15_0934441.speaker: Scott
a15_0934441.text: Okay; understand. Mass Spec. Discriminator to High.

a15_0934441.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0934441.text: This is Apollo Control. Just had Loss Of Signal with Apollo 15 as it passed behind the Moon near the end of the eighth revolution. During the wake-up call after the crew responded, spacecraft communicator passed up 2 or 3 items that the crew should be thinking about, such as doing the so-called DOI trim maneuver, which is an optional item shown in the Flight Plan, at 96 hours, 17 minutes. It's rather like a midcourse correction maneuver in trans-Earth or translunar coast. If required, it would be done. And apparently the pericynthion has drifted somewhat lower during the night than was anticip

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Your candy, Dave, is in that bag over there. Your breakfast is right here.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Thank you. You're a good guy.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Well, looks - looks like it's about the best way to do it here.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Is it actually a what, plus or minus...

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: What?

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Yes; 33's not so bad, except a...

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Plus or minus 9; that's a 24.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: [Garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: I don't know whether we can or not. Let me ...

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Put a - put a 50-degree mark on the window.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes. I know it, I want to get ahead. We got - got time to do it now. I just like to get everything done we can, and I'd like to be sitting and waiting.

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: We should have turned that cabin fan off last night. It wouldn't have been so cool - been less noisy.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Well, I tell you, I woke up at one time - and I listened to the noise, and I thought the thing was off. I thought to myself, 'Great, somebody got up and turned the cabin fan off.'

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: I was burning up down there. I just about got up and got the hoses ... them down there.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Boy, you should have done that before you went to bed. Get yourself some air.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Yes.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Did you get any sleep, Jim?

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Yes, about like the first night.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Well, you should have got up and got the hoses then. You need your sleep, babe.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Yes.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Huh! We're moving it. I can't believe it!

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: The [garble]! That biomed is working.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Al has them.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Oh, thanks. Son of a gun.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Well, I reckon what we ought to do is the burn, and then get suited. Burn and then get suited, you know - finish up the burn. You can put on your suit; get it out of the way. Go clear out the tunnel.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes. It really is.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: I couldn't tell whether the spacecraft was moving or whether Dave was shifting in his couch.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes, we must have used a fair amount.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Need some more? I can get it for you.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: [Garble] any more [garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: You ready?

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes. Don't push. Just let it go, Jim. Pull it out and let it - and release it. Pull the handle out.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Again?

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Just pull out - now let go. That a boy. You don't - you don't push it in. Have you been pushing it in?

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Sometimes it sticks.

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: No, it never - no, it - it - you - it counts up and - it has a little accumulator in there.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Here.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Now, just pull it out and - and let it - and leave it go.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Okay.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: The accumulator builds up, and then it'll shoot you. That's where you get your measurement.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Take a shot of cold right here.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: All right.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: [Garble] than caught short.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Ready?

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Yes.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: [Garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: [Garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: [Garble] hot chocolate I just grabbed?

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Yes, sure.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: [Garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: [Garble] this good stuff is for the kid's stamina.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: That all right?

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: The opposite end.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: There. Eat it.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Al, I'll leave some bacon squares for you.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: [Garble] remembered.

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: [Garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: 100 hours and 13 minutes, I think we ...

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Hmm.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: You like bacon squares? I'll leave you some, too.

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Too much salt. Too dry and salty for a whole meal. I don't [garble].

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Ten minutes until AOS. Huh!

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: You going to get this PAD on the next rev?

a15_0934922.speaker: Worden
a15_0934922.text: Mm-hmm.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Al, why don't you end I switch off here when ...

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: I'd like to take a crap if I can work it in, Dave.

a15_0934922.speaker: Scott
a15_0934922.text: Okay.

a15_0934922.speaker: Irwin
a15_0934922.text: Tell me when.

a15_0934922.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0934922.text: This is Apollo Control; 94 hours, 34 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Slightly over a minute before predicted acquisition of Apollo 15 as it makes the ninth lunar revolution front side pass. During this pass, we'll have Command Module television camera view of the landing site as the spacecraft swoops down to something like 7 [nautical] miles above the surface. We're awaiting word from the Network controller that we've had Acquisition Of Signal. The crew should be finishing up their breakfast meal period.

a15_0934922.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0934922.text: We've had Acquisition Of Signal. Let's join the air/ground for the initial communications on this ninth revolution.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Apollo 15, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Houston, Apollo 15. You're 5 by [5, meaning loud and clear].

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Roger. You're 5 by also. And we got three more Flight Plan updates due you, if you're ready. [Pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay. First one I'd like to mention's at 95:02 - 95:02. And it reads, in addition to those two lines on the O 2 Heaters at the top of the page, we want to add a third line that says "cb O 2 Tank 100 Watt Heaters, 3, Main B, Open. Panel 226." Over. [Pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; understand. "cb O 2 Tank 100 Watt Heaters, 3, Main B, Open."

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Roger. And after you guys give us the PDR [means PRD or Passive Radiation Dosimeters] read-outs, we'd like to exchange the CMP and CDR PDRs because, Dave, yours appears to be malfunctioning, and they'd like to have two working ones on the surface. Do you copy?

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; understand. Exchange CMP and CDR PRDs.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay. And the next updates for the LM Activation Checklist. And while you're going - getting that, I'll give you a little update on our expectations for the DOI burn.

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. Go ahead, Bob.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay. The update for the Activation Checklist is on page 2-6. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; 2-6. Go.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay. We'll delete the third line of step 2. And we'll add a step 5, which reads: 1, "LMP's Suit Isol valve to Suit Flow; Commander's Suit Isol valve to Suit Flow, for 15 seconds." And then "Suit Disconnect, for both." And then 2, is "Suit Gas Diverter, Push/Cabin." What we're doing here, Dave, is basically making sure that we're blowing any glass particles that might have settled in through the little holes into the inlet hoses. Going to blow those out. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; understand. Step 2, scratch the third line. Step 5, "LMP and CDR Suit Isolation to Suit Flow for 15 seconds," and then "Suit Disconnect, for both." And then "Suit Gas Diverter, Push/Cabin." And that sounds like a pretty good idea.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay. And, I'll give you a few clues as to what's liable to be coming up for the DOI trim burn. Currently, we're showing a 5.87 [nautical mile, 10.9 km,] perilune on rev 14, which is 35,000 feet plus or minus 9,000 [10,600 metres ±2,700 metres] with that RLS uncertainty. And what's being proposed now is not an SPS burn, because it'll be very short, but an RCS burn of 20 seconds which is 3.2 foot per second [1 m/s], which would raise us to 50,000 feet [15,240 metres]. [It] will cost us about 27 pounds of gas [12.2 kg], and we're looking at a T IG time [of ignition] of 95:56 [GET], which,

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. Understand 95:56. And looking over the Flight Plan, it looks like, had we gone on the original DOI trim, we had about 40 minutes of SIM [bay instrument] data there. Maybe we can just scratch that. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Roger, Dave. We're just going to have to trim that SIM stuff off a little bit early, because we don't have the time right here.

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. I guess what I'm thinking is, it takes us a lot of time to go through that. Turn it on and turn it off. And, of course, we could always use time, but we'll get it. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Dave, we don't show you turned anything on this morning; it's just a long protracted business of turning it off. And I guess, that was - used to be starting after the TV pass. And I guess that - what we're saying right now is it looks like we're going to start turning that off during or before the TV pass.

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay. You're right, Bob. We'll do that; that looks good.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Okay, and we'll be getting you a real [DOI trim] PAD coming up some time soon.

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; we'll be standing by. [Long pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: And, Dave, if practicable, we'd prefer to have it turned off before or after the TV, because then we can watch it being turned off; otherwise we can't see it during the TV. But you can certainly turn part of it off before and part after. [Pause.]

a15_0943500.speaker: Scott
a15_0943500.text: Okay; understand. We - we'll do it sometime other than the during the TV.

a15_0943500.speaker: Parker
a15_0943500.text: Correct.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Okay, Dave. And we got a few updates here for the time after the TV pass, if you're ready to copy. Some other stuff that we are moving up because of this. [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay; ready to copy. Go ahead.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Okay. At 95:28, we will schedule a "P52, option 3." [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay. "P52, option 3."

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Okay. At 9...

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Roger. At 95:33, we'll delete the "P00 at pitch, 033." [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay; delete "P00 at pitch, 033" at 95:33.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Roger. At 95:35, we will delete "P52 option 3," and that's the one we've moved up by 7 minutes [to prepare for the early burn].

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Roger. And at 95:43, we will delete the "P52 option 1," because we will be staying on [the] landing site REFSMMAT.

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay; very good. Go ahead.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: And at 95:30, we're going to start - we're going to move the activities that start around 95:47 to 95:55. Those will be moved up to 95:30. [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay. Do you want - Okay, I got it. Fine.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: That's that little block there. And the time to show on the Flight Plan anyway is 95:56 for the DOI trim. [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Rog; 95:56. [Long pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Houston, 15. Is that all you have?

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Roger. Sorry Dave. That's the end - for now.

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Worden
a15_0944808.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Go.

a15_0944808.speaker: Worden
a15_0944808.text: Okay, Bob. We've got the TV turned on if you want to catch it down there.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Rog. We'll do our best.

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay; Houston, 15. We're coming up on the edge of [Mare] Crisium, and we've got a good picture up here.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Rog. Don't see anything down here yet, but we're anticipating. [Long pause.]

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: 15, can we verify that you're in Transmit on the TV switch, please?

a15_0944808.speaker: Scott
a15_0944808.text: Okay; that was the problem. We've got it.

a15_0944808.speaker: Parker
a15_0944808.text: Thank you.

a15_0944808.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0944808.text: Television picture from the spacecraft now coming in on the large Eiderphor projector at the front of the Control Room. Meanwhile, in the viewing room, among the people watching the television pass this morning are Mrs. Jim Irwin, Mrs. Dave Scott, Mrs. Scott's mother Mrs. Isaac Ott, Apollo 11 Commander Neil Armstrong and Doctor Wernher von Braun.

a15_0945526.speaker: Parker
a15_0945526.text: Okay, 15. We got it now. Couple of big holes in the ground out there.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay; Houston, 15. If you want to orient yourself on a TV there, Bob, we just came over Macrobius A, and the small crater that you just saw - we just went by, is Römer J. We're coming up on - on Römer K here in a moment, which means that very shortly, we'll be coming up over the Littrow Rille - Rimae Littrow.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Roger. We've got our little charts out here.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay, that looked like Römer J we're just coming up on now. In fact, we'll pan down into it.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Beautiful shot.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay, Bob. You can see we're up over one of the Littrow Rilles now. You can see the rille cutting diagonally there from about - 6 o'clock to 2 o'clock across the picture, and you can see some of the wrinkle ridges. In fact, there's a beautiful wrinkle ridge right below us right now.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Roger. I believe you. I see it.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: I'll pan up along the wrinkle ridge so you can see. And they're a very, very distinctive thing, now we're out over Mare Serenitatis. You can see some of the Littrow rilles in the background there, some of the graben-type rilles, and some of the wrinkle ridges down on the - on the far - or on the - on the close corner here. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Yeah, we should be coming up on the inner ridge system here in a moment, and we - we'll try and pan down along the - the inner ridge. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Yeah. That looks like the inner ridge system there, and if your picture's like mine, you should be picking it up pretty well. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Those ridges in places look like they could be nothing more than a - than a - than a flow that stopped there - flow front. In other places, they look like the - like a - like it's buckled material underneath, folded to - to give it some elevation.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: And that was a good one, Al [meaning the view of Sarabhai]. And if someone, who's not just looking out the window, will give us P00 and Accept, we'll send you up a - not P00, just Accept. Pardon me. We'll give you state vectors and targets...

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: ...while we're taking a view.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: You got it. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0945631.text: Apollo 15's present altitude now 7½ nautical miles [13.9 km, 45,600 feet] above the lunar surface.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Bob, I'm going to pan forward a little bit, and you can see the beginnings of the Apennine Front showing up on the far side of Serenitatis.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Roger. We see that. [Pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: And off on the left there, that's the Haemus Mountains around south of the Apennines. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: See how - when you're coming up at low altitude on these mountains, how - how striking they are in the distance? It's really hard to miss them, you can see them a long ways away.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
