a15_0945631.text: I hope you can miss them. [Pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Guess that's up to you guys.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Rog. Speaking of that, the burn attitude's going to be 104 degrees [in pitch], so you might keep that in mind when you get done here. You're getting kind of close to it now, or - beginning to get close to it.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: There's a very interesting little fissure just below us here, Bob. It looks like there might be a little flow coming out of it, but it's - it's almost an arrowhead-shaped affair. And, it certainly doesn't have any features like any - any impact. It's very sharp and distinct and makes a very distinct arrowhead. Here we come up on the ridges on the west side of Serenitatis, just at the foothills of the Hadley Apennines.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: And you can see, there is - there is some relief as we look back to the south there, there is some very distinct relief in - in - in the shore of Serenitatis, with some wrinkle ridges that follow the contour.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: And some - what look like fairly distinct arcuate rilles that also follow the contour. I think that when we get up very close here, you can see...

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: ...In - in the field of view there right now is a lineament that looks like it might be some sort of a collapsed lava tube, and you can also see down in here the - the mare material looks like it's pooling in the - in the foothills of the mountains; and in some places, you can even see what appears to be a frozen shoreline, so to speak.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Beautiful, beautiful. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Rog. We can take black now, too.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay. [Pause.] Okay, Bob. I'm going to take the TV out of this window and get it located in window 3, so we can all have a good look at the landing site.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Sorry about that; we're just a little bit late, but you can see the edge of the rille [Hadley Rille] there as we go beyond it. And you can see the blocky features inside the rille. And now we're out across the plain on the other [western] side. That was very fast.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: That was a quickie. [Long pause.]

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay. In the field of view right now, Bob, is the beginnings of Bradley Rille, and you can see it cutting back off to the southwest there.

a15_0945631.speaker: Parker
a15_0945631.text: Roger. Looks kind of like our rille.

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Yeah. It does, doesn't it?

a15_0945631.speaker: Worden
a15_0945631.text: Okay, Bob. I guess that about does it. We're at the terminator, and we'll pick up the attitude [for the trim burn] now.

a15_0950927.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0950927.text: This is Apollo Control. At the conclusion of the television pass, the crew held up a sheet of paper on which appeared to be written the word 'finis' [meaning end].

a15_0951251.speaker: Parker
a15_0951251.text: And, Apollo 15, Houston. We've got a DOI trim PAD for Jim when he's ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15_0951251.speaker: Irwin
a15_0951251.text: Morning, Bob. I'm ready to copy.

a15_0951251.speaker: Parker
a15_0951251.text: Roger, Jim. The P30 PAD. Purpose, DOI trim, RCS/G&N; 38264; Noun 48 is NA; 095:56:42.50; plus 0003.1, the last two Noun 88s [means Noun 81s] are 0; 180, 104, 359; Noun 44 is 0059.4, plus 0009.6; 0003.1, 0:20, 0003.1; 30, 192.8, 11.1 the rest of the PAD is NA. GDC Align stars are Vega and Deneb, roll, pitch and yaw are 288, 340, 346. It's a 4-jet RCS burn and we do not want to trim any retrograde residual, so any extra burn you get in that direction, we will not trim. Over. [Pause.]

a15_0951251.speaker: Irwin
a15_0951251.text: Okay, Bob. DOI trim PAD readback. RCS/G&N; 38264; 095:56:42.50; plus 0003.1, 0 and 0 for Y and Z; 180, 104, 359; 0059.4, plus 0009.6; 0003.1, 0:20, 0003.1; 30, 192.8, 11.1. Vega and Deneb; 288, 340, 346; 4-jet RCS, no trim of any retrograde residual.

a15_0951251.speaker: Parker
a15_0951251.text: Roger. Copy. Correct, and one last comment: We will not be passing you up a TEI-9 - TEI-19 PAD at this time.

a15_0951251.speaker: Parker
a15_0951251.text: And that should take care of all little squares in that MSFN update box at 28 - at 95:25. [Pause.]

a15_0951251.speaker: Parker
a15_0951251.text: Roger. I was just telling you that fills - that takes care of all squares there at the MSFN update at 95:25. We've taken care of all those in one way or another this morning.

a15_0951251.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0951251.text: This is Apollo Control. At 8 o'clock Houston time, astronaut Harrison 'Jack' Schmitt will make a briefing in the Houston News Center on the Apollo 15 EVA periods, they three EVA periods. Still up live here on the ninth frontside revolution of the Moon by Apollo 15. Another 21 minutes until Loss Of Signal. The crew presently is maneuvering to the burn attitude for the DOI trim maneuver, which will be an RCS burn. The burn time of 20 seconds. Looking for 3.1 feet per second [0.95 m/s] change in velocity to raise the pericynthion. Ignition time is 95 hours, 56 minutes, 42 seconds Ground Elapsed T

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: And, 15, people down here are recommending that you terminate your roll at this attitude to help your P52 before you press on to the burn attitude.

a15_0952445.speaker: Worden
a15_0952445.text: Hey, very good, Bob. Thank you. We will.

a15_0952445.speaker: Irwin
a15_0952445.text: Houston, this is 15 with some retraction times for you.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_0952445.speaker: Irwin
a15_0952445.text: On the Mass Spec., it was - on the Mass Spec., it was 02:33. On Gamma-ray, 03:09.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Copy, thank you.

a15_0952445.speaker: Irwin
a15_0952445.text: It was 2 minutes and 33 seconds, 3 minutes and 9 seconds.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Say again, 15. Was that 233 seconds, and 3 minutes and 9 seconds?

a15_0952445.speaker: Irwin
a15_0952445.text: No; 2 minutes and 33 seconds, 3 minutes and 9 seconds.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Roger. We had that; thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0952445.speaker: Worden
a15_0952445.text: Houston, 15.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Go ahead.

a15_0952445.speaker: Worden
a15_0952445.text: Okay, Bob. I'm sitting looking right at the surface with the optics in this attitude. Give me a good roll angle to go to.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Okay; stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Stand by. We're talking about it guys.

a15_0952445.speaker: Worden
a15_0952445.text: Okay, Bob. [Long pause.]

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: Roger, 15. Now that we told you to stop [the roll], why don't you press on to the burn roll on 180 [degrees].

a15_0952445.speaker: Scott
a15_0952445.text: Okay; thanks a lot.

a15_0952445.speaker: Parker
a15_0952445.text: [Laughter.] For what? And now, if you lose High Gain [Antenna] by going to the burn attitude before you go around the corner, it will be Omni Delta in the burn attitude.

a15_0952445.speaker: Scott
a15_0952445.text: Roger. Omni Delta.

a15_0953417.speaker: Parker
a15_0953417.text: And, Apollo 15, we'd like Track Auto [on the HGA] as you go around the corner here. It'll help us keep you on data for a couple of minutes there at the end. And we've got a couple of stars for you, if you want to take any more advice. And that's a 25 and 26.

a15_0953417.speaker: Scott
a15_0953417.text: Okay; 25 and 26. And you've got Auto.

a15_0953745.speaker: Parker
a15_0953745.text: And, Apollo 15, you're 5 minutes from LOS, looking good, and Go for the burn for DOI trim.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: Okay; understand. Go for DOI trim. See you on the other side.

a15_0953745.speaker: Irwin
a15_0953745.text: I can't get in there among all the helmets.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: You got another 15 degrees to go, Al.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: ...go ahead and finish what you're doing; I'm sorry.

a15_0953745.speaker: Irwin
a15_0953745.text: Al, you've got to change those Logic Powers, too, and go back an Off; I'm sorry. I was thinking we had to retract the booms. They're already retracted.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: Okay. I'll be glad when I get rid of you guys. I won't have to worry about those switches anymore.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: Oh, that's right. You don't have any maneuvers.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: No, I - I laid it on them. I said, 'Those switches, as long as I'm by myself, are going to stay in Deploy/Retract all the time.'

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: That's good. Okay, you're almost there.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: And I'll tell you what. Why don't you do your P52, and just stay down there, and I'll do a P30...

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: ...and let you do the star check.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: All right. [Garble] warning lines. Jim can pick up the checklist.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: I'll - I'll get the numbers. They recommend 25 and 26.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: Right. If 25 doesn't come up, I'm going to punch it in.

a15_0953745.speaker: Scott
a15_0953745.text: Okay. Well, you've got 16 minutes, so you're in good shape.

a15_0953745.speaker: Irwin
a15_0953745.text: Do you want to start an EMS Delta-V test over there...

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: Twenty-six; comes up the right stars.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: Oh, yes, there's Gienah; this must be Spica.

a15_0953745.speaker: Worden
a15_0953745.text: One, 2, 3 - Okay, I'll torque them on a minute.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Well, wait a minute. Oh, you want to do it right here? Okay, sextant star is number 30.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Take a look at your shaft and trunnion, if you can.

a15_0954300.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0954300.text: This is Apollo Control. We've now had Loss Of Signal as Apollo 15 sailed behind the Moon nearing the end of the ninth revolution. Coming up in about 13 minutes on the DOI trim maneuver, which will be an RCS burn to raise pericynthion from the present 7½ nautical miles [13.9 km] to 9.6 [nautical miles, 17.8 km]. 3.1 feet per second [0.95 m/s velocity change with a] burn time of 20 seconds. 1 hour and 8 minutes until - [correcting himself] I'm sorry about that, about 47 minutes actually to acquisition of signal again. At 95 hours, 44 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, this is Apollo Control, ou

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, it should be 192.8 and 111. You've got 192.1 and 114.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Why don't we just - Let me do a...

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Do you want to just take those numbers?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: No, let me do a P - P30-P41 real quick and get you to - the right attitude.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Well, we want to do the sextent star check on their attitude anyway.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: There, I - you're in good shape.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay. Good. Okay, why don't you clean up down there? I'll do a 30-41.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I want to go to P00, okay?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: They're really getting down to nitpicking. Okay, I'm all cleaned up down here, Dave.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Your TSBs are getting pretty full, aren't they?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: I think there's a lot of space in the bottoms of them.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Well, if you guys leave today, I'll - I'm going to get the jett bag out and start filling it up with that stuff.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, we're in P41. Trim it out. There, attitude looks pretty good. Okay. Why don't you come up here and do your KS check?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: That's all right, I wouldn't feel too comfortable at 24,000 feet on the verge of a 22,000-foot mountain.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes, well, this'll bring you up 10,000 feet.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Are you running a null bias check here?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: No. I just started to set it up now when you got...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Did you run the Delta-V test?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes. That's good. It's a minus 21.9.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Your clock's set, but for some reason it isn't set exactly right. I think that timer drifts on you.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes. I suspect it very well might.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Have we got the DAP set in there that we want?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes. Let's go check the waste...

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: I ch - I put that in.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: That's the only thing there was to put in.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay. Roll, pitch, and yaw looks okay.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay, you want to get ROT Control Power, Normal, two, to AC/DC?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: ROT Control Power, Direct, two, to Main A, B.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: I didn't get the chance to check the DET.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes, you can turn it right and the next time you look it's - Oh, [garble], forgot to give you that.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: That's all right. I put your film in your TSB.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay BMAG Mode, three, are Rate 2.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: And we're at CMC in Auto?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: We'll wait until the Delta-V test is complete to do the trim?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Delta-V test is complete, and it's .8 feet per second per 100 seconds. It's getting better.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay, do you want to - do you want to trim?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: I said you want to set Delta-V C , I suppose?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Ah, let's set - Yes, better - Your 100 is probably good. Delta-V C should be 3.1.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Looks like it's about 3 or 4 seconds off, and I'm really not sure I understand why.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Okay, 3.1. I've got a 103.1 set in there.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay, do you want to trim it?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes, we might as well. Get it all in plus-X. Okay?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes. Okay, push up close to [garble]. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Manual Attitude, three, to Rate Command.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: What happened to your Translation Control Power?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Where's the THC Power? Well, now...

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Do it for a GDC Align. That doesn't make sense.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: No? No, it sure doesn't, does it?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: And we're standing by for 5 minutes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Have you timed this thing, Dave?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, at some point you got to go Attitude 1/Rate 2 to have your SPS...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: ...in attitude hold. Let's not call down anymore. So you might as well do it now.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Okay, we're in Att 1/Rate 2, just in case we need it.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay. Did you get the 85 display? I guess it's...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay. After the burn, there's not much. I think we're in good shape. I'll tell you what we might do. After the burn, let's pressurize the LM.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: And let you get suited. And it might be better if you just pull your suit out and stuck it in the corner and got all that stuff out of the tunnel. [Garble], we can put it here and...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: ...down under that couch, where we've been putting it.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: And try to [garble] it back. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes, and I think there's enough room for you to get suited there.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Then we can start working on that [garble] I'd like to do that landing site thing - the P24.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: And I'll be getting all the transfer gear.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes, get all the transfer gear. Yes. As a matter of fact, you can start taking it over, once we get the tunnel opened up.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Boy, I tell you, we go by that landing site awful fast.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes, you really go zipping by.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Did you get a good picture of it?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: It was a little too dark.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: I just - All I could do was point down, and I just picked up the rille going past the edge of the window. I was just too slow getting to it, so - I knew I didn't have much time, but I didn't know it was that fast. I didn't realize we were going to get through it that quickly.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: ...[garble]. In the LM when - when we'd do that, we'd run it several times across PDI with the window. We should have done that in the LMS with you. I didn't - I didn't...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: ...[garble] about the - No, you never came over there and watched us do it from 9 miles.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Really give you a feeling for it.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I never thought about the TV pass, though, to tell you the truth.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Tell them it went awful fast?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Could you - did you have any...

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Well, all - all I could do was stick it in the window and catch - catch the rille going out of the edge of the picture, and that was it, Dave. So, all I saw was - all I saw was St. George and - and Elbow Crater.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Did you get a good chance to point it at the Apennines coming up, though?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Did you see the mountains on the horizon and all that stuff?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Well, that ought to be pretty impressive. Well, we're down to 2 minutes, Jimmy.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: And don't - don't forget on that Activation Checklist that one of them has that ECS stuff, and the other's got - Make sure we have both of those. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: One minute. Okay, 20-second burn [garble] Jim will count because your clock is sort of [garble].

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Mark; the burn time. DSKY's count?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Now trim it a little bit. Yes, that's [garble]. That's good, Al. [Garble].

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: What did they want it trimmed to?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: They didn't say. Why don't you - Could you take that to 3/10ths?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: They didn't want us to trim any...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: We got a P00 after that?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, there's a maneuver to P52 high-gain attitude. If DOI trim required; roll, pitch, and yaw. Well, beautiful, they didn't give us that one. Did they? Did they give us an attitude to go to, Jim - after the burn?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: No, I don't think so. It's not on the PAD.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Well, for God sakes. They forgot it completely.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay. They're not too with us this morning.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: What - what kind of high-gain antenna angles do we get in this attitude?

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Why don't you look for it...

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Let's look in the book and see if that's in a clear area.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Right up there. Do you want - want to clean up of SIM bay here, Dave?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: X-Ray - Alpha Ray/X Door to Alpha On.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Wait, hold it. Gainstep to Shield On?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I don't know. What is it?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I don't know. It doesn't say that over there.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, Mass Spec Experiment to Standby.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Okay, Mass Spec Experiment is Standby.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Pan Camera - You got the mode? For the Pan Camera [garble]...

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Oh, Power - Pan Camera Power to off. I'm sorry.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: What does that look like? I said that to you.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Oh, my. Well, let's see. Getting range and no coverage, though. Next thing we go to is landing site observation attitude at 96:55, which is 015, 290, and 000. So that ought to be a good attitude. You see we come down through here and do all that.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Well, we don't have anything else, do we?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: S-band. Says P52 HGA attitude, if DOI trim required. Well, we'll give it to him. And the next attitude we have to do - it looks stable for maneuver, because they're surely to give us a - an extra maneuver.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: They didn't give us that. Here we come around here, and the next thing we have to do is burn status - maneuver to this attitude. Okay?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: That'll be Charlie there, huh? That's not a good - that's not a good high-gain attitude.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: But it's better than the one we've got, though.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: How can you tell we're there?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Huh? Well, the landing-site observation attitude is not a good high gain.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: ...That's - that's corrected better than what we've got.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Well, we got Omni now, anyway, don't we?

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Yes. Now we can just sit here. You've got Omni B here or Omni Charlie in that other attitude.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Let's see, we have AOS at 96:30. Okay, and then we only got 20 minutes to maneuver. I guess you're right. I guess that would be better than - kind of - We only have Omni, but that's too bad, I guess. But at least it's better than this one.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Got a long ways to go.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: So we might as well do it. Go to [garble]. Okay. Next order of business is the tunnel.

a15_0954300.speaker: Irwin
a15_0954300.text: Al, I want to change lightweights with you. I'm going off comm.

a15_0954300.speaker: Worden
a15_0954300.text: Okay, and I'd better put some biomed on.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Oh, yes, that's right. Why don't -

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: You're going to have some time - Oh, you got to get your suit on.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Why don't - why don't we do the tunnel and get that stuff in here. I don't think it's going to be in the way too much, once we get your suit out of the way. Oh, do your biomed stuff, and we'll get all the transfer stuff together. Then we'll have it all, and we won't have to do any more shuffling.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I - I'll get it. Jim, go ahead and get the transfer stuff. I'll - That's the wrong thing, Jim. You're in the right wall.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Need any help, Jimmy? What - UCW2 [?]. Oh, that thing. Yes, okay. Where it is? I'll go get it. Oh, I know where it is; it's in A-8.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Did you leave Al one jettison bag?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay. How many did you have to start with?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: (Clanking) No, I really guess not. Okay, we'll just take one. Okay, LM Data File, huh? What should - what should be in it, Jim? Huh? Yes. I know this is in it; I saw it the other day.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: No, it's - it's an extra one of ours. I had - that's a backup. Command module. I had them put on. (Laughter) It's the only kind I understand. It's not going to work (laughter). Here, I know where I'll put it, right in here. Right there.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Time line. Go. Data Card Book. Go. Okay, go.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: All right. I'd like to time it [garble].

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Maybe I got a PRD, Jim.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: There it is. I've got to get Al's, really. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: It wasn't? Why? Really? Oh, let me write this

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Do you know where your PRD is, Al? Yes, give me to it [sic]. I'm switching you right now.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Some day they may want these readings. They're in here. They're in here at the beginning of the day, if you ever get around to it. Okay, Jim, my PRD. I thought I Just handed you one. Huh?

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Oh, shoot, I don't see it, Jim. No, don't check it off; we'll look for it, as we go around. Oh, is that the list you're checking? Oh, come on. Okay. Yes. Yes, I put mine on. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes, we're - Yes, but - Yes, okay. I've got mine in my pocket. Okay. Yes. Got that? Yes. Yes.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Okay, yes - yes. What I - We also want to take these over and bring the new ones back. CWGs.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes. Yes, we have them on.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: I'm going to have mine in my pocket, in this thing when I bring it over. So I got mine. Do you want to take yours? Okay, it's in the tube, Jim.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes. I was going to put them in my pocket, too, before I got hooked around. Here, I can stick it in this pocket up here - in my strap-on pocket. When are we going to put them over there? Okay.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes, got mine ready to snap on.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: We got both Activation Checklists? Sure, huh? Okay.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Yes. Well, all right. We're going to go early.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Well, I don't think we've left you with too much to do, Al. I hope not. Keep an eye on those guys down there.

a15_0954300.speaker: Scott
a15_0954300.text: Let them watch the systems and you do the flying, which is the way it ought to be.

a15_0954300.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0954300.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about 4 minutes from re-acquiring the spacecraft, Endeavour and Falcon, on their tenth revolution of the Moon. Here in Mission Control, we've completed a shift handover. The on-duty Flight Director at this time is Glynn Lunney. Our spacecraft communicator is astronaut Edgar Mitchell. The off-going Flight Director [is] Gene Kranz. And we do anticipate having a change of shift press briefing in the MSC News Center briefing room probably in 15 or 20 minutes. On reacquiring the spacecraft, the first order of business will be to get a report on the Descent Orbit In

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Okay, I guess the - next thing we ought to do - when you get ready - is go through the tunnel. No, I don't need that. System Checklist.

a15_0962553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0962553.text: I think you had the Systems Checklist, didn't you? Oh, here it is. Okay. Well, that's your job, because - Say again?

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Think we ought to try and get them on the high gain? Hey, Al, you think we ought to try to get them on the high gain?

a15_0962553.speaker: Irwin
a15_0962553.text: I mean - Okay. I could easily go through it, because I could tell which ones to check - skip through .... get.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0962553.text: We're less now than 30 seconds from reacquiring Apollo 15. Flight Director Glynn Lunney has completed a review of the status of the mission with all of his flight controllers, and all of the buttons on his console from each flight controller indicate green. And we're standing by now to reacquire in about 5 seconds.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Hey, we're getting them. How about that. Yes. There, got a lock.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0962553.text: And we've had Acquisition Of Signal.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Rog, Houston; 15 here. We had a good burn and have a burn report for you.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Okay; [the burn was] on time - burn time was about 18 or 19 seconds. The residuals were minus .1, plus .2, plus .2, Delta-V C was plus .8, and the G&N has us in a 59.4 by 10.3 [nautical mile orbit or 109.9 by 19.1 km].

a15_0962553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0962553.text: You heard Dave Scott report the results of that burn almost precisely as planned.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0962553.text: And, 15, I have a landing site observation PAD for you when ready.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Rog. We're there, and T-horizon: 96:57:10. Standing by for TCA minus 20.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0962553.text: 15, Houston. We have an up-link for you, state vector, and a REFSMMAT, if you'll give us P00 and Accept. [Pause.]

a15_0962553.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0962553.text: And, 15, Houston. I have a couple of words for Al on the System Test Meter if he can listen.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Sorry, he - he's busy right now. What do you need? I'll tell him later.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0962553.text: Hey, it - we'll get it to him later. It's simply that the Systems Test Meter is okay to use for the LM checkout on the LM [electrical] current.

a15_0962553.speaker: Scott
a15_0962553.text: Houston, 15. We're equalizing pressure now, and the Delta-P was 1.0 [psi] before we started.

a15_0962553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0962553.text: The Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] reports that that Descent Orbit Insertion trim maneuver was just about precisely as planned. That will change the pericynthion from about 7½ nautical miles [13.9 km] to about 9.6 [nautical miles, 17.8 km]. Scott reported on board that their guidance and navigation system calculated their orbit after the burn to be 59.4 by 10.3 [nautical miles, 110 by 19.1 km] which would agree very closely with the ground calculation. A few minutes ago, Dave Scott reported that they were equalizing the pressure in the tunnel between the LM and the CSM. This would put t

a15_0962553.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0962553.text: This is Apollo Control at 96 hours, 43 minutes. We're going to transfer at this time to the MSC News Center briefing room for a change of shift press briefing. We'll follow our usual procedure of recording any conversations with the spacecraft that occur during the briefing and play those back immediately following.

a15_0964826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0964826.text: Al, we didn't get your last torquing angles and torquing time. Could you read them down to us, please?

a15_0964826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0964826.text: If you're busy, we'll get them later.

a15_0964826.speaker: Worden
a15_0964826.text: I'll give them to you now; anything for you. Okay; we used stars 25 and 26. Noun 05 was four balls, one; torquing angles were plus 00.022, minus 00.032, plus 00.038, and they were torqued out at 95:43:00.

a15_0964826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0964826.text: Roger; copy. And, as long as we have you on the loop, your REFSMMAT 00 time is 104:41:43.00.

a15_0964826.speaker: Worden
a15_0964826.text: I'm sorry, Ed. I didn't get that. Would you say that again, please?

a15_0964826.speaker: Worden
a15_0964826.text: Understand. REFSMMAT time is good for 104:41:43.00.

a15_0970143.speaker: Scott
a15_0970143.text: Okay; looks like FAO [Flight Activities Officer] owes us one. I had no trouble picking up Index Crater at all. The surface looks generally smooth. I saw no big boulders. I saw more craters than we're normally used to seeing [in the simulator], but I think that's because of the [low] resolution of the [Lunar Orbiter] photography. I can see a - a fair amount of boulders in the bottom of the rille. Most of the surface seems to be pretty subdued and rounded. I did see some debris around some of the fresher craters. And, of course, I don't know exactly what size, but if we're looking at 3-feet reso

a15_0970143.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0970143.text: Okay, Dave. We copy. Thanks a lot.

a15_0971034.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0971034.text: Apollo 15, Houston. If there's someone available to copy a TEI-19 PAD, I'll give it to you.

a15_0971034.speaker: Worden
a15_0971034.text: Okay; hold for about 5 [minutes], will you please, Ed?

a15_0971034.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0971034.text: This is Apollo Control. That completes our playback of the accumulated tape. We'll continue to stand by live now. Dave Scott, in that playback, reported the surface of the landing site appeared to be subdued and rounded. He said nothing larger than about 15 feet [4.5 metres] or so. And also added that it should be no problem for Al Worden to track on the - on the site from the Command Module.

a15_0971034.speaker: Scott
a15_0971034.text: Okay, Houston; go - go ahead with the TEI PAD.

a15_0971034.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0971034.text: Roger, 15. TEI-19: SPS/G&N 38009; plus 0.61, plus 1.05; 115:27:55.59; plus 2845.1, minus 0831.7, minus 0219.7; 180, 102, 346. The rest, NA. Ullage, 4 jet, 12 seconds; and some notes. One is, burn is undocked; two, assume Circ.; three, longitude at T IG is 166.0 [degrees] west; and the fourth note is, the attitude's based on landing-site REFSMMAT. [Long pause.]

a15_0971034.speaker: Scott
a15_0971034.text: Okay, readback. TEI-19: SPS/G&N; 38009; plus 0.61, plus 1.05; 115:27:55.59; plus 2845.1, minus 0831.7, minus 0219.7; 180, 102, 346; 4 jet, 12 seconds; burn undocked; assume Circ.; longitude 166.0 west at T IG , and landing site REFSMMAT.

a15_0971034.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0971034.text: That's affirm; and we have a few centiseconds update for your CMC clock, whenever you're ready.

a15_0971034.speaker: Scott
a15_0971034.text: Okay, you want P00 and Accept?

a15_0972323.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972323.text: Falcon - rather, Apollo 15, Houston. Omni Charlie, please. [Pause.]

a15_0972323.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972323.text: Haven't had a chance to say good morning, Al, so good morning.

a15_0972323.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0972323.text: That was the Command Module Pilot Al Worden exchanging good morning greetings with spacecraft communicator Edgar Mitchell.

a15_0972923.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972923.text: Rog. We need to redo the REFSMMAT update that we gave you a little while ago. Could we have P00 and Accept please? [Pause.]

a15_0972923.speaker: Worden
a15_0972923.text: Okay, Ed. You caught me just in time, doing a P52.

a15_0972923.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972923.text: ...what - what we were hoping to do.

a15_0972923.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972923.text: The story here, Al, is that, apparently, the block update changed some registers in the REFS - REFSMMAT and screwed it up a bit.

a15_0972923.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0972923.text: 15, Houston. The computer's yours. And, Al, before you do [P]50 [correcting himself] [P]52, be advised you can use the Systems Test Meter on the backside for any of the normal LM checkout functions; on the front-side, we'll watch it for you. And go ahead and leave the test meter in whatever position you're - you're testing with. You understand?

a15_0973532.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0973532.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Thirty seconds to LOS.

a15_0973532.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0973532.text: And we've had Loss Of Signal now. While on the backside of the Moon, on this tenth revolution, and going into the eleventh revolution, Scott and Irwin will be getting suited up. By the time we reacquire on the frontside of the Moon. They should be in the Lunar Module and beginning to power up and check out the LM prior to undocking and separation at 100 hours, 14 minutes. As the spacecraft went around the corner, Al Worden was in the process of doing a program 52, which is a platform alignment. This is normally performed prior to and following maneuvers with the spacecraft, aligning the stable

a15_0973532.speaker: Worden
a15_0973532.text: [Yelling] In case you guys are wondering, I'm dumping.

a15_0973532.speaker: Worden
a15_0973532.text: Fuel cell purge, huh? Okay, fuel cell purge. Two for 2 hours. Two of them on.

a15_0973532.speaker: Scott
a15_0973532.text: When you almost get there, how about [garble]?

a15_0973532.speaker: Scott
a15_0973532.text: [Garble] coming up [garble] to AOS [garble] up to - be ready for AOS.

a15_0973532.speaker: Worden
a15_0973532.text: I think I'm just about ready.

a15_0973532.speaker: Worden
a15_0973532.text: Yes. Where is the tape? Anybody know?

a15_0982200.speaker: Worden
a15_0982200.text: [Yelling] No. You guys are too far ahead.

a15_0982200.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0982200.text: This is Apollo Control at 98 hours, 22 minutes and we're now about 2 minutes from reacquiring Apollo 15 on its eleventh revolution of the Moon. Flight Director Glynn Lunney just asked all of his flight controllers to be on their toes for this revolution. The frontside pass, he said, would be a very - a very busy one. The crew will be primarily involved with the activation checklist on board the Lunar Module - Scott and Irwin. Coming up on the succeeding two revolutions, 12 and 13, we'll have some important landmark trackings being performed by Al Worden in the Command Module updating the knowl

a15_0982200.speaker: Scott
a15_0982200.text: Okay there, Endeavour. How do you read the Falcon on...

a15_0982200.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982200.text: And, Al, how do you read me?

a15_0982200.speaker: Worden
a15_0982200.text: Read you loud and clear, Jim.

a15_0982200.speaker: Worden
a15_0982200.text: Hey, did you say something about T EPHEM ? Did you want a T EPHEM , Dave?.

a15_0982200.speaker: Worden
a15_0982200.text: Okay. I'll give it to you if you want.

a15_0982200.speaker: Scott
a15_0982200.text: Stand by. Configure for Simplex A.

a15_0982200.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0982200.text: And we've had Acquisition Of Signal.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Al. How do you read on A?

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Loud and clear, Dave.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: That's nice.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: And, Al, how do you read me?

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Loud and clear, Jim.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Very good.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay. Now you can give me your T EPHEM .

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Ready to copy?

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Go.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Just like SIM. All balls in the R 1 . R 2 is 32251. R 3 is 26157.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay. All balls, 32251, 26157.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Great.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Want a clock sync?

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Stand by 1.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Give me a mark. I'm waiting.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Roger.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Apollo 15, Houston; standing by.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: And I'm coming up to get the umbilical now.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Read you loud and clear.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Roger, Houston. This is Falcon. Read you loud and clear.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Falcon; reading you. We have a lot of noise on the loop - maybe it'll go away in a moment.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Okay. Let's hope so. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Endeavour, Another Noun 65 if you're ready.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: On your mark.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: ...Mark.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay. We're within three hundredths.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Endeavour, Houston. Do you read?

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Hello, Endeavour, Houston, this is Endeavour. Loud and clear.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Al. We read you through the static. Let us have Narrow on the High Gain [Antenna], please.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, you've got it. Narrow and Reacq.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: And, Houston, this is Falcon. We're going to configure for secondary S-band transmitter and receiver.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Falcon. Press on with secondary S-band. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Roger.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Houston, this is Falcon. How do you read?

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Endeavour, Houston. Verify [that] on your last P52, you used option 1.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go ahead.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Roger, Al. Verify that on your last P52, you used option 1.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: I think that's a negative, Ed. I used option 3. Stand by one and I'll check.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Roger. We're standing by.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Houston, how do you read Falcon?

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. You're coming through; we have a lot of static on the line and they're trying to clear it up now. You're way down in the mud.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Okay. I can give you my time with that - [garble] time - 97:54:55.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Go ahead, Endeavour.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Ed. I did do that on an option 3.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay. We'll have some words for you, and we're ready to uplink to you, Endeavour, if you'll give us - P00 and Accept.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, you got P00 and Accept.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. Your S-band check is okay. You can press on, and I'll have your updates for you in a little while.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: And, Apollo 15; Houston. I'm going to hold off reading you any PADs at the moment until we can clear up our comm on the ground.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Roger.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. Bring up your steerable [antenna], please. See if that helps our comm.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: In work.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0982351.text: We think the noise coming on the communication circuits at the present time is due primarily to the fact that the Lunar Module is still using the omni[-directional] antennas for communication. We've asked Scott and Irwin to bring up the LM steerable antenna and once they get that in operation we expect that the noise on the circuit will drop off significantly.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Houston, this is Falcon. We're locked up on the - the High Gain. How do you read?

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Jim. Reading you loud and clear now; that has seemed to improved our comm. And I'm - I'm ready to start with the PADs. I'll start with the CSM first, Al - whenever you're ready.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Okay; he's working right now. Are you ready for an E-memory dump on the Falcon?

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. We're ready for the E-Mod [Erasable Memory Module] dump.

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: Okay; Stand by. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: En - Endeavour, Houston. The computer's yours.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Rog, Houston. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0982351.text: The Erasable Memory Dump, which is in process at the moment, allows the Flight Controllers here in Mission Control, to look at the Erasable Memory Module in the Lunar Module Guidance Computer and see that everything is in order.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. We will stay with the REFSMMAT you have.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Ed. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. Give us P00 and Data. I have an uplink for you.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Roger, P00 and Data.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: And I'm ready to give PADs, Falcon, whenever you want them.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: [To Worden] Okay, Al; I'm checking it.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Go ahead, Ed.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: All right, your LM DAP [Digital Auto Pilot] data first. CSM weight, 37679; LM weight, 36630. Your GDA [Gimbal Drive Actuator] drive angles onboard are good. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay; copy. CSM weight is 37679; LM weight, 36630.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: That's affirm. AGS abort constants. 224...

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Go ahead.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay; readback on the AGS abort constants. 60442, 29365, 60449, 01659, 55021 and 32306.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Affirm. The first 3 are plus, the last three are negative.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: That's affirm. Houston, Falcon.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Go ahead, Falcon.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay. Everything is in order up to this point as far as the checkout goes, with the exception of the - LGC [LM Guidance Computer]. When we pushed in the LGC circuit breaker, we got a program light - with a 400 and R1. A Verb 5 Noun 9 gave us an 1105, which seems to be of little consequence; just thought you might like to know.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: We copy, Dave.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Falcon, Houston. The computer's yours.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Roger.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. Are you about ready for your PADs?

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Rog, Ed. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Houston. Endeavour's ready to copy.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay. Falcon, the first one's a SEP[aration] time, if you would like that one, too. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Houston, Falcon. Go ahead; we'll stand by.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay. SEP: GET 100:13:56.00 - the pitch angle of 108 [degrees] [Pause.].

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Understand, Ed. That's GET of 100:13:56.00. And that's a pitch angle of 108.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: That's affirm, Al. Okay, the next one is CSM DAP data. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay; go.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Roger. CSM weight, 37679 [pounds, 17,091 kg]; pitch [trim], 0.49; yaw [trim], 1.04.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Understand. The DAP data is weight, 37679; pitch trim is 0.49; and yaw trim is 1.04. And do you have some signs on those?

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: It's a good readback, and say again your last?

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Roger, Ed. I need a sign on the pitch and yaw trims.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: All right - Let me check that.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: It's affirm, Al, they're both positive. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Understand; they're both plus.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Okay; your P24 is next.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: T-1, 100:46:29; T-2, 47:07; TCA, 47:37; T-3, 47:59; roll, pitch, and yaw are 008, 296, 000; north, 3 nautical miles. Noun 89, longitude-over-2, plus 2.149. Latitude and altitude are nominal. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Roger, Ed - Ed - Understand. P24 landmark tracking PAD: T-1 at 100:46:29; T-2, 47:07; TCA, 47:37; T-3, 47:59. It's a roll of 008; pitch, 296; yaw, 000. Expected north at 3 nautical miles. And understand the longitude-over-2 is plus 02.149, and latitude and altitude are as in the Flight Plan.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: Good readback, Al. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Irwin
a15_0982351.text: And, Houston, this is Falcon. ED [Explosive Devices] batteries both reading 37 volts.

a15_0982351.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0982351.text: We copy that, Falcon; thank you. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Endeavour; Falcon. We're ready for a Docked IMU Coarse Align, if you are.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Falcon. Stand by one.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay; give us a call when you are in Min[imum] Deadband, Attitude hold.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay, Dave; we're there.

a15_0982351.speaker: Scott
a15_0982351.text: Okay; if you [could] read us your gimbal angles, please. [Pause.]

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Okay; R1 is plus 001.24, R2 is plus 101.66, R3 is plus 005.37.

a15_0982351.speaker: Worden
a15_0982351.text: Rog.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Falcon...

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Houston, Falcon. We got about 9 minutes 'til sunset here.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Okay, Dave. And we have a clock update for you of about 66 centiseconds if you'll give us P00 and Data, please.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Okay; P00 and Data. You got it. [Pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: And, Houston; Falcon. We'd like to do the RCS pressurization now since we're a tad ahead, if - you're ready to take that?

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Okay; we're ready, Falcon; go ahead.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: And, Endeavour, Houston. When you get a moment, we'll take your read-outs from the last P52.

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Okay, Ed. [Pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Falcon, the computer's yours.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Roger.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Houston, Falcon. A slight pause here while we look at the landing site; we're going right over it.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Ah. Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Okay; a few interesting differences there. Index is much more subtle than we've seen on the simulator. And Earthlight is much sharper with a much deeper shadow.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Copy, Dave. [Long pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Houston, Endeavour. Here are the P52 numbers.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Say again, Endeavour.

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Roger; I got the P52 numbers for you.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Ready to copy, Al.

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Okay, Ed. Stars 41 and 42; Noun 05 was plus four balls 1. Gyro torquing angles were minus 00.010, minus 00.009, minus 00.025. And they were torqued out at 97:39 even.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Copied that, Al. And could you give us your LM power switchover time, please? [Pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Roger. That was at 97:35.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: We copy that. And what was the result of the VHF check; does it work okay?

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: That was satisfactory both ways - far as I know.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Thank you.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Rog, Houston. It was good both ways. [Pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Hey, Endeavour; Falcon. Did you copy that on the difference between Earthlight [Crater] and Index [Crater].

a15_0985045.speaker: Worden
a15_0985045.text: Rog.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: And, Houston. The RCS looks good up here on the Falcon.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: And it looks good down here, Dave.

a15_0985045.speaker: Scott
a15_0985045.text: Okay. We'll pick up the alignment now and get back to you later on with the RCS checkout.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0985045.text: Okay.

a15_0985045.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0985045.text: At the present time Scott and Irwin are aligning the stable platform used as an attitude reference by the Lunar Module guidance system. We presently show the docked spacecraft in an orbit 62 by 9.4 nautical miles [114.8 by 17.4 km] and presently at an altitude of about 10.6 nautical miles [19.6 km].

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Houston, Falcon. That P57 up here, docked, works pretty well. [Long pause.]

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Houston, Falcon, do you have the torquing angles?

a15_0991039.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0991039.text: Roger. [Pause.] Observe the five balls there.

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Yeah; a couple of interesting things, we have [a] reflection off the Command Module apparently from Earthlight. And it's sort of tough to track the star with the Command Module deadbanding, but seems like if you get the star in the crosshairs, why, the optics take care of it for you.

a15_0991039.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0991039.text: And, Falcon; Houston. Will you - you verify the roll CAL for us, please? [Pause.]

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Okay, Endeavour; Falcon. Mid [correcting himself] - min[imum] deadband no longer required.

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Okay, Houston; Falcon. We're ready for the RCS checkout, if you are.

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Okay, Houston; Falcon. Do you have your High Bit Rate?

a15_0991039.speaker: Scott
a15_0991039.text: Okay. And, Endeavour. We need you in a wide deadband Attitude Hold.

a15_0991730.speaker: Scott
a15_0991730.text: Endeavour, Falcon. Do you have any jet fires going on over there?

a15_0991730.speaker: Worden
a15_0991730.text: You want me to go Free now?

a15_0991730.speaker: Scott
a15_0991730.text: Okay, Endeavour. We'll be firing the direct coils.

a15_0991730.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0991730.text: Scott and Irwin are now preparing to fire each of their attitude control thrusters in the Reaction Control System in a check out here.

a15_0992047.speaker: Scott
a15_0992047.text: Okay, Endeavour. Hot fire check is complete. Everything looks good. You can go back to wide deadband Attitude Hold.

a15_0992047.speaker: Worden
a15_0992047.text: Okay. And I'm going to turn the roll jets off and put the hatch in, if you don't mind.

a15_0992047.speaker: Scott
a15_0992047.text: And, Houston, Falcon. How did it look down there?

a15_0992047.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0992047.text: I was just going to tell you, Dave, hot fire check looked good here.

a15_0992047.speaker: Scott
a15_0992047.text: Okay. They're nice and positive, aren't they?

a15_0992047.speaker: Scott
a15_0992047.text: Endeavour, Falcon. Could you verify RCS thruster, B-3, Off, and the Transponder, Off, please?

a15_0992047.speaker: Worden
a15_0992047.text: And, Falcon; Endeavour. I'm cocking the latches now.

a15_0992813.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Apollo 15; Houston. You're Go for undocking. You're 45 seconds from LOS, and we observed your Rendezvous Radar test. Falcon, also, we have not seen you reset the DAP [Digital Auto Pilot].

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, understand. I'll get the DAP reset, and the tapemeter looks like it works fine.

a15_0992813.speaker: Mitchell
a15_0992813.text: Very good, Dave. Glad to hear it.

a15_0992813.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0992813.text: And we've had Loss Of Signal. That last report from Dave Scott that the tapemeter appears to be working well. That's the - one of the onboard indicators used to read out the Rendezvous Radar and also the Landing Radar altitude and altitude rate information, and is one of several means available to the crew and to the guidance system for getting that needed information. As Apollo 15 went around the corner, the spacecraft was in an orbit of 61.9 nautical miles [114.6 km] at its high point and 9.4 nautical miles [17.4 km] at its low point passing over the landing site. Apollo 15, Endeavour and Fa

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Falcon; Endeavour. I got the hatch in and you want to verify your hatch closed?

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, that's verified. Closed and locked.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, I'll do a hatch integrity check then.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Endeavour; Falcon. Our radar checks out okay, and your B-B, Off, and transponder, off, are no longer required.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay. Thank you.

a15_0992813.speaker: Irwin
a15_0992813.text: And, Al, we're going B data.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Falcon, Endeavour. Your transponder checked out okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Oh, very good. Thank you.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Falcon; Endeavour. We're maneuvering to Sep attitude.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Endeavour; Falcon. Have you vented the tunnel?

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Roger.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay; thank you.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Hear that noise with us, Al?

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Al, are you about in attitude now?

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Right, Dave. About 5 degrees to go.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay. We're down to...

a15_0992813.speaker: Irwin
a15_0992813.text: Oh, yes. We should...

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: ...just about everything and it's all shipshape.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Good.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Even the old broken tape meter seems to work.

a15_0992813.speaker: Irwin
a15_0992813.text: That figures.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, we're at attitude now.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay; thank you.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Falcon; Endeavour. Doing the trim maneuver.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay. We're setting at attitude and I've got 10 minutes -

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Mark - to go.

a15_0992813.speaker: Irwin
a15_0992813.text: Okay, we're right with you.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: And we're right on the attitude.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, good.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, Al, at 5 minutes to go, we need a - 06 20. Okay?

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay, you want it now?

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: No, let's wait down until 5 minutes. Okay?

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Okay.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: I'd like to give them as much time on the platform as we call.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Coming up on 5 minutes in 10 seconds.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay, I'll give you a mark.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Mark.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Give me that last one again.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: The last two were okay. The first one was 35975.

a15_0992813.speaker: Scott
a15_0992813.text: Okay; 75. I don't write too good with gloves on.

a15_0992813.speaker: Worden
a15_0992813.text: Roger.

a15_0992813.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0992813.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about 2 minutes from re-establishing radio contact with Endeavour and Falcon . And when next we hear from the 2 vehicles, they should be separated and moving apart at the rate of about 1 foot per second [0.3 m/s]. About a second after separation, Al Worden was to fire the thrusters on the Command Module for about 3 seconds to give them that 1 foot per second separation velocity. The Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] reported that we're seeing a consistent downtrack error of about 15,000 feet [about 4,600 metres] per revolution. This is not unduly large, and is th

a15_0992813.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0992813.text: And we're coming up now on 30 seconds until reacquisition. The first order of business will be to confirm the undocking and separation.

a15_0992813.speaker: Mission Control
a15_0992813.text: And the guidance officer has just reported that a review of the Erasable Memory on the Lunar Module shows that the LM guidance system Erasable Memory is in very good condition. And we've just had Acquisition Of Signal.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Endeavour, Houston. Standing by for a Sep report.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay, Houston; this is the Falcon. We didn't get a Sep, and Al's been checking the umbilicals down on the probe [garble].

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Okay. We didn't read that, except no Sep. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: Dave Scott reporting we have not gotten separation. They said they were going to be checking the probe umbilicals. We'll stand by for further reports.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay, Houston; Falcon. We got no Sep, and Al's going back into the tunnel to check the umbilicals now. And I guess we'll stand by for your recommendation.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Okay, Falcon. We copy. And we'll have some words in a minute.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay. [Pause.] There was not even any motion on the probe.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Roger. We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Falcon, Houston. We have no probe temp[erature data], which indicates the umbilical is probably not well connected.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay. Well, that's just what he's checking. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: And, 15; Houston. Be advised that we have plenty of time here on the Sep, up to 40 minutes or so. Procedures will be to get vertical or get - now get vertical on the orb rate ball and standard Sep procedures.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay, fine. We can handle that. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: To recap the situation here, you heard Dave Scott report that we did not get a separation. The preliminary indication is that we may have an umbilical that is not properly connected in which case power would not flow to the probe and this appears to be the most likely cause at the moment. The Flight Dynamics Officer has reported that we can go up to about 40 minutes without separating before we run into problems in an on-time powered descent.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Hey, Al, I hope you made sure the Extend/Release switch was Off when you went in there.

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Rog.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Apollo 15, Houston. We're seeing the telemetry on the probe now. I presume that [loose umbilical plug] may have been our problem.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay, very good. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Okay, David. I'm venting you down now.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay; good show. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: And that probe was loose in the - the umbilical was loose in Victor [its socket].

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay, I'm glad you found something. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: The indication here on the ground that we had...

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Okay.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: And there's plenty of time to get a good hatch integrity check, 15, and do the procedure leisurely.

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Okay, Ed. That's in work now.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: The - the indication here on the ground that we had a loose umbilical to the probe was a - an off-scale high temperature reading on the probe which indicated that that umbilical was not connected. Al Worden, on inspection, confirmed that indeed, the umbilical was loose. We presume at this point that we'll be able to go ahead with a normal undocking.

a15_1001551.speaker: Irwin
a15_1001551.text: Houston, Falcon. In the meantime, can I give you the gimbal angles under Verb 06 Noun 20. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: This is Houston; go ahead.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay. The GET was 100:08:56; and the CSM, 35975, 10818, 35995. The LM, 30009, 28836, zip, zip, zip, zip four [00004].

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: We copy.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. Reminder: We want the Sep in a local vertical attitude.

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Rog; understand. Local vertical. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Houston, Falcon. You know, we've - You might run out of an attitude and a time, and it might save a little gas. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Okay. In 2 minutes, we have an angle of 55.7 [degrees]. We're working on one for 5 minutes later.

a15_1001551.speaker: Unidentified voice
a15_1001551.text: Go ahead.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Well, it's going to take fairly sizeable maneuver, and it takes a little while to maneuver [at] two-tenths of degree per second.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Rog; understand. We're getting another for you for 5 minutes from now. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Better make it 10.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Yeah; we'll have one for every 5 minutes, Dave.

a15_1001551.speaker: Scott
a15_1001551.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: And 15; Houston. We're not going to be able to make the P24 this pass, we don't believe. So don't worry about it. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: P24 is the landmark tracking of the landmark near the landing site which Al Worden was scheduled to perform from the Command Module. We'll be doing that again on the next revolution. And at the moment we're standing by for another attempt at undocking and separation.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: Endeavour, Houston. Let's head for a - an inertial pitch gimbal angle at the 30 degrees. And we may have to touch that up, but that's approximate. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. Going towards 30 degrees pitch.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: That's affirm, Al. [Long pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1001551.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. That angle is good for 100 hours and 38 minutes [GET], and it's not very critical. We'll use it anytime around there. [Pause.]

a15_1001551.speaker: Worden
a15_1001551.text: Yeah. Roger, Houston.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: Our Guidance and Control Officer estimates that it will be about 6 minutes before the spacecraft are in the proper attitude for separation.

a15_1001551.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1001551.text: This is Apollo Control. At the moment we're awaiting the spacecraft to maneuver into the proper attitude for separation. Again to recap, a separation was to have occurred about 4 minutes prior to reacquiring spacecraft on the 12th revolution. Dave Scott, once reacquired, reported that separation had not occurred. On the ground we noticed at that time an indication of a high temperature - off scale high on the probe assembly which indicated that we possibly did not have electrical power to the probe, which in turn, is an indication that the umbilical is either not connected or not firm in its s

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay, Falcon; this is Endeavour. And I'm all set up again. The tunnel's sealed in and the pressure's good.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay, very good. Give me a minute.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay. And I'll stop the maneuver at local vertical.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay. Have you - Are you in Attitude Hold now?

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Negative. Will be in just about another 10 degrees.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay.

a15_1003507.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1003507.text: That's Al Worden and Dave Scott talking back and forth between Endeavour and Falcon .

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay. As you get all set, I need about one minute to get P47 up.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay, Dave. About a minute and a half.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay; a minute and a half 'til you get to your attitude?

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: 'Til we're ready to Sep.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay; good. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay; let's go on one minute.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay; you got P47 running. You can Go anytime you want to.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay; I've got P47 running also. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: 10 seconds.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay; we're on the capture latches. Good.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: And you're on your own.

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay; good clean Sep. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1003507.text: You heard Al Worden and Dave Scott report separation and we confirm that on the ground, a good clean separation at 100 hours, 39 minutes, 39 seconds.

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Endeavour, Houston. Be advised your current attitude is a good one for your P52, if you'd like to hold it.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay, Ed; if you think we can't get there for the P24s.

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Negative. You've only got 6 minutes. They say "No way."

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Okay. We'll hold this.

a15_1003507.speaker: Irwin
a15_1003507.text: Okay. Falcon's going to yaw left. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay. Falcon's going to pitch up 90.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Roger.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: And you got four good-looking gear. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: And, Falcon, Endeavour. Looks like you got one radar there that's - rotating away from me [DSE has 'rotating quite freely'].

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Okay. We've got you in sight; we're looking straight at you. It's really pretty.

a15_1003507.speaker: Worden
a15_1003507.text: Roger?

a15_1003507.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1003507.text: That was Al Worden confirming to Dave Scott and Jim Irwin aboard Falcon that they have 4 good looking landing gears. The principal effect of the late undocking is, as I mentioned, going to be to delete the possibility of doing the program 24 landmark tracking on this revolution. We do have another opportunity on the next revolution to do that landmark tracking, although, we would prefer to have two revolutions of the tracking prior to the powered descent, we can get by with a single revolution of the landmark tracking.

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Falcon, Houston. Low Bit Rate, Aft Omni, please. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Scott
a15_1003507.text: Roger. We're Low Bit Rate and Aft Omni.

a15_1003507.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1003507.text: We've had a drop out in communications while the spacecraft is maneuvering to a new attitude and we'll be reacquiring on the High Gain Antenna shortly and that should clear up the communications. Again to repeat the situation. On reacquiring the spacecraft at the beginning of the 12th revolution, Dave Scott reported that we had not gotten separation at the scheduled time. On the ground we had an indication through a high temperature indication telemetered back from the spacecraft that perhaps the umbilical to the probe assembly was not firmly connected. On inspecting the assembly, Al Worden fo

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Endeavour...

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Roger. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1003507.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1003507.text: Falcon, Houston. Give us, on the steerable, Pitch, 155; Yaw, minus 50.

a15_1003507.speaker: Irwin
a15_1003507.text: Roger. Pitch, 155; Yaw, minus 50.

a15_1004738.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1004738.text: Okay, Falcon. We're reading you well now. Give us High Bit Rate, please. [Pause.]

a15_1004738.speaker: Scott
a15_1004738.text: And, Houston, we're ready to go with the DPS throttle check, whenever you are.

a15_1004738.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1004738.text: And, Endeavour, Houston. Give us P00 and Accept; we have an uplink for you.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: And, Falcon, Houston. We didn't see the [DPS] throttle actuator move on that test. Check your DECA Power circuit breaker, please.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, the computer's yours. [Pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: ...open.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Roger.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: And say again, Dave.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. You want to run it again real quickly, Ed?

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Was the circuit breaker out?

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: ...take at it - take a look at it again with the - [pause]. Yeah. Rog. The circuit breaker is out.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Very good.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Do you want to look at the test again?

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: That's affirm, Falcon. Let's have again, please.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Roger-D. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Ed. CDR's at min, 11; soft stop, 51; max, 101.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: We copy. And it looks good this time.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. And the circuit breaker is still in.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Roger, Roger. And we're ready to give you an uplink, if you'll give us P00 and Data, please.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Stand by. Let's run the LMP check here. [Pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: And it looked good here, Falcon.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: And, Falcon; Houston. Do you know if the circuit breaker was out, or did it pop? Can you verify what - either?

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: No, I can't verify either. We checked them over before undocking and - I can't tell you whether it popped or was open.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Okay; we understand. Thank you.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Houston. We'll take the uplink anytime you want to give it to us.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Here she comes.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay; Endeavour, Falcon. We're going to run the [rendezvous] radar checkout now. [Pause.]
