a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: And, Falcon, the computer's yours.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Falcon, Endeavour. [Pause.] I mean Endeavour, Falcon. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay; Houston, Falcon here. Would you give the Endeavour a call. Tell them we're going to run the radar checkout now, please. We seem to have lost contact.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Roger. Endeavour, Houston. Falcon is calling, and he's ready for the rendezvous radar check. [No answer.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Houston. Do you copy? [No answer.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Houston. Do you read? [No answer.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Falcon. [No answer.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Falcon. Simplex A and B. How do you read?

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: I read 5 square, Falcon.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Well, we lost you there somewhere along the way. We need to check out the radar and Houston seems to not be able to get a hold of you either.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay. I'm in.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: We're reading you now, Al.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Ed...

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: I was...

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Ed; I was off for a couple of minutes reconfiguring inside here.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Roger.

a15_1005119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Al. If you'll go back to Simplex A, then we'll give you the voice ranging, and we'll check out the radar.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay. I'm Simplex A.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Voice ranging coming up. We're going to check the radar.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Falcon. You got your Transponder, On?

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: [Faint] Rog. Roger. Transponder coming On. [Pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Say again, Falcon. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Endeavour; Falcon. Can you give us your range, please?

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay, Falcon. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Endeavour, Falcon.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Hello, Falcon. This is Endeavour. How do you read now?

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Yeah, five by. Can you give us your range, please?

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Okay; .4 [nautical miles], Dave.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay; .4. We're looking at .78.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Rog. Let me reset.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Reset. [Long pause.]

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: I have you at .41 now.

a15_1005119.speaker: Scott
a15_1005119.text: Okay. Maybe we're just in too close. We're looking at .79 mile. We'll press on.

a15_1005119.speaker: Worden
a15_1005119.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Endeavour, Houston. We're going to recommend you skip your P52. GUIDO's satisfied with your alignment, and we're ready with your Circ. burn - Circ. PAD any time. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Roger, Houston; Endeavour. Stand by one. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Endeavour, Houston. Did you say standing by? [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Yeah, Houston, Endeavour's ready to copy.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Okay, Al. We'd like for you to go ahead and start going to the burn attitude. I'll give you the roll, pitch, and yaw, and you can get that in, and I - then I will give you the rest of the PAD. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Roger, Houston. Go ahead.

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Rog; understand. 000, 107, 358. I'll put that in and be right back with you.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. We're maneuvering. Go ahead with the rest of the PAD.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Okay. Circ.: SPS/G&N; 37679; plus 0.49, plus 1.04; GET is 101:38:58.19; plus 0068.3, minus four zeroes 1, minus four zeroes 7; 000, 107, 358; 0064.9, plus 0054.3; 0068.3, 0:04, 0057.2; sextant star 10, 171.3, 40.0. The rest NA. GDC Align, Vega, Deneb; 288, 340, 346. Ullage four jet, 14 seconds. [Long pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Roger, Houston. Understand. P30 PAD, Circ. burn, SPS/G&N; 37679; plus 0.49, plus 1.04; 101:38:58.19; plus 0068.3, minus 0000.1, minus 0000.7; 000, 107, 358; 0064.9, plus 0054.3; 0068.3, 0:04, 0057.2; 10, 171.3, 40.0. Vega, Deneb, set stars; 288, 340, 346. Four jet, 14 seconds.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: That's a good readback, Al, and I have an erasable change for you. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Okay, Go ahead.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Verb 21, Noun 01. Address 1765 and Enter 01605. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Understand. Verb 21, Noun 1, Enter, 1765, Enter, 01605, Enter.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: That's affirmative, and that's - a short burn constant change, Al.

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: And, Al. Be advised that your sextant star will be occulted at 101:16 - 7 minutes from now. And a gentle reminder, this is a single bank, bank B burn.

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Rog.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Okay. PDI zero PAD, when both vehicles are ready. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Irwin
a15_1010348.text: Falcon's ready. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Roger, Falcon. And did you get the Circ. GTI [means T IG ]?

a15_1010348.speaker: Irwin
a15_1010348.text: Affirmative, Ed.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Okay. And, Endeavour, you're ready for a PDI zero PAD?

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Endeavour's ready.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Okay. PDI zero. Alpha: 102:39:35.35; Bravo: plus 0100.0, plus all zeros, plus 0001.8; 0138.3, plus 0009.0, 0100.1; 0:34; 000, 273; 0159.6; plus 0100.0, plus all zeros, plus 0002.4; Cocoa: 103:40:24.00; Delta: 105:22:30.00. Readback. [Pause.]

a15_1010348.speaker: Irwin
a15_1010348.text: Okay. Houston, this is Falcon with PDI zero readback. 102:39:35.35; plus 0100.0, plus all zips, plus 0001.8; 0138.3, plus 0009.0, 0100.1; 0:34; 000, 273; 0159.6; plus 0100.0, plus all zips, plus 0002.4; 103:40:24.00, 105:22:30.00. Over.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Good readback, Falcon. And, Al, did you copy?

a15_1010348.speaker: Worden
a15_1010348.text: Endeavour copied.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1010348.text: Roger, Roger.

a15_1010348.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1010348.text: Al Worden has maneuvered the Command Module, Endeavour into the proper attitude now for the circularization burn. That maneuver will be performed near the end of this revolution, after the spacecraft goes behind the Moon, and will place the Command Module in a more or less circular orbit. At the beginning it will be about 64.9 nautical miles by 54.3 [120.2 by 100.6 km] and over the next few days the effects of lunar gravity will modify that orbit so that, at the time Falcon rendezvous with the Command Module, it will be a roughly sixty-mile circular orbit. The maneuver will be performed on the

a15_1011455.speaker: Irwin
a15_1011455.text: Okay, Houston. We'll talk in a minute.

a15_1011455.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1011455.text: And, Falcon; Houston. We copy. Thank you.

a15_1012018.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1012018.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. You're Go for Circ. as soon as you get your short burn constant loaded.

a15_1012018.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1012018.text: And we observed it here. Endeavour.

a15_1012018.speaker: Irwin
a15_1012018.text: Go ahead, Houston. Ready to copy.

a15_1012018.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1012018.text: Okay, Apollo 15, Houston. We're about 1 minute from LOS. We seem to be caught up [with the Flight Plan], and everything is looking good from here.

a15_1012018.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1012018.text: And we've had Loss Of Signal on the 12th revolution. At 101 hours, 38 minutes or about 14 minutes from now, Al Worden will be performing the circularization maneuver in the Command Module Endeavour. This will entail a 4-second burn with the main engine on the Command Module, the SPS engine, placing the CSM in a more or less circular orbit, about 64.9 by 54.3 nautical miles [120.2 by 100.6 km]. This maneuver is performed at the time that it is, in order to put the Command Module in the proper position for any subsequent abort and rendezvous should that become necessary. It's preferable to do a

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Think I'm minus at least one fingernail, though.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Oh, gad. Where did you lose it?

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: On - as a matter of fact, on A-1 when I went after the sextant adapter.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: [Laughter.] That's okay, just a little loose.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: So long as you're not leaking.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: I'm not, no. Okay, I'm all set up for the burn here, I've done P40, done the sextant star check, and everything's looking pretty good. And I've got 14 minutes to go.

a15_1012018.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1012018.text: Coming up on the next revolution, one of the principal activities will be to accomplish - accomplish that landmark tracking which had been scheduled to occur on both revs 12 and 13. This will place added importance on getting the landmark tracking on rev 13, the upcoming revolution. The tracking is performed from the Command Module by Al Worden using the scanning telescope. He'll be taking marks at - on Index Crater near the landing site to improve the knowledge of where the landing site is and also the orbit. And this information is used in updating the Lunar Module guidance system just prior

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Okay, very good. Oh, yes, I wanted to tell you a little bit about the landing site there - on the - on the craters. There's a - Earthlight Crater, of course, is a lot sharper than Index. And then there's a great big one to the east of Index, which is the same size and quite sharp, and I think - you won't have any trouble as long as you see the Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Index. Index is a pretty subtle crater, and there probably won't be much shadow in the bottom of it at all, when you get there.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Yes. Okay. I - I - I know where it is, I think, well enough in location so I can look for the - for the shallow depression.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Okay. Both of those will probably have shadow in them.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: But - gee, they're real super; you can't miss.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Okay, do you want the Noun 81 values for this burn now, or do you want to wait until after?

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Okay, I've gone through the primary gimbal check and turning on number 2 now.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: [Garble] we feel like we're right there with you.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: FDAI scale 5/5. Rate, High, and looks like we're going.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Everything checks fine; 2 minutes and 12 seconds.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Okay. Delta-V Thrust B is On. And B Pilot Valve is closed.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Right with you on the time.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Thrust, Off. What a kick in the tail!

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: You did! Had to see it for myself.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Yes, man. That's like really flying, isn't it?

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Did you get it all in, Al?

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Sure did, Dave. Right down to the gnat.

a15_1012018.speaker: Worden
a15_1012018.text: Sorry about that. I had - only had 9/10ths residual in X and I - I trimmed it out. That short burn constant made it a lot better.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: How about that! We have you in a 65.2 by 54.6.

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Al, how do you read now?

a15_1012018.speaker: Scott
a15_1012018.text: Okay. We had an antenna change called here and sounds like you're pretty good, so we'll just stay with you this way.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Endeavour, Houston. Standing by for your burn status. [Long pause.]

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Endeavour, Houston. Standing by for burn status.

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Hello, Houston. Endeavour. Rog. Stand by one.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Roger. Roger, Al.

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Okay, Houston. The burn got off on time. Burn time, 4 seconds; V GX , minus 0000.9 [fps]; and I trimmed that to 0 at - roll of 0 [degrees], pitch of 107, and yaw of 358. V GX was plus all zero's, V GY was plus all zero's, V GZ was minus 0000.5. Delta-V C was minus 11.2 [fps]; fuel was 29.25 [per cent]; oxidizer, 29.15 [per cent]; and unbalance meter was decreased 50. And I've got me in a 65.2 by 54.8 [nautical mile orbit, 120.7 by 101.4 km].

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Okay, Al. We got everything except the item after the burn time. [Pause.]

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Roger. The V GX at shutdown was minus .9. [repeat] 0.9.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Okay. We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: And, Al. I'm ready to give you a P24 PAD, when you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Okay, Ed. Go ahead.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Rog. 15-1; T-1, 102:37:27; T-2, 42:17; TCA, 43:57; T-3, 44:45. The attitude is nominal, and you'll be off track 3 miles to the north.

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Roger. I understand. [P]24 landmark tracking PAD, tracking 15-1; T-1, 102:37:27; 42:17; 43:57; 44:45. Nominal attitude is off track north 3 miles.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Good readback.

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Rog. [Pause.]

a15_1020803.speaker: Irwin
a15_1020803.text: Ed, I have some AGS Cal numbers for you.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Okay, Falcon. Ready to copy.

a15_1020803.speaker: Irwin
a15_1020803.text: Roger. The initial values: plus 02, minus 04, plus 03, plus 02, plus 90, minus 07. Cal values: plus 02, minus 04, plus 02, plus 21, plus 81, and minus 15.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Copied all of them. [Pause.] Those numbers look good, Falcon.

a15_1020803.speaker: Scott
a15_1020803.text: And, Houston; Falcon. We're ready to go with the DPS.

a15_1020803.speaker: Scott
a15_1020803.text: Okay. And we're ready to go with the DPS pressure checkout any time you are.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Okay. We're ready. Press on.

a15_1020803.speaker: Scott
a15_1020803.text: Roger.

a15_1020803.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1020803.text: Endeavour, Houston. Give us Narrow please on your High Gain [Antenna].

a15_1020803.speaker: Worden
a15_1020803.text: Rog.

a15_1021826.speaker: Scott
a15_1021826.text: Okay, Houston; Falcon. We've done the descent start. The ambient pressure is down to 450 but the manifold pressure hasn't moved. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Stand by. [Pause.] Okay, Falcon. We believe you turned your PQM [Propellant Quantity Monitor] Off, and - and that's your PQGS [Propellant Quantity Gauging System] Off, and - probably your problem - your hed - Helium Monitor. I think you got it inadvertently. [Pause.] And, Endeavour, we'll take P00 and Accept. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Rog. DPS looks good from down here.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1021826.text: The Descent Propulsion System on the Lunar Module is pressurized and looks good at this time.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: And, Falcon; Houston. A couple of items. Dave do you have a warm feel for the LPD decal.

a15_1021826.speaker: Scott
a15_1021826.text: Rog, Ed. It was right on.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Good enough. And we'd like for you to take your Propellant Temp/Press Monitor to Ascent and give us an Ox[idizer] tank read-out, please.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: We copy. Thank you. And, Dave, be advised, there will be no gyro bias updates - or gyro drift updates.

a15_1021826.speaker: Scott
a15_1021826.text: Houston, Falcon. Going into landing radar checkout now.

a15_1021826.speaker: Scott
a15_1021826.text: Altitude Transmitter is 3.6. Velocity Transmitter, 3.8. [Long pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Okay, Endeavour; Houston. Computer is yours, and you can start your maneuver. [Long pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Endeavour, Houston. The computer is yours. You can start your maneuver.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Endeavour, Houston. We're recommending a half a degree per second for your maneuver. You've got quite aways to go.

a15_1021826.speaker: Scott
a15_1021826.text: And, Houston; Falcon. The Landing Radar looks good up here.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Falcon, Houston. If you'll let us have P00 and Data, we have uplink for you.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: And I have PADs for Endeavour and Falcon, when you're both ready. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Okay. Here we go. With Echo, 104:42:30.00; Foxtrot, plus 0108.2, plus all zeros, minus 0050.0; 0144.9, plus 0008.6, 0119.2; 0:36, 000, 270; 0282.5; plus 0108.5, plus all zeros, minus 0049.3; Golf, 107:37:30.00; Hotel, 109:18:45.00. Readback. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Irwin
a15_1021826.text: Okay. Falcon with the readback on no PDI plus 12. 104:42:30.00; plus 0108.2, plus all zips, minus 0050.0; 0144.9, plus 0008.6, 0119.2; 0:36, 000, 270; 0282.5; plus 0108.5, plus all zips, minus 0049.3; 107:37:30.00; and 109:18:45.00.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Okay. You got cut out there. Your AGS Delta-V Z , confirm it's a negative [sign] and [the GET for] Hotel [is] 109:18:45.00. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Okay. Endeavour, give us Omni Charlie, please. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Roger. And did you get the readbacks, Al?

a15_1021826.speaker: Worden
a15_1021826.text: Endeavour copied them - copied the PADs. Rog.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Okay. The T-2 time is at 20:39. [Pause.]

a15_1021826.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1021826.text: The Flight Activities Officer [FAO] reports that Al Worden in Endeavour is nearly in the proper attitude for the landmark tracking. That's scheduled to begin in about 8 or 9 minutes from now. The landmark will first come into view over the horizon at 102 hours, 37 minutes, 27 seconds. And it will be about 4 or 5 minutes after that before Worden actually begins taking marks on the landmark.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1021826.text: Reviewing our status briefly, we've nearly completed the systems checkouts on the Lunar Module. Everything appears to be in order at the moment both with the LM and the Command Module for the powered descent, which will occur on the next revolution, 14th revolution. And we're standing by now for the landmark tracking which Al Worden will perform from the Command Module Endeavour.

a15_1021826.speaker: Worden
a15_1021826.text: Roger, Ed. Just checking over this P24 PAD again. And you didn't update the longitude over 2 on this one. Did you want to do that?

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Stand by. [Pause.] Negative, Al. Go with the one in the Flight Plan.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Roger. Check your CO 2 Sensor circuit breaker. We're showing off-scale low.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1021826.text: Endeavour, standby for T-1 minus 30 seconds.

a15_1021826.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1021826.text: T-1 is the time at which the landing site landmark will first appear on the horizon.

a15_1024119.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1024119.text: Flight Activities Officer [FAO] reports that Worden has begun taking marks and we're seeing those here on our data displays here in the Control Center. We'll get a qualitative assessment from Worden following the landmark tracking.

a15_1024119.speaker: Worden
a15_1024119.text: Okay, Houston. It's out of sight.

a15_1024119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1024119.text: Roger, Endeavour. How did you feel about them, Al?

a15_1024119.speaker: Worden
a15_1024119.text: Oh, I felt good about them, Ed. Right on.

a15_1024119.speaker: Worden
a15_1024119.text: No question about the landmark. And every mark, I had the - the crater centered, Crater Index.

a15_1024119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1024119.text: Very, very good. Thank you. And I have an update to the PDI abort PAD, when Endeavour and Falcon are ready. [Long pause.]

a15_1024119.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1024119.text: Okay. It's item Kilo. Should be 107:20:30.00. [Pause.]

a15_1024119.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1024119.text: The Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] has confirmed Al Worden's assessment of the landmark tracking. He reports that we appear to have gotten sufficient information from the landmark tracking to update the location of the landing site, and this would appear to clear the way for carrying out the landing on the planned revolution on the next rev. We'll be giving a Go for the powered descent on reacquiring at the beginning of the 14th revolution. The Command Module, Endeavour, now in a more or less circular orbit. Al Worden reported that the onboard computations of the orbit following the circulariz

a15_1025406.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1025406.text: Let's see if you can reach Endeavour and ask him to bring the High Gain [Antenna] up. Flight Plan angles, please. Minus 69 and 114. [Pause.]

a15_1025406.speaker: Irwin
a15_1025406.text: Roger. Endeavour, this is Falcon. How do you read? [Pause.] Roger. Houston would like you to bring up the High Gain [Antenna] to a minus 69 and a 114.

a15_1025924.speaker: Scott
a15_1025924.text: Houston, Falcon. Do you have the torquing angles?

a15_1025924.speaker: Worden
a15_1025924.text: Houston, Endeavour's up on High Gain.

a15_1025924.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1025924.text: And, Endeavour, we copy your Noun 93s.

a15_1025924.speaker: Worden
a15_1025924.text: Okay, Ed. And I'll torque them out on the minute.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay, Houston; Falcon. How's the P63 look?

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Okay, Dave. It looks very good. Time's okay. And be advised, both Endeavour and Falcon, that the P24 looked good. There will be an update, but we feel very confident about it. [Pause.]

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay, Falcon here. Very good.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: And, Falcon, we'd like to see a Verb 47 down to the AGS, please. And be advised that your platform, both gyros and PIPA [Pulsed Integrating Pendulous Accelerometers]'s, are [in] good shape. No updates to them.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Very good. [Long pause.]

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Houston, Falcon. While that's running through there, we're going back through notes, checking over the activation. And one thing we missed there was, just before undocking, we ran the suit pressure integrity check, and the first time around, we got a greater than 3/10ths decrease in one minute. So we cycled through both regulators, did that test, and came back and ran the suit integrity check again, and it was just fine. It was about 1/10th in a minute.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Okay, Falcon. We copy that. Thank you.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Falcon, Houston.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Houston, Falcon. Go.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Rog, Dave. Talk about reviewing notes, we did so, also, and we found one we'd like to pass to you before LOS.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Dave, we - working out a procedure down here that we simmed [that is, ran in the simulator], and it's in the event of a low thrusting DPS during PDI. We're prepared to call to you - an RCS thrust augmentation for one minute, at about one minute or a minute and a half into the burn. And recommend doing it on the LMP's TTCA [Thrust/Translational Control Assembly], if we have to do it at all. What do you think?

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: That's fine. We'll try that if we need it.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Okay, the procedures are very simple. We'll call it to you as we've measured the thrust.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay. And I guess you'll call "On" and call "Off" with the TTCA, is that correct?

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: We can. That'll just be a one minute - a one minute burst.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Okay, fine. And by the way, when we went by PD - PDI-0, we took a couple of hacks at the altitude. It showed 10 [nautical] miles even.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Very good.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1030938.text: We're about three minutes away now from loss of radio contact with the Lunar Module. However we won't be losing contact with the Command Module due to its higher orbit for about 7 minutes - 7½ minutes. The contingency procedure which Ed Mitchell passed up to Dave Scott related to the use of the Reaction Control System thrusters on the Lunar Module in the unlikely event that the LM descent engine is significantly below normal in thrust. Normally that engine should produce about 9,900 pounds of thrust. If the thrust level should be about 260 pounds low or more, it would be possible to mak

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Falcon, Houston. You're about a minute and 40 seconds from LOS. We'd like to see your 400 plus 30000 before LOS.

a15_1030938.speaker: Irwin
a15_1030938.text: Rog. In work.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1030938.text: We're about 1 minute now from Loss Of Signal with the Lunar Module. And would like to reemphasize that that technique for using the Reaction Control System thrusters is a backup technique. The normal procedure would be to use only the Descent Propulsion System for the braking required for the landing. The Reaction Control System thrusters would be used solely for attitude control. And in the unlikely event that we have a low thrust engine once we turn on the Descent Propulsion System, then we'll have up the sleeve the possibility of using the Reaction Control System thrusters.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1030938.text: Falcon, Houston. LOS in 30 seconds.

a15_1030938.speaker: Scott
a15_1030938.text: Roger, Houston; Falcon. All set.

a15_1030938.speaker: Worden
a15_1030938.text: Omni Delta...

a15_1030938.speaker: Worden
a15_1030938.text: Endeavour; Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1030938.speaker: Worden
a15_1030938.text: Okay.

a15_1030938.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1030938.text: We've had Loss Of Signal with the Lunar Module, Falcon. We're getting weak signal strength from the Command Module, although we do have about 3 minutes left before we lose radio contact with Endeavour. And as Falcon went around the corner behind the Moon, we were showing the Lunar Module in an orbit, 60.6 [nautical miles, 112.2 km] at its high point; 60.6 nautical miles, and with a low point of 8.5 nautical miles [15.7 km] above the lunar surface.

a15_1031940.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1031940.text: Rog, Al. Your a minute from LOS. We recommend, on the next pass, check your S-Band Squelch Switch, Off.

a15_1031940.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1031940.text: And, we've had Loss Of Signal now with the Command Module. When next we reacquire the Lunar Module, Falcon, will be about 25 minutes away from the scheduled time of the powered descent, the beginning of the powered descent to the lunar surface. And as both spacecraft went around the corner, everything appeared to be normal. At this point we see nothing that would interfere with a normal landing. We'll be getting the - taking a final look at the status of the trajectory in both spacecraft on reacquiring, and at that time a decision for the powered decent will be made. However, as we say at the

a15_1031940.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1031940.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about 4 minutes from reacquiring the Lunar Module Falcon , now on its 14th revolution of the Moon. On reacquisition of the Lunar Module, the crew will be in final preparations for the powered descent. The Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] reported that results of the landmark tracking were all satisfactory. And we're, as far as the trajectory is concerned, in good shape for the powered descent. We will have to steer out about 3.3 miles - nautical miles of cross-range error and this will be taken into account in the targeting for the powered descent. I would like

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Roger, Falcon. We're ready for your Ascent Bat On time and your ED Bat report. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Roger, Ed. The Ascent Bats were On at 103:50:45, and I'll check the ED Bats now. [Long pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: And, Houston, this is Falcon. ED batteries both check at 37 volts.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Copy; 37 volts. And I have an update to your PDI PAD. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: And, Falcon, give us P00 and Data, and we'll give you an uplink. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: P00 and Data. Go ahead with the PAD.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Ed, if you're reading us, you ought to call us after the - the uplink. We cannot read you.

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Here it comes; don't change it. It's coming in.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Falcon, Houston. How do you read now?

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Read you loud and clear, Ed. I'm ready for that update now.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Roger. India: 104:30:08.54; Noun 61 crossrange, plus 0003.3; DEDA 231, plus 56943. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Readback is correct, and be advised that crossrange number means you're going from south to north. You'll probably see some roll during the PDI.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Okay, your T - your Throttle in min? Okay. Throttle, min.

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Check DPS, APS, RCS, ECS, EPS. Okay?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mission Control
a15a1040100.text: We're coming up now on 20 minutes until ignition for the powered descent. The landing point for Apollo 15, in a plains area boxed in by mountains on one side, actually on two sides and a rille on the third side. We'll put Falcon down about 1 mile from the Hadley Rille. They'll be coming in about 2 miles to the south, rather to the north of the point where Hadley Delta begins to rise abruptly to an altitude of about 13,000 feet above the landing site, and approximately 6 miles behind their approach path, about 6 miles from the touch down point to the east, the Apennine Front itself begins to ri

a15a1040100.speaker: Mission Control
a15a1040100.text: And here in Mission Control, we've switched over from the large display of the lunar surface that we've had up on our front plot board since going into lunar orbit. We now have the analog displays which will tell the Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] how well the descent trajectory is progressing and includes abort lines that will tell him if any of the parameters or the characteristics of the trajectory are approaching unsafe limits.

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Did you check the RCS? Okay. ECS look all right?

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: If we should be up-linked, Dave, I'll need a - Verb 47.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mission Control
a15a1040100.text: And our Instrumentation and Communications Engineer reports that we should have lock on now with Endeavour . Al Worden in the Command Module.

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Okay. Looks like I just screwed. Okay.

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. You're on the scan limit. Go to Reacq when you're at the angles. [No answer.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Irwin
a15a1040100.text: Get - I think we Enable on the - S-Band?

a15a1040100.speaker: Scott
a15a1040100.text: Okay. Houston, how do you read Falcon?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. How do you read?

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Roger, Endeavour. I have an update for the PDI PAD, India. [Pause.]

a15a1040100.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1040100.text: Endeavour, Houston. We're ready for Auto on the High Gain [Antenna] please.

a15_1041842.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1041842.text: Roger. We did not see the 231 load go in. Can you verify that, please? [Pause.]

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: There's the readout. I didn't put the 231 in. You want that also, Ed?

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: We're coming up now on 10 minutes until the beginning of this 12-minute powered burn to the lunar surface. At the initiation of this maneuver, the Command Module Endeavour will be about 350 nautical miles [650 km] behind the Lunar Module. The Command Module will pass overhead at just about the time the Lunar Module is touching down. Aboard the Lunar Module Falcon the crew has completed updating their backup guidance system with the same information that has been loaded into the Primary Guidance [and Navigation] System.

a15_1041842.speaker: Scott
a15_1041842.text: Hey, Houston, Falcon on Vox. How do you read?

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: And the crew has now switched on the guidance program - program 63 which will guide the Lunar Module during the initial portion of the power descent, the principal braking phase.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay; you ready for the DPS configuration card?

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay; CBs on 11. DECA Gimbal AC, Closed.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Command Override logic is Closed. Att Control circuit breakers, all Closed, except AEA, Open.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Okay. The throttle, Yours to Min and mine to Soft Stop.

a15_1041842.speaker: Scott
a15_1041842.text: Soft stop. And you're - you're clipping a little bit on the first part, Jim.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: We're down here where I can take a Verb 40, Noun 20.

a15_1041842.speaker: Irwin
a15_1041842.text: Stand by for 5 minutes [to PDI ignition].

a15_1041842.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1041842.text: A last look at the Lunar Module orbit showed it to be in an orbit with a high point of 60.6 nautical miles [112.2 km] and a low point of about 8.1 nautical miles [15.0 km]. The Command Module Endeavour , that was in an orbit of 64.6 by 53.8 [nautical miles, 119.6 by 99.6 km]. And we're now coming up on about 6 minutes prior to the beginning of the powered descent. Everything continuing to progress very smoothly, and rather quietly here in Mission Control at the moment.

a15_1042352.speaker: Irwin
a15_1042352.text: [Garble, may be landing radar] breaker is in. Altitude transmitter.

a15_1042352.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1042352.text: Flight Director Glynn Lunney, at this moment getting a final status for powered descent.

a15_1042352.speaker: Scott
a15_1042352.text: Okay. Go for the final trim.

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: And, Falcon, you are Go for PDI.

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: And, Falcon, you are Go for PDI (Powered Descent Initiation).

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Go for PDI.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Go for PDI. (Long Pause) [Stephen Tellier has provided a pre-mission illustration of the planned LM ground track from PDI to landing ( 2.9 Mb or 640k ).]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (Garbled)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Endeavour, how do you read the Falcon?

a15a1042610.speaker: Worden
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour. Reading you loud and clear there, Dave. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Endeavour, Falcon. If you're reading, we're not reading you.

a15a1042610.speaker: Worden
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour. How do you read? (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Endeavour's reading you loud and clear.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay; fine. Thank you. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Stand by for 1 minute.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (The readings) on our oxidizer...They're low, aren't they?

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Yeah. [In Houston, the knowledgeable Flight Controller tells the Flight Director that this condition is normal prior to the ullage burn described below. The readings will rise to normal values after the PDI burn starts.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (Garbled) cycle the cir(cuit breaker). [Journal Contributor Frank O'Brien notes, "Jim is probably referring to the Propellant Quantity Measurement Device (PQMD) circuit breaker. His suggestion to 'cycle the breaker' - which means turning power to the system off, and then back on - is intended to reset the PQMD, with the hope that a more 'normal' reading will result."]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: No. That's all right. Be accurate later on. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Houston, we're reading 87 and 85 on the Fuel Quantity (gauge).

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Roger. Roger. It'll come up here in a moment. (Pause) It looks good to us, Jim.

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Mark. One minute. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Master Arm's On; I have two (pyrotechnic system) lights. (Long Pause) [With the Master Arm switch On, Dave will be able to fire the small explosive charges that open the valves connecting the helium pressurization system to the tanks holding the descent stage oxidizer and propellant.] [David Woods has released an annotated version of the DAC (16-mm film) footage that includes the air-to-ground audio and transcript plus commentary. Synchronization is superb, of course. Available on YouTube 16:14 .]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Average G . Armed the Descent (engine). We have guidance.

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: (Standing) by for ullage.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Standing by for ullage. (Long Pause) [In normal usage, 'ullage' is the empty portion of a cask. Here, the word is used to denote a brief firing of the LM's steering jets against the LM's orbital motion. This brief firing of the Reaction Control System (RCS) will provide enough acceleration to separate the propellant in the tanks from the helium that provides tank pressure. The ullage burn settles the propellant to the bottom of the tank next to the exit ports so that the heavier propellant - and not the lighter helium - flows through the valve at engine ignition. The LM computer will perform t

a15a1042610.speaker: LM Crew
a15a1042610.text: Ullage.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Go for the Pro. Pro. [Next, they will tell the computer to continue execution of the program that will fire the descent engine and control the descent down to an altitude of about 7000 feet (2.1 km). Other programs were then run to provide guidance from there to the surface.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Pro-ing. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Auto ignition. (Pause) Eleven percent (throttle); the (Descent Engine Command) Override is On. (Long Pause) [O'Brien - "The Descent Engine Command Override, as the name implies, allows the crew to override the computer's commanded thrust level of the descent engine. The Thrust/Translational Handcontroller, which is at Dave's left hand, is used to adjust the engine thrust. For the first 26 seconds, the engine fires at about ten percent of maximum thrust so that the guidance system can gimbal the descent engine to point through the LM's center-of-gravity. This procedure must be completed before

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Throttle up. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Master Arm, Off. [O'Brien - "I'm still trying to determine why the Master Arm was always turned off after a few seconds into an engine burn. I know it has to do with computer-initiated engine shutdown, but it doesn't completely make sense. Pete Conrad forgot to turn it off during the Apollo 12 ascent, and had to shut down the engine manually, resulting in a ~1.5 second overburn."]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. Master Arm is coming Off. Lights are Off. Looks stable.

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: H-dot 's looking a little higher than normal.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. We're a little higher than normal. (Pause) [They have begun the burn at a slightly higher than planned altitude and, to compensate, the computer is giving them a descent rate slightly greater than planned. H is altitude and H-dot is the rate-of-change of altitude (descent rate), that is, the time derivative. Jim is consulting a table in the LM Timeline Book which shows the planned altitude and descent rate at various times during the burn and is comparing those figures with the computer displays of the Primary Guidance and Navigation System (PGNS) computer and the Abort Guidance System (

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: One minute (into the burn). H-dot's about 20 (feet per second) high.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay.

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: Fuel is a little low; oxidizer is a little high. (Pause)

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Houston. A (Noun) 169: minus 02800. [This is a guidance update - based on Earth based tracking - to correct for about a 2800 foot undershoot of the planned landing site.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger, minus 02800. Standing by for the Enter. [Journal Contributor Paul Fjeld notes that the ability to update the LM targeting "was added on Apollo 12. DLAND - Noun 69 - was an unusual vector! It was added to the Position of the landing site (RLS) every 2-second cycle, then zeroed. The crew had to verify that the three registers were all balls (all zero), then only put the Delta Z value (downrange change in position) in R1, then only press enter when MCC looked at the DSKY downlist to verify that the number was good. A bad Noun 69 was an easy way for the crew to mess up the landing."]

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: You're Go for Enter.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Go for Enter. (Long Pause) [Houston can watch them do the keyboard entry of the update and is confirming that they have entered the correct data. By punching the Enter button, Dave and Jim are telling the PGNS to incorporate the keyboard entry into memory. While Dave types the entry, Jim watches him do it and, in effect, they have a triple check of all entries into the computer.] [In Houston, the Flight Director polls the Flight Controllers and confirms that LM performance is as expected.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Houston. You're Go at 2 minutes.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Roger, Go at 2. PGNS and AGS compare. [The PGNS and AGS use independent sensing systems to determine the trajectory and the fact that they agree is reassuring to all concerned.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: H-dot's a little high. We're about 2 percent low on fuel.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
a15a1042610.text: Okay. [Journal Contributor Paul Fjeld - "Up on the CDR's main panel beside the timers were two small digital EL (Electro-Luminescent) displays that showed fuel and oxidizer percent remaining. The crew could monitor either set of tanks by pushing the PRPLNT QTY MON switch to DES 1 or DES 2 depending on which was more conservative (Houston would make the call)." Here, Jim is comparing the number he sees on the panel with a chart of values expected at various times during the descent.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: At one (minute). (Long Pause) [In Houston, Ed Mitchell requests permission to tell the crew that the Flight Controllers believe that the fuel quantities are actually normal.]

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Fal...

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: 3 (garbled) good...

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Houston. We're...

a15a1042610.speaker: Irwin
a15a1042610.text: H-dot's 4 (feet per second) high.

a15a1042610.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1042610.text: Falcon, Houston. We're happy with your fuel.

a15a1042610.speaker: Scott
