a15a1161913.text: Roger. We copy. [Comm Break] [The water tank percentages that Parker read up were the gauge readings, rather than the actual values. Jim is implying that he expected a read-up of the actual values.] [Scott- "On board, the reading is from a dial or a gauge. The gauge was probably put in a couple of years before the flight. And there are some divergences in those kinds of systems, so they have to be calibrated. And what you try to do is get it so that your apples and oranges are all apples and mean the same thing."]

a15a1161913.speaker: Parker
a15a1161913.text: Okay, Hadley; this is Houston. The actual on-board figures - not the gauge figures that you'll read, but the actual onboard figures for water - are, descent 1, 70.7 and tank 2, 68.5. Over.

a15a1161913.text: Rog; we copy that. Thank you. a15a1172236.text: Roger, Dave; that sounds good to us. We'll be watching.

a15a1172236.text: Okay, Houston. It looks like it's still with us.

a15a1172236.text: Roger, Dave. That's good news. [Very Long Comm Break. It's not the fun part of getting out, but it's a necessity. It's real hard work. Boy, wh

a15a1172236.speaker: Scott
a15a1172236.text: Houston, Hadley Base.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Falcon, Houston. Apparently, Jim's data is not very clean, and we're not getting your data at all, Dave. Other than that, it looks beautiful. [Irwin - "Joe always does a great job. See this? 'Apparently Jim's data is not clean, and we're not getting your data at all. Other than that, it looks beautiful.' (Both laugh)"]

a15a1172236.text: Well, I guess I don't mean right now, because you shouldn't be getting any data right now. (Pause)

a15a1172236.text: Stand by. a15a1172236.text: As a matter of fact, while the good surgeons are thinking that one out, Jim's going to plug in through the suit now, and you can check it out.

a15a1172236.text: Rog, Dave. That sounds good, and we'll be watching. (Long Pause) [Without putting his suit on, Jim can connect his biomed sensors to the suit electrical circuitry and, thereby, to the telemetry stream so that the flight surgeon can judge the quality of the signal.]

a15a1172236.text: Okay. You should be receiving it, and we'd appreciate a call as soon as you can verify it's good. (Pause)

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Dave, it looks real good to us.

a15a1172236.speaker: Scott
a15a1172236.text: Okay, thank you. And I'll let you take a look at mine as soon as I get to the suit part.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger. [Long Comm Break]

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Jim, this is Houston. Verify for us, please, that your biomed data is unplugged now.

a15a1172236.speaker: Scott
a15a1172236.text: Well, he's off the headset, Joe; but, yeah, it's unplugged. We're getting him into the suit.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger. Thank you. (Pause)

a15a1172236.speaker: Scott
a15a1172236.text: What we'll do is get all hooked up to the suit, and then let you check it out, and then climb into the suit, just to make sure.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Sounds good, Dave. We'll be standing by. [Comm Break. Jim's next transmission indicates that he is in his suit and that they will soon start to get Dave suited.]

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: Joe, how do you read? I'm back on comm.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger, Jim. Loud and clear.

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: You're the same. [Comm Break]

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: And, Joe, looking at a battery management change at about 118:05 (on checklist page 2-11). Should we do it on that time?

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Stand by, Jim. I'll be right back with you.

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Falcon, regarding your question on battery management, we would like you to do it per the checklist on the time listed there, please.

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: We understand. [Very Long Comm Break] [The NASA Public Affairs commentator reports to the press that Jim Irwin's heart rate at 79 and Dave Scott's about 60.] [The battery management procedures involve taking some batteries off-line and putting others on-line in order to have even usage during the course of the surface operations. The procedures here on Surface 2-11 can be compared with the set they will perform after the EVA on Surface 5-3.]

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: Houston, this is Hadley Base. Will you check the Commander's biomed?

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger, Jim. Dave's EKG (electro-cardiogram) data looks clean as a whistle.

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: Very good. He's going to complete the suiting-up.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger.

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: And I'll get to the batteries shortly.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger. [Long Comm Break]

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: Okay, Joe. I'm going to press on with the battery management now.

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger, Jim. (Pause)

a15a1172236.speaker: Irwin
a15a1172236.text: And both ED batteries check at 37 (volts).

a15a1172236.speaker: Allen
a15a1172236.text: Roger. [Comm Break] [Jones - "What are the ED batteries?"] [Irwin - "Explosive Detonation? They were the batteries that provided power for the charges that would cause staging...(correcting himself) not staging, but fire pyrotechnics to separate the stages. We never drew power off of them. They were reserved just for that function. They were for the Explosive Devices, that's what it is."]

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: Alfredo, Houston is calling. How are you doing up there? [Pause.]

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1184816csm.text: Good morning, Houston; this is Endeavour. Doing - doing fine. Reading you loud and clear.

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: Glad to hear from you, Endeavour. We'd like to have Accept, when you have a chance to reach up that direction.

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: Roger. And down on panel 230, Mass Spectrometer, Multiplier, High, at your convenience. [Pause.]

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: Thank you. And, I've got that batch of updates there, whenever you can copy.

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: Al, on that mass spectrograph, we want the Multiplier, High and the Discriminator, Low.

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1184816csm.text: Okay; understand. Multiplier, High, and Discriminator, Low.

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: That's - that's the right way, yeah. [Long pause.]

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: And, if you can reach up to the panel 3 there, we'd like the High Gain [Antenna], Auto, at your convenience. [Pause.]

a15_1184816csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1184816csm.text: And, Al, the computer is yours at anytime.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay, Houston. This is Endeavour. I'm ready to copy some updates there, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Hello, Houston, Endeavour.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The first thing we'd like get through to you are the Mapping Camera photo PADs over on the next page at 119:30.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay, Karl. Go ahead.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: "Start: 119:34:33; stop: 121:33:02." And a note to that is that the - the - the extend/retract times on the Mapping Camera seem to be getting longer with time, and, until further notice, we'd like for you to record and send down the Delta-T on each extend and retract.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay; understand. Yes, those times do seem to be getting longer, and I'll record the Delta-T and tell you what they are.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Roger. And, over there at 119:20, on the mass spectrometer boom retract, it says "record the retract time Delta-T." Instead of "in barber pole," we want all of these in the future "from switch on to gray." That corresponds to what we can monitor here on the ground, and we - we need to - we need to calibrate - comparison of your data and ours. I'm sorry; that's not what we monitor, but this is - this is - this is...

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Roger. Instead you want that "switch on to gray."

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Right. That compares with our test calibration data, that's what I should say. And while I'm reading up...

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: ...while I'm reading up to you, I'd also like to get something in on the ECS [Environmental Control System] radiators, the outlet temperature is running high 10 to 15 degrees [Fahrenheit], primary radiator outlet temperature. And we like for you to verify, first of all, that Flow Control on the ECS Radiators is Auto and Power. Is that the way they're setting?

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: That's verified. Auto and Power.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay. And three circuit breakers over on panel 5, ECS Radiators, Controller, AC1 and AC2 should be closed, and, also Controller Heaters, Main A should be closed. All three closed.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Yes, that's verified. They're all closed.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay; thank you. You got a status report to send down to us?

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Okay. Got about 5 and a half to 6 hours of sleep in 2 segments. My PRD [Personal Radiation Dosimeter] is reading 23105, but I'm not sure that's any good. And no medication, and standing by for a consumables update, and the rest of it.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: Roger. Consumables update. Are you ready?

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Rog. Go ahead.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1185456csm.text: The time is 118:00; RCS total is sixty - is 63 [percent]; quad A, 63; 64; 61; 64; H 2 tank 1, 76.9; 75.6; 51.9; O 2 tank 1, 79.3; 87 - 82.5; 61.7.

a15_1185456csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1185456csm.text: Roger on the consumables.

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1190320csm.text: Al, if you can listen while you work, I got a couple of short goodies for you before you go round the corner. First of all, the experimenters on the SIM bay are as happy as can be. I think on the Gamma-ray experiment, they say on that first rev data, they have enough to justify the whole flight; they're so happy with it. I have a more complete science report for you, which I will send up on the next rev. And just bringing you up to date on the news, the egress down on the surface will be beginning on schedule in just about one hour.

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1190320csm.text: Hey, that all sounds real good, Karl. And, as you can see, I'm right in the middle of a P52 here. I'll have the second star and the gyro torquing angles in just a second.

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1190320csm.text: And if you've got those torquing angles, I'll get them on the minute. [Pause.]

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1190320csm.text: We don't have any CMC data at the present time. You'll have to read them down to us, Al.

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1190320csm.text: Okay, Karl. I'll read them to you. P52: the stars were 01 and 36. The torquing angles were minus 3 balls 28; minus 3 balls 58; plus 3 balls 12; and they were torqued out at 119:05 on the minute.

a15_1190320csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1190320csm.text: We copy all of that. Loud and clear. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: (Burst of static) Okay, Houston; Hadley Base. We're ready to go into a PLSS comm check, if you're ready. (Static clears)

a15a1190546.speaker: Henize
a15a1190546.text: And as you go around the corner Al, all your systems are looking good.

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Roger, Dave. We read you about 3 by. [Scott - "Five-by-five means 'loud and clear'."] [Jones - "So Joe is saying it's a little faint and muddy."] [The fact that they are using aviation terminology generated the following discussion.] [Scott - "A lot of what we did, as you can see, was based on aircraft operations - which is one of the keys to the success of Apollo. When they started it, they brought in a lot of people who had aircraft operations and hardware experience. The group from Langley that formed NASA from NACA and the group from Langley that moved to Houston were all from the airplane

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Stand by until I get a go-ahead from INCO here.

a15a1190546.speaker: Worden
a15a1190546.text: Roger, Karl. Thank you. See you on the other side.

a15a1190546.speaker: Henize
a15a1190546.text: Roger.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: (Clear comm) Okay. (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Okay, Dave. We're go on the FM and high power. We've got it down here.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. We'll be talking to you. [Comm Break]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: (Reading Surface 3-7 at the bottom of the left-hand column) (sensitivity) VOX Max. VHF A to T/R; B to Receive. Okay. CB(16) Comm: SE Audio, open, and you connect to the PLSS comm. (Long Pause) [In this section of the audio tape, there are definite instances of words and/or parts of words not picked up due to slow VOX activation, also called clipping. This is a sensitivity problem that plagued Buzz Aldrin throughout the Apollo 11 EVA. Here, the problem will disappear shortly and, on the whole, the comm will be the best received from any crew while suited in the LM.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay, CB(16) Comm: SE Audio, close. PLSS PTT (Push-to-Talk) ... Maintain right, verify. Okay, PLSS mode, A, wheel counter-clockwise.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: (Some interference) ... mode A. And wheel is full counter-clockwise.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. Tone-on, vent flag P, Press flag O, O2 momentary.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay; they're on.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. PLSS O2 pressure gauge greater than 85 (percent).

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Verified.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. You've made your comm check with me. Give Houston a call.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Houston, how do you read the LMP?

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Jim, you're loud and clear. There's a squeal in the background.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Roger. I have that squeal, also. (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Jim, stand by; we'll...(Stops to listen)

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I'll turn the squelch down a little bit to see if that...

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Roger. And, Jim, stand by; we're thinking about that tone a minute here...(correcting himself) about the squeal in the background.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay. I'm standing by. (Long Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Jim, this is Houston. Could you turn your volume down a little bit for us, please? (Pause) And that's volume on the wheel.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay. The volume's down now.

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: That's...

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay. It's down about three quarters of the way. How do you read now?

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Jim, that's beautiful. The squeal's gone and you're 5 by. (Pause) And we're ready to go to the next step.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay; very good.

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Rog. We're ready to go to the next step.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. CB(11) Comm: CDR Audio, open. [Comm Break, as they get Dave off of LM comm and on to PLSS comm.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. I have a tone-on, vent flag P and pressure flag O. O2 pressure gauge is reading about 94 percent. And, how do you read me, Jim?

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I read you loud and clear.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. You need to make a comm check with Houston then.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Houston, how do you read the LMP?

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Jim, you're 5 by. (Pause) And, Dave, you're 5 by. Sounds beautiful.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: You're the same.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: (Garbled) he can't (clipped) talk to me.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Understand. [As is mentioned on Surface 3-8, in the current configuration Houston can hear both Dave and Jim, and they can hear each other, but Dave cannot hear Houston. Note that, while Dave and Jim are wearing the Snoopy headsets, which muffle all sounds but those coming through the earpieces, they have not yet donned their bubble helmets and, obviously, could talk even if the headsets weren't connected.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. PLSS mode LMP to...Now you won't be able to hear Houston.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Yeah.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: PLSS mode, LMP to B and CDR to A.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: (Garbled) on B.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. I'm in A; how do you read?

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I read you loud and clear, Dave.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay; I read you loud and clear. Houston, how do you read the CDR?

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Dave, you're 5 by; and Jim's 5 by. 119:13:07 Scott: Okay. PLSS mode, both, to AR, tone-on. [Short whistle]

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay; I'm AR.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay; I'm AR, and you're loud and clear to me. How me to you? [The comm quality is now excellent.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Same.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay, Houston. How do you read the CDR?

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Dave, you're loud and clear.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. And we need a TM (telemetry) check with you, and O2 quantity on the CDR is 94, and give them yours, Jim.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay, I'm reading about 92.

a15a1190546.speaker: Allen
a15a1190546.text: Roger. We copy. (Pause) And, Falcon, the data looks good. We have the TM check. [Here, they have made sure that Houston is seeing the same oxygen quantities that they are seeing on their suit gauges.] 119:13:48 Scott: Okay. CB(16) ECS: LCG Pump (circuit breaker), closed. (Responding to Joe) Okay. Understand, a good TM check. Good. [This is one of only a few occasions when there is any noticeable effect of the 2.5 second -two-way communications delay on the flow of information between Joe and the Falcon crew.] [Scott - "When Joe pauses, the delay gets us. Because he'll say something, and he'll

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay. LCG Pump going closed, now.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. I hear the pump. (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. LCG cold as required.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I feel it already. It feels good.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Yes. It sure does, doesn't it? [They are circulating LM water through the Liquid Cooled Garments, cooling down prior to disconnecting the LM water hoses. They won't be able to operate the PLSS cooling system until the cabin has been depressurized.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. CB(16) ECS: Cabin Repress, close; verify.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Verified.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Suit Fan Delta-P, open.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Open. [Here, they are disabling a sensor which detects a pressure difference across the fans in the ECS when the fans are operating.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: SUIT Fan 2, open.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Open. [Here, they are turning the fans off.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Suit Fan, select number 2, and I'll get that. (Pause) ECS caution, H2O Sep Component lights on. (Pause) [With the fan now off, the water separator slows to a stop and warning light comes on after about a minute. This is primarily a convenient check to make sure the sensor is working.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. And I've got a Press flag O and a vent flag P.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Same here. [These flags are telling them that the PLSS fans are not yet turned on and, as with the LM warning system, that the PLSS warning system is working. Next, they will verify that the ECS is still in the proper configuration for cabin depressurization.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. It's gone. Okay. ECS caution lights are (still) out. (Pause) Okay. Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Pull Egress; verify.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: That's verified.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. Cabin Gas Return (Valve) to Egress; verify.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Suit Circuit Relief (Valve), verify?

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: That's verified.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Okay. OPS connect (as per Surface 3-9). (Pause) Suit Isolation (Valve) to Suit Disconnect. And disconnect the LM O2 hoses; and secure that to PGA. (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay. Dave, let's take those one at a time.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Oop. We got a Master Alarm. See what it is.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I think it's just the second one on the fan. ECS. Let's see. Water Sep (which has finally slowed down enough to trip the sensor). 119:15:34 Allen: [Over a garbled crew exchange] Guys, it looks okay. It's a Water Sep light.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Yeah. Read those next steps there, Dave. I didn't...One at a time

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Yeah, okay. (Pause) "Connect the OPS O2 hose to the PGA, blue to blue." [Next, they will connect Jim's OPS hose to the appropriate connector on the front of his suit.]

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Okay; let me find that. I might have to turn around and let you do that.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Yeah, I can get it. Here. (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: That is verified.

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: In fact...

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Yeah, why don't you turn around?

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Yeah. (Garbled) (Pause)

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Hey, that's pretty good cooling. Isn't it?

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Beautiful.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: You had enough? [They both laugh]

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: I'll turn this (garbled) up. Yeah, we'll need it. We ought to cool down as much as we can (before disconnecting from LM water).

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Scott - "We've talked about how good the LCG was and how cool it kept us. In fact, it would freeze you. We never got hot. And we were never on max cooling. I mean, that was a great suit."] [Jones - "And what you're doing here is running LM water through the LCG because, once you disconnect from LM water, it's going to be a while before you can hook up to the PLSS and get the hatch open."] [Scott - "Yeah. And the basic concept of a liquid-cooled garment is another excellent piece of an optimum approach to lunar operations."] [We then discussed the air-cooling system that was used

a15a1190546.speaker: Irwin
a15a1190546.text: Wait.

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott
a15a1190546.text: Am I hooked? (Pause) 119:16:30 Irwin: Yeah. Here, let me get it. Your hooked on the handle for the PLSS. Can you get down a little bit? (Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "We started having some problems hanging up in the cabin. I think that they were magnified by the one-sixth-g environment because we didn't compress the suits as much as in one g, and I think we were both riding a little bit higher, and a little lighter. Turn-arounds within the cabin were very difficult, and my hang-up problems were on the mounting lever, or shaft, that holds the PLSS in the recharge station. J

a15a1190546.speaker: Scott

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. Looks like we must have just run across a little funny there, Karl, because it started okay now and is running.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: And back to intermediate (cooling), Joe.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Roger, Dave. (Long Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Roger. Do you have a time source, or would you like a hack down here to get it started again, on the right number?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: I used the CMC time.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: You want both LRV battery covers open, is that correct?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: That's affirm. (Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) There's one open. (Long Pause) (Won't) stay open! Hmmm. (Long Pause) There. Oooh, me! They're open. (Pause) [Jones - "Am I right in assuming that this flight Rover had never been exercised."] [Scott - "Other than to check it out and make sure it worked."] [Jones - "So that cover hadn't been opened and closed numerous times like the one on the one-g trainer."] [Scott - "And we're in one-sixth g, so the weight of the cover wouldn't hold it as well."]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: And now for a future reference, we'd like to know whether you found the quick disconnect? [Pause.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: Negative.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: We copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: How you doing, Jim?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Getting it. (Long Pause) I'm in, Dave.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Good boy. (Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I guess you had the same problem getting in (at 121:17:52 , when Jim entered the LM to set the comm switches) because of the same reasons. I think once we got everything in and you discovered that the hatch wasn't fully open, why, that made it a lot easier from then on. I guess I didn't have any problems getting back in because, again, you were able to guide me as I came in through the door."]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Where are you out there?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: (Garbled) the Rover (tasks at the bottom of CDR-29).

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: (Breathing heavily) Okay, because I've got a pallet here that should come out; I'll put it on the porch.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Al, they want me to ask you once more about - tell - tell you once more where - where the location was. The waste management bag in A-8, but I think you know that already. Incidentally, it's a rather short thing, 2 or 3 inches long. It's got a thread on one end and a quick - quick disconnect on the other.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, I can dump it when I get here. [As indicated in Figure 10-3b from the Apollo 15 Mission Report, Jim's heart rate is above 160 beats per minute.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Dave. Jim, take a breather, if you would, please; and, Dave, you're getting (the) LCRU blankets at 35 percent open at the same time, I'm sure.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Yeah, let me just check on down the checklist, will you, Joe? 125:56:04 Allen: Rog. Rog. No problem. (Long Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: Yeah, Karl, that's exactly what I was looking for. And, problem is, the waste - the small waste management bag is not in A-8 right now. I'm going to have to - have to look around. Maybe Dave or Jim got it out on the way out. I'll look around and see if I can find it.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, fine.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: I just haven't had - haven't had the free minutes since they came up to do that.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Right. And there's no reason now to be troubled by it at all. We were just asking that for future reference. Sounds like it's only a matter of it being dis - misplaced somewhere, so let's forget it. [Long pause.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Jim, did you carry the SRC up into the LM with you?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Yes, I did, Joe.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Good show.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Hey, Jim.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: I've got something for you. (Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Oh, great.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Now I'll take the pallet.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Don't tell me, Davey, let me guess.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Say again?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Roger. Don't tell me; let me guess what that was.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Endeavour, we'd like to have High Gain Antenna, Auto.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: (Chuckles) Oh, you'd never guess, Joe. (Long Pause) [Jones - "The way I interpret this is that, during the Long Pause at 125:56:04 , you went up the ladder. And that you're headed back down, now. You were supposed to bring up SCB-4, but Jim put all those samples in the SRC in SCB-1. What would you have brought up?"] [Scott - "If that's not the Seatbelt Basalt, I'm not sure what it is."] [Jones - "That's what I think, too."] [Scott - "And I don't know what Joe had in mind that I had. Unless it was the Aggie Rock."] [Jones - "No, the Aggie isn't yet."] [Dave first spots the glass ball called the

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. You've got High Gain, Auto, and I've got the Pan Camera Power, On.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Very good. Any time - any time on this rev, we'd like to have an update on the magazines. And in the meantime, let me give you a few good words on the surface activity. The boys have spent the last hour deploying the ALSEP, and I think all of the experiments got out, except we had some trouble, as anticipated, with the - with the drill. Dick Gordon is down here saying "I told you so." The - Dave was in the process of making - for the world discus record, when he just about fell flat on his face he threw it so hard. That was - that was the high spot of the whole ALSEP deployment procedure.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay. Joe, I'm going to power down the LCRU now. (Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Jim, we want you just to take a breather there. We're in good shape, and just take it easy a sec.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, there's nothing much I...(Burst of static)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, LCRU Power Switch is Off; LCRU blankets (pause) are 35 percent open; that means 65 percent closed!

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: How far did he get it?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Or thereabouts.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: We need more calculation. (Pause) Okay, Joe, I'm ready to hop in. Do you have anything else you need done out here?

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Oh, I suppose we'll claim something like 2 or 3 kilometers. Who knows for sure. [Laughter]. But the gyrations he went through to keep his footing after that big heave...

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1255118csm.text: Better than golf balls, even.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Yeah, yeah. It was really funny to see him scrambling to keep his footing though after he swung around.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Dave, we're real good on the time, if you'll just stand by a second. You'll carry the ETB up with you, I guess.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Yes, sir. I have it in my hand right now. (Pause)

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Dave, we are in such good shape on the time, we'd like for you to deploy the solar wind (composition experiment or SWC).

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1255118csm.text: (Laughing) Gee, I should have done that, Dave, before I came up.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Joe, I'll give it a try. It's been, like, 2 years since I've done it; but, I'll give it a try. Where is it, Jim? [Dave and Jim trained as the backup crew on Apollo 12 and, during 1969, practiced deploying the SWC.]

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Dave, I'll tell you what, let's stand by on that We'll have plenty of time next EVA. No problem.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Well, okay. I can do it, I think. I used to do it back on 12.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Is it not, these days, can everybody put up a (lost under Joe).

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1255118csm.text: Dave, dealer's choice.

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1255118csm.text: Well, is there something else I can do for you, like gather up some rocks. (Long Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 27 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15_1255118csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1255118csm.text: Okay, Al. We're ready to have the Pan Camera Power, Off.

a15a1260008.speaker: Allen
a15a1260008.text: Dave, I guess we don't have anything else for you right now. It's been a(n) outstanding EVA here; why don't you go ahead and get in at your leisure. Might want to pick up that glass rock (the Aggie) on your way in.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay. Hey, Jim, can you see me out the window? (Pause) Hey, Jim?

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Yeah, I'm looking for you. You weren't in the left window; are you in the right window?

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Yeah. Talk me through the solar wind; let's get it up, they really need lots of data; we can give them lots of data. [If the SWC deployment had been deferred to early in EVA-2, it wouldn't have been done before about 142:33:52 . By deploying the experiment now, Dave is giving the experimenters an extra 16 hours of valuable exposure time.]

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Okay. Just take it out there about 50 feet.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay. Right about here, huh?

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Farther, if you want. Yeah. And just pull the tube out to full extension. Careful when you get to the end...

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: The little thing popped off the end.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: That's okay. Just pull it on out.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: And, careful when you rotate the screen that you rotate in the right direction, so it doesn't pop off.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Did the...

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Just extend the tube several sections. Make sure they're in the red, indicating it's locked.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay, red, red, red. Red.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Keep pulling.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: And pull that...Yeah, pull that out.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Oh, yeah. Window shade...

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Just be careful you rotate in the right direction so it doesn't drop off.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Want to rotate it against the opening, right?

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Yeah.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Like that. Okay; that's easy enough to do.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Okay, and then...

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Yeah.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: ...grab that there, and...

a15a1260008.speaker: LM Crew
a15a1260008.text: Pull it down.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: And make sure you get the - not the wire, but the bottom of the screen - over the loop.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Okay, I see that. (Long Pause) Okay the bottom of the screen is over the loop. It says "Sun," I guess that means that's...

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Yeah.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: ...what you face to the Sun, doesn't it?

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Isn't that a neat experiment?

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: Yeah, that's the kind of experiment I like.

a15a1260008.speaker: Irwin
a15a1260008.text: Yeah. 126:02:08 Scott: Okay, we're out here at good distance where it won't get any dust on it from the Rover. And I'll turn it into the Sun here; stick it into the ground. It's core tube. (Pause) There. Okay, Joe, solar wind is deployed. (Pause) And I'm going to...

a15a1260008.speaker: Allen
a15a1260008.text: Beautiful!

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: ...pick up a...

a15a1260008.speaker: Allen
a15a1260008.text: Ingress the Falcon, please.

a15a1260008.speaker: Scott
a15a1260008.text: ...a couple of rocks. (Responding to Joe) Yes, sir. (Long Pause) Oh, my! (Pause) I couldn't resist this one, Jim.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1260305csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You can turn Pan Camera Power, Off, now.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: That the glass one?

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Oh, look at what I got! You wouldn't believe it! (Pause) Okay, pick up the ETB. [This is sample 15015 , a 4.7 kilogram, glass-coated, regolith breccia, the third largest rock collected during the mission. This is the 'black rock' Dave described after the SEVA at 107:33:34 .] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Through the windows, prior to leaving the LM, we had seen a large black fragment on my side. And you had seen a black frag on your side, as you looked out the front window. These were unique to the local surroundings. I don't think we'd seen other fragments that black and prominen

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1260305csm.text: Roger, Houston. Got it off.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: And we got the LEC that we should stow out on the porch (to get it out of the way).

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Well, we don't need the LEC...Oh yeah, you mean the...

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: ...LEC up there.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Yeah; okay. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Oh, I like one-sixth g! (Long Pause) [Dave probably just hopped up on to the ladder and is now climbing up to the porch.]

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Okay, here's the ETB. How about handling that with care; there's a piece of fragile in there. I'll get it to you. (Pause) [Jim can't bend down very far and Dave is pushing the ETB far enough through the hatch that it is in reach.]

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Grab it here.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Got it? Real easy with it, so we don't get film and stuff dirty. Give me the LEC. (Pause)

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Let me get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna .

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Yes, sir.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: (Garbled) it here.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Wait a minute; let me hang up the LEC, here. (Pause) Okay, I got hung up. Can you get my antenna? Oop!

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Can you bend over a little more? Come in a little more. Good; just hold it right there. (Pause) Okay, your (PLSS/OPS) antenna 's stowed. [Jones - "I suppose that, with you out on the porch and the top of your OPS just in the hatch, he could reach down and get the antenna. I suppose it would have been less of a reach than the dump valve ."] [Scott - "No problem."]

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Okay. Come back out here and get ready to take a dive. (Pause) [Dave has to get his belly as low as possible to get his PLSS through the hatch. Because the midstep is not vary far from the hatch, Dave has to raise his helmet and then his shoulders to clear it. He probably angles to his right, away from Jim and, after getting his PLSS past the DSKY, can get to his knees and then stand. He probably ends up facing away from Jim, either toward the left rear of the cabin or the left bulkhead.]

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Come in low and slow.

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260305csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) Got it made!

a15_1260305csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260305csm.text: Yeah, if I...Can you get the ETB out of the way?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1260600csm.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) (Garbled). (Pause) Just a minute; I'm... (Pause) Okay, I'm kind of hung up on you, Dave. Let me move back.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1260600csm.text: Go ahead, Endeavour.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1260600csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Go ahead.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Oh, okay.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, now you're clear. (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, Karl. Just for your information, I finally dug all the way through A-8 and got a hold of the quick disconnect. And it's - it's as I expected it. But, it was there, and we're squared away now.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: There you are! (Pause) [Dave probably has just gotten to his feet and has turned enough that he sees Jim.]

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay; close...

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1260600csm.text: Very good. That makes people feel better down here. We did stow it, after all.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: (Reading checklist page Surface 5-1) Prim(ary) Water, Close.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Oh, wait a minute. I'm not ready to do anything yet. Let me turn around. (Pause) [They need to turn off the primary feedwater valves on their PLSSs. Dave needs to get his right arm free so that he can reach back.]

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah, well, one of my problems is that I've got the center couch underneath the right-hand couch, and I've also got the L-shaped bag and a few other things stowed on top of A-8. So, it's not quite so easy to get to.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Joe, do you read us?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1260600csm.text: Loud and clear. Loud and clear.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay. Prime Water, Close, huh? (Pause) If I can find it.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1260600csm.text: Right-o. We understand.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Want me to get it for you? (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, Prime Water's Closed.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Did you get yours?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: (Garbled under Jim) Huh? I got mine.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Turn around and get mine. (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Can you get it? (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: No.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: (I'll) get it for you. (Pause) Got it. Okay, turn around to the right here. I mean left. I'm sorry. Here, turn around. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Okay, I've got a flag and a tone. (Long Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Your PLSS seems to have really shifted.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: That's the problem. It seems like it's riding a lot higher.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah! Way, way. No wonder you can't get those things.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Hey, you're caught under...Here, Dave, you're caught under that shelf.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: (Garbled) Okay. (Pause) Okay, Prime Water's, Closed. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When we got back in, I noticed that things seemed to be much more crowded than I had remembered several hours before. I guess that's (because) we had the freedom of mobility outside. And I had a tough time getting to my water to turn it of; and I think you did too."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "In fact, I think I asked you to get mine. It could have been a function of our hands being so doggone tired."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Yes, I think it probably was. But, stil

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1260600csm.text: Jim, you should be in Disconnect on your...

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: (Lost under Joe)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1260600csm.text: ... Suit Isol(ation) valve.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah, I am Joe. (Pause) [They put the Suit Isolation Valves in Suit Disconnect prior to depressurization at the start of the EVA. Joe's call suggests that the valve got hit when Jim came in the cabin.]

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Oh, me! (Pause) Stay right there; can you, Jim?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah, I'm getting back here in the corner. (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, hatch is closed and locked. Now, let me move out of the way for you (to close the dump valve ). Wait. (Pause) Ain't no room in here. (Pause) Gee whiz! (Pause) Okay. Now, can you get to the dump valve? (Pause) To Auto?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay. Dump valve in Auto.

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Now, the next thing is (Reading) "PLSS O2 and Press flags may come on during Repress. PLSS O2 less than 10 percent, manually control..." Okay, I've got about 10 percent (oxygen remaining). Why don't you go Cabin Repress (valve) to Auto?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Cabin Repress going to Auto. (Pause) Getting...What was the first one?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Say again?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Oh, I thought the circuit breaker...

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Oh, wait a minute. (Looking at the checklist) You got Cabin Repress in Auto?

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Yeah. [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "We never really tried to memorize the procedures and always used the checklist. But some of them became familiar from repeated use."] [Here, Jim thinks he should have closed the circuit breaker before putting the valve to Auto. On those rare occasions when the Apollo crews made procedural errors, the problem was that they had relied on memory rather than the checklist. An example is comm problems Pete Conrad and Al Bean experienced during their EVA-1 Preps. As the astronauts told me repeatedly, procedural success requires both the familiarity that comes with

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, "CB(16) ECS: Cabin Repress, close."

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Now, if I can get around the...What am I hung up on? (Pause)

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1260600csm.text: Nothing I can see. Except me. [Jim was facing aft to get the valve and now has to turn to reach the circuit breaker panel ( CB(16) ) on the righthand bulkhead.]

a15_1260600csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1260600csm.text: Okay, Cabin Repress? 126:11:10 Scott: Okay, there she goes. (Sound of repress audible) And we're up to half (a psi); up to 1 (Pause) 1.5 (Pause) 2.0. (Pause) Okay, you can go...Cabin pressure's increasing; let's go Press Regs A and B to cabin. (Pause) Okay. "PLSS O2 Off when the cabin is full to two and a half," which it is now. (Long Pause; repress ends) Okay, my PLSS O2 is Off. And warning light, off. Okay, "verify cabin pressure stable at 4.6 to 5," and it looks like it's 4.5 and stable. (Pause) Okay. "Use purge valves to depress (if necessary). CB configuration." Okay? CB(16) ECS: Suit Fan

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1261230csm.text: Al, the boys are in the LM, and they're repressurizing the cabin now.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1261230csm.text: Roger, Karl. Sounds like they had a pretty good day.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1261230csm.text: Yes, sir. They had a terrific day. I think they're going to sleep well tonight.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Suit Fan 2 coming - I didn't read...Where are we, Dave? I can't read you.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1261230csm.text: Yeah. I wouldn't be surprised.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: Right here; "CB(16) ECS: Suit Fan number 2, closed."

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Okay, closed.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P closed."

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Closed.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: Okay, get these lights up here so we can see those warning (garbled). (Pause)

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: Okay. "ECS caution and H2O SEP component lights" are out. "Doff gloves! Stow on the comm panel." Boy, that's a nice idea. (Long Pause)

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1261230csm.text: Jim, your Suit Isolation Valve ...

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Yeah, let's find the (lost under Joe)

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1261230csm.text: ...still shows connect down here.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Okay, it's in Suit Disconnect up here, Joe.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1261230csm.text: Good enough, Jim. Thank you. (Long Pause) [This exchange suggests either a telemetry problem or that the valve did not seat and needed to be cycled.]

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Dave, could you...

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: What? What do you need?

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261230csm.text: Could you get my gloves. I tell you, my fingers are so sore.

a15_1261230csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261230csm.text: Mine are, too. (Joking) Wonder why? (Pause) There you go. [Comm Break] Drilling Troubles Apollo 15 Journal Post-EVA-1 Activities

a15a1261602.speaker: Scott
a15a1261602.text: Okay, put up the old helmet bag. (Pause) [Some of the crews hung the helmet bag over the forward instrument panel and this may be what Dave and Jim are doing.]

a15a1261602.speaker: Irwin
a15a1261602.text: There's a funny smell in here.

a15a1261602.speaker: Scott
a15a1261602.text: Yeah, I think that's a lunar dirt smell. (Pause) Never smelled lunar dirt before, but we got most of it right here with us. [Jones - "How would you describe the smell of lunar dirt?"] [Scott - "Like gunpowder."] [Jones - "That's what most people say."] [Scott - "I hadn't heard that before we went. I don't think."] [Jones - "Here, you don't actually describe it as gunpowder."] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "I actually whispered it to Jim so that nobody would become alarmed."]

a15a1261602.speaker: Scott
a15a1261602.text: Okay. "Doff helmets with visors, lower shades, stow in helmet bags. Verify safety on the dump valve ."

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1261633csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You getting a good look at Littrow up there?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: (Garbled) get down?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Can you get that? (Pause) [They are talking about getting down to verify that the safety is on the dump valve.]

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1261633csm.text: Yes, sir. Just went by Littrow. And right over Serenitatis now, coming up on the landing site.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. Where are we here? Okay, "Descent Water valve, Open". (Pause)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1261633csm.text: Very good. Hey, you been looking the Littrow for a couple of days now. Are you forming any opinions whether that dark area is lava flow or ash flow?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Descent Water, Open. 126:17:06 Scott: Okay. Now "remove purge valves, stow in the purse." Uh, oh; the purse fell down. [The purse is a bag that normally attached to the front of Panel 5 on the CDR's side of the cabin. Putting the purge valves in the purse keeps them handy at waist height, keeps them clean, and reduces the chances of dropping them.]

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1261633csm.text: Well, Karl, if I had to give you the opinion right now, I'd say it was all some - some kind of ash. I don't - I'm not sure it's flow. But it certainly is - it looks like a deposit over the entire surface. You can see it - mostly in the upland areas and down in the mare areas and mostly in - in valleys - in depressions, this stuff seems to have collected almost like it was - there was some mass wasting down the hills making the - making the valleys darker in color and maybe a little thicker with that kind of material. But there are - there are still at least three different distinctive colorati

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: I took it down, Dave. I thought that was one of the things that I was hanging up on.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yeah; okay. (Pause) Where did you put it, Jim?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: I put it right behind you. (Pause) 126:17:33 Scott: Whew! (Garbled; Pause) Oh, yeah. Okay. Mag bags all fell out. [These are probably transfer bags for the film magazines, listed in the Stowage list ( ) for transfer from the CM to LM on page 75, for LM Lunar Launch on pages 97-98, and for LM to CM transfer on pages 111 and 112. Dave and Jim apparently stowed them in the purse .] 126:17:50 Irwin: Now that purge valve is really dirty!

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yeah, I bet it is. (Pause) Okay; I'll show you what you were hanging up on. Thing right here.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Huh?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: I'll show you later. (Pause) [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I'm trying to think of when we noticed the break in the bacteria filter."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I think it was right after we got our helmets and our gloves off. I think you looked down and saw it. The water was in and out of there, the hose right at the connection where the bacteria filter joins the water hose. The bacteria filter has some plastic attachments to it. There were two little nicks about, probably, a quarter of an inch long and about a quarter of an inch wide out of the side of the plasti

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay; purge is up. (Correcting himself) Purse .

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Mine is up. [Jim may mean that he has removed his purge valve.]

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yeah. I guess what we ought to do is not get this clean stuff dirty. (Pause) They really ought to have another neat bag for the dirty stuff.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. I guess we better let you go back to work on Hadley, which is coming up any minute now.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1261633csm.text: Rog.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: We should have kept all those camera bags.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yep. Not too sure we'd get this dirty.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Well, we could wrap them in tissue. (That) might help. (Pause)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yeah. (Pause) Okay, we'll try that. (Pause) Here, I'll tell you what; I'll put them in this...(Pause) And we got to use this purse (for the purge valves)...Let me take all this stuff out of the purse that's clean and stick them in here. (Pause) Okay, just hand me the purge valves, I'll take care of it. (Pause) Let's go on down this thing (meaning checklist page 5-1) here. "Disconnect the OPS O2 hose." [Dave is saying that, because the purge vales are so dirty, they should take any items out of the purse that are clean and stow them somewhere where they can stay clean.]

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. It's in work. (Pause)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Should have brought that (dust)brush in here.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: True. (Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "The first order of business after we got repressed was to go through the checklist and do the EVA post, and try to come up with a plan on how to handle all the dirt in the cabin. We were pretty dirty. We had planned, prior to the flight, to take the jettison bags and step into them with the suits (still on) to keep the lower portion of the suit isolated from the rest of the cabin. Our legs from about thigh down were just about completely covered with dirt. I guess the dustbrush worked fairly well. I got the most part of it (before sendin

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: That's disconnected. "Connect LM O2 hoses, (mis-reading the checklist) red to red, blue to blue."

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. Red to red and blue to blue, huh?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Yeah. I mean red to blue. Did I say that right? No, reverse them.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. [They would normally attach the red hose to the red connector and the blue hose to the blue connector but, here, they are going to reverse the flow and connect the red hose to the blue connector, etc.]

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Slow. (Pause) Shoot! (Pause) Okay. (Long Pause) Okay. It says...Okay; "diverter valve to horizontal. Suit Isolation (Valve) ..."

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: I'm not hooked up yet, Dave. (Long Pause) (Garbled)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Say again?

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: (Garbled) in there.

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. Turn around; I'll get you. (Long Pause) Can you back into your corner there? (Long Pause) Okay, you're plugged in. "Suit Flow." (Pause)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1261633csm.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15_1261633csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1261633csm.text: "PLSS pump, Off; PLSS fan, Off." (Pause) "Disconnect PLSS water from PGA; connect LM water." That's a good idea. [With the PLSS pump off, they aren't getting any cooling. Next, they will get on LM comm, as per checklist page 5-2.]

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1262304csm.text: Okay, Karl. I'm over the Hadley area now. I've gone by it. And nothing more to report on the Hadley, except one observation that I meant to make on the last pass and didn't. I'll make it now. That is that the landmark, 15 dash 40, is readily visible, even with the naked eye. You don't need a sextant to see it.

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1262304csm.text: Yeah. Let's cool off. Got a ways to go. (Pause) Oh, that's okay; let her run. (Pause) Okay, "PLSS mode, both, to O. Audio circuit breaker open and connect to LM comm." (Long Pause)

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1262304csm.text: Does that secondary crater complex stand out in any special way that gives you some idea as to its origin?

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1262304csm.text: Well, I didn't look at it from that standpoint when I was going over it before, but - I guess I'll have to take a special look at that to answer your question.

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1262304csm.text: (Garbled) ? Okay, you got your comm? (Pause) Okay. And Audio, CDR and LMP, VHF A, Receive, and B, Off. (Pause) Okay; Mode, ICS/PTT, and Relay, Off. (Long Pause)

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1262304csm.text: Pressure Regs to A and B, Cabin, please. (Long Pause) [They were supposed to have put the pressure regulators in Cabin at 126:11:10 and, while it is possible that the step did not get done, there may be a telemetry problem.]

a15_1262304csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1262304csm.text: Good show. [Very Long Comm Break] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Once we got the hatch closed and repressed, why we sort of took a break right there, which I think wasn't really in the timeline. But it was a good place to take a piece of our rest period. I remember we got the helmets off and stood there and talked about it for a while before we went through the rest of the function."] [During this comm break, they are recharging the PLSS with oxygen.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 39 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263405csm.text: Hey, Al, how's that sunset look down below you?

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263405csm.text: Well, I can't see it from here Karl.

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263405csm.text: Any - any chance - you got light - in the Aristarchus area yet? Seeing anything down there?

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263405csm.text: That's a very interesting observation. You still see some of it out there now, do you?

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263405csm.text: Yeah, that's affirmative. I do, and - Now, I dimmed the lights down; and I have a pretty nice view of the Moon in Earthshine.

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263405csm.text: Ah, hah. Any chance you see Aristarchus? Are you, - maybe you're not looking that way, I guess. Are you looking down on Aristarchus by any chance?

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263405csm.text: Well, just a second, and I'll turn the lights down and let you know.

a15_1263405csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263405csm.text: Good. That's Schröter's Valley, you know, and was once known to glow red.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263753csm.text: Rog, Karl. I've been sitting here looking at Aristarchus, and I finally had to check the map to make sure; because it's - it's so bright in Earthshine, it's almost as bright, it seems like, as it is in sunshine. Very, very bright crater. It looks very much like Copernicus at night.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263753csm.text: I'll be darned. Sounds real interesting.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263753csm.text: Yeah. And I can quite clearly trace out Schröter's Valley going off toward the northwest. I can't see it. It's a little bit out of range; it's north of [my] track, and so it's somewhat out of range for me to see.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263753csm.text: Very good. Hey. Spence [Spencer Gardner] is asking me to remind you about the film magazine update if you have any time yet this rev.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263753csm.text: Okay. I'm going to have to go back through the Flight Plan and get the numbers out. But I will do that.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263753csm.text: Okay. I'm not sure we want you to do that at the expense of anything else here, like to P52. Hang on.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1263753csm.text: So, I'll go ahead and do the P52, Karl.

a15_1263753csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1263753csm.text: Right. We'd rather have you do the P52 if there is any either/or there.

a15_1264232csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264232csm.text: We've got your torquing angles, Al.

a15a1264238.speaker: Worden
a15a1264238.text: Okay, Karl. Get them [torqued] out in a minute.

a15a1264238.speaker: Allen
a15a1264238.text: Hello, Hadley Base; this is Houston.

a15a1264238.speaker: Scott
a15a1264238.text: Rog. How is everything down there?

a15a1264238.speaker: Allen
a15a1264238.text: Dave, the dust may have settled up there; I'm not sure if it's settled down here. We've got more data than we know what to do with at the moment. What can we help you with?

a15a1264238.speaker: Scott
a15a1264238.text: Oh, just wanted to tell you, we've got two PLSSs charged with O2: one at 95 (percent oxygen) and one at 93.

a15a1264238.speaker: Allen
a15a1264238.text: Roger. We copy that. [Deke Slayton joins the conversation. Slayton was a Mercury Astronaut who became head of Flight Crew Operations and was responsible for crew selection.]

a15a1264238.speaker: Slayton
a15a1264238.text: Real fine day's work up there, guys. Why don't you take the rest of the day off?

a15a1264238.speaker: Allen
a15a1264238.text: Dave, on that PLSS reading, could you tell us which number belongs to which PLSS, please?

a15a1264238.speaker: Scott
a15a1264238.text: We should have done that. Jim's got a 95, and I've got a 93.

a15a1264238.speaker: Scott
a15a1264238.text: Give us about 30 minutes to get a bite to eat, and we'll press on for the next one. Then we won't have to doff the PLSSs.

a15a1264238.speaker: Allen
a15a1264238.text: Dave, Deke says okay, but I'm not sure if the question was understood.

a15a1264238.speaker: Slayton
a15a1264238.text: I thought you added one more word there, like "eat and rest".

a15a1264238.speaker: Scott
a15a1264238.text: Roger. [Scott - "This was just banter. 'Hey, we've got the PLSSs charged, give us 30 minutes to get something to eat, and we'll press on and do the next EVA!' And that's why Slayton comes in and adds, 'Eat and Rest'. It's all light-hearted stuff. But he does want us to rest!"] [Very Long Comm Break] [During this Comm Break, they remove the PLSSs, disconnect the OPSs, and, as per checklist page 5-3, replace the PLSS batteries and LiOH canisters.] [Scott - "It was hard work to suit and unsuit ! There was no room in there."] [Jones - "But it was also true, was it not, that you could not have func

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264506csm.text: Hey, Al. You've got a couple of people interested down here in particle clouds now. And, first of all, we'd like to have you verify that you saw particles all the way until you went into the shadow. I certainly believe you did. You were telling me about them just as you were in that position. And likewise, if you have a chance at sunrise tomorrow where you are in that same position, with the Sun illuminating you, but not the background, could you see if you - there is any remaining signs of those particles?

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1264506csm.text: Okay, be glad to. Now, as far as how long I saw them; I saw them as long as the spacecraft was still in sunlight. However, I was beyond the terminator - surface terminator. And, - right now, looking out the window I don't see any of them.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264506csm.text: Okay, fair enough. And I got some words for you on that bad attitude that we had on the oblique mapping camera photography this morning. If...

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264506csm.text: Evidently, we - sent you up the right attitude angles, but somehow or other we had a - slightly erroneous omicron. And, the actual photograph - I think we were something like 10 or 15 degrees off attitude - were perfectly good. No problem there. But, we have gone through the Flight Plan and made sure in the future that we will have the proper omicron and everything will be right on the nose.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264506csm.text: Just in case you was wondering what in the heck went wrong that time. [Changing subject.] And, I have a TEI-37 any time you have time to copy it.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1264506csm.text: Okay, Karl. Go ahead with the TEI-37.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1264506csm.text: Go ahead with your TEI-37 PAD.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1264506csm.text: Roger. TEI-37, SPS/G&N; 37350; plus 0.60, plus 1.01; 151:00:17.43; plus 2979.1, minus 0745.2, minus 0243.3; 180, 109, 349; the rest is NA. Ullage, 2 jets for 17 seconds - 17 seconds - and the longitude at T IG is minus 179.52. That's all.

a15_1264506csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1264506csm.text: Okay, understand. TEI-37, SPS/G&N; 37350; plus 0.60, plus 1.01; 151:00:17.43; plus 2979.1, minus 0745.2, minus 0243.3; 180, 109, 349; 2 jets, 17 seconds; longitude at T IG is minus 179.52.

a15_1265302csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1265302csm.text: Al, how's your exercise machine going up there. Getting - getting all you need for the - for the big day in the future.

a15_1265302csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1265302csm.text: Right now I'm trying to figure out your film usage.

a15_1265302csm.speaker: Worden

a15_1282833csm.speaker: Allen

We're getting a very high signal strength from the Central Station, and every experiment seems to be working normally. It's an outstanding job. I thought you'd be interested in the fruits of your labors there. Over.

a15_1282833csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1282833csm.text: Well, thank you, Joe. We had a good time doing it. We'll be back with you in about probably 10 or 15 minutes to talk over the rest of it.

a15_1282833csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1282833csm.text: Roger, Dave. We're in no hurry. 128:37:35 Scott: We're coming along pretty good. We've got things pretty well cleaned up, and we're getting into our nice white suits now.

a15a1284901.text: Okay, we're all settled down now with some good beefsteak, and all cleaned up and ready to talk.

You could add cold water to the food packs, but that was about it."] [Scott - "Yeah, but I think we had some bite-sized items. Either in orbit or...I'd have to look at a menu. But I remember that, when we got back from Apollo 9, one of the things we pointed out that we missed was chewing. When we got back after ten days, part of the debriefing was 'What did you miss?' And we, all three, agreed we missed chewing things. And they said, 'You had chewing gum,' and we said 'It's just not the same.' And I remembe

a15a1284901.text: We've got a list of questions here; some fairly general geology questions at the last, and, depending upon your answers, we'll build a good part of EVA-2 on it. Didn't Joe go to school in Heidelberg or somewhere? And in the months that we

a15a1284901.speaker: Allen
a15a1284901.text: And I'll just start off at the top of the list here. Dave, which ALSEP photos did you get out of the way?

a15a1284901.speaker: Scott
a15a1284901.text: I got them all but the heat flow, Joe.

a15a1284901.speaker: Allen
a15a1284901.text: Roger. Copy all but the heat flow. And, Jim, when the LSM (magnetometer) sunshield was deployed, do you think the instrument stayed more or less steady? Or do you think it may have moved a little bit?

a15a1284901.speaker: Irwin
a15a1284901.text: (Faint) It might have moved a little, Joe.

a15a1284901.speaker: Allen
a15a1284901.text: (Making a mis-identification) Dave, say again. I didn't copy that.

a15a1284901.speaker: Irwin
a15a1284901.text: Is there a problem with the...(Stops to listen to Joe) Hey, Joe, this is Jim. It might very well have moved. In other words, it's not level any longer?

a15a1284901.speaker: Allen
a15a1284901.text: Negative, Jim. We don't necessarily know that. As far as we know, the data looks pretty as a picture. We just want your own feel for it. (Pause) In other words, we have no reason to believe it moved. We just wanted to get some words from you on that. (Pause)

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285137csm.text: When you took the double core, did you notice any soil falling out of the core tubes while you put the caps on?

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1285137csm.text: Yes, there was a slight amount of loss from the lower and a little bit from the upper, but very little.

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285137csm.text: Okay, that sounds good. And regarding the question about the Rover tracks, Jim, you told us they were one-half inch deep or less, and we're wondering if that was a typical number over the course of the entire traverse, as far as you could notice?

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1285137csm.text: Well, that was my impression. Half an inch, in general; but Dave probably has another comment.

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285137csm.text: No, Joe, I'd say no more than a half an inch. It seems to ride very lightly; I think the bearing on the surface is very light, and the wire wheels seem to work very well. They've got good traction, and even though the rear end did break away several times, it was primarily because of the locked-up front wheels. And I was very pleased with the operation. I think the thing performs better than we'd expected. 128:53:10 Allen: Okay, Dave, thank you. [Scott - "It worked better than we expected it to."] [Jones - "Based on the performance of the one-g trainer that you used on the field trips?"] [Scot

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285137csm.text: Now a series of questions about the heat flow. We want you first to describe the drilling characteristics, and do you think you're drilling into a layer of rock? Over.

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285137csm.text: I'd say yes, Joe. The drilling characteristics are: it's a gradually increasing requirement for force to get it in. More so than any force I experienced in the one-g training, even when we had the packed soil. One time we did have some that was packed so tightly I couldn't even get it in, but that was because of the weak battery on the training unit at the time. The drilling requires more and more force the deeper you get. And, you could probably see the TV there at the end on the second one, I had the second probe about half way in, and I was putting almost my entire weight (on the drill). Ev

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285137csm.text: Roger, Dave. We hear you on that. A similar question, was the drill torque high while you were drilling?

a15_1285137csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285137csm.text: Well, "high" is a relative term. I had to maintain quite a bit of pressure on it to keep from being turned, but I tried in the one-sixth-g airplane several times to see if I couldn't hold it, and I could always hold it. And I can hold it here, even though the torque was fairly high.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1285501csm.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. We're 4 minutes to LOS. A couple of comments before you go around the corner. First, the Surgeon thinks you may have loosened part of your EKG harness while you were exercising. Would like you to check that at your convenience. Second, we have a new Gamma-ray [boom] retract time on the back side of 129:20. Over.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, Dave, that's a clear description. We know that the stem is loose in the hole as far as the rotational motion goes. We're wondering if it's loose in the up and down direction. Do you think you could pull it out?

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: I don't know, Joe. I don't really know. (Pause)

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, Dave, copy that. Is the drill thermal shroud off the drill unit?

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1285501csm.text: Roger, Houston. Understand going around the back side. I'll check out my biomed harness. I may have loosened it exercising. And understand you want the gamma-ray boom retracted at 129:20.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: Oh, yes. You mean the small aluminum-colored shroud that goes over the battery?

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285501csm.text: That's affirm.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott

a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, and were the Boyd-bolt guide cups removed from the heat flow experiment?

a15_1285501csm.text: Roger. We won't be able to see it to keep track of [retraction] times, remember, Al. And, also I guess the Mass Spec. people would appreciate any more comments you can think of, next time you take a look at those particles at sunrise. Over.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: Gee, I guess I have to think about what you mean. All the Boyd bolts are off of the box (meaning the Heat flow Electronics package), as far as I know.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, Bob. Will do. [Long pause.]

a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, Dave. Our question concerns the covers (also know as 'sleeves')for the Boyd bolts. They're calling them "the guide cups" down here.

a15_1285501csm.text: Houston, Endeavour. One last comment.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: Do you mean are they off now or were they off when we started?

a15_1285501csm.text: Go.

a15_1285501csm.text: Okay. When I took the battery B off charge and checked the systems test meter for battery pressure - battery compartment pressure - and it was - systems test meter read 1.4, which is - looks like it's getting pretty close. Is that test - test meter still working all right?

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285501csm.text: Dave, we mean are they off now. Did they fall away from the unit when you picked the unit up. It's of relative unimportance, really, but it would be an interesting data point.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: I didn't pay much attention, Joe, but I think all the Boyd bolts came off the heat flow, finally, I think. (Pause)

a15_1285501csm.text: Roger. Stand by. We're looking at that.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1285501csm.text: Yes, it was, Joe.

a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, and I'm sorry I skipped over a question here. Dave, where is the drill vise and the drill treadle right now, as you remember.

a15_1285501csm.text: Okay. That's - they say that's nominal. That looks good.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1285501csm.text: The drill vise is next to the second probe, which is the western probe, and the treadle is at the point at which we parked the Rover.

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1285501csm.text: Okay, that agrees with...

a15_1285501csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1285501csm.text: Oh, it was within, oh, one-eight to one-quarter of the center.
