a15a1430355.text: Okay, you going to torque to 283 Dave.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah, just hold on. That darn cannon plug again down there. [Having helped Jim with his seatbelt, Dave is now trying to get his own belt on and is having the same trouble he had during EVA-1 with his belt catching on the cannon plug which is alongside the seat on the outside.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You want me to hold it for you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: No. I have to get off and unhook this thing every time.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: That's bad because every time you bend over like that you put strain on that PLSS antenna.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Do I really?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: It bumps against this low-gain (antenna which is mounted on Dave's inboard handhold).

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Oh, I have to be careful. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Here we go. (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, my seatbelt's on. Is your seatbelt on?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Yes, sir.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay. (Pause) Here we go!

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You got to torque that 283...

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: ...It's almost on 283. (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, it's 283. Okay. 143:11:13 Irwin: Okay, we're off, Joe; we're moving.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: What's the heading, partner?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: (To Joe) Give us that heading again.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger; and we're marking. We want you to proceed towards Checkpoint Number 1. Your general heading is 160 at 1.9 clicks and this may take you down between Salyut and Index Craters.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay. [Salyut is at BO.2/74.5 and Index is at BO.8/76.5 on the EVA-1,2 Part A map . A larger scale map shows the named features at the site and a map by Journal Contributor Ken Rattee shows an excellent approximation to the actual traverse. The latter can be compared with a traverse map from the Lunar Sourcebook , which has significant errors.] [By chance, the bearing of the planned landing site from the actual site is about 160 degrees, so Dave and Jim actually are driving toward checkpoint 1.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay 160. I'd like to go down there and see those (two craters), just for drill.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. No one should come to Hadley Rille without seeing Index Crater, and we'll try to keep you posted on when you're coming up on that.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: (Chuckles) Okay, fine.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Joe, I'm going to start the (16-mm) camera here. Will you keep track of it? I'm on 12 frames per second.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Jim. We're marking it now. Thank you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Wait a minute. Why don't you hold off for awhile, Jim?

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay. Never mind.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Hold off.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Let me get squared away here.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Hey, Joe, the steering is a new task, Joe. It's really responsive now. I guess I got pretty used to quiet steering, and this thing really turns!

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. We don't want it to be too easy for you.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Hey, look. We can always disengage the rear steering.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: No, I'll get used to it, it's just a matter of getting used to. 143:12:48 Irwin: Okay, on our left, now, we have a very large subdued crater. I'd estimate 4- or 5-hundred meters across. It has a crater of about 25 meters (diameter) on its eastern, inner wall, about half way to the bottom. And on that smaller crater there's some rock exposed. Looks like some bedrock exposed, in that particular crater. [The 'very large subdued crater' is Last Crater, which has an actual diameter of about 200 meters. The smaller crater on the eastern wall is readily visible in a detail from Pan Camera frame 9809

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: I'm going to hold up here.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: You want to disengage rear steering, maybe?

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're stopping, Joe.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Just a minute.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Jim. Stopping.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Okay, try it that way.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're moving again.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. And your description is remarkable, remarkably similar to Index. Perhaps you're looking at Index Crater.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I guess it's the largest crater that I've seen, Joe, as far as (lost under Joe).

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. We'll reserve judgment on that, but keep describing, please. Sounds great. [Based on the bearing and range they report at 143:15:30 , they are now somewhere near the southern end of Last Crater, and are about a kilometer northwest of Index Crater.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, we're heading 155 and at our 1 o'clock position, there's a doublet. Gee, I think it's the doublet we drove across yesterday. I'll tell you in a moment when we see our tracks. Do you want to talk, Dave?

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: I just want to tell them I turned off the rear steering to see how she works with the front and it's really a lot better. The double Ackerman's a little too responsive when you have the lack of traction, especially on the slopes. [Double Ackerman means having both front and rear steering.] [Jones - "Does 'lack of traction' refer to the wheels being off the ground?"] [Scott - "Yeah. Moving relatively fast on an irregular surface, you don't have much grip. And then, with both front and rear wheel steering, you oversteer because, if the wheel comes off and it's being turned, it comes down at angl

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger, Dave. Copy that. Why don't we save the double Ackerman for the rougher terrain later on.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah. I think that's a good idea.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Joe. I mentioned those...It's really a triplet arrangement here that we just passed on our right. I did not see our tracks.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: So we're definitely east of our track from yesterday.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. We agree.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: We're heading 170. (Pause)

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Okay, Jim. And you...

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: And our range is 0.5. 143:15:30 Allen: ...may very well be coming up on Arbeit Crater. [A range of 0.5 kilometers on a heading of 170 degrees puts them near BQ.4/73.6 . Arbeit Crater is still a kilometer SSE of their current location.]

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: I think we are.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I think so, Joe!

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: I think so. There's a fairly fresh one here with angular blocks on the rim.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: Roger. Give us the size...

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: Look at that one directly ahead, Dave.

a15a1430355.speaker: Allen
a15a1430355.text: ...on the largest, please.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: Yeah, I see it.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: That's Pahoehoe (a Hawaiian term for the smooth, rope-like form of solidified lava). (Answering Joe) Yeah, the largest ones I would estimate 2 or 3 feet, angular. There's one on the southeast rim that has a flat top. In fact, it looks like a rectangular block. But there are several fragments down there that have the Pahoehoe texture that Dave mentioned yesterday.

a15a1430355.speaker: Scott
a15a1430355.text: However subtle, though.

a15a1430355.speaker: Irwin
a15a1430355.text: (Chuckles) Yes. However subtle. [Jones - "You'd been out to Hawaii..."] [Scott - "Aa and Pahoehoe. We'd been schooled on that, extensively. And it's a good cue for the guys in the Backroom on what we're seeing. Aa is the jagged and Pahoehoe is the smooth."] [Jones - "And everybody in the loop - at least you and Jim and Joe and the people in the Backroom - knows what Pahoehoe is."] ["What did you mean by 'however subtle'?"] [Scott - "Well, it's not really a distinct Pahoehoe. It's got the characteristics of a pahoehoe, as differentiated from an Aa. And the only reason we use the terms is to say

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; copy. [The cuff checklist pages covering the traverse are CDR-6, which is blank: CDR-7, which covers the to the now-deferred Station 4; CDR-8, which is a sketch map of Station 4; CDR-9 which lists features of potential interest on the way to Checkpoint 2; and CDR-10, which covers the traverse between Checkpoints 2 and 3. Jim has identical pages in his checklist. The decision to defer Station 4 was discussed at 139:43:48 . The checkpoint locations are shown on the EVA-2 contour map .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, range is 0.6. We're heading 160.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: And we're doing about 8 to 9 clicks.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Dave. Sounds good. Standing by for amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay; amp reading is...Let me get my hand down there, Dave (to shadow the gauge). I want to put my hand down there to get the amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, go ahead. (Pause) Let me get it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I got it. Okay, the max looks like about 10 amps.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, good enough. 143:16:58 Irwin: Get no reading on 2. (Pause) Okay, coming up on our right is a very subdued crater again. No blocks at all on its rim, and it is about 50 meters in diameter. [Jones - "In talking about crater sizes and the presence of blocks on rims, some people would use that as an indication of the depth of the regolith. Would that have been something you were thinking about?"] [Scott - "I think this is an observation, not a conclusion."] [Jones - "But you're providing data for that kind of analysis."] [Scott - "Sure. And subdued and old and rounded versus sharp, angular.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay. Let me stop and get the rear steering going.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We stopped, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Now we're going again, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: And I see a very large crater over at 1 o'clock. [This may be Salyut.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, let me just get the steering squared away here, Jim.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. Okay, we've stopped.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Jim; and that might very well be Earthlight at 1 o'clock. And Domingo Crater should be on your left, now. [Earthlight is at BJ.5/75.5 and Domingo is at BK.3/76.3. Houston still thinks Dave and Jim are a kilometer south of their actual location. See the EVA-2 map and the map showing feature names .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We'll give you a little more report when we get a little closer to it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I'm going to hold off too many comments here until Dave gets the steering squared away.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. [Scott - "There is so much to see up there, all of which is brand new - because, again, we had no photography at this resolution, whatsoever. So, old Jim is just having a ball! All this stuff to talk about, and it's all different and all new. And I'm trying to get the thing to steer. I can't wait! That was part of the excitement of the whole region, 'cause you could have just stopped there, and you could have looked around, and you could have spent several hours describing what you see, 'cause it's all so different."] [Jones - "Even at the 17 site - where they had good overhead photogra

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Joe, it feels like the rear steering, when I turn it off, doesn't center. Feels like my rear wheels are drifting. So I guess I better turn it back on. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Dave. We agree...

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: And we're gradually increasing. A very gentle slope.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: ...maybe you should turn it back on.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: (To Joe) Yeah, I guess you might think about why they don't center for us.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. That sounds like the Rover moves like Jim's sand crabs move. (Jim laughs)

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, that's just exactly what it feels like too.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Dave, if you could swing to the right here, we could go by the rim of Earthlight - what Joe is calling Earthlight (but is probably Salyut).

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Good. Let's do that. Well, there's a big thing here in front of us, too.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, but we could swing...Can you get around to the right? Maybe not!

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: No, let's go to the left. We're not going to stop at Earthlight. Let's go left.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Because that's a big excursion there. (Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, now we're going downslope.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Well, we're going in and out of the craters.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I get the impression, out to our left, that there is a shallow depression there.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Gee, over to the left there is a big hole. Huh? See that over there?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: A big subtle crater. Oops, and we're coming up on a sharp one!

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Hey, you got those two ahead of us there?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. See if we can find a reasonable path through here. (Pause) [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "(The preceding dialog) is a pretty good indication of the irregularity of the surface. I have yet to see a photo that captures the many, local elevation changes. It would be great if somebody could do a surface model and then put the LRV on it, provide a driver's-eye view, and then 'IMAX' it!]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we're heading 140; we're out to 1.0 (km from the LM).

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; Jim, copy. [What seems likely is that, in order to avoid Salyut, Dave has turned to a heading of 140, as indicated on Ken Rattee's map by the bend to the east immediately north of Salyut and directly west of Index. If they are 1.0 kilometers from the LM at a bearing of 160, they are near BO.6/74.7 . The 'sharp' crater that Dave mentioned at 143:19:42 could be the raised-rim crater at about the 1:30 position just outside the rim of Salyut that is marked on a detail from Pan Camera frame 9809.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Doing 9 clicks.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Beautiful.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: I think we're going by a very large one here, over at the 9:30...9 o'clock, Jim, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yes. [On a heading of 140 passing northeast of Salyut, they would have Index would, indeed, be at a 9 o'clock with the near rim no more than 250 meters from them. Index is about 350m in diameter.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: What do you suppose that is?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: It could be Domingo.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: No, it's too big!

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Too big for Domingo?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Couple of hundred meters.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Let's see, 1 out...Let's see, Checkpoint 1 is...You said 1.7.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, that could be, possibly, Index Crater, if you started from where we thought. The distance is right on that. And continue on towards Checkpoint 1.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, I would say that probably was Index. It was about that size.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, you've got the right bearing.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. That's nice, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. We're going for 1.7.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Going for. Yeah, okay, we're 1.2 now.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. [Houston suggested an average heading of 160 degrees and, as Dave indicates at 143:21:55, their average heading - corresponding to a bearing of 340 degrees - is very close to the suggested figure. At a range of 1.2 kilometers, they are near BN.9/74.9.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: There's a nice deep one there that's smooth and rounded, about 30 meters across. [The 'smooth, round' crater could be the one at about BN.4/75.1 which is also marked on the detail from Pan Camera frame 9809.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: You know, on one of these trips, we ought to stop at one of these very fresh ones and really sample it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: On the way back we'll get that one.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. I mean these small ones, you know, just filled with...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Oh, yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: ...rock debris and glass in the middle. Just do a systematic sampling on it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Like this one over here at 1 o'clock.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, I know what you mean. (Pause) Okay, bearing is now 339 and the range is 1.3. Look out, oh! [Dave took his eyes off the "road" to look at the Nav readouts and didn't see a crater. They are now near BN.5/75.2 . That location is on the rim of the 'smooth, round' crater . Note that, because the range is given by the nav system in tenths of a kilometer, the range uncertainty is at least plus or minus 50 meters, which corresponds to plus or minus 0.2 map units. That is, for this location more or less south of the LM, the indicated location is between BN.3 and BN.7.] [Rattee puts Dave and Jim a

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Ohhhh! Whoa baby!

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay. We're all right.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yup. (Pause) Great machine.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; does it good. (Long Pause)

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Rover, Checkpoint 1 is 160 at 1.9 clicks, and there's no need to stop there. We can press on towards Checkpoint 2, if you're satisfied.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; Rog. I guess we're okay, Joe. [Jones - "Would you have ever contemplated stopping at one of these checkpoints? It's just a distance/bearing point, isn't it?"] [Scott - "I don't recall. It was a feature, but it wasn't a station. But, if it was of interest, you might stop because you would think you knew where you were."]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we've got the right bearing. We're at 1.4 now, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Okay, Jim, and we're enjoying your description.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Why don't you just give them a running comment; I'll keep my eyes on the road.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, there's a...

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Sounds like a good idea. 143:23:22 Irwin: (Lost under Joe)...a crater on our right now about 50 meters in diameter with a lot of gray fragments on its rim. And we're just passing one (rock) that's sitting right on the surface - about 2 feet, subangular. I can look out now and see the South Cluster and I get the impression of perhaps, some horizontal beds in the first mound in the South Cluster. I do see a lot of blocks over in that direction; particularly the second mound - the west side of the second mound that appears to be in the Secondary Cluster.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger, Jim. Copy.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Probably over the area of Crescent. [As indicated on the map showing feature names , Crescent Crater is the northwestern member of the South Cluster.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, we're 1.7. And, again, we have a very fresh crater on our left with several blocks. [They left the LM at 143:11:13 and, therefore, have an average, straight-line speed - or range rate - of 7.8 km/hr.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: The blocks (are) about a meter or so and the crater is probably about 15 meters, like it might have excavated or been a secondary, huh?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, well, notice all the debris here, that the surface is covered with more debris in this particular area than what we've seen before.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, it sure is.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Just around that particular crater.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, "more" being probably 2 percent (surface coverage).

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: (Chuckles) Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: It's noticeably more.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. We copy that. And, Jim, you may want to start your (16-mm movie) camera, if you think this is a good area, and don't hesitate to fire off shots from the hip with your 70 millimeter. [On Apollo 16 and 17, Charlie Duke and Jack Schmitt took traverse photos at regular intervals with their Hasselblad cameras during the traverses. They were wearing their cameras on their RCU brackets and had no trouble getting good horizon centering. Photo AS15-85- 11471 , which Jim took at the start of the EVA, shows Dave seated on the Rover with his camera pointed virtually level.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, I'm going to start the...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Point it (meaning the 16-mm camera) down, Jim; it's pointed up a little too much, here.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay. (Pause) About like that?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, that's dandy.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, I'm starting the camera, Joe.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger. We got the mark, and we'll watch it. 143:25:38 Irwin: Tracking...(Responding to Joe) Okay. [Jones - "I wasn't aware that the vertical pointing of the 16-mm camera could be changed but, in AS15-85- 11471 , it is definitely pointed up. In the picture, we can see that Jim's got a map mounted on the accessory staff. We can even see your OPS antenna. This was taken toward the west, so Bennett Hill is in the background. Its got good definition on the Rover wheels. TV camera pointed down and aft in its stowed position. We can see where you taped the cable to the high-gain antenna staff. There'

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Reckon we can get between those two there? Yeah. (Pause) It's a bridge between two, about 20 meters in diameter, a little doublet and the one on the left has got a bunch of debris, and the one on the right has got nothing, huh, or very little.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Boy, there was a very large crater over on our 1 to 2 o'clock position.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Oh, yeah! [They have been driving for two minutes since giving their last range readout of 1.7 km and, if Dave has been driving more or less away from the LM, they are now at a range of about 2 km and are somewhat north of Earthlight Crater . As Jim indicates in a moment, they are also somewhat east of Earthlight, perhaps near BL.1/76.5 .]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: That's the largest one...Oh, I guess it would be equal (to or) maybe larger than...Well, larger than Elbow, certainly.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, it looks like it. You can't see too much of it but it does...

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I don't see that on the map.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, we think you might be looking at Earthlight now. It might be...Its long (meaning north-south) dimension is greater than the east-west dimension. [The north-south elongation of Earthlight is not terribly obvious on Pan Camera frame 9809 . On the north side, Earthlight appears to overlap a smaller, shallower crater which may have contributed to the apparent elongation shown in the pre-flight maps and may be visible from the ground.]

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, well that's certainly true. Certainly true. (Pause) Okay, you would have us east of Earthlight.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Hey, here's a big deep one here (lost under Joe) 143:26:57 Allen: That's exactly correct. And Arthur Clarke would be proud of you. [ Earthlight is a Clarke novel.] [Journal Contributor Harald Kucharek calls attention to the following from Clarke's novel 3001: The Final Odyssey : "It gives me particular pleasure to pay this tribute to the crew of Apollo 15. On their return from the Moon they sent me the beautiful relief map of Falcon's landing site, which now has pride of place in my office. It shows the routes taken by the Lunar Rover during its three excursions, one of which skirted Earthligh

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: ...about 50 meters...(Stops to listen to Joe) 143:27:03 Irwin: Okay, and on the south...I can just barely see the western slope of Earthlight. But the southern slope of it, I can also see, has several blocks on it.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Hey, Jim. Check the camera. I don't think it's running. I don't see any change in the...

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Not changing?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: ...the quantity indicator. Why don't you feel it?

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: I did and...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: The film apparently is not running through.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, it's stopped now.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah; why don't you try it again. (Pause) Make a little turn here.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, it's trying to run, Dave.

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Okay, point it to the forward and let's see if it will...I just noticed that the film counter wasn't going.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah. I hope we don't have another...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: Yeah.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: ...film problem.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Dave and Jim, the film counter may not have dropped off the hard-stop yet. It's only been going a couple minutes. We need a range and bearing, if you'll give it to us, please. And continue on; we'll watch the camera.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, bearing is 358; range is 2.2.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger...

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: I think bearing's 338.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: ...and let the camera run.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Yeah, isn't that what I said? What did I say?

a15a1431615.speaker: Scott
a15a1431615.text: You said 358.

a15a1431615.speaker: Irwin
a15a1431615.text: Okay, 338.

a15a1431615.speaker: Allen
a15a1431615.text: Roger; copy. 338. (Long Pause) [They are now near BK.2/76.6 . On Ken Rattee's map , they are very close to that location, which is east of Earthlight and NW of Crescent , which is the large crater immediately NE of Dune. .] MP3 Audio Clip ( 12 min 11 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Get around this blocky area here. (Pause)

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Boy, it looks like we're coming down...have to go through a small valley.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, sure does.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: That valley off to the left.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Oh, yeah! And that's a north-south trending, isn't it?

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: I hope we can get through this way.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Oh, the old Rover will make it - with a few little excursions.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: It looks more like a valley, you know, that runs east-west.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, sure does. (Quietly) Oh, come on. Easy does it. (Pause) Look at that big hole there, Jim! Are we up on Dune? Yeah, there's a rampart over there.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: I was wondering whether we could possibly be at Dune.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Could we be at Dune?

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Or Crescent?

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Dave, I think you're probably...

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Crescent? Boy, that's the biggest one we've seen.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: ...looking into Crescent. [As shown on the larger-scale, Apollo 15 Named Features map, Crescent Crater is the northwest member of the South Cluster.]

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I think it is.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I guess you're right, Joe.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: 'Cause this little one, just to the right of us here, I see it on the map. [The 'little one' may be a small feature east of Earthlight and northwest of the larger crater on the rim of Crescent at BJ.0/77.0 . The 'BJ.0/77.0' crater is circled in yellow on Ken Rattee's map .]

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: So, yeah, that's Crescent.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Yeah, I guess you're right. That's a big fella isn't it? [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When we went by the big craters, Crescent and Dune, they were really subdued. They sure weren't very obvious."]

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: In fact, Dune should be dead ahead, Dave; so we'll probably have to steer a little to the right to go around the western side of Dune.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Okay.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Exactly correct, Jim...

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Here's a blocky area here.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Oh, yes.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: ...your thinking corresponds to ours. And you'll be wanting to head more towards the south...towards the numbers 334 and 3.3 clicks.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Jim, disregard...

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: You want a bearing of 334?

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: ...that's a bad number. You're heading towards checkpoint 2.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Okay. Yeah, checkpoint 2. Okay. [Checkpoint 2 is at BA.7/76.8 .]

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Hey, we're in a debris field now, Joe, with fragments on the order of 6 inches to a foot, in general, and maybe, oh, I'd say almost 5, (to) 8 percent coverage. Wouldn't you, Jim?

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Yeah.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: And there are some (rocks) that are up to a couple of feet that require some maneuvering.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Roger. [The Rover has a 14-inch (0.36 m) clearance.]

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Let's see, I think I'll go left around this one, Jim, and then swing over to the right.

a15a1432900.speaker: Irwin
a15a1432900.text: Okay, yeah, that'll be good.

a15a1432900.speaker: Scott
a15a1432900.text: Lots of...The smaller ones are deeper here. Man, there's one (meaning a crater) and that's got direction to it (that is, a noticeable asymmetry). (The crater is) about 4-meters across and (it has) a big block in it on one side, on the south side.

a15a1432900.speaker: Allen
a15a1432900.text: Roger. [Dave's observation strongly suggests that the crater was dug by the block and that the impacting object was coming in from the north at low speed and a relatively low angle.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston, how do you read? [Pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: (Lost under Joe) being about a meter.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: ...just like a secondary impact from the north.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: That's just exactly what it looks like, Joe.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Hello, Houston. Endeavour reading you loud and clear.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, range is 2.7.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Reading you loud and clear likewise. [Long pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay. [If the bearing to the LM is 340, they are near BH.3/77.0 or, possibly, a bit west of that point.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Should be Dune straight ahead.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, which way do we want to go around? I'll tell you...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: To the right.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Right, yeah. Okay. Looks like the better way to go from here. (Pause) Up a little hill here, about, oh, I'd say this must be a 5 (to) 7 percent grade. The old Rover's going right up just like it knows what it's doing.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: A little more to the right, Dave.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, coming right. Think I'll get up on the rim here where I can take a look.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, I'm afraid the rim might be (lost under Joe)

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, Jim. And turn off the 16-millimeter camera, please. The film should be run through.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Not a single motion on the little ball on the indicator, Joe.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Al, if you have time to listen, I have some news bulletins down here; and, somewhere in the middle, I'll break in for the High Gain Antenna, Auto. [Pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, Dave. We copy that. We'll worry about it later.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, Karl. Go ahead.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Right. This is the morning national and world news - the world being, of course, the planet Earth. President Nixon, yesterday, declared his administration is determined to revitalize the American country...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, we tried running that through with our fingers last night and I guess it didn't do much good.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: We'll get the next one; don't worry.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Let's see...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, we can definitely look down into Dune Crater.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Can we ever! [They are on the north rim of Dune Crater, possibly at BG.5/76.6 . They last reported a position at 143:28:21 which corresponded to BK.2/76.6. The implied speed is a reasonable 8.8 kph.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Man, it sure likes a ray of blocks that run north and south on the southern slope of the crater.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: [Garble.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Go ahead. I missed that one; Al, say again.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: That's your world right now.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, and there's no big rampart like we were thinking we'd see. (Pause) [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I think we recognized Dune by the notch on the (south) side. Although it was more subdued (than they expected) and there was no rampart, I think it was quite recognizable by that notch on the south side."] [The "notch" is formed by a 100-meter crater located at about BF.2/77.4 on the south rim. See, also, Pan Camera frame 9430 .] [Jones - "What do you mean by 'rampart' in this context?"] [Scott - "It's a bench. We thought there might be a bench on the internal part of the crater.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: That's right; that's our world.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Our world's up here right now, Karl.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: [Laughter] I - I'll give you some news bulletins on that at the end. Things are coming along good in the EVA. Okay. President Nixon was what - he was at ceremonies dedicating a dam in Iowa, and he said the economic potential of rural areas must be developed, quote, "so that the people who live there can be first-class citizens enjoying a first-class way of life." Unquote. In the labor area, about 4,000 Houston area steel workers are expected to be off the job today in a nationwide strike against nine major steel companies. That's beginning to loom as a pretty big factor in [the] economic world

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, we're heading now 250 to get over on the west side of Dune. [This part of the traverse is the arc shown on the western rim of dune in Ken Rattee's rendition of the traverse map.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Roger; copy. (Pause) And, Jim, checkpoint 2 is out at 4.3 clicks...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: And we're doing 10 clicks (km/hr).

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: ...bearing 348.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, 348 at 4.3?

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: That's affirm. (Pause) And nothing magic about that number as you know.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Understand. (Pause) [Joe is reminding them that it is a crew decision as to where, exactly, they go on the Front. As indicated on the Pre-Flight Site Sketch , they had planned to make perhaps three stops in the hand drawn ellipse that contains provisional stations 5, 6, and 7: one at the east end of the ellipse, one in the middle, and one at the east end.] [The bearing and range of 348/4.3 for Checkpoint 2 indicate that Houston is using Dave's estimate of BS.4/73.3 for the LM location.] [Scott - "I wonder if they have correlated our tracks (seen in blow ups of the pan camera photos) with our h

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, when we get clear of the west side here, Dave, we could just head about 180 (which is south).

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: For the front. (Pause)

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Lots of debris here. Wooee! Up again to about 5 to 7 percent. Very rough-textured, subangular blocks. Gray. Partially buried, some of them, and some of them are on the top (that is are sitting on the surface), huh?

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Roger. And Jim, give us range and bearing, please.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Boy, look up at Hadley Delta...(Stops to listen) Okay, bearing is 348 and range is 3.0.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Roger; thank you. [They are near BF.7/75.8 , almost due west of the center of Dune and, as indicated on Ken Rattee's map about 100m west of the rim. Ken puts them on the rim.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Look up at that Hadley Delta, Dave. Don't you get the impression that those craters, (the) secondaries on the side there, are oriented, going right up the slope?

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Oh, yeah, you called them right, I think. Secondaries. I think they just splattered right up the slope. Because they're the only craters on the side of the mountain. [Jim's observation suggests that, like the craters of the South Cluster, the craters visible on the flank of the mountain show signs that they were dug by low velocity material coming from the north or, alternatively, by ejecta from the South Cluster.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Driving down (to the Front), we discussed the secondary sweep up onto the Front. It's obvious that the only craters within the Front itsel

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah. And they're lined up so nicely! Good-sized one (meaning a crater) ahead, Dave.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Up on your planet, the latest word is that the Rover is still functioning - functioning brilliantly, and the fellows are well into EVA number 2 and just recently passed Crescent Crater and Dune Crater - well on their way to exploring the Front at Hadley Delta.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yes, sir. Avoid that fella. [Hate to get] stuck in there. (Pause) Okay, we're going south. (Pause)

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, Jim, and please continue. (Pause)

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Sounds great.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Yep. Everything's going great, both in orbit and on the surface. Everybody is very pleased. [Pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: (Dave laughs) Okay, we're on about the southwest side, now, of Dune Crater. As Dave mentioned, we're heading, oh, 155 now. A very fresh crater at our 1 o'clock position with a lot of angular blocks; very slight raised-rim about 2 feet above the general surface; but a very fresh crater. It seems like the albedo was lighter around that one than others that we've seen. In fact, you might be able to see that on your map, Joe. The lighter albedo in the southwest side of Dune. It's a fresh crater...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: Great, we're listening. [Pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, I'll take the items one at a time as they come. First off, the central peak. The central peak is a - is a very large - smooth peak on the - on the south and east sides, getting blocky on the north side; and there's what appears to be some layering visible on the - on the south and west exposed scarp of the peak, dipping to the north at about 30 degrees. [Pause.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Roger, Jim. We have it; thank you. [This may be the small, fresh crater marked on the detail from Pan Camera frame 9809.]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: And what's the bearing and range to the next checkpoint, Joe? (Pause)

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: It was 348 at 4.3.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: That's affirm, Jim. And you'll want to continue heading south.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1433145csm.text: You're coming through loud and clear.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1433145csm.text: The - Okay. The light material - light colored flow material - around the edges of the - of the basin - texture appear to be nothing more than just simple mass wasting off of the edges - or off the - of the rims around the basin. The rims themselves are quite - cut with the mass wasting in a - oh, I'd say an extent of about 330 degrees on the north, east, and south sides. Now, on the west side, the rim there is a very, very, large, clean scarp; and when I say clean, it goes almost from the basin floor to the - to the rim itself in one large chunk. And that scarp appears to define the limits of

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Okay, that bearing now is 348 at 3.3. [They are near BE.5/76.0 or, more likely, about 200 meters east at the location labeled 'Rest Stop' on Ken Rattee's traverse map .]

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: Wouldn't it be nice, Dave...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1433145csm.text: Roger.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: ...if we could line up with that chain of secondaries...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, that's right.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: ...going up the side of Hadley Delta. But now, look up the slope there at...if you can take...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: Yeah, I can...

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1433145csm.text: ...your eyes off the road there for a moment.

a15_1433145csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1433145csm.text: As a matter of fact, I'm going to stop right here and take a little break. [Jones - "For some reason, I had forgotten that you stopped here. (Pause) [A christie is a skiing turn made by shifting one's body weight forward, forcing the heels of both skis to one side and sliding through the turn on parallel skis. In a stem christie, the skier begins the turn by pushing the heel of what will be the downhill ski outward and then bringing the other ski parallel to it. A snowplow is a slowing maneuver in which a skier spreads his/her legs and brings the ski tips together, creating a broad wedge which literally plows snow aside and slows the skier. References to skiing and to ski country abound in Apollo becaus

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: Yeah. We could actually walk in and do a radial sample.

a15a1441840.speaker: Henize
a15a1441840.text: Take 3. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Yep. (Pause) [Because the crater is on the side of the mountain, the downslope (northern) rim and inner wall form a more or less level surface.] [Dave picks up the gnomon - which he had put down, undoubtedly, to free his hands for picture taking. He starts down hill, with Jim following. Dave occasionally gets both feet off the ground as he makes his way down to the north rim, going relatively quickly. Jim follows more slowly, sidestepping downhill, facing toward the west and leading with his right foot.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Boy, look at how the zero phase wipes everything out. Man. (Pause) [In the direction directly opposite the Sun, they get a maximum amount of reflected light and virtually no shadows. Those factors, coupled with the virtually uniform grey color of the surface, mean that the down-Sun scene is almost featureless.] [The brightness of zero phase is due to the phenomenon of Coherent Backscatter .]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: (Reaching the bench) Yeah, we can get this here, easy. 'Cause we don't want to go too far downhill, so we don't have to climb back up to our Rover friend. Jeeper, this...They're all too big (to fit in individual sample bags). [Jim stops short of the bench and watches as Dave looks for suitable samples. On purpose, no doubt, Jim is also in about the right position to take the down-Sun photos.]

a15a1441840.text: Take 4. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.text: Notice you're kicking up some white material there, Dave?

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: No, I didn't notice. Hey, you're right! [Dave kicks a patch of the surface soil aside to uncover some of the underlying white material.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: We ought to trench it.

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: You're right. Sure should.

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Good idea, Jim. Sounds great...

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: We ought to use a core tube here.

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: ...A trench sounds great.

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: 'Trench sounds great.' Okay.

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: Trench or a core?

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Yes, sir. A single core would be nice. They're always nice.

a15a1441840.speaker: Henize
a15a1441840.text: Take number 5. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: You guys are easy to please today. [Dave has dropped the gnomon to the surface near a cluster of rocks that are visible in the TV image.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Why don't we go to the upper rim up there and pick up the core, Jim, on the way back up?

a15a1441840.text: Take number 6. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Okay. I think the big one is too big to put in, as usual. Of course, we'll never be satisfied with that; but I'll take some of these others.

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: Okay. [As Dave picks up a sample with the tongs, Jim joins him, he already has a sample bag in his left hand. He plants his scoop and opens the bag.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: I think they're the same. (Pause) (Get the) dust off a little bit. (Pause) [Dave taps the rock several times with the handle of the tongs to knock some of the dust off.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Henize
a15a1441840.text: Take 7.

a15a1441840.speaker: Worden
a15a1441840.text: Roger; take 7, and I just went past the spacecraft terminator.

a15a1441840.text: Another breccia.

a15a1441840.text: Bag number's 192. (Pause) [Dave puts the sample in the bag and then reaches for another sample, which he puts directly in the bag.]

a15a1441840.text: Say again? Roger; we copy.

a15a1441840.text: Just hold it (open) and I'll get a bunch of these frags right here.

a15a1441840.speaker: Worden
a15a1441840.text: Okay, I just went by spacecraft terminator.

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Roger. 144:22:18 Scott: Some with some glass. (Long Pause) [In all, Dave collects five fragments.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Henize
a15a1441840.text: Roger; we copy.

a15a1441840.speaker: Henize
a15a1441840.text: Take 8. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.text: Okay. That ought to do it. Why don't you close it (meaning the sample bag) up, and I'll photograph, here. (Pause) [Scott - "There; I just took the post-collection photo. The TV is real good with that."] [Dave's cross-Sun "after" is AS15-86- 11637 .] [Jones - "I'd never paid much attention to what you were doing with your hands on the camera; but, now that you mention it, we can go back a look at that closely. You're checking and changing settings, sometimes having to clean dust off."] [S

Let the work be done when you get back, in sorting out..."] [Jones - "And use the bags only for soil samples?"] [Scott

a15a1441840.text: Take number 9. [Long pause.]

a15a1441840.text: Like to get some visibility. [Dave probably means that, by splitting the rock open, he will get a better look at it's structure and composition.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Hold my tongs, please. Let's see if it's got any variety up here. (Pause) [Standing with his right foot forward about 30-40 cm short of the rock and his left keg back, Dave flexes his knees, almost touching the ground with his right knee, and delivers a solid blow to the rock, which breaks it into several pieces. a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: (Commenting on Dave's prowess with the hammer) Not bad at all.

a15a1441840.text: Yeah; sure is. (Responding to Joe) Yeah, not bad for a beginner. (Pause) (To Jim) Okay. Give me the tongs, and let's just get another bag and pick up those two little frags there. What do you say? (Pause) [Dave takes a stereopair of the broken rock, AS15-86- 11638 and 11639 .]

a15a1441840.text: Take number 10. Change the shutter to 1/500th, cover the lens, and cycle one frame.

a15a1441840.speaker: Worden
a15a1441840.text: Okay; thank you.

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: (To Joe, referring again to Joe's comment on Dave's prowess with the hammer) Evidently your TV is working okay today, Joe. Is that right?

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: It's beautiful, Dave. Either that or it's another ESP experiment. ["ESP" (Extra-sensory Perception) is a reference to Ed Mitchell's controversial and unauthorized ESP experiments conducted on the way back from the Moon on Apollo 14. Journal Contributor Bertrand Ouellet suggests that, here, Joe is saying that he knew that Dave had broken the rock open either because the TV was working well or because he was reading Dave's mind.] [During this exchange with Joe, Dave collects a piece of the broken rock and takes it in his hand for a close examination.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: (Chuckling) Okay. A microbreccia with millimeter (sized) white clasts, and there's a gray clast in there that's about 3 millimeters. It looks a little different. Let me go down and get this other one that came off. [Dave puts the first piece of the broken rock in the bag Jim is holding and then, to avoid disturbing the sample area, goes around the west side of the gnomon to get a fist-sized fragment that rolled south of the parent rock after Dave broke it.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Irwin
a15a1441840.text: And 193 is the number on the bag. [Dave rejoins Jim and drops the second fragment directly in the sample bag.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Roger. Copy 193. And we're standing by when you start the trench. 144:24:17 Irwin: (To Dave, having closed his SCB) Okay. [While Jim seals the bag, Dave backs up and takes a cross-Sun "after", AS15-86- 11640 . David Harland has assembled a mosaic consisting of "before" frame 11636 and "after" frames 638 and 640. The samples are 15265-66 , which are 0.27 and 0.31 kg pieces of regolith breccias.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: (To Joe) Okay. Well, would you like a trench or a core, Joe? We'll give you your choice today.

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: We'd like one of each, if we could, Dave. [Dave grabs the gnomon and then steps to his left toward Jim so that Jim can put the sample bag in his SCB.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: (Sounding doubtful of the value of doing both) A trench and a core?

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Yes, sir. 144:24:39 Scott: Okay. We'll go up and trench it first and see if it's worth coring.

a15a1441840.speaker: Allen
a15a1441840.text: Okay. QuickTime Clip ( 1 min 05 sec )

(Long Pause) [Dave starts uphill, going around the east rim of the crater using a shortened version of the skipping stride. He travels relatively quickly and makes the trip up to the level portion of the south rim in about 22 seconds. Jim grabs his scoop and follows, moving noticeably slower. His time over the same path is about 48 seconds.]

a15a1441840.speaker: Scott
a15a1441840.text: Right up here where it's nice and fresh. (Pause as Dave positions the gnomon) Hey, Jimmy. Dig me a little trench when you get up here!

a15_1442520csm.text: (Garbled) (Pause) [Dave takes a cross-Sun stereopair while he waits for Jim. These are AS15-86- 11641 and 11642 .]

I guess it was just greater bearing surface for the Rover than there was on our boots."] [Jones - "Did you notice any stress in the calves or knees fr

a15_1442520csm.text: Oh, yeah! My word! Look it, they're dipping to the northwest, right?

a15_1442520csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1442520csm.text: That's right; that's what I said.

a15_1442520csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1442520csm.text: Oh, yeah! It looks like a big block tilted up on its side.

a15_1442520csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1442520csm.text: Just like you called it, Jim...

a15_1442520csm.text: Sure does, Dave.

On the sixteenth scoopful, what appears to be a 4- to 5-cm rock comes out.]

a15_1442520csm.text: Yeah. [If Dave stands north of the trench, he will be on the inner slope of the 10-meter crater, a precarious perch at best. The problem is that, unless Jim starts a new trench, any change in position will make the digging more difficult.]

a15_1442520csm.text: Did you hear him, Dave, he wants the SESC from the bottom of that. 144:28:41 Scott: Okay. [Dave faces the trench again and takes AS15-86- 11645 . He then steps to his right and takes 11646 .]

a15_1442843csm.text: Al, are we in time to get a mark from you to when you start the Gamma-ray boom [going] out?

a15_1442843csm.text: You get a bag; I'll sample the bottom.

a15_1442843csm.text: Okay. (Pause) I'll get your bag. (Long Pause) [Dave hops sideways to his left to get out of the way while Jim moves in to sample the trench. a15_1442843csm.text: Rog. I'm ready now. Gamma-ray boom going out.

a15_1442944csm.text: Yeah. [While he was talking, Dave moved over to Jim, who turned slightly so that Dave could put the sample bag in his SCB.]

a15_1455705csm.text: Yup. (Pause) [Scott - "I got carried away with that rock, I know that. I really did. That rock was so much fun that I'm sure I burned up fifty pictures just because it was a neat rock."] [Fendell finds Dave as he approaches his Rover seat. We get a good view as he pulls a sample bag off his camera, opens it, puts the rock in, rolls the top of the bag and seals it with the metal strips.] [Jones - "Nice sequence of you bagging the sample and closing the bag."] [Scott - "These are good engineering films."]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: And, either Dave or Jim...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Joe, there was a...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: ...when convenient...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: ...frag...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: ...our TV camera's starting to warm up considerably. We'd like for you to clean off the camera top and the LCRU when convenient, please. [While he listens to Joe, Dave raises his Rover seat so that he can put the sample bag in the enclosed area under the seat.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: All right, Joe. And...Shoot. [Dave forgot to look at the bag number before he rolled the top closed and it takes him a second to find the number.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Log bag 171 for a frag off of that big boulder, I'm pretty sure. It was exposed right on the surface, fairly clean, right next to the boulder and looked like the same material.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: Roger. Wouldn't be at all surprised. [Dave attempts to clean the top of his Hasselblad with his fingers, apparently by tapping it.] Video Clip 2 min 54 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPG )

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: And I think I'll brush off the (TV) camera for you, and I can brush off my camera before I change the film. [Dave hops sideways to the back of the Rover to get the dustbrush. In the background, Jim has just finished a long swath with the rake and is holding it vertically and shaking it to get the soil out.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: And, Joe, this looks like a pretty good place to rake. I've raked one swath here about 2 feet long and I've collected, oh, about 15 rocks.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: That's a jackpot! (Pause) [Evidently, Dave has gone around the other side of the Rover to get to the TV. The TV picture jiggles, presumably as Dave dusts the camera and the LCRU.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Put them in a big pile; I'll be right over.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [Jim turns to his left, probably looking for a clean patch of ground where he could pile the collection of rocks.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Oh, I don't know whether I want to do that, Dave. [The idea is to collect all the rocks in the swath and, by dumping the collection on the ground, they risk losing some and/or risk adding rocks that came from the dump site rather than the swath.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay. Well, then, I'll be right over.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: I'll just do my film...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Though I think we can fill up the bag pretty fast, here.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay, then, you take the pictures and I'll just change my film later.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay. I'll...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Save the (the time that would be taken by) film changing here. Let me get you a bag. (Pause) [Dave comes into view from the front of the Rover, puts the dust brush on his seat and joins Jim.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1455705csm.text: Roger, Al, you're...

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1455705csm.text: And that ledge looks like it's caused by a - a harder material.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Oh, yeah! You did get a bunch. 172.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1455705csm.text: Roger. You're coming through loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1455705csm.text: Roger. (Pause) [Dave bends his right leg and gets the bag down to about knee height. Jim makes the pour without any apparent difficulty.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay. (I'll) get a little more swath.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Yeah. It (meaning the first swath)'s about 1 meter long and one rake-width wide. (Long Pause) [Jim positions himself and does a second swath next to the first. Rather than stand still and pull the rake with his arm, he holds his right arm out and walks backwards, using his legs to pull the rake at a steady pace through the soil. After a meter or so, he raises the rake and shakes the soil out.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1455705csm.text: Do any of the other craters around that area, around Bessel, show the same sort of interior ledge like that?

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Yeah. Good! (Pause) Glass on some. Most of them are rounded; right size. (Pause) [Fendell zooms in and, with Dave and Jim in slightly different positions, we get a good view of the pour.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1455705csm.text: Well, unfortunately, Bessel is the only one of that magnitude around - around that particular area. And I don't see any other craters that appear to go down below - whose depth appears to go down below the depth of the rim in Bessel.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1455705csm.text: Right. I - the only two I see possible here are Bessel E and Sulpicius Gallus; and I guess they might not go that deep even so. [Long pause.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Okay, do another one. (Pause) Oh, you're stepping on my tongs. [Dave's dropped tongs are out of view behind the Rover.] Video Clip 2 min 40 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: That's all right. I'll get them.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: I can get them with the scoop here in a little bit.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: Yeah. Sure miss that yo-yo. (Jim finishes the third swatch) Oh, good! That's three swaths 1 meter long apiece. (Pause as Jim makes the third pour) And the bag isn't full yet. Let's shoot for a full bag. What do you think? (It will) take you just a second to go one more sweep there. (Pause as Jim starts the fourth swath) Oh, my poor old tong!

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1455705csm.text: Hey, Al, have you ever looked at Autolycus and Aristillus with the thought in mind of determining which overlaps the other; which is the younger? [Pause.]

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1455705csm.text: No, I haven't yet, Karl. Maybe this is a good time to do it.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Oh, I don't weigh that much up here, Dave, to break your tongs.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1455705csm.text: I don't know what I'd do without them.

a15_1455705csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1455705csm.text: Just so I don't bury them. [Jim finishes the fourth swath.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 59 sec )

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Good, good, good. Don't shake anymore, you('ll lose some of the rocks)...(Pause) Yeah. That's too bad; we didn't get many out of that one. Why don't you take one over...Let me move the gnomon about 3 inches here; and take one on this side, Jim. Okay? Move the gnomon back about a foot. Why don't you take a swath here and I'll...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, you know, because we're moving a little farther from the rim

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. [Each of Jim's swaths had been taken closer to the Rover than the previous one, apparently with the starting points on a line at an angle to the rim. Dave moves the gnomon to our right, about a foot closer to the rim.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: We get less and less each swath.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: This one ought to be a more fruitful one. Either that or my arm's getting tired.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: That's probably true, too. (Pause while Jim takes the final swath) (To Houston) How about a double core here, Joe? Got any ideas on that one?

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: (While Jim makes the pour) Dave, we're coming up on the departure time about 10 minutes from now. All we really need is soil from this same area. And we're making money hand over fist. Maybe a few walnut-sized rocks if there's some around.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: We got...Okay, Joe.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: A bagful.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (Closing the bag) We got a whole bagful of those in the comp(rehensive rake sample). And that's in 172.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Roger; copy 172. I guess all we need is a soil sample from this area and perhaps even larger rocks, if there's some grapefruit to football-size rocks there. [Dave stows the rake sample in Jim's SCB.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. (Pause) Yeah, we'll just finish off Jim's collection bag here. I want to stow it anyway. (To Jim) Oh, look at that glass spherule down there. (Pointing) See that big one? I got to...Listen

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Oh, yeah. I see it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you back off and document the area. Let me get my tongs and pick that up.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Perfectly round, about...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. Here, let me help you. Video Clip 2 min 49 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. Get the tongs. (Pause) [Partly hidden by the Rover, Jim uses the rake tines to lift the tongs.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. Good, good.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Keep an eye on the spherule.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Tongs are right on it. I got the tongs. (Long Pause) [Dave takes the tongs, knocks some dirt off them, opens them, and collects the glass sphere.] [Jim takes a stereopair of "afters" of the rake site, AS15-90- 12233 and 12234 . In 12233, Dave is examining the tongs for damage.] 146:04:50 Scott: My little taw. [A taw is a shooting marble.] [Jones - "Were you part of the generation of marble shooters."] [Scott - "Was I ever! Oh, absolutely. Did a lot of marble shooting. Bull ring, mostly. That's where you put a little circle in the center of a bigger circle and you try to knock them out from the

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: So I'll get you a bag; (and) let you take a picture of that. I'll get a bag; then you can get the soil.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Where you going to put that little spherule?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: In the bag.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Not with the soil, though, are you?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Came out of the soil. I just didn't want to miss it. We'll remember that. That goes in bag number 173, and...Well, our friends in the back room are writing that down right now.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: How right you are! And we want to leave in about...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Little fat ball.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...5 minutes, and we still need the soil.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: It's coming right now.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Rog. We see it coming in. [According to Bailey and Ulrich, the glass ball is sample 15307. There is, however, no mention of it in the Preliminary Science Report.] [Jim uses the side of the rake to collect some soil.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: A little more?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. Let's fill the bag. (Pause) (Laughs) [Jim's second pour fills the bag almost to overflowing.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: (Joking) Is that a full bag there?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yes, sir. That's a full bag. That's a full bag.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: I want to see you shake that one down.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: All right. (Chuckles; Pause) [Dave shakes the bag up and down but doesn't get enough settling. He then tips out a small quantity of soil]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Don't guess I will. (Pause) [Dave tries to close the bag but decides that he needs to tip out some more soil.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Pause) Better (to) have a 90-percent bag for sure than...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Just don't pour your spherule out.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (Sealing the bag) Okay; I think you need to reconfigure, and we'll get ready to leave here. [Here, "need to reconfigure" means that Jim needs to take the rake off the extension handle and re-attach the scoop.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. I'll go over and take this off, then.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. [Jim turns to do the tool change at the left-rear corner of the Rover.] 146:06:35 Scott: Here, let me put this (soil sample) in your backpack. Stand there; that's good. I'll get it. [Jim's SCB is on his right side - the one opposite Dave's current position - and, rather than interrupt Jim's work, Dave decides to go around him to get at the SCB.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: I'm going to get a couple of big rocks, Jim. And we'll just fill your bag (with the big rocks) and call it a day here. Video Clip 2 min 41 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG ) [Dave grabs the tongs and the gnomon.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Sounds good, Dave. And we want to move in about 3 minutes. We're coming up against a hard stop here. [This may be a walk-back constraint. Houston wants them to leave soon so that, if the Rover fails for some reason, they will have plenty of oxygen and cooling water for a walk to the LM.] [During my 1989 discussion with Jim, I asked him about walk-back constraints.] [Irwin - "I think on the last three missions, walkback constraints defined our maximum distance from the Lunar Module. And also defined the speed at which we traveled, because we had to get to that furtherest point as quickly as pos

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay; 3 minutes. Okay; that doesn't give us time to really do much then.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Maybe one big rock wouldn't hurt.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. (Pause) [Fendell starts to pan clockwise and, just before we lose sight of Dave, he heads for his Rover seat, probably to stow the gnomon in its pouch behind his seat. Fendell gives us a good view into Spur before pointing the camera down at the LCRU mirror and, after a few seconds, the camera's own shadow on the ground in front of the Rover.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Jim?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yes.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you come over here and get your scoop and scoop me up one big rock?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: And...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: And get your camera on it, because I don't...I don't have any film. How about this one right here that looks like it has some layering in it? Maybe...

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, that's the one I was talking about.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Right there?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you...? 146:07:51 Irwin: You want to point to it with the...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, I've got my foot right there. Why don't you take a couple of cross-Suns real quick?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Seven feet, cross-Sun? (Pause) (You're) a little too far away, old buddy. (Pause)

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. [Jim's cross-Sun stereopair is AS15-90- 12235 and 12236 , which, indeed, show Dave pointing at the proposed sample with his foot.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. Now come grab your scoop and we'll take it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: It's a pretty big one to try and get with a scoop.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah; you're right. I don't see anything else (suitable for collection).

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: This little fracture. (Pause)

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Too big.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Too big. Get another one.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Oh! Here, Dave. 146:08:28 Scott: Oh, sure. Good boy. Get that one on your side.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Pause) [The sample is 15459 , a 4.8 kg breccia. It is the second largest of the Apollo 15 samples but, evidently, is not the one Dave was pointing at with his foot.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Getting it. That a boy. There.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Should have left the rake on.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yep. (Pause) Can you get it? Good show. Easy does it. Easy does it. That's it. Up a little more. Keep your balance. (Pause) Can you get it up higher?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Whup! Don't fall backwards.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. (Pause) [There are two possibilities here. One is that Jim has gotten his scoop under the sample and is raising it, undoubtedly gingerly, into Dave's reach. The other is that Jim has actually gotten down low enough to get the rock in his hand and then against his leg as he rises. He then works it up his leg high enough that Dave can grab it. The latter scenario comes to mind because of a similar maneuver performed by Charlie Duke at the rim of Plum Crater at the Apollo 16 site.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Man! I got it.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Good. (Pause) Video Clip 2 min 20 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 21 Mb MPG )

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay, fill that square. Okay, Jim. Let's get on the Rover and head back.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Okay, I haven't secured the rake there, yet.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. You secure the rake, and I'll secure the TV, and we'll get moving. [We see the shadow of somebody working at Jim's seat. This may be Dave, looking for a place to stow rock they've just collected.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Sounds good, Dave and Jim. And we want to leave...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: I wonder how I'm going to do this (that is, stow the rock).

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...the TV camera where it is right now. It's stowed in the proper position.

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Okay. (Looking under Jim's seat) Oh, shoot!

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Hardly room there, is there?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: "Hardly room there" is right. Any place we can put your bag on it?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Why don't you put that in one of those bags, Dave?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah. I'm going to put it in the seat pan now. And then, why don't you put your bag in here. Here, let me have...Come over here. I'm going to put your bag in there. Your carrier is awful loose, and I don't want to lose that bag. Put this on the Hand Tool Carrier. [Dave has probably taken an empty SCB out from under Jim's seat to make room for the SCB Jim has been wearing. The TV image shakes as he works around the seat. His shadow goes out of view, probably as he joins Jim at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: What's in there? Rocks?

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Oh, I don't know what's in there. No...

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: And, troops...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: ...(garbled)...

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: How many big rocks did you pick up? One?

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: I think that's our best...(Stops to listen to Joe)

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: Yeah, one, Joe. We're about out of time, here.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: Rog. Although we're not hurting all that bad, but...

a15a1460226.speaker: Scott
a15a1460226.text: (Probably getting Jim's bag off) Bend over, Jim.

a15a1460226.speaker: Irwin
a15a1460226.text: Yes, sir.

a15a1460226.speaker: Allen
a15a1460226.text: ...we think you should be climbing...
