a15a1475024.text: Hey, Joe, if Jim took a picture of the heat flow box, the one he took probably isn't representative of the proper alignment, which it now has. 147:55:01 Irwin: I'll come over and take another one.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Okay. Come on over.

a15a1475024.speaker: Allen
a15a1475024.text: Jim, just make sure you are well clear of the (Central Station) antenna, with your PLSS there, old friend. (Pause) [Jim backs away from the Central Station and then goes to join Dave at the HFE.] [Scott - "They're dying, back in Houston, watching Jim. 'Don't step on it! Don't move back! Don't move forward. Don't hit the antenna!' Maybe it's not good to have TV, right?. It gives 'em heart palpitations back in the Control Room."] [Jones - "Especially this first time they've had this much TV."]

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: (To himself) I don't...Okay. (Pause)

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I need an antenna like that on my PLSS. (Long Pause)

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: I picked up that black, glassy rock, Dave.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Good.

a15a1475024.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475024.text: And I picked up another pink one that looked like it had a lot of the plagioclase glass in it.

a15a1475024.speaker: Scott
a15a1475024.text: Good. Don't step on this (cable between the HFE and the east probe); I'm trying to get it stretched out flat. (Pause) There. (Pause) [After Dave finishes with the cable, he goes to the HFE to double-check the alignment, accidently dropping the wrench along the way. Jim takes AS15-92- 12416 . The Central Station is in the background and we can also see the RTG, the Solar Wind Spectrometer, the PSE, and assorted trash. Dave's shadow is in the foreground.]

a15_1475550csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475550csm.text: Okay. While I'm trying to get a bite of lunch here, I thought I'd just tell you that after the dump, the same thing happened - the same kind of cloud, the same kind of particles that - that I described yesterday. And they've just about - they've just about dispersed now. Well, you know, Karl, the interesting thing, I guess I hadn't thought about it before, but when you're sitting up here looking at the surface through one window, it's just pitch black out the other windows. So you go from a very bright scene in one window to a black in the other.

a15_1475550csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475550csm.text: Okay, it's dandy. It's got some dirt on it, but that's all right. Return to the LM Apollo 15 Journal Index The Dreaded Station 8

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay, Joe, what's next on the agenda?

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Station 8.

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: I copied your question, Dave, and stand by and take a breather. We're thinking about it here. [Dave resumes his effort to straighten the cable to the east heat flow probe. All through this sequence, it is obvious that Dave and Jim are conscious of the cables underfoot and we see them repeatedly stepping or hopping over them.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Dave, if you'd just pick a site, I could sure start digging.

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Yes. So, actually out - out the dark window...

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Dave, why don't you do that?

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay, Jim.

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: [Garble.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: I've been resting. (Pause) [Dave is using the UHT handle to pick up the wrench, which he dropped about a minute earlier.] ]

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Out the dark window, you are still able to see particles?

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: Yes, I see particles; there's no cloud now.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Okay; (I'll) just go after it (meaning the wrench) here. 147:56:48 Irwin: I'll be over at the Rover, Dave.

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: You - you did see...

a15a1475618.speaker: Worden
a15a1475618.text: You could until just a few minutes ago, and the particles dissipated rather quickly; and now I don't see any particles out that window.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Be right there. (Long Pause) [Jim runs to the Rover, using the loping stride, and we get a good view of the motion of his backpack. He covers the 25-meter distance in about 24 seconds and his average speed is about 3.7 km/hr.] [Jones - "The backpack's going side-to-side, a little bit, relative to the suit. It's a pretty normal motion that I've seen on all the flights. It's a function of the side-to-side stride, I think."] [Scott - "Probably is. I don't remember. Did we ever say anything about that, about feeling it?"] [Jones - "No. Nobody did. Nobody was bothered by it."] [Scott - "That's inte

a15a1475618.speaker: Henize
a15a1475618.text: Roger. We copy.

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Dave, we've got some instructions when you're ready.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Ready, go. (Pause)

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Rog, get Jim started on the ditching experiment, if you would please; and then I've got another good one to lay on you here. Don't quite know how to explain it. We'd like for you to try to get the deep core for us with the drill.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: (Jim laughs) Aw, Joe, you didn't even have to tell me, because I knew darn well that was coming with the stuff that we must be on top of here. Okay. [This comment suggests that, at this point, Dave believes that the troubles he has been having with the drilling are due to hard subsurface layers.]

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: Roger. Look at it like this...

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: Shall we take Station 8 with the (garbled)?

a15a1475618.speaker: Allen
a15a1475618.text: ...Jim is going to be digging at the same time.

a15a1475618.speaker: Scott
a15a1475618.text: Rog.

a15a1475618.speaker: Irwin
a15a1475618.text: (Looking at his cuff checklist) Well, the thing is, do we want to do the whole Station 8 activity. The comprehensive sample? Video Clip 2 min 58 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Al, another bulletin from the lunar surface. The fellows have been back at the LM for some time and working again on the ALSEP. And the problems they had with the drill, they're trying to catch up with now. And yesterday they got in one of the heat sensors and then had trouble finding the time to get in the second one. But they did get the second one in today, and I guess now they're going to go after the core - the core drill sample.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Sure! I guess if they want to do Station 8, they want to do Station 8.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay. [The Station 8 proceedures and cuff checklists can be found on pages 117-123 from Apollo 15 Final Lunar Procedures . There are slight differences between the CDR and LMP checklists.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: (Laughing) I guess. Comprehensive sample first, I reckon. Okay, LRV is not parked in the right spot. They could get TV. [Cuff checklist page CDR-15 indicates that they had planned to do Station 8 with the Rover pointed south and the trench west of the LM. This configuration would give good lighting on the trench wall for both the TV and the 16-mm camera. As per CDR-16, they had planned to load a fresh film magazine in the 16-mm camera and film the Station 8 activities at 12 frames per second.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Hey, let's just turn it around. Lift it up an turn it. 147:59:03 Scott: No, they won't like that because the TV is all messed up then. Oh, boy! Listen. Let's just play it out here in front, right out over there (pointing west) and pretend like that is the side of the LRV, except the 16-millimeter won't be in the right spot. Oh, boy! Show biz. [This is one of the few times during Apollo when both members of a crew are standing around, basically doing nothing while a decision is being made. Indeed, since Jim finished the ALSEP pan at 147:38:40 , he has done very little other than change film mag

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: (Pointing) We could aim the 16(-mm camera) out this way; out to the west.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Sounds like they're pretty busy down there, Karl.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Yep, they are having a good time there, all right.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, let me...Hey, Houston; what would you rather have? 16 millimeter movies of Station 8 or TV movies of Station 8?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Well, good for them. I'm having a hard time keeping my lobster bisque in the bag up here.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Hey, that sounds like a tough life you've got there. [Long pause.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Dave, we copy that question. Stand by.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: (Getting a little frustrated) You know, by the time we stand by, and you get to a decision (lost under Joe)...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Roger; and we'll take TV; that's plenty good enough.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: ...squared away. Jim, let's...(Hearing Joe) Oh, okay. [Dave's tone of voice indicates that he is very pleased with the quick decision.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: And, Jim, you just get...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Fine.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: ...started with the trench there...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: We could turn the Rover around and...(Stops to listen to Joe)

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: ...And, Dave, once you get him started, we can begin with the drill.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, I guess we want to really start the trench first, Dave.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, let me get the gnomon. [Dave's level of frustration must not be very high because he playfully uses a hard, non-silent "g" when he says "gnomon".]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, and I'll get the comprehensive later, if we have a chance.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, Jim, and you...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: That's affirmative, Jim.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: ...you better...Boy. I better have your camera, because...Let's go out here where it's fresh. [Dave takes the gnomon to a spot about 8 to 10 meters northeast of the TV. Jim goes to his seat so that he can put the scoop down while he takes his camera off.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Let me take the camera off. (Pause)

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Bring it to me.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Well, just leave it there. Yeah, I'll take it, and I'll come do...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: You're coming by here anyway.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Just get me started,...

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: (Joking) I know, you want me to dig down to that bedrock.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Say again?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: I just stopped to look at the clock, Al, and I see that the [Imbrium lava] flow photos are coming up on us almost immediately, if you'd like to take them.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: You want me to dig down to bedrock.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Oh, that's...Yeah, that's down (Sun?). Yeah. Bedrock. You remember how the Rover would normally be.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, we need the pictures.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, I'll get it (meaning the CDR's camera, which Jim has been using). (Long Pause) [Dave skips to the Rover, circling around the undisturbed patch of ground he picked for the trenching.] 148:01:13 Scott: Okay. I got it (meaning the camera).

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Rog.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Dave, a couple of comments here, and Jim as well. We're going to be departing this site for the closeout in about 30 minutes. So you're looking real good on the time, and we'll just pick up whatever we can. No rush on any of it. Dave, you'll want to think a minute about where that (drill) treadle probably is. Video Clip 2 min 49 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, I think I know where it is, Joe. (Chuckles) I've been thinking. (Pause) [Dave turns and faces the gnomon and takes a stereopair of "before" photos, AS15-92- 12417 and 12418 .]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, Jim. Have at it, old buddy.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay, Dave. Thanks for getting me off to such a good start here.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Over there by the gnomon (Laughs).

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah. [Jim is standing east of the gnomon and Dave joins him. Jim starts to walk carefully toward the gnomon. I don't know if Jim was joking or being ironic or what. Certainly, he could have done what Dave just did.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: And take a little right turn there and let me get the down-Sun pre-picture here. [Jim steps out of the way to the north (his right) and Dave takes AS15-92- 12419 .]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: I've got it. Okay, have at it. (Almost singing) While I go find my favorite little piece of gear. I see it.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: You've got your favorite task and I've got mine.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, man. (Pause) [To dig the trench, Jim faces east, with his legs spread well apart. He holds the scoop with his right hand at the top and his left hand wrapped around the shaft. His hands are separated by a few inches. He plants the tip in the ground and then pulls it back, flipping a scoopful of dirt back between his legs. The idea is to create a vertical, sun-facing wall as he digs down as deep as practical. Three frames from Dave's pan show Jim as he digs.] [Irwin - "It was a small shovel, and it was just rather awkward to do it in the pressurized suit. If you look at the tape, I actual

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: As I look at the Flight Plan, I had that marked at 148 hours and 0 minutes. They must have given you a 5-minute pad[ding] there. [meaning extra time, not PreAdvisory Data] As I see your position on the Moon, you've got a while before you get there. Is that correct?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Right, Karl. That's the way it looks to me.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: I have you coming up on Hadley, right - Well, you've just passed Hadley, I guess.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1475841csm.text: Yes, that's right. I'm just going over Archimedes right now.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1475841csm.text: Righto.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Joe, do you only want it 12 inches deep?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: What ever you think's reasonable, Jim.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: I'm down that far already.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Boy, you do fast work. (Long Pause) [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Digging the trench went much faster than I had expected. I estimate (that), in five minutes I had the trench dug."] [At this point, Jim has only been digging for about a minute. He will finish at about 148:08:51 , after about 6 minutes 30 seconds of digging.] [Scott - "Jim's telling them that he's down 12 inches. We're not really conscious they're watching us. We never really think about that. So Jim is probably not conscious of them watching him dig. He's trying to tell them what he's doing."] [Jones - "Did they us

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: The wall that I'm...Too bad the TV's there, Joe. You can't see the (vertical, sunlit) wall. Too bad, (because) the wall is very smooth.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Now, you're bragging. [After a ten-second pause, Jim resumes digging. The timber of his voice gives clear indication that he is working hard. In the next 82 seconds, Jim digs 22 scoopfuls out of the trench. Because of the increasing depth of the trench and, most likely, increasing hand and forearm fatigue, Jim doesn't fling the dirt nearly as far as he did the early scoopfuls.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: The wall is fine, yet very cohesive. Video Clip 3 min 04 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Roger. And we'll stand by for a verbal description, in fact. (Pause) Any sign of layering?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: No signs of layering. I do find some small fragments: white fragments, black fragments. I just exposed a very small fragment about 3 millimeters of a black glass. But the wall that I've got here is only...No signs of layering at all.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Roger. (Pause) [Jones - "I can see why this is such hard work. Jim's using both hands he's been gripping the scoop for five minutes."] [Scott - "And he's gripping it way up at the top, 'cause you can't get down; so it's a long lever which puts a lot of force on his hands."] [Jones - "Plus having to bend both arms against the pressure of the suit."]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Tell me when you're ready for pictures, Jimmy.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: I think I'm just about ready, Dave.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Pause) Okay, let me take your pictures then.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Come over and see what you think. Check... [Jim stops digging as Dave joins him.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Oh no, I think that you're not getting the penetrometer all the way down there. It's a great trench.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: But not wide enough, you don't think? [The trench is about a meter long in the north-south direction.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: I don't think it'll be big enough for the ears.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Not long enough, huh? Okay. [The penetrometer is a soil mechanics experiment. As shown in Figure 7-1 from the Preliminary Science Report , the penetrometer is basically a long rod with a tip of known shape and size. Later, when Jim pushes the tip into the soil, a device at the top will measure the force he has to use, giving an indication of soil strength. He will make some measurements at the bottom of the trench and, consequently, the trench has to be big enough to accommodate the flat, metal plate - the "ears" - that supports the tip.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Yeah, I hate to tell you that. Sorry about that.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Do you want to make a bet on that one?

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1475841csm.text: Oh, yeah? (Long Pause) [Jim resumes digging and, in the next 77 seconds, gets 23 scoopfuls. Fendell pulls back on the zoom. Although Jim's hands are in shadow, it appears that, because of the depth of the trench, his left hand is now at the very top of the shaft.]

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: When I get down under the 12-inch layer, the surface is much harder, harder to dig through.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Copy that, Jim. [Irwin - "You know, when I dug that ditch, when I got down to about a foot, it was just a completely hard pan. I couldn't dig through it. I could scrape it with the sharp blade of the shovel but, you know, it was almost impossible to dig through it. I can imagine how difficult it would be to try to drill."] [Jones - "How much were you able to scrape off with the tip of the tool?"] [Irwin - "Very little. Just a foot down, it was like a layer of hardpan. It amazes me that we were able to get other (hammer-driven) core tubes in; and I can identify with Dave trying to drill into it

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: I also find more of the black glass fragments. Much more cohesive down about...(Pause) Well, we ought to get a good sample at the bottom of this.

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1475841csm.text: Yes, sir!

a15_1475841csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1475841csm.text: Boy, it's easy to make a flat bottom because it's so hard. I can see why Dave had a hard time drilling through it, now. (Long Pause) [Jim takes another short break.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: Karl, Endeavour. Just for your information, at the present time I'm right over Timocharis, and Lambert's coming up on - on the - just to the south of me, with Lambert R a very subdued ring just to the - to the south of Lambert. And the photos I want to take are over around the area of Mount La Hire and La Hire Rilles, a little bit west of Lambert.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: (Laughing) You know, Jim, I got a checklist on the left arm for one thing that's going on now, and a checklist on the right arm for something else that's going on now. [The checklist on Dave's right arm is the EVA-1 checklist from the previous day, covering the drilling activities which should have been long-since finished; and the one on his left arm is the EVA-2 checklist which covers Station 8. At 138:52:18, before they started EVA-2 preparations, CapCom Gordon Fullerton tolad them, "we suggest that you each wear your EVA-1 cuff checklist on your right arm for use at the end of EVA-2. That'

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480647csm.text: Wild, isn't it?

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: (Hearty laughter) Unreal. (Long Pause) [After a 15 second break, Jim starts extending the trench toward the south. He digs 14 scoopfuls in about 43 seconds.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1480647csm.text: We copy that.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: And, as a matter of fact, I have - Mount La Hire seems to be in view now and looks like I'm heading right at it.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1480647csm.text: Hey, as I look at the map here, it looks like about three - three hills with a crater in the top of each - look like volcanoes here although this map is lousy from that point of view. What do they look like to you?

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Okay. (Probably reading from the checklist) "Change 16". (Long Pause) Okay. It looks like the Echo magazine worked okay. [Members of some of the other crews tended to read aloud from their checklists. Dave and Jim hardly ever do. EVA-2 checklist page CDR-19 lists "LMP: change 16-mm mag".] [Jim takes about a 10-second break and then resumes digging.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480647csm.text: Well, I can see a - the - the - they're a chain of hills - ridges, and I can't see much more than that from here right now.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1480647csm.text: Rog.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1480647csm.text: Roger, Dave. Was that from you?

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Yes, sir. That's from me, and I'm going to put Foxtrot on the 16.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1480647csm.text: Okay, beautiful.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Do this according to Hoyle. (Long Pause) [The expression refers to Hoyle's Rules of Games ; but, here, Dave means the checklist.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1480647csm.text: Jim, that's a beautiful trench. Let's stop with that one and document it. We'll want samples from the bottom please.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480647csm.text: Gee, I think I've hit bedrock. I think I've hit the bedrock! [Scott - "He's trying to hit bedrock. He thinks he's getting down there 'cause it's getting harder. And if you hit bedrock, that's a big deal, right?"] [Jim steps back from the trench, having gotten another 13 scoopfuls out in the last 40 seconds.] 148:08:51 Irwin: Okay, Dave, you want to...

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Yeah, I'm coming over right now. (Garbled) the right time. [Dave may be saying that the tasks he decided to do around the Rover took just the right amount of time so that he would be ready to take pictures when Jim finished lengthening the trench.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1480647csm.text: Dave, you might want to bring the SESC (Special Environmental Sample Container) from under the seat.

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1480647csm.text: Okay, Joe. (Long Pause) [As shown in Judy Allton's Apollo Tool Catalog, the SESC is 12.7 cm tall and has an inside diameter of 6 cm. It has a knife-edge vacuum seal like those on the rock boxes. In the picture, the seal is covered by a Teflon seal protector. Photo AS12-49- 7278 shows Al Bean holding an SESC during the second Apollo 12 EVA.] [The TV picture jiggles as Dave gets the can. Jim is resting.]

a15_1480647csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480647csm.text: I'll take a break while you photo, Dave. [Jim walks off-camera to the right, going slowly to avoid kicking dirt back into the trench.] 148:09: Scott: Probably a good idea. Good idea! I'll come do some photos then. Ohh! That's a neat trench. [Dave gets into position east of the trench.]

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480937csm.text: Okay, Karl. If you're following on the map, I'm right south of the intersection of the La Hire Rilles and the wrinkle ridge [Dorsum Zirkel] that runs off to the northwest there, just by Mount La Hire. In fact, I'm directly over Mount La Hire now, and it looks like there's a volcano in - or not a volcano, but a crater, in the top of the western-most hill.

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: Do you think it's long enough? 148:09:39 Scott: Oh, yeah!! That's just super. (Pause) [Dave adjusts the focus and f-stop settings on the camera.]

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: I really do think I'm almost down to bedrock. It really is hard.

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1480937csm.text: Yeah, we ought to have some good sample there from the bottom. (Long Pause) [Dave positions himself northeast of the trench.] Video Clip 3 min 24 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPG ) MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 21 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15_1480937csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1480937csm.text: And I'm starting to take some pictures to the west now.

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: It looks like it has a little color change down there, too. [Dave takes a stereopair, AS15-92- 12439 and 12440 . He then changes the camera settings.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Yeah, maybe a slight...Seems to get a little darker...A little lighter, then a little darker. (Pause) [Dave gets into position to take down-Sun pictures of the trench.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: A shadow in the way here. (Pause) [Dave takes a half step to his right and takes a stereopair, AS15-92- 12441 and 12442 .]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: I have the photos. [Dave has been carrying the SESC in his left hand and, while Jim talks to Houston, takes the top off.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: Walls are just about vertical on the trench, Joe.

a15a1481011.speaker: Irwin
a15a1481011.text: (To Dave) Three quarters full. 148:10:44 Scott: Yes, sir. (Pause)

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: Okay, Dave and Jim. Jim, we think you can collect the samples here pretty well. And, Dave, in order to get that drill task accomplished, we're going to have to get you started on that shortly. [During Joe's transmission, Jim positioned himself southeast of the trench and, with some difficulty, dug a scoopful of soil out of the bottom of the trench. While he was digging the trench, he scraped soil out without having to penetrate very far. Here, he has to push the scoop into the soil and that is a more difficult task.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: Okay, he can't get the SESC very well by himself, I don't think, Joe. It's tough for two of us to get. (Pause) [Dave is standing north of the trench and holds the SESC out at about waist height.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: Okay. When you finish that, press on with the drill.

a15a1481011.speaker: Scott
a15a1481011.text: (To Jim) Okay, rotate it a little bit. (Pause) [Jim couldn't raise the scoop handle high enough to pour the dirt out of the end and, at Dave's suggestions, rotates it around a horizontal axis to pour the dirt out the side.]

a15a1481011.speaker: Allen
a15a1481011.text: And while you're looking down in there, how deep do you think it is now? [Jim gets another scoopful and, after he gets the tip of the scoop balanced on the top of the can - spilling about half of the dirt in the process - he raises the handle with a rotation of his left shoulder. Evidently, Jim puts some downward force on the can.] 148:11:51 Scott: (To Jim) Easy, don't lean the handle on me, I'll drop it. It (meaning the can)'s too slippery. I need one more.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Al, can you clarify a little more exactly where you're photographing. I see a wrinkle ridge running northwest toward Caroline Herschel from the La Hire Rilles, so this is where I'd guess you're working. Is that correct? [Pause.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: (Answering Joe) Oh, I'd say it's 14 (to) 16 inches deep, Joe.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Extraordinary. Thank you. (Pause) [Jim gets a third scoopful and, although his body hides most of the scoop, he seems to use a pouring technique more like the one he used for the first scoopful than the second.] Video Clip 3 min 1 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, babe. Can you tilt it up? Got it. (Pause) White clast in there. A little bit more; keep coming. Good job.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Negative. That's the large wrinkle ridge running off toward C. Herschel. No, I'm working directly west of La Hire Rilles in that open area out there. Say on a line between Euler and Heis.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Think we got enough.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Yes, sir. We got 75 percent full.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Outstanding. [Dave removes the Teflon seal protector and drops it on the ground next to the trench. The tranch sample is 15014 , consisting of 333 grams of soil.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Dave) Okay, you're going to leave me, and I'll sample it myself. I guess I'll fill the bags myself then. [As indicated on LMP-17, Jim will get samples from various depths in the trench wall.] [Dave removes the seal protector from the lid and drops it on the ground next to the first protector.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. I copy.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: I guess you'll have to.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. [While Dave puts the top on the can, Jim walks to the Rover.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: And there's nothing particularly significant that you can see on the map there. It's just that the La Hire Rilles seem to be associated with a lot of those flows, and the flows - there's so many of them, and they're so overlapping and intermingling that I just want to get some general pictures of those flows coming out of La Hire.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. (Brief pause) Unless you want to go do the drill.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Not at all, brother! You got her. I'll do all the...(Pause) Why don't you loan me your checklist.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: LM Crew
a15_1481159csm.text: (Sustained, hearty laughter at the thought of Jim with three cuff checklists)

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Oh, yeah! (Jim continues laughing) Guess what!

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah, I...(Stops to laugh) Oh, I think I can get...Joe'll talk me through it. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "You did all the penetrometer yourself. That was an interesting departure from our pre-flight plan, because we had planned to do the Station 8 together. I had all the procedures in my checklist (see CDR-17 to 19), since (in the planned Station 8) I just walked you through them. Apparently, you made out all right without having all those detailed procedures."] [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I had just enough abbreviated details (see LMP-17 to 19) that I could follo

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. That sounds like a very interesting region, and I see over by Diophantus there, you've got some very prominent rilles at the present time that probably are just on the - on the terminator, aren't they?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Yes, Karl. I'm - I'm beyond the terminator now.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: (Answering Dave) Any one's fine.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: ...for now so I can get going. (Hearing Joe) No; (you're) too late. [Jim is still standing at his seat and, off-camera, Dave may be trying to put the SESC in Jim's SCB.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Get up. Jim?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. Nothing; press on. [Dave's transmission at 148:14:39 suggests that he has given up on the attempt to get the SESC in Jim's SCB.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe, I'm going to do a little (laughing) sampling of the trench.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Next time you get the Flight Plan in hand, let me give you the T-start for the zodiacal light photography.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: I hear you. (Pause)

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (If I can) just hang on to the (individual sample) bags. (Pause) [Jim has dropped the sample bag and, rather than waste time retrieving it, returns to the Rover to get another.] 148:14:11 Scott: (Garbled) A little unorthodox. I'm going to drill. Watch me.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. 148:34:26 is the zodiacal light photo PAD.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Houston) Probably won't be quite as much of a sample here, since I'm doing it myself, Joe. [Jim walks to the trench and, initially, kicks some dust ahead of him. However, when he gets close to the trench, he slows and is even more careful to lift his feet and gets into position without kicking any noticeable amount of dust into the trench.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Understand, 148:34:26.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: That's affirmative. [Long pause.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Dave, is the SESC stowed now? QuickTime Clip (0 min 52 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Oh, it's in a seat pan right now; we'll get to it later, Joe.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: That's fine. That's a perfect place; couldn't have suggested any better myself.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Good. [Jim extends the scoop into the trench with his right arm. He has virtually all of his weight on his right leg but has his left leg and his left arm back for balance. During Joe's next transmission, Jim raises the scoop and, holding the sample bag out from his left hip, moves his right hand out to his right until he gets the scoop head in the bag. He then pours the sample into the bag without difficulty. On Apollo 17, Jack Schmitt had considerable difficulty with this maneuver and had to learn how to get a grip lower on the scoop handle. Part of the difference in experience may be due to

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: And D(avid). R., as you probably know already, all we need from this EVA is really the hole in the ground. The drill (battery) will probably give out on us during your rest period. And, if need be, we can pull up whatever you get later on.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe. Fine.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: You wouldn't want to go on towards the North Complex without visiting the ALSEP site again, would you? Video Clip 2 min 41 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Say again, Endeavour.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Shoot, no. Never! (Pause) [Jim got a second scoopful of soil from the bottom of the trench into the bag and, now, walks to the Rover.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: Go ahead.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Disregard, Al. I thought I heard you call, and it was just something else in the background, I guess.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe. The soil samples from the bottom of the trench is in 252.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: 252; great. (Pause) And, Dave and Jim, we're coming up on fifteen minutes, "one-five" minutes, before closeout.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Jim is busy drigging [sic] - digging trenches there by the LM, and he just about dug a hole big enough to - to build a swimming pool in. He did a good job. [Long pause.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Doing our best, Joe.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger, and you've done yeoman service. (Pause) [Fendell followed Jim and we get a relatively good look as he seals the bag, puts it down, and gets another. Dave is at the back of the Rover getting two drill stems out of an SCB and joining them together. See page 33 in the A15 Final Lunar Surface Procedures ( 9 Mb PDF ).]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: I have to get in your way there, old buddy.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: I'll get out of here.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah, that'd be a good idea. I need to use this area. [Dave goes to Jim's seat with the drill stem. He probably has the drill sitting on Jim's seat.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Can you see as far south as the Carpathian Mountains, Al?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Joe, I'm going to skip sampling the side (of the trench), I'm just going to sample the top over here.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Jim. Sounds good, if you don't see layering.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: So I can get on with the penetrometer.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jim had planned to get samples from the bottom of the trench, from the middle of the vertical wall, and from the top. The absence of obvious layering suggests that the soil is well mixed and that the wall sample would not add to the amount of information gained from the samples.] [Jim takes a sample from the trench wall at a depth of 5 to 10 cm (2 to 4 inches).] [Dave takes up a position east of the trench. He is carrying the drill and the treadle, which is a flat plate with a hole in the center to accommodate the drill stems. He drops the treadle and tries to get it level

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1481159csm.text: That's negative, Karl. I'm in - I'm - I'm beyond the terminator now in total darkness.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: Right.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1481159csm.text: If you - if your orbit ever brings you far enough south to look at those Carpathian Mountains, I should think that would be pretty interesting. I - well, you probably know better than I, I guess, that's probably an overflow of Procellarum into Imbrium there. Probably sort of - well, if that's true, it should have the appearance of the front edge of a lava flow, although it is a tremendous thing.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Shadows really make a difference up here. [On Earth, dust in the air scatters enough light that shadows aren't really very dark. Here, Dave is still trying to get the treadle in a good position and, when the shadow of his foot falls on the treadle, he has trouble seeing what he's doing. He finally gets it in postion so that, when he steps on it, it will remain steady.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe; the top of the trench, 253. QuickTime Clip (1 min 45 sec) by Peter Dayton

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger; 253.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Hey, Jim, you're in the way of the (16-mm) camera, old buddy. [We can just see the treadle under Jim's PLSS.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Am I stealing your picture?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah; if we're going to use all that (16-mm) film...

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: I got to get some bags here, man. [Jim moves a step closer to the Rover and unblocks Dave, who grabs the drill handles and then lets out a mild oath when the treadle moves. He will emplace six 40-cm drill stems and, to start, has two of them already assembled.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: (a the treadle moves from under his right foot) Oh, shoot.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: (Responding to Dave) That's fine. We can still see (with the TV). 148:17:39 Irwin: (Responding to Joe) Dave's talking about the other one. [Dave seems to push the stems into the ground about 6 inches, although he may have had the drill running. Penetration is then steady and, in under seven seconds, gets about half of the string of two drill stems into the ground. He then realizes that he is still wearing a camera, takes it off so that it won't get in his way, and takes it toward the Rover.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, I'm going for the penetrometer. (Pause) Video Clip 3 min 7 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Your (70-mm Hasselblad) camera's in your seat pan if you need it. [Readers will remember that this is actually Dave's camera.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: No, I don't think I'll...I can't take pictures and do penetrometer at the same time.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: (Joking) Why not?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Sorry about that. [Dave gets about 30 cm of core into the ground in two short bursts of drilling of about 4 seconds each.] [Scott - (Tongue-in-cheek) " You know, with all my training and all my experience, I've never had a chance to use my drill talents since? You'd think somebody would invite me out to drill."]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Dave, you'll get a warning horn and you'll want to go over to your Aux Water shortly. Just wanted to advise you.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: (Grunting as he leans down) Okay, Joe. Thank you. [Dave steps on the treadle and tries to remove the drill by rotating it. As with the heat flow drilling, he has no luck.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: And, Dave, you'll want it to drop (meaning "drill" or "penetrate") into the ground as slowly as you can easily control.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Oh, I forgot! I'm sorry. Just in a hurry to get it done, and I just forgot your one inch per second; and I'll do that. (Pause) (With a touch of self-criticism) Some days... [Dave got about 70 cm of core into the ground in about 16 seconds of drilling. That works out to about 17 inches per second, nearly twice the desired rate.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "As I started out, the soil was very soft, and the drill went very easily and too fast down to the bedrock. The ground gave a call on the rates, which I had forgotten in my haste to finish up the drill. We were supposed to go an

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Hey, Jim? Jim, would you get my Aux Water?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: I just can't feel in there. [There are three controls on the bottom, right-front corner of the PLSS . The feedwater control is on the outside and is easiest to reach. The Aux water and oxygen controls - which are on/off switches that are rarely used - are harder to reach and, here, Dave needs some help. The three controls have different shapes so they can be distinguished by feel.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "My fingers are probably not in very good shape for feeling at this stage."]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah, I know what you mean. [Jim joins Dave, carrying the penetrometer and, in a matter of a second or so, changes the Aux Water switch.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. It's on. You want me to put you on Min Cooling at the same time?

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: No, I got the Min Cooling part, I just couldn't feel the Aux Water.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay. I can get it; I'm right here.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: No, I got the Min Cooling.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Oh, okay. (Pause) [Jim returns to the Rover and Dave returns to the problem of removing the drill. He turns it in the hole, again with no success.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: (Chuckles) (Pause) Oh, my! (Pause) [Dave goes to the Rover to get what appears to be a UHT (Universal Handling Tool). During the next minute or so, Fendell has some trouble figuring out where to point the TV. He follows Dave to the Rover but, because his reaction time is necessarily slow, Dave is gone by the time Fendell gets there. He then reverses direction but overshoots the drill and stops with the camera pointed at the trench. Just as Jim arrives with the penetrometer, Fendell reverses direction again and ends up - at about 148:20:49 - with Jim at the left edge and Dave at the right edge

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Cable's caught on the (treadle) collar.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. [Dave may be referring to the loop cable he uses to carry the drill. With the drill pointed down, the cable drags on the ground and on the treadle.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Joe, I have the half-inch cone installed (on the penetrometer), and I'm going to...It's sitting on 1, I'm going to index it to 2. [Jim is probably talking about the recording drum at the top of the instrument. There are a number of recording positions and, apparently, Jim is going to start with position 2.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Jim. Dave, as soon as you get that (cable) unstuck, you'll want to back it off one and one-half turns. It'll come loose. [Dave clears the cable and sticks the UHT in the ground to his left.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: I know, Joe. (Pause) You can't bend over as far here as you can in one g. (Pause) [Off-camera, Dave starts to remove the drill.] Video Clip 2 min 47 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Joe, I hope you can watch this on TV. The ground plate...I pull it down; and the spring is too strong. It pulls the ground plate up. [During Jim's last transmission, Fendell re-aimed the TV to get both astronauts in the field-of-view and, with Houston watching, Dave removed the drill with relatively little difficulty.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, Jim, we watch. No problem. [Before Jim finishes adjusting the ground plate, Fendell shifts his aim to concentrate on Dave.] [With the cable out of the way, Dave has no trouble removing the drill.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: The ground plate's there. Maybe it'll stay there...

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: That's no problem. [As Dave puts the drill down, Fendell re-aims the TV at Jim, who is on the north side of the trench.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: ...And I'm doing the one adjacent...I'm doing it adjacent to the trench...

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: ...right here. And I'm pushing. (Pause) I'm bottomed out.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. [Jim did the first penetrometer test at the north end of the trench. As he puts the penetrometer down, he just has his right hand on the shaft just above the recording drum and, although Fendell zooms in on the ground plate, there is no change in Jim's leg positions that would indicate that he went to two hands.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: These (ground-plate) prints might stay here, Dave, so I can photograph them later.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (The imprints will show) where I took it. Okay; that was adjacent to the trench. [Fendell pulls back on the zoom and we see Jim adjusting the recording drum.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: I'm indexing to 3; and I'm going to do the trench bottom. [Jim pulls on the ground plate to get it out to the end of the shaft again. The ground plate had slid up the shaft when Jim raised the tip to get at the recording drum.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Beautiful. And, Dave, you might check your (16-mm) film mag, if you're back at the Rover now. See if it's run out. (Pause) And I'm talking about the DAC...

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: No, it wouldn't have run out by now, Joe. (Responding to Joe's last sentence) That's what I'm saying. It wouldn't have run out by now. I just turned it on; 12 frames per second, and it looks like it's 90 percent gone.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay, beautiful; outstanding.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: And, hey, I need a call when my sublimator gets going, Joe. [Dave wants to have more cooling than the minimum setting provides.] [Jim has carefully placed the ground plate in the trench and, this time, appears to use two hands, probably expecting to meet greater resistance.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: Okay; I'm in the trench bottom, and I'm pushing. And I'm bottomed out. [Although, once again, Fendell has zoomed in and we only see the bottom of Jim's legs, the fact that his left legs slips backwards right at the end suggests that he put his full weight on the shaft. Jim removes the penetrometer from the trench and resets the drum.]

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: Roger. And, Dave, the diverter valve is yours.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1481159csm.text: Thank you!

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Joe) Okay, I'm starting for (drum index position) 4.

a15_1481159csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1481159csm.text: (To Dave) Okay, verify flags for me, please. MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 34 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah. The water flag's clear, Joe. (Going to higher cooling) Ohh, that feels so good! [The Sun is currently about 30 degrees above the horizon and, from Figure 9-9 in the Apollo 17 Preliminary Science Report , we can estimate that the current surface temperature is about 50 C or 120 F.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, I'm going for the Rover tracks.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Jim moves up-Sun, going slow enough that Fendell has no trouble following. As Jim passes behind Dave, we see that Dave has threaded two more drill-stem sections on the string in the ground and is attaching the drill.] [Jim stops behind the Rover to make the next penetrometer measurement.] Video Clip 2 min 47 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, I'm on the very freshest Rover tracks...(Pause)

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: The very freshest.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: (Garbled) And I'm pushing.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger. [Jim has both hands on the extension handle and, as he pushes, moves both feet back, getting up on his toes as he puts his weight on the instrument.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I've bottomed out. (Long Pause)

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I'm indexing to 5.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Pause) And, Dave and Jim...

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: And the one adjacent (to the Rover tracks)

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: ...it's coming up on 5 minutes remaining before close out.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Fendell zooms in on a dark patch on the surface NNE of the right-rear Rover wheel.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, adjacent to the Rover tracks. (Pause) Pushing.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) Bottomed out. (Pause) We don't want to leave here before I get a chance to collapse my trench, Joe.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: You've got 5 minutes, Jim. Play it accordingly; and I thought that was my job. [This is obviously a training reference. Jim will attach a fixed plate to the penetrometer and will measure the amount of force it takes to collapse the trench wall by pushing on the surface a short distances from the wall.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: (Chuckles) (Pause) Okay, I'm going for the plate.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [While Jim goes to the Rover, Fendell aims the TV at Dave, who is twisting the drill off the drill string. Dave grabs the wire loop, puts the drill on the ground, and heads for the Rover.] 148:25:25 Scott: I see why we planned all this before we came. (Pause) [Scott - "One of the more fun parts of the whole mission was the planning. Certainly the geology planning was fun. In the crew quarters, at night, we worked on all these traverses. Doing all the planning and putting everything to fit together, that was a lot of fun. Lot of guys involved."] [Jones - "And you were an act

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay; the plate's installed.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger, Jim. [The plate is the small, rectangular object on the tip of the penetrometer shaft.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Did I index it after the last one, Joe?

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Say again.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I don't think I indexed it after the last one.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay. Try it again. No problem. We've got several...

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I'm index... [Jim walks slowly toward the trench as he adjusts the recording drum. Dave bounds past him with a joined pair of drill stem sections.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Index it again. Video Clip 2 min 44 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I'm indexing to six.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: I'm indexing to six here for the trench bottom.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Fendell is watching Dave as he threads the drill-stem pair on the string in the ground.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay; here goes it for trench bottom.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: It bottomed out.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave's breathing is intermittently audible. Dave is still having trouble getting the stems threaded.] [Jones - "The thing that amazes me is that the threads on those cores really had a big pitch. In shirtsleeves, it's trivial to get those things attached. I've tried it and it's easy. But standing there at the end of that lever arm, wearing those gloves with the huge fingers..."] [Scott - "Yeah. And you've got to move the suit. The suit's good, but you still have to move against it (and) overcome the pressure."] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "I got all the sectio

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Indexing to seven. 148:27:01 Allen: Roger. (Long Pause) [Just before Jim's next transmission, Dave finally gets the drill stems threaded. At some point during his struggles, he knocks the drill over but, this time, has no trouble bobbing down to get it. He doesn't quite go to his knees.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay; I'm going to be collapsing the trench side. I hope. (Long Pause) [Dave threads the drill on the drill string and, as Fendell zooms in on the treadle, Dave steps on the treadle and starts to drill.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay. I'm about four inches out from the side of the trench. (Pause) And I'm pushing. (Pause) It's bottomed out. A slight amount of collapse.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: It won't collapse?

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) I'm continuing to push. Yup. It just collapsed.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: ...collapsed. I'll take a quick picture here so you can see the location of all of those. (Long Pause) [Jim passes in front of the TV on his way to the back of the Rover where he will remove the extension handle and stow the penetrometer.] Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPG )

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Dave, are you working on the last stem there?

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: You are one fast worker. (Pause) [Dave's breathing is can be heard again. After about 57 seconds of drilling, Dave comes close to finishing the last two sections. Probably following Houston's request to let the drill go in slowly, his average rate for this 80 cm was about 1.4 cm/s or 0.6 inches/s. Dave relaxes his grip and hops back to rest. When Fendell pulls back on the zoom, we see Dave leaning forward with his arms hanging down.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. Take a breather. And I've got one last instruction for you here. Using the drill, we want you to break it loose (meaning "free the drill string in the hole") and then let the drill and the stem sit there in the surface and we'll pull it out later.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Okay. Let me finish it off. (Long Pause) [Dave starts drilling again and completes the remaining 20 to 30 cm. When he steps back, the drill chuck is only a few centimeters off the ground.] 148:29:26 Allen: And just leave the drill on stem, handle away from the Sun, as long as flutes pull free. [Joe's "flutes" is difficult to understand. He may, in fact, have said "lutes".]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: As long as what?

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Rog. As long as the threads pull free from the hole.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah. Well, we'll try that now. [Dave leans forward and grabs the drill handles. He pulls up sharply, raising the drill perhaps 20 cm.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: (Grunts) Ahh, we can get it! Okay, Joe; we're in good shape.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. We want the handle away from the Sun. And we're ready for you to get back on the Rover.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Wait a minute Joe. [Dave grabs the drill again, gets his feet on either side of the drill stem and twice uses his legs to pull up on the drill. He ends up with the chuck just below knee height.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: (Grunting) I'm not sure I'll ever get it out. (Pause) What bothers me, Joe, is...Okay. Handle away from the Sun. (Pause) (The battery) box is sort of dirty. [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "When I got the drill all the way in, I attempted to pull it out and, not surprisingly, it was very difficult to pull out. We expected that from our training. In certain cases during training, people observing in shirtsleeves couldn't get the drill out of the ground at the Cape. I wasn't at all surprised to find that, after having drilled through bedrock, I couldn't pull the drill out. I got maybe

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Get pictures of the drill will you, Jim? Take...Go...Hey, just south of the drill, I really need a (locator)...I already did a pan here. Get your trench (pictures) and get a couple of pictures of the drill to show its position.

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay.

a15a1482253.speaker: Allen
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Jim. A few pictures and you can walk back and, Dave, we want you to start on the Rover, please.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah, Joe. I'm on the way. 148:31:11 Allen: Okay. (Long Pause) [Fendell stops his pan to look at the Central Station. Note how little of Hill 305 is visible beyond the local horizon. As with LM visibility near Station 4, the fact that relatively little of the mountain is visible is probably due to local terrain.] [Jim takes only one picture, AS15-92- 12443 , which is a down-Sun after of the collapsed trench.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Dave. I think everything...You're not going to drive too fast are you?

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Heck no. [Fendell resumes his pan.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Okay, I'll meet you back there.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Yeah. (Pause) Much dust when you drive fast. [Jim is concerned about the possibility of getting sprayed with dust as Dave drives by him.]

a15a1482253.speaker: Irwin
a15a1482253.text: Keep it clean.

a15a1482253.speaker: Scott
a15a1482253.text: Okay, Joe, you going back PM1/WB . (Long Pause; heavy static which continues until noted below) [TV off.] Heat Flow Reprise Apollo 15 Journal EVA-2 Closeout

a15a1483216.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483216.text: Okay, Joe, I'm back at the LM. (Pause)

a15a1483216.speaker: Allen
a15a1483216.text: (Making a rare mis-identification because of the static) Okay, Dave, copied you back at the LM, parking the Rover normally, and we're standing by for TV again.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The Rover boys have finished their tasks - most of their tasks with the ALSEP, and they are just now beginning ingress into the LM. Dave managed to get the core drill completely in; and, although he hasn't pulled it out yet, he'll pull it out on the next EVA. The time to set the mission timer, or to set your countdown for the zodiacal light photos is going to be about in one minute. And the word down here is that all of your systems are Go; everything's looking super.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: No, that's Jim. Jim is back. I don't know, Dave might be close.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: I'm getting on the Rover now Jim. I'm just parking your TV for you. (Long Pause)

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: (Static fades) Hey, Dave, you do have some cores now to go in the SRC. Is that right?

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: No.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: No?

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: Roger, Karl. Thank you very much. See you on the other side. And, if you'll check my DSKY, you'll see I got the time count down there too.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: No, Jim, I didn't get them out yet.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Okay. Well, I guess I'll go ahead and put the bag that I have here in SRC 2.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: Very good.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1483228csm.text: Jim, if you can get the SESC in there that would be great, and then go ahead and close out that rock box. (Pause) No problem on those drill stems, we'll get them later. (Long Pause) And, Dave, this is Houston. If there's dust on the LRV Batt(ery) covers, brush it off before you open them, please.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: And I'm even managing to finish my lunch. Thank you.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: That is a soft life up there, when you get a chance to finish your lunch.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1483228csm.text: You better believe it. Some times it's not so easy.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1483228csm.text: I can believe it.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: Okay, Joe. (Looking at CDR-21) I guess we head north, cross-Sun, remember. (Pause)

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Is that right? Put it in your parking place.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: Huh?

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Put it in your parking place here.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: Yeah. This is north, cross-Sun isn't it.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1483228csm.text: What I thought. (Pause) There's north, cross-Sun. Okay. How's that, Jim, is that okay for you?

a15_1483228csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1483228csm.text: Good. (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 23 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Dave, this is Houston.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Go ahead.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Roger, Dave. While you're brushing the LRV BAT covers, you might as well give the whole area a good dusting and cleaning. The LCRU covers, the TCU, the television camera, please.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Be glad to, Joe. (Pause) Taking three up this time, Jim?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Huh? 148: Scott: This go in that bag? 148: Irwin: Yeah. Just put all those rocks - I can get those, Dave.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, here's one for you. I'll set it right up by your camera. Okay?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Jim, are you packing the rock box yet?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Yeah; I am.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Did you happen to get a number off the SESC?

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: No, I didn't. But, shoot, you ought to be able to track that one, Joe.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: We'll track it. No problem. (Long Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, Dave, we assume that you're dusting and cleaning now; and we'll be standing by for TV.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Well, okay, Joe. I'm not sure I'm going to take the time to give you the TV, unless you really need it.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Dave, we've got a lot of time. We're going to deploy the flag now and we need the TV please. (Jim laughs)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe.

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: And, we're in good shape on the time. We're back at the LM; and we've got a lot of time to work with. So no problem.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe. Why don't you just give us about five minutes with no comments and let us just cool it for a while. Okay? [Houston has handled this situation badly. At the very least, they should have taken a few minutes during the drive back to explain what was contemplated, rather than feed one revision at a time, keeping the crew in the dark about the schedule for the rest of the EVA. The disruption caused by the drilling problems has been frustrating enough and, having rushed to get things done in expectation of an immediate close out, to be told now that "we've got a lot of time", must have be

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Roger. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Cool it, Jim. Just take it easy. Take a break. That's enough.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: We've got plenty of time. We're going to cool it right now.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Okay. (Pause) I'm having the same problem with that SRC today as I did yesterday. I had to pound on the handle to get it sealed. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, well just take your time.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Well, I'm not rushing.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Use these five minutes as part of our rest period tonight. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Dave and Jim, while you're taking a breather there, let me make a comment. We've got 37 minutes before repress. So we're in good shape on the time. And just for your own information - I know you're curious - your oxygen consumption has been considerably less today - considerably less - and we're running well over a seven-hour PLSS capability.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Okay, Joe. Very good. Just give us five minutes with a nothing, will you? (Pause) Just (to) make sure we've got a good last twenty-seven minutes. [Having made his point, Dave relaxes quickly.]

a15a1483501.speaker: Allen
a15a1483501.text: Yes, sir. (Pause)

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: Dave, I going to get you to give me a hand with this.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Sure.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: It's almost a two-man operation. (Pause) Bring it over here.

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Huh? Want to go to the MESA table? Let's go to the MESA table.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: No, its...Well...

a15a1483501.speaker: Scott
a15a1483501.text: Yeah, it's easier to work with; it's higher. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1483501.speaker: Irwin
a15a1483501.text: If you can push down on it, I'll lock it. You might have to hit it down.

Because of the tilt of the Earth and of the Moon's orbit, at this moment the Moon is directly over the southern tip of Africa. Readers should note that this figure includes LCRU usage and an unknown level of uncertainty. Of relevance here is the fact that the indicated use rate is much less than the pre-flight prediction of 3.67 amp-hours/km. See, also, the discussion at 167:35:58 .
