a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Isn't that a neat picture?

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Get little...(Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: (Garbled)

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Try another setting. How about an f/8?

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah, try f/8.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Leave it at...

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: ...f/11, there.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah. That's what it called for in the...

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Yeah. (Pause) Okay, I'm taking you again, boss.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Okay. [The TV image brightens as Dave salutes.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Oh, you look colorful.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: How about that? Even with the dirt, huh? (Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Okay. [Dave hops off camera to the left.] [Jim took four pictures of Dave, AS15-92- 12448 to 12451 . Frame 12451 is the best of these. Note the footprints and Rover tracks in the crater to Dave's right. This is the last surface picture on magazine 92. The remainder of the magazine was used in orbit.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: You like that flag there, Joe?

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: It's beautiful.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah. We think it's pretty nice, too. (Long Pause) [Dave crosses in front of the TV, headed for the LM.] [Note the slight motion of the lower righthand corner of the flag after Dave passes. Journal Contributors have suggested a number of possible causes: (1) Dave could have brushed against the flag with his left arm as he went by; (2) he could have kicked some dirt with his boot that hit the bottom of the flag; (3) he could have pushed a mound of soil sideways with his boot that pushed against the flagstaff ; (4) the impact of his boots on the ground as he ran past could have shaken the flagst

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: (To Houston) Can we get in now?

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: Jim, you're coming up on feedwater tone, probably.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: What else have you got for us, Joe? (No answer) (Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: (To himself) Okay.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: That was good timing, Joe. I've got it. [Fendell pans right, looking for Dave and Jim at the LM.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Dave will you put me on...

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Get my (feedwater) diverter valve, too, to Min if you would.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Sure. Diverter valve's to Min; Aux Water is Open. Okay, we got everything? Video Clip 3 min 56 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 35 Mb MPG )

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Think we do.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Now to start back in. [Fendell finds Dave and Jim at the MESA.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: Okay...

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Okay.

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: ...Dave and Jim, we know you've dusted off our TV gear, we want you to open the LRV Batt covers, please. And give us a status check...

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: All right; what do you want...

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: ...of the battery mirrors. Mainly, are they dusty or not?

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Good thought. [Dave goes to the front of the Rover; Jim goes to the back.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Let me wait until I get a good startup on mine, Dave.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Okay.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: I might go to Intermediate (cooling) for getting in.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Not a bad idea. [Jim wants to make sure that his PLSS cooling system is fully functional before he climbs the ladder.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: We got to dust each other off, too.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Yeah, I need to dust these battery covers, too.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Okay, I'll bring the brush around. (Long Pause) [Dave goes to Jim's seat and leans in front of the TV as he raises the battery covers. By opening the covers, Dave will expose the cooling mirrors to deep space. Don McMillan has provided an animation ( 0.8 Mb ) of the battery covers on a his Virtual Rover being opened.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: (Struggling with a battery cover) It's really glued. (Pause) Oh, my! There, it's open. (Pause) Oh, Jim, the maps! I almost forgot the maps. [Dave grabs the maps off the clip next to Jim's handhold and heads for the MESA so that he can put them in the ETB.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: Dave, this is Houston.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: Roger, Dave. I think you still need the mag from the DAC and from the 500-millimeter camera. [The ETB is hanging off the front of the MESA. Dave opens the ETB and stows the maps.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: No, they're both in here, Joe. And I called them both out. Both tucked away in ETB. (Long Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: One of the mirrors is cracked, huh?

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Which one?

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: (On top of the) TV.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Really!?

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: Yeah. [Dave uses the skip stride as he runs out to join Jim at the front of the Rover.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: (I didn't) see that? Yeah! Two little squares. (Long Pause) [Jim comes into view at his seat and reaches across in front of the TV, probably dusting the batteries.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Oh, we've got to turn the (16-mm) camera around too, Jim.

a15a1484757.speaker: Allen
a15a1484757.text: Okay, Jim, your diverter valve ...

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Turn the DAC around to point...(Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: (Responding to Joe) My option now (on the PLSS cooling), huh? Okay. (Pause)

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Okay, let's head on in, Jim.

a15a1484757.speaker: Irwin
a15a1484757.text: (I) knocked one of the covers down.

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Here, let me dust you off; you're dirty. Let's head on in. (Long Pause) [Jim joins Dave at the back of the Rover and hands him the dustbrush . Most of the following dusting operation takes place off-camera to the left. All we see is about half of Jim. Dave is undoubtedly standing in a position from which he is dusting the sunlit surfaces of Jim's suit.]

a15a1484757.speaker: Scott
a15a1484757.text: Okay, turn around to your left. Hold onto you here. (Long Pause) Okay. That's most of it. (Pause) [Jim now has the dustbrush . Dave is standing between Jim and the LM and we can see Jim wielding the brush with his right hand, which is just in view. He is using short, quick strokes.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 8 min 54 sec ) by David Shaffer Video Clip 2 min 12 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 19 Mb MPG )

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: How did your front get so dirty? Oh, I know. (You) pulled an Irwin. (Long Pause) [This is a reference to Jim's fall during the Rover deployment at about 120:16:05 . The phrase "pull an Irwin" was also used during Apollo 17.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: And, Dave and Jim, while you're doing the dusting there, did you get a check on the LRV mirrors for us? If so, I must not have copied.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah, they're both open; and all four have been dusted.

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: Okay, good. [Jim finishes the front of Dave's suit, having started high and then working his way down. Now, rather than have Dave turn, Jim moves around him.] 149:03:02 Irwin: (At the back of Dave's PLSS) That tape came off your PLSS, Dave.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Did it really?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah, it's ripped on both sides now.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: I wonder where I'm getting that.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Might be getting it in the Rover.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yep. Could be. I think I see where I'm getting it. No, couldn't be there. No, the seats are smooth.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay, Dave.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay. Give me the brush. I'll put it back. You can head in and crank up the LEC, and we'll haul all that stuff up nice and easy like. [Dave takes the brush to the back of the Rover and Jim heads for the ladder.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay. Okay, I won't even try and take a bag up then.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: No, let's take it easy.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: We have plenty of time and (there's) no sense pressing.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: (At the ladder) What's the battery that I have stowed here under this footpad, Dave?

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: That's the LCRU battery ...

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: ...for the next go.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: I guess we leave it there, don't we...

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yes.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: ...Houston?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah. Leave it in the shadow.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah.

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: That's affirm.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Don't step on it...

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: ...or knock it out of it's little blanket. (Pause) Video Clip 3 min 38 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 32 Mb MPG )

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: You're going to have to come up and hand me the LEC because we didn't...you didn't...

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: ...get it in last time. MPEG Clip by Kipp Teague (52 sec; 6.3Mb)

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay, I'll do that. (Long Pause) [Jim grabs the side rails on the ladder and jumps up. As was the case on the first EVA, it does not appear that he makes the bottom rung and has to pull himself up to it with his arms. He then does a pair of two-footed hops up the next rungs until the porch handrails are in reach. From that point, he walks up the remaining rungs until his knees reach porch level and then uses his arms to pull himself onto it. From the time he makes the first jump until he is on the porch 38 second elapse. Another 22 seconds pass until his feet disappear through the hatch and, o

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: Dave, this is Houston.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Houston, go. 149:05:10 Allen: Rog, D.R. We're thinking that that SRC (Sample Return Container or rock box) is not closed very well. We're wondering if it'll go on the LEC properly. (Pause)

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah, you're right. It would, probably; but I guess we'll not take a chance. I'll carry it up (garbled)

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: Okay. Fine.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: I could send some tape out, Dave.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: What?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: I can send some tape out. (Dave chuckles) Hey, Dave, I know what you could do.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: What?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Is put it in one of those Bull Durham sacks.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: No, I'll carry it up easy.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay. (Pause) [Dave closes the ETB and then grabs the SRC with his left hand.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay, I'll carry it up right (garbled) here. (Long Pause) [Dave goes to the ladder but, unfortunately, just as he grabs the right side rail, the TV camera begins to rotate up. It will wind up pointing straight up at the zenith. About 15 seconds after Fendell starts the upward rotation, Earth comes into view. Journal Contributor George Giusti quotes the following from notes he took on August 1, 1971 while watching television coverage of Apollo 15: "The Earth is very, very small (less than a quarter full) and nearly all white with a very small blue tint." In 1997, he added, "In watching this tap

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: How are you doing in there?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: I'm in.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: You are?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah, I'm waiting for you.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: A lot easier with the hatch open.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Huh?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: It's a lot easier with the hatch open.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Oh, all the way you mean, huh?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) Maybe a little 5 psi on that SRC will close it. [Jim means that, if they do have a good seal and a vacuum in the box, then the 5 psi of cabin pressure may finish closing the lid.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah. (Pause) Let's see, let me get up to where I can get the handle around to you.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Well, I don't know whether you can get it or not. Maybe...Here, can I help you?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: If you'll hand me the LEC. I used that yesterday. I can use the hook on the LEC to grab it and pull it up. Video Clip 2 min 29 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 22 Mb MPG )

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay, wait. Maybe I can just stick my middle in here.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: The LEC makes a good handle, a good claw to grab those.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Oh that! Yeah, that's a good ...Oh! The front part of the LEC.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yeah.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Hand it to me. (Pause)

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: Dave and Jim. We're standing by for the four pieces of luggage as they go in. We'd like for you to call them out to us.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Sure will. (Long Pause)

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: And, Dave, this is Houston. The next time you go back to the Rover, we need some help on that good old TV camera again. We got it stuck pointed straight up.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Oh, my! You're looking at the Earth, huh? Earthgazing. (Long Pause) Okay. The SRC is in, Joe.

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: We copy.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay. The ETB is up, Dave, or the LEC, rather.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay. Just a second. (Pause) [Jim has hooked up the LEC in the cabin.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: (Commenting on the TV camera) Straight up. (Laughs) I knew Ed (Fendell) would get hung up sooner or later. There you go. [Dave moves the TV down to an almost horizontal position and then skips to the MESA.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Are you ready?

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: No, no, not yet, Jim. I was just fixing the TV.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Oh.

a15a1490204.speaker: Allen
a15a1490204.text: Thank you, Dave. We were belly-up there, momentarily.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Well, that's all right, Joe. Nobody is perfect. (Long Pause) [Dave hooks the ETB to the LEC and goes to the bottom on the ladder.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: (The LM) shadow's sure getting short. Okay, partner, have at it. Video Clip 3 min 41 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 33 Mb MPG )

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay. What am I pulling up?

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: ETB. (Pause)

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Tell me when to slow down.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay. You're doing fine. Keep going. Okay, now...That's it. Now pull it once (sic) more time. (Pause) You got it. Okay. Right... [The ETB bumps against the porch lip.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Oh, shoot! I'm sorry There's so much dirt on this thing. (Pause) [Dave shakes the LEC to loosen some of the dirt.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Caked. [Dave pulls the LEC taut and the ETB rises enough to clear the lip.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay, now ease it over...Okay. (Pause) [The ETB clears the porch and, as it approaches the hatch, Dave pulls the LEC taut again so that it will clear the sill.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: There you go. Got it?

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Yup. (Pause) [Dave drops his end of the LEC.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Guess I got dirty again.

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Brush yourself off.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Yeah. I'd better. (Long Pause) [Dave goes to the back of the Rover to get the dustbrush . He does the brushing off-camera.]

a15a1490204.speaker: Irwin
a15a1490204.text: Okay, the LEC is ready to come back out, Dave.

a15a1490204.speaker: Scott
a15a1490204.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Fendell begins a counter-clockwise pan.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 16 min 00 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. I'm going to just carry the rock bags (SCBs) up. (It's a) lot easier. [This is the last use of the clothesline version of the LEC on Apollo. The dialog following 167:53:39 clearly indicates that Dave and Jim don't use the LEC during the EVA-3 closeout. The Apollo 16 and 17 crews don't even take clothesline LEC's to the Moon, although both crews do take simple lanyards so that they can raise and lower the ETB over the porch rail.] [Scott - "What's the path of least resistance? And it obviously appeared to be easier to haul it up by hand than to do all this stuff where I got fairly dirty.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Okay. When you get down, pull the LEC out.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Yeah, I will.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Stow it on the porch. 149:12:05 Scott: Oop. Heavy rock bag.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. Watch the lid doesn't come open.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: (Laughing) How'd you guess. (Long Pause) [Dave is probably closing the top of an SCB which, as Jim suspected, came open.] [About a quarter of the way through the TV pan, the TV begins to tip down, probably suffering another malfunction. We get a good view of various footprints and scrape marks at the front of the Rover.]

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Just hold up, Dave. I'll get my claw (meaning the end of the LEC) and use it to grab the...

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Got it.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Good. Okay. I'll be right back with another one.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Okay.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: I think we got a few rocks today.

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: I think we made up for yesterday.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Yup. (Pause) Let's see, we got our food in, don't we? Video Clip 3 min 15 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 29 Mb MPG )

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Yup. You working up an appetite?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Boy, you better believe. (Long Pause) [Food for the remainder of the surface stay was stored in the MESA and came up on the pallet early in the EVA at about 142:29:05 .]

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Dave, this is Houston. Give me a call on what you're loading now, please.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Oh, I just took in...What rock bag was that, Joe...(correcting himself) I mean Jim?

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Well, we have all the samples.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: I know. But what rock bag did I just give you?

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: Oh.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: You know?

a15a1491150.speaker: Irwin
a15a1491150.text: It's number 6.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Okay. And I guess the ETB to go, is that right?

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: The ETB is in, Joe. Yeah.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Okay; four items. I'm just marking down four marks here.

a15a1491150.text: That's right.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. Good show. I'll bring those up with me on the last trip. All right, Houston, what would you like to do with our friendly Rover?

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Okay, Dave. A few...Let's see, three easy steps. The LCRU power, Off, the LCRU blankets 100 percent open - and that's a change - 100 percent open; and the TV is presently pointed exactly how we would like it left. Over. [Dave's feet come into view at the left-front of the Rover and we get to watch the motions of the soil as he moves his feet.]

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: Okay. The third one is the easiest. And the second one is the easiest (too, because the blankets are already open). And I'll turn the LCRU power Off right now.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Roger. [TV off.]

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: There, it's Off. Okay. The power is Off, and the blankets are 100-percent open anyway, as you can probably see.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Roger.

a15a1491150.speaker: Scott
a15a1491150.text: So, it looks like it's all tidied up for the night.

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Roger. (Pause) 149:17:10 Scott: Anything else, before I hop in, Joe? (Pause)

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Not a thing, Dave. Beautiful job all around.

a15a1491150.text: Houston, anything else before I hop in?

a15a1491150.speaker: Allen
a15a1491150.text: Not a thing, Dave.

a15a1491150.text: Well

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Understand.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: And the second one is, it looks like we'll be delaying your Mapping Camera business at 150:10 in the Flight Plan, and we'll get back to you later on exactly what we'll be doing and when on that. And now if you'll turn to 151 hours, we have a Mapping Camera photo PAD for you.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Do you mean a Pan Camera photo PAD?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Negative. It says M - A - P.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: (It isn't) locked. Lock it again.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Huh?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Push it in again.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. (Pause) You just got a magic touch. That was easy. How did you do it?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Try it out. It was already unlocked. (It was) sliding, hard.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, Al, a little explanation. It's a photo PAD I'm due to read you at 150 and 10. You can find the little block there, and it happens that the pass and all that will be taking place on the 151-hour frame. So it's at the 151:10 - 150 and 10 that you'll find the little squares for it.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Oh. Yeah.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: It helps. Having them back that far.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Did it? Yeah. Yeah, you didn't have any trouble getting it off today, did you? (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. I'm with you. Yeah, when you call out a time like that, that's the time I go to the Flight Plan.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. I thought that's what you should do - but I guess I was wrong. Okay. T-start, 151:09...

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, 150 plus 10?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Okay. T-start, 151:09:22; T-stop, 152:09:01. And there's a little note that says at T-start...

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: I'll have to put them this way. (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay; let's get a little suit flow.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Understand.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Stow mine, I'll have you plug mine up. [Jim's use of the word "plug" suggests that he is having trouble installing a seal in the PLSS/OPS hoses.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: [Garble.] [Pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Yeah; I thought you had them. Sorry. (Pause) [Jim is having trouble getting his LM oxygen hoses connected.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Go ahead with the rest of the PAD, Bob.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. At T-start, "Mapping Camera Image Motion, Increase, talkback barber pole plus 4". At 151:52:00, "Mapping Camera Image Motion, Increase, talkback barber pole". And then I have a Pan Camera photo PAD, if you're ready to copy that.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Better to come the other way. Let me pass them the other way.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Yeah. Okay.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Got them?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: No, I don't, Jim. Where are they?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: I'm going to get the water here.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Why don't you turn around, back into your little corner. Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave and I discussed the factors that led to the choice of LM cabin size in the final design.] [Jones - "Am I right in assuming that the volume of the LM is constrained primarily by the Saturn V shroud? Increasing the volume a little bit wouldn't do much to the weight, but it sure would make it tough to stick it in the Saturn V shroud."] [Scott - "Yeah. But you'd have to go back early (in the design process). Somebody had to decide how much room you needed for two guys - long, long, long ago. And then they probably de

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Let's get this mapping camera straightened out first. T-start is 151:09:22. T-stop, 152:09:01. At T-start, go "Image Motion, Increase, to barber pole plus 4"; at 151:52:00, go "Image Motion, Increase, to barber pole".

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. And this Pan Camera is the one at 151:03 in the Flight Plan.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Go.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. It says T-start, 151:13:13. T-stop, 151:37:01. And the next Pan Camera PAD will voiced up [on the] next rev. Over.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Ran out of my suit.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: What?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Water came blowing out. (Wonder where) the water's coming from?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Water?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, Bob. Understand. T-start is 151:13:13; T-stop, 151:37:01.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: (Garbled) water; it's been blowing out my helmet duct.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: You'll have to back up, Jim. [Dave wants Jim to back away from him so that he can get a look at Jim's neckring.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Huh. That (PLSS feed)water off?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: (Garbled) check.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: It is coming out. Yeah, you're right. Let me check it.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: I don't think it's off. (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Whew; it sure wasn't. Up and off. (Pause) Backwards from the rest of the program. (Long Pause) [At 160:10:54 , immediately after wake-up for EVA-3, Jim explains that his PLSS feedwater valve was not shut off at repress and, consequently, he lost some water from the sublimator. What Jim means by "helmet duct" is probably the opening in the PLSS cover behind his helmet which gives the sublimator direct access to the lunar vacuum. Dave's "backwards from the rest of the program" indicates that the normal Off position for Apollo switches is Down.] [Scott, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "Wasn't t

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, Al, and another addition is that at 1505 [means 150:05] in the Flight Plan, you'll see some Mapping Camera activities, and you'll find that 150:05.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. And we will move the activities that start with the "Laser Altimeter, On" - that's the third line down in that little block. Move the activities starting with "Laser Altimeter, On", to "Mapping Camera Image Motion, Increase, to [talkback barber pole], On" which is the last line in that little block. Those will be moved to 151 hours and we will supply you with a T-start later.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Turn?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Yeah. No way.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Turn...Dave, I'm coming that way, maybe...Don't.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger; understand. All items between "Laser Altimeter, On", and "Mapping Camera Image Motion, Increase, to barber pole" should be moved to a GET of 151:00 and you'll supply a start time later.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Wait. Okay. (Long Pause) [For the next several minutes, the NASA Public Affairs commentator summarizes the EVA for the press. One point that interested Dave as we listen to the tape was a comparison between the physical effort expended during the two EVAs. The Apollo 15 Mission Report gives average figures of 1097 and 1002 BTU/hr for EVA-1 and EVA-2, respectively, for Dave and 976 and 808 BTU/hr for Jim. The amount of time spent driving - a very restful activity - is a major factor; but so, too, is the efficiency that comes with experience.] [Jones - "In talking about the difference in BTUs be

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Be easier to go in through the top. (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: And Al, that T-start - turns out I gave to you - is the 151:09:22.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1493403csm.text: I see. Convenient, isn't it?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1493403csm.text: Well, sort of.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Can't do it unless I take these off. (Long Pause) [During this comm pause, they finally get Jim's LM oxygen hoses connected.] [In a 1996 letter, Dave suggested that the troubles they have been having may have been due to "the accumulation of lunar 'material' around the connector."]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Ear plugs. (Pause) [The ear "plugs" contain the audio elements that produce the sound that Dave and Jim hear during the EVA.] [Scott - "Those were specially molded earplugs. Did you know that? Individually molded."] [Jones - "Well, you were wearing them for eight hours at a stretch. Did you have individually molded earplugs in the military?"] [Scott - "Didn't have earplugs. Had earphones."]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: "PGA diverter valve, horizontal."

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: Horizontal.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: "Suit Flow, for both; PLSS Pump, Off to the left; PLSS Fan, Off to the left. Disconnect the PLSS H2O from the PGA and connect the LM H2O." (Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: You've disconnected me already, huh?

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: The water, yeah.

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1493403csm.text: (Garbled) the water connected...(Pause) Connected. [They are now finished with Surface 8-1 and are now starting 8-2.]

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay. Okay, it's connected. "PLSS Mode, both, to O." (Long Pause)

a15_1493403csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1493403csm.text: Okay, the Audio panels. VHF, A to Receive and B Off. ICS/PT... [Very Long Comm Break. During this Comm Break, they will perform a PLSS oxygen charge and doff the PLSSs and OPSs as per Surface 8-2 and 8-3.] The Dreaded Station 8 Apollo 15 Journal Post-EVA-2 Activities

a15_1495257csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1495257csm.text: Roger. Whenever you got a moment, we've got a few questions the King [Farouk El-Baz] would like to have asked of you concerning your photo activities so far.

a15_1495257csm.speaker: Brand
a15_1495257csm.text: Okay. Hey, Al, Vance here. If you've got a pencil and paper and I'll let you write these things down. Should take about 5 minutes.

a15a1495323.speaker: Gordon
a15a1495323.text: Falcon, Houston.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay, just a sec. [Long pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Scott
a15a1495323.text: Hello, Houston. Go ahead.

a15a1495323.speaker: Gordon
a15a1495323.text: Okay, Davy, when you get to (Surface) 8-6 on water recharge, I've got a change for you. When you can take it, just let me know.

a15a1495323.speaker: Scott
a15a1495323.text: Okay, Richard. We'll do that.

a15a1495323.speaker: Gordon
a15a1495323.text: You two guys really know how to impress people, I'll tell you.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay, Vance, go ahead.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. These are going to all refer to your visual sighting targets, and so the first one is V-1B, Tsiolkovsky. You don't need to pull out the book, just - but I'll reference them to pages in the book. First question - or the first comment is, would you mark area on - in your book - on the central peak where you saw layering and when you get back we can look at it?

a15a1495323.speaker: Scott
a15a1495323.text: Well, you know, we sure have a lot of good things going for us. [Very Long Comm Break. Jim's next transmission relates the battery management procedures on Surface 8-3. They had planned to reach that point in the checklist at a Ground Elapsed Time of 148:55 or, as noted in the checklist, at 13:29 Houston time. Jim's next transmission comes at 15:05 Central Daylight Time in Houston and, by both measures, they are about 96 minutes behind schedule.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 4 min 24 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay, got that one. Go ahead.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. You spoke of a crater on the north-east side of Tsiolkovsky's rim, and you said it had a fault line. Could you mark that on your map, also? [Pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay. I think I already have, but I'll double check.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. Next, referring to the - the rim of Tsiolkovsky, you know, the famous sections that appear to be moved inward and outward. The question - Does it appear to you that the west segment of the wall moved inward, or did the northwest segment move outward? [Pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: I think it's just the other way around, Vance, I'll - I'll check it again and mark it on the map next time by; but, as I recall, I think the west section looks like it's moved westward.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. Next, and this would be the V-1A, question 2. We'd just like to have you make sure that you take in a look at that one.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay. What's the title on V-1A?

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay, that's Tsiolkovsky also. Question 2.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Oh, I see. Yeah, okay. Yeah.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay, going to V-2. Referring to Picard, you talked about the layering on Picard wall. Do the layers have a uniform thickness and any estimate of how thick the layers are?

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Yes.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: You might speak of the thickness of the layers in terms of the total depth of the crater.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: In terms of the depth of the crater - or in terms of the diameter of the crater?

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Well, either way - [whatever is] most convenient with you.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Well, okay. That's a - that's a little difficult to do because the layering is - most of the layering is pretty - pretty thin. I would say - maybe 1/20th of the thickness or the - 1/20th of the depth of the crater and - very small - [in] comparison with the total diameter. I'd say maybe 1 percent thickness layer as compared to the diameter.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay, going to V-5. This is Littrow. Al, you mentioned the cinder cones, and there's just some curiosity on the relative size of these cinder cones. And - [to help you] in judging the size, it's 12 kilometers between each line on your V-5 photo. And while we're at it, are the cinder cones fairly evenly distributed or are they concentrated in the spots on this darkest unit?

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: They're concentrated in spots on the darkest unit, and they seem to be concentrated in localized areas also within the darker units. There'd be a relatively high density of these small cones, and then a few scattered ones in the - you know, in the outlying areas. But I would say they were concentrated within the darker areas, more on the lowland side, you know, in the valleys and in what looks like the lower areas. And within - within concentrations of cinder cones there seems to be one locus of major activity, one locus of greatest number of cones, and then they thin out beyond that.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. Maybe you can mark that on your map where you see these concentrations.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Yeah, I can do that, but I think the pictures will be better, Vance, because the cinder cones are much smaller than the definition in the picture.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. And I'll give you one more, V-8, and that's the landing site. Just like to make sure you try to get an opinion of questions 1 and 2 and the age relationship also on that question we asked earlier about Aristillus and Autolycus and that's all I'll give you right now.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Yes. Okay, Vance. I'm over the landing site now and that unit up along the western edge of the Front there to the northeast of the landing site very definitely looks like a flow unit that's - that's flowed along or parallel to the base of the Front.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay. Copy that. I guess you got some other stuff coming up.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: You can make - you can make out some... [Pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Go. [Long pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Okay, that's about it, Al. I'll turn you back to Bob and - just some things to mull over.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay, Vance. Thanks much.

a15a1495323.speaker: Brand
a15a1495323.text: Righto.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay. And, incidentally, on this Mapping Camera pass, you started that block at "Laser Altimeter, On". Do you want that to start at - at the covers opening or do you want me to go ahead and extend the camera now?

a15a1495323.speaker: Parker
a15a1495323.text: We had a PAD that started at "Mapping Camera Covers, Open", and they explicitly took that one away and gave me one that started "Laser Altimeter, On". So I presume they want the first two lines done.

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to go ahead and open the covers and extend the camera then. [Long pause.]

a15a1495323.speaker: Worden
a15a1495323.text: Okay, camera's extending.

a15a1495323.speaker: Parker
a15a1495323.text: Copy.

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1501706csm.text: Rog. At your convenience, we'll take P00 and Accept and send you up a state vector, and - we need Accept, and we'll send you a state vector and clock update. And, I've got a TEI-45 PAD, at your convenience.

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1501706csm.text: Okay, we're talking to you and I've got the TEI-45; [it] says SPS/G&N: 37264; plus 0.60, plus 1.00; 166:38:58.32; plus 2832.6, plus 0290.1, minus 0078.2; 180, 129, 009. Rest of the PAD is NA. Notes: 1. Longitude at T IG plus 163.63. 2. Assumes no plane change. And ullage is 17 seconds...

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1501706csm.text: Okay, Al. And ullage is 17 seconds, two quads, Bravo and Delta. Over.

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1501706csm.text: Okay, Houston. Understand. TEI-45, SPS G&N; 37264; plus 0.60, plus 1.01; 166:38:58.32; plus 2832.6, plus 0290.1, minus 0078.2; 180, 129, 009. That's two jets for 17 seconds, and you want quads B and D used. And this assumes no plane change, and longitude at T IG is 163.63.

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1501706csm.text: Roger. And, the Noun 48 values are plus 060 and plus 100. Is that right?

a15_1501706csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1501706csm.text: And Endeavour, computer is yours again.

a15_1502926csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1502926csm.text: And Endeavour, Houston. We'd like to terminate Battery A charge at this time.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: Yeah. Are y'all ready to go ahead with this battery management? It's called for at 13:29.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Now, I know where you are in the checklist.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: We're trying to get to lunch time here. 150:32:15 Gordon: Well, the sooner you do it, the sooner you get to sleep, and we'll be very anxiously awaiting that. [Comm Break]

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: Dick, I missed your comment when we lost comm there.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Jim, I gave you a go-ahead on that battery; and, concerning your lunch, we're anxiously awaiting you to do all that so you can get to bed. We've got a time problem, as you might well recognize.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: And, we'll talk to you a little bit about that when you get a chance.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: That's a...I'm sorry, I got the wrong one, Dick.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, we didn't have you on high bit rate, but we'll get it as soon as you do.

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, we are looking at your batteries now, they look great. (Long Pause)

a15a1503140.speaker: Gordon
a15a1503140.text: Okay, Jim, we're getting good high bit rate and we'll watch those batteries for a little while.

a15a1503140.speaker: Irwin
a15a1503140.text: Okay. (Long Pause) Houston, ED (Explosive Device) batteries both checked at 37.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Parker
a15_1503557csm.text: And Endeavour, as you go around the hill, you're looking good. We'll look for you on the other side.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1503557csm.text: Okay, Houston. See you on the other side.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Gordon
a15_1503557csm.text: Thank you, Jim. (Long Pause) [While Jim was performing the Battery Management tasks, Dave was weighing the sample containers as per Surface 8-4.]

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1503557csm.text: Houston, this is Hadley. I have a weight report for you.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1503557csm.text: Roger. SRC was 40 (terrestrial pounds); bag 3 was 30; bag 6 [was] 33 - for a total of 103.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1503557csm.text: And Houston, Hadley Base again, standing by for your cue to go PCM, Low, and Power Amp, Off.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Gordon
a15_1503557csm.text: Say, Jim, just give us a couple more minutes. (Pause) I'll call you back on it.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Gordon
a15_1503557csm.text: Falcon, Houston. Okay, we're through looking at your batteries. You can proceed.

a15_1503557csm.speaker: Irwin

a15_1532419.text: Yeah. Keep talking.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. As I say, we'll come back up and let you copy down some of those specific words again tomorrow, before you get involved. First of all, was the talkback ever one-half barber pole during the extend, while attempting to recycle for retraction? Over.

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: The answer to that one is no.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. Two, was the barber pole indication a half or between a half and three quarters of full during retract? [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Don't know how to answer that one, Bob, because the barber pole itself - if you get a full barber pole, you only get about two thirds.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. Understand. Did the talkback change state after approximately...

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: And I was getting about half of that.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. You're getting about half of the normal 2/3. [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: That's correct.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. Third question. Did the talkback change state after approximately 3 minutes, or was it a half barber pole all the time during the retraction? [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Well I can't answer that one specifically, since I didn't sit there and watch the barber pole all the time.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay.

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: However, I did - When I went back to the Mass Spec., to cycle the thing to Deploy and Retract to see if there was any possibility of the cabling out there getting kinked, that was when I noticed that it went to half barber pole on the retract side.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. Copy that. And did you - talk the back - did you ever tap the barber pole [means talkback] when it was half barber pole? [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: I'm sorry. Say again.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Did you ever tap the talkbacks to see if you could make it flip over? [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: I noticed a couple of times, when I went to Retract, the barber pole [means talkback] would go - it would go full barber pole and then very slowly slip down to about half barber pole and stay there.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. But did you tap the talkback at any time? Tap?

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Oh, did I tap it? Negative. Negative.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. And, during the recycling of the switch, can you estimate the maximum time you were in the Extend position? [Long pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: I'm not sure I understand your question. You mean the maximum time I was in the Extend position during the retract cycle? [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Stand by.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Al, what's wanted is the total accumulative time that you went back to the Extend position, and back and forth, while you were trying to recycle it in order to free it. In other words, if you went back to 30 seconds and then to Retract, and then back to Extend for 40 seconds et cetera. What was the total accumulated time, or an estimate thereof, that you were in the Extend position?

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Okay, Bob. I would estimate that I was in the Extend position a total of about 15 seconds. [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. And what was the longest single time?

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Oh, probably 4 seconds.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Okay. A couple of other small ones, Al. Reminding you that we - we're deleting the cabin pump up from the presleep checklist. And a reminder when we get to the presleep checklist and the crew status, would you please remember to give us the PRDs. We just didn't get that from the crew on the ground and the Surgeons were very anxious to get yours, at least. And we also, I guess, are due some P52 torquing angles. [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Okay. He wants my PRD, even though it's the one that's not working, huh?

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Well - they - Anything's better than nothing. [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: I guess you're right. Here's some torquing angles for you, Bob. [I] used stars 41 and 43. Noun 05 was plus 4 balls one. Noun 93 was plus 00028, minus 00031, plus all zeros. And it was torqued out at 152:46:00.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Roger. Copy. 01, 28, 31, all balls, 152:46:00. [Pause.]

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: And I've got a film update for you, there, Bob, to give to Spencer.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Go ahead.

a15_1532419.speaker: Worden
a15_1532419.text: Okay. The magazines used today, and the exposures. These are a total - a total frame readings, too. Magazine Q is reading 31, magazine F is reading 111, Magazine T is 37 and that one's been changed out for Uniform, for U, Uniform. And Uniform's now reading 31.

a15_1532419.speaker: Parker
a15_1532419.text: Roger. Copy, Al.

a15_1535240.speaker: Worden
a15_1535240.text: Okay, Houston. I got your status reports for you, if you're ready to copy.

a15_1535240.speaker: Worden
a15_1535240.text: Okay. Crew status, no medication. Everything seems to be fine. PRD is 23163. [Pause.]

a15_1535240.speaker: Worden
a15_1535240.text: And the onboard read-outs: Battery C, 37 [volts]; Pyro Bat A, 37; Pyro Bat B, 37; RCS A, 70 [per cent remaining]; B, 68; C, 69; and D, 70.

a15_1535240.speaker: Parker
a15_1535240.text: Roger. Copy all that stuff, Al. [Pause.] And, Al, we'd like one final confirmation and that is that you've got Narrow, Reacquire [on the High Gain Antenna] and Pitch at plus 25; Yaw, 185. Over.

a15_1535240.speaker: Parker
a15_1535240.text: Okay, Al. That's all we've got. You can turn the light out and go to sleep.

a15_1615936csm.text: Endeavour, this is the planet Earth calling this morning. We'll start off with a little bit of wake-up music and then we'll get into the day's activities. If you're awake enough to hear this, you can express your appreciation for our fine music by sending us down an E-memory dump. [No answer.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Hello, Hadley Base. This is Houston calling. Over.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger, Jim. We're looking for a rough hack on where you might be in your EVA number 3 Prep. We're standing by for a crew status report plus the radiation devices (as per Surface 8-8). And, we're wondering when you might be switching over for Dave's biomed data. Over.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay. He's getting in his suit now. We could switch over to his biomed right now. Well, stand by, it'll be a few minutes.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, fine. Thank you, Jim. (Long Pause)

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay. Why don't you check Dave's biomed now. (Long Pause)

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: We got it, Jim. Clean as a whistle. Thank you.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, Joe. [Long Comm Break] [Jim's next transmission indicates that they have completed the CDR suit donning as per Surface 8-10. Normally, they would switch to Biomed-Right at this point.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. How do you read now? [Pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. If you are reading give us Accept and we'll send up a state vector. [Pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Allo, Terre. Salute de l'Endeavour.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Good morning, Al. How's the morning up there?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Well, I'll let you know when I wake up, Karl. I had another very peaceful evening.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Glad to hear it. [Long pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: We're ready for High Gain [Antenna to] Auto, Endeavour. [Pause.] And I have - and I have a Flight Plan update, the most important one being that, at 162:06, in about 3 minutes, we will delete - delete the "Gamma-ray [Spectrometer] Gain Step, Shield, Off." [Pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, Karl; understand. Let me get the Flight Plan out here.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, Off" has been deleted.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. And I have Mapping Camera photo PAD and some further Flight Plan updates when you are ready to copy.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Mapping Camera photo PAD down there at 162:55. T-start: 162:59:30, T-stop: 163:59:11.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, understand. Mapping Camera photo PAD, T-start: 162:59:30, T-stop: 163:59:11.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: That's correct, and further Flight Plan changes; we have very few today. At 162:16 we can delete the "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Understand. 162:16; delete "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. Over on 163:10, we add "Map Camera, Image Motion, Increase" with appropriate barber pole comment. Increase, and then leave it on. "Increase/On" would be a better way of reading that to you.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; understand. At 163:10, you want the "Image Motion, Increase to barber pole and On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. And at 163:40, we can add, "Mapping Camera, Image Motion, Increase/On." And also, "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, Off."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Understand. At 163:40, you want the Image Motion, Increase to Increase/On. Do you want that - How many steps past barber pole do you want it? [Pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, Al. I - I missed a beat there. The one at 163:10 was "talkback barber pole plus 4 steps" at that time. And at 63:40, take it to "talkback barber pole" and leave it there. [Long pause.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Did that come through okay?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; understand. The one at 163:10 is "Image Motion, Increase to barber pole plus 4, and then On". And then at 163:40 is "Increase to barber pole On", and "Gamma-ray Gain Step, Shield, On."

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. 163:40, that was Shield, Off; O-F-F. and at 163:50, the Gamma-ray Gain Step will go Shield, On; Shield O-N.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay. Understand 163:40, Shield is Off; and 163:50, the Shield goes On.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Houston, this is Hadley Base. Do you want to leave the Biomed on Left? And I'm going S-band voice to voice.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger. And that's the end of the Mapping Camera and the Flight Plan update.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Roger, Jim.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Rog.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: The computer is yours, Al. And I have [a] consumables update, if you'd like it.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: And, are you ready for the battery management called out at 160(:15)?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay; go ahead.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: GET [Ground Elapsed Time] is 162 hours, 0 minutes; RCS total 60 [percent full]; Quad A: 60, [B] 60, [C] 59, [D] 61; hydrogen tanks: [1] 65, [2] 64, [3] 46; oxygen tanks: [1] 71, [2] 74, [3] 58.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Stand by. Okay, Falcon. We're ready.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, in work. (Pause) ED batteries both check at 37 (volts).

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1615936csm.text: Copy. [Long Comm Break] [During this comm break, they are probably cleaning up the cabin as per Surface 9-1.]

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Understand. RCS total is 60. That's with quads: 60, 60, 59, 61; H 2 tanks: 65, 64, 46; and O 2 tanks: 71, 74, 58.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: That's correct.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: And where do we stand on the RCS budget, Karl. Do you know?

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Stand by on that, Al. We'll give you a good report in a few minutes.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. On your RCS fuel, you are running roughly 6 percent below Flight Plan values, and you're still running roughly 15 percent above the red line. Quad Charlie is the lowest - the most critical quad. But, there's no big deal at the present time in any of them. Quad Charlie, incidentally, is 10 percent above the red.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay, Karl.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1615936csm.text: Quad Charlie, incidentally, is 10 percent above the red line.

a15_1615936csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1615936csm.text: Okay. Sounds fine.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1621351csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. The latest information from Hadley Rille is that the crew is awake and about one hour from egress time. This EVA number 3 has been shortened in length somewhat to about 4½ hours in order to get our time line back on time for the nominal ascent. You can expect that you'll have some company later this afternoon.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621351csm.text: Very good, Karl. And, let's see, I guess I can give you a crew status report if you want it.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1621351csm.text: Okay. I've got 7½ hours of sleep in one period. No medication. The PRD [Passive Radiation Dosimeter] is 23164.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1621351csm.text: Houston, this is Hadley Base. We'll be starting the EVA-3 prep card in about 3 or 4 minutes.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1621351csm.text: Roger, Jim. We copy that, and we want to just remind you again on the bottom of 8-10, the page in your (Surface) checklist there, the Suit Gas Diverter Valve should be at Egress and Cabin Gas Return (Valve) at Egress. Over.

a15_1621351csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1621351csm.text: Okay. Thank you, Joe. [Long Comm Break] [Dave and Jim have probably started the PLSS donning procedures on Surface 9-2.]

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Worden
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Houston, Endeavour. If you're copying the DSKY, the gyro torquing angles are up [on it].

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Roger. We've copied them, thank you. [Long pause.]

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. [A] couple of quick questions. First of all, the Surgeons see something of a difference in your heart rate between the two nights sleep, and just out of medical curiosity, they'd like to have your subjective evaluation. Did you sleep better last night than the night before, or vice versa?

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Worden
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Gee, I guess subjectively, I slept pretty well both nights.

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Just about equal in other words? Okay, and...

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Worden
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Yes, I think so, or maybe I slept a little better last night.

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Glad to hear that. You're con - confounding their theories. On... [Long pause.]

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Allen
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Hadley Base, this is Houston. We're still showing the Cabin Gas Return in Cabin. Could you reverify that it's in Egress, please. (Pause)

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Al, we'd like to have you verify tape motion at LOS; and if it isn't, start the tape running for us.

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Henize
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: And, on this P30 business; I see something of a - a long comment they made to you last night. Is everything on that clear? [Pause.]

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Irwin
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Cabin Gas Return is presently in Auto. I think we pick it up at Egress a little later on in the procedure. (Pause)

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Worden
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Rog, Karl. I think so. I - I guess for the story there is we'll stay away from using the clock at P30 as much as possible, and when we do use it, especially when we're in deadband, we won't let it run more than 30 minutes.

XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.speaker: Allen
XXXXXXa15_1621835csmXXXXXXXX.text: Jim, Rog. Actually we should have picked that up on page 8-10 in your checklist. So we think it should be in the Egress position now.

a15a16241xx.speaker: Irwin
a15a16241xx.text: Okay. I'm going Egress. [Very Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip ( 13 min 14 sec ) by David Shaffer [During the comm break, the Public Affairs commentator tells the press that cabin depressurization is expected at about 163:14. This estimate is remarkably close since depress will actually happen at 163:18.]

a15a16241xx.speaker: Henize
a15a16241xx.text: Okay. Everybody down here thinks that's a - a great philosophy. Good. [Long pause.]

a15a16241xx.speaker: Worden
a15a16241xx.text: And, Houston; Endeavour. There were a couple of questions on the Flight Plan. I guess I'm wondering what we're going to do about the Mass Spec[trometer] today. We've got some things in here. Of course, we didn't use it last night, so there are, I guess, a few steps that you're to delete.

a15a16241xx.speaker: Henize
a15a16241xx.text: Righto. We don't intend to use the Mass Spec. today so you can delete these particular steps about retracting, or about extending the boom, et cetera . We just are not - That was it. Delete any action on the Mass Spec.

a15_1622345csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1622345csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. As you go around the corner, all your systems look to be in good shape.

a15_1622345csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1622345csm.text: Roger, Houston. See you at the other side.

a15_1622345csm.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1622345csm.text: This is Apollo Control at 162 hours, 41 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. The crew aboard Falcon presently donning their Portable Life Support System and pressure suits in preparation for the third and final extravehicular activity period of the mission, which will last about 4 to 5 hours depending on various circumstances. Meanwhile Al Worden was waked up during this last front-side pass, revolution 43. He was waked up at 161:59 Ground Elapsed Time with a little bit of Tiajuana Brass music being piped on the second of the two air/ground circuits. Unofficial estimates on the poundage or weight of s

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Houston, Hadley Base. We'll be coming to you with a comm check (on Surface 9-3) in about 2 or 3 minutes.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Roger, Dave. Looking forward to it.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston. Be advised we've got an EVA update for you, which you can copy onto the checklist if you want, or we can read it to you as you progress through the EVA, and we can talk about that when you want to. Over.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Well, where does it fall, Joe, and what does it concern.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Okay, Dave. It's going to be very simple changes to the checklist. I think just a few words concerning the general picture will be plenty sufficient; and then we'll give you the details as you come to them. I just want to give you an idea of how the traverse is going to look before you actually get started. Over.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Oh, okay. You mean our cuff checklist?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Roger. You're going to be able to follow your cuff checklist for EVA-3 almost exactly. Just a few changes.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. Well, can we proceed on here and you want to give us the changes now? It might be better for us to proceed on out, and you change us as we drive or something.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Okay. That sounds like the second option is a good one, Dave. Although you might want the big picture before you proceed on out.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Well, why don't you give us the big picture now, before we get too deep in the comm checks and all. (Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Okay. Roger, Hadley Base. Taking it from the top, we're going to ask you to stop first at the ALSEP site and spend a few minutes recovering the successfully drilled core tube and, then follow that with the Grand Prix photography. From there, press on towards Station 9, as planned. We're going to skip the Delta stop in between. [EVA-3, part B map and cuff checklist pages CDR-26 and 27 indicate a brief, supplementary sample stop 0.8 km west of the LM at BQ.1/70.7. The planned location is marked with the Greek symbol D.]

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Station 9 is exactly as we planned it. From Station 9. up to Station 10, exactly as we planned it; and at Station 10, we're going to hit a branch point. We can update you there when you arrive at Station 10. The two options are basically, to head north for the Complex, although we think it's more probable we'll just want to loop back towards the north across Alligator Chain doing good mare sampling, and wind up at Quark West crater, that's the western crater of the Quark triplet, and use that as a Station 14 stop. Over. [As shown on the Named Features map, the Alligator Chain is a string of cr

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. I guess we'll proceed on to Station 10 and take a look at it there. I'd sort of would like to get up to the North Complex if we can.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Roger, Dave. We copy that, and it may well be we can get up there. We'll just see how it goes.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. On with the comm check.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: (Reading from the last lines of Surface 9-3) "Mode, Vox; Vox Sensitivity, Max; VHF A, T/R; B, Receive." (Reading from Surface 9-4) Okay, "CB(16) Comm: SE Audio, open; and collect (sic)"...Have you connected those...

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, "CB(16) Comm: SE Audio, closed; PLSS PTT, Maintain, Right; PLSS mode to A; wheel, counter-clockwise."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay, I'm A.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. "PLSS O2 pressure gauge greater than 85 (percent)."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Verified; reading 94.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, you're 5 square (that is, 5 by 5) to me; check with Houston.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Houston, how do you read the LMP?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: LMP, you're loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: You're the same.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: " CB(11) Comm: CDR Audio, open and connect to the PLSS comm ." (Long Pause) Okay. CDR's to B; PLSS O2 pressure gauge is reading 91 percent, and how do you read me, Jim?

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Oh, I read you loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, you make a comm check with Houston.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: And, Houst...

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: You make a comm check with Houston?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Houston reads...

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Houston, how do you read the LMP.

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Jim, both you and Dave are loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, "PLSS mode: LMP to B and CDR to A." Okay, I'm on A. How do you read?

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, Houston, how do you read the CDR on A?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: CDR, you're 5 by (5).

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: "PLSS mode (both) to AR. Tone on." (Pause) Okay, how do you read me on AR?

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Read you loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, Houston, how do you read the CDR on AR?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Dave, you're loud and clear.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, you're 5 by, and how's the TM (PLSS telemetry)? (Pause) (To Jim) Okay, you make a check with Houston.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Joe, how do you read the LMP?

a15_1624100.speaker: Allen
a15_1624100.text: Okay, Jim, you're 5 by and the TM's good.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay. "CB(16) ECS: LCG Pump, closed, which it is; cold as required. CB(16) ECS: Cabin Repress, close; verify."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Verified.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P, Open."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Open.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: "Suit Fan 2, Open."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Open.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Okay, "verify ECS caution, H2O Sep Component lights." About a minute. (Pause) Okay, here they come. [They have completed the tasks on Surface 9-4 and are about to start 9-5.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "Once we have completed the comm check, the reader/listener can hear all of our EVA prep; whereas, before we reconfigure, all of our EVA prep discussion is internal to the LM only."]

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: " Suit Gas Diverter (Valve) , Pull Egress; verify."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Verified.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: "Cabin Gas Return, Egress; verify?"

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: That's verified.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: " Suit Circuit Relief (Valve), Auto; verify."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: That's verified.

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: "OPS connect: Suit Isolation (Valve) to Suit Disconnect. Disconnect the LM O2 hoses and secure about the PGA."

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: I'll come back around here. (Pause) (Garbled) get for...

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Why don't I take care of you and you take care of me?

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Yeah. I think you ought to.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay, you want me to put you on Suit Disconnect?

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Not yet. Why don't you come on around? (Long Pause) Okay, you're on Suit Disconnect, yeah. (Long Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Secure that about the PGA, Dave. Why don't you put those under one of my belts?

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Yeah. (Pause) I'm sorry.

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: That's okay. (Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
a15_1624100.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Scott
a15_1624100.text: Get it? (Pause) Okay, "OPS O2 hose is closed and locked The purge valve"...Okay, it's closed. Locked low and the pin's in. (Pause) Closed and Locked. Get your PGA diverter valve to vertical. (Pause) Okay, and you can get me. Oop. Wait a minute. (Pause)

a15_1624100.speaker: Irwin
