a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Back behind me?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Say again.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: If you can turn right, I'm turning left.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. That's right. Doesn't matter. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: (Garbled) turn that way. Try the other way. (Pause) Am I pushing against you?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. You sure are. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: I'll have to turn the other way then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No, go back in your corner. Maybe I'm unhooked now. Are you back in your corner?

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. I'm back here as far as I can.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. I'm clear. Open the door. Oop. Door won't open all the way.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Hitting my foot, I guess.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Pause) It's hitting your PLSS!

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Stand up a little bit here.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: There, okay.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Before you go out though, let me turn around so I can watch you.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Jones - "Jim must be facing the bulkhead with his body in the corner between the outside bulkhead and the ECS and his PLSS out in cabin. Sort of like a kid who's been bad, standing in the corner. This is the only clear statement in Apollo as to whether an LMP 'standing in his corner' has his face to the wall or his PLSS to the wall."]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: How are you doing?

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Oh, I'm okay. Where are you?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, I've just got my feet out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay, understand. This is plane change 1; SPS/G&N; 37202; plus 0.33, plus 1.07; 165:11:31.96; minus 0009.2, plus 0330.3, plus 0018.4; roll, pitch, and yaw are all zeros; 0064.4, plus 0053.3; 0330.9, 0:18, 0319.1; 36, 012.8, 39.2. Vega and Deneb are set stars. And 189, 256, 330. Ullage is two jet, 17 seconds, using quads B and D.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, let me turn around then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Well, I'm not sure you can. I'm going out. I'm all right. Then you can turn around easier when I get to where you get my (PLSS/OPS) antenna .

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Oh, okay. I'll just stay over here in the corner then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: In fact, if you want, Dave...Shoot, I'll get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna when we get down to the surface.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Chuckles) There. Okay; I'm out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, I'm going to turn around. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's all correct. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: You might...See the little cover on the outside hatch handle? You might cover that; it's open.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay. (Pause) Just stay there on the porch until I get all the gear out to you.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, yeah.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Like the jett bag and...

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) How you doing? Go easy. (Pause) [Jim has probably closed the hatch partially so that he can get over to Dave's side of the cabin and open the hatch fully.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Al, we'd like to verify that the Oxidizer Flow Valve was in the Decrease position at the end of the last burn and has been there since then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Doggone comm cord of yours was hung up on me.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Negative, Karl. It was in Normal at the end of the last burn, which was the circularization burn and it was - it's been in Normal since then. It's in Decrease now; I put it there after you called it out on the PAD.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, ... jett bag.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Jim, this is Houston. Could you verify for us, please, that one of the two dump valves is Open?

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Thank you, Al. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Yeah, the forward one is Open, Joe.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Sounds good, Jim. Thank you. [Houston wants to make sure that, if the door were to fully close and gas of some sort were released into the cabin, the gas would be able to vent. In principle, the crew could operate the dump valve from outside; but this simple check reduces the chance virtually to zero of problems later on.] [Scott, from a 1996 letter - "Actually, the forward dump valve would not have been difficult to open from the outside on the porch. We probably tried it in the one-sixth-g airplane. It would have been much more difficult to open the top hatch dump valve from the outside!!"]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay. Send her out.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Send that and then I'll get you the ETB.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: It's the world's biggest jett bag . (Long Pause) [Dave probably drops the jett bag over the right porch rail, the side away from the MESA.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Just a reminder, Al. Since I've been reading a lot of things to you, about the Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Standing by with the ETB there, Dave?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah, standing right by. 163:31:20 Allen: And, Dave, while you're waiting. A word about the polarimetric filter. We are going to ask you to pick that up from the MESA and put it on your camera from the very first. We've got a dandy spot for you to do some polarimetric photographs later on. [A series of photographs taken with and without the polarimetric filter had been planned for the end of EVA-1, as per CDR-26 and 27. Because of the drilling problems, those activities were dropped.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog. It's there now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: And I have a TEI-52 PAD anytime you're ready to copy. [Long pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: All righty. (Pause) Okay, I'm heading down, Jim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: I don't see the LEC out there. Where is it; down on the surface?

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No; it's over here on the right.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: TEI-52, SPS/G&N; 36003; plus 0.60, plus 1.07; 180:31:51.88; plus 3030.0, minus 0893.9, minus 0231.0; 180, 088, 346; the rest is NA. We have two jets for 17 seconds with the B and D quads, Bravo and Delta quads. The Lambda at T IG is plus 177.77; and it is assumes LOPC; and ascent REFSMMAT.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay; listen, when you get down, Dave, remember that LCRU battery is in that footpad.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Rog!

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Good thinking, Jim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: As soon as you get down, I'll come down, I'll getyour ( PLSS/OPS antenna ).

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Oh, it's in the checklist somewhere.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Sure. (Pause) Okay; if you're clear, I'll come down.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yep. Clear.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Ohh! It's nice to be outside where you can stretch a little bit. (Long Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Rog; understand. TEI-52, SPS/G&N; 36003; plus 0.60, plus 1.07; 180:31:51.88; plus 3030.0, minus 0893.9, minus 0231.0; 180, 088, 346; 2 jet, 17 seconds, using quads B and D. And Lambda T IG is plus 177.77; and the PAD assumes the plane change and asc - ascent REFSMMAT.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, the hatch is closed, Joe.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Okay, Jim. Thank you. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: And, Joe, the LCRU Power is going to Internal now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Okay, Dave. And could you check the LRV batt covers closed at the same time?

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: No, they're open and I will close them now.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Rog. Those automatic devices fail us every now and then.

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: That's all correct. [Pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah. I reckon nothing's perfect. Okay, they're closed. (Pause)

a15a1632212.speaker: Henize
a15a1632212.text: Endeavour, we're ready for Pan Camera Power, Off, now. [Pause.]

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay, Joe. I'm on the surface.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Roger, Jim.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: I'll come over and get your (PLSS/OPS) antenna , Dave.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Okay.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Although it doesn't appear like you really need it.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Sure doesn't, does it? Why don't we just leave it there.

a15a1632212.speaker: Worden
a15a1632212.text: Roger. Power is Off.

a15a1632212.speaker: Irwin
a15a1632212.text: Okay. If we have marginal comm, I'll lower it.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Yeah.

a15a1632212.speaker: Allen
a15a1632212.text: Rog. And you're both loud and clear.

a15a1632212.speaker: Scott
a15a1632212.text: Good. (Pause) [TV on.] Video Clip 3 min 21 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPG ) MP3 Audio Clip ( 9 min 54 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Did you get the LCRU battery already, Dave?

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: No, I haven't. (Pause) You're supposed to get that (as per LMP-23).

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Yeah. I know it. That's why I reminded you of it being down here.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Reminded me of what?

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: It was in this ( plus-Z ) footpad instead of the plus-Y .

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, okay. (Pause)

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Might be a little dirty.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Really? Brush it off. (Long Pause) [ Fendell pans left, raises the camera, and finds Dave at his seat emptying the ETB as per CDR-25. The "P.O. Package" mentioned in the checklist is the postage-stamp cancellation kit he will use at the end of the EVA. Jim is at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Houston. Into the CDR's footpan goes Mag Union. (Long Pause) And we got (only) a little bit on November, so we brought that along. (Pause) Get organized here. (Pause) The LMP's camera with Tango.

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Roger. (Pause) [Dave reaches across and puts the LMP camera on Jim's seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: CDR's camera with Sierra. (Pause) Mag Romeo. (Pause) And Mag Whiskey, which I'll put on the 500. (Long Pause) [Comm Break] [Dave removes the dark slide from Mag Whiskey, gets the 500-mm camera out from under his seat, and installs the magazine.] [Scott - "The camera was one of the best geologic sampling tools we had. Learn more geology from one photo than almost any other one thing we got, except maybe a really good rock."] Video Clip 3 min 13 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 28 Mb MPG )

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: And I'll check it out. (Long Pause) [Dave turns to the north and appears to take a picture with the 500. There is, however, no such picture in the Apollo collection. The usual procedure was to expose two frames after installing a magazine and these were, of course, badly sunstruck.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: And it's all right. (Long Pause) [Dave puts the lens cap on the 500 and puts the camera under his seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Joe. I have a BSLSS bag out (as per LMP-24).

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Okay, Jim. And, Dave and Jim, we'll lose comm here perhaps. However, we'll get it back when the battery's changed, so don't worry.

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Okay. Understand, Joe. And into the ETB go 16-millimeter Hotel, Juliett, and Golf. (Pause) [Dave has mis-spoken. He is actually taking the 16-mm mags out of the ETB and putting them under his seat.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: (Mag) Item. And we'll put Foxtrot on the camera. (Long Pause) [After Dave finishes with the 16-mm magazines, he puts what may be the stamp-cancellation kit on his seat and takes the EVA-3 maps out of the ETB.] 163:40:40 Irwin: Dave, I'm going to stand up on the Rover. Get the BSLSS (Buddy Secondary Life-Support System) bag locked. [Jim is attaching the BSLSS bag to the forward surface of the geopallet as per LMP-24. The BSLSS is a set of hoses and fittings that would allow Dave and Jim to share cooling water in the event that one of them had a cooling system failure.] [Scott - "All this work o

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, here. Maybe I can reach it, Jim. Let me try it, Jim...

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: ...My arms are longer. Just a second.

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: (Garbled)

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: Okay. (Pause) Video Clip 2 min 29 sec ( 0.6 Mb RealVideo or 22 Mb MPG )

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: I'll give you your maps so you can put them on. (Pause) [Dave takes the ETB and the maps around the front of the Rover to Jim's seat. During the following, Dave and Jim are just off-camera to the left.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Allen
a15a1633446.text: Dave, a reminder to pick up the polarimetric filter when you're at the MESA. [At 163:31:20 , Joe told Dave that they wanted him to put the polarization filter on his camera. At 164:01:09 , Dave will report that the filter won't fit over the lens.]

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Thank you, Joe. (Pause) See if I can get...down a little bit.

a15a1633446.speaker: Irwin
a15a1633446.text: It's hard to get into the lock, Dave. I think if you have any difficulty just let me stand up. I can lean over and get it. (Pause) Down. We have to swing that lock on the left side forward to lock it in there. (Pause)

a15a1633446.speaker: Scott
a15a1633446.text: Oh, yeah. (Pause) I'm not sure you're going to get to that at all.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634151csm.text: Endeavour, a reminder on the Gamma-ray Gain Step. We need the Shield, Off, at this point.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: I could get it if I could stand up and lean over. 163:42:00 Scott: You can try. Be careful. (Long Pause) [Journal Contributor John Pfannerstill notes that, at this point, Dave affixes the LRV commemorative sign to the righthand side of the console, smoothing it down several times with the back of his glove. Jim will take two photos of the sign at 163:58:27 . Dave leaves the field-of-view to the left, probably going to the MESA.] [Fendell pans right.]

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: Okay, Joe; I have the polarimetric filter.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634151csm.text: Okay, Dave, and just plug it on to your camera at your convenience. You'll want to change the exposure time to 1 over 125, and you might call out the filter position. Video Clip 2 min 52 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 26 Mb MPG )

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: Okay. Let me get to it later, Joe.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634151csm.text: Rog; no hurry. (Pause)

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: Is that the BSLSS lock on the...(Did) you said the left side or right? Oh, it is. I see it.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: Left side.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: I can get it.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: What?

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: I can reach that.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: If you can reach around the...If you want, I could...

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: No, I can get it.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: You can't reach the strap, the bag's too wide.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: Up or down?

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: Forward.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: It was already in forward. Must have got it. No, it's got to go aft, Jim. [Fendell reaches the clockwise pan limit and has a close-up view of Jim's right shoulder. When Fendell pulls back on the zoom, we see Dave at the back of the Rover.]

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: It's easy to lock. (Pause) Here, I'll hold the bag down. Just push it aft. Push aft - Oop! (Pause) If it's aft, no sweat, Dave, just leave it there. I'll push it aft. Let me work on it. You've got other things to do.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: All done. (Pause) I think I'd see what the problem is. (Pause) It is forward. No, that's aft; that's right. Locked. (Long Pause) Huh. Well...

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: If there's any question, Dave, let's put it under my seat, rather than lose it.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: We're not going to lose it, Jim.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634151csm.text: That sounds good to us, Jim. It's not worth the trouble.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634151csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1634151csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634151csm.text: There. I got it. It's locked. Huh! (Long Pause) [Irwin, from the 1971 Technical Debrief - "We had trouble getting the BSLSS bag locked. I think that's because the bag was larger than the collection bags, and you just couldn't get your finger in there with a suit on to get it locked."] [Jim gets an SCB from under his seat and, once Dave moves out of the way, takes it to the back of the Rover. Dave gets the LCRU battery from Jim's foot pan, and pounds it with his right fist to knock the dust off.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 18 min 55 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1634559.speaker: Scott
a15a1634559.text: Okay, Joe, I'm going to change the LCRU battery .

a15a1634559.speaker: Scott
a15a1634559.text: Okay, ( LCRU ) power's going (Off). [TV off.] [Motion picture film shot during training shows Dave installing a LCRU battery.]

a15a1634559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1634559.text: Joe, we have bag 7 on the left-hand side of the tool carrier and bag 2 on the right side.

a15a1634559.speaker: Irwin
a15a1634559.text: And I'm wondering whether we should leave...

a15a1634559.speaker: Allen
a15a1634559.text: ...if it's easy to do just keep bag 2 under the seat and follow your checklist normally. Bag 2 is just an extra bag for us. (Long Pause) [Cuff checklist page LMP-24 indicates that they had planned to have bags 7 and 8 on the back of the Rover.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We have one small change in our set-up for the plane change burn, and that is that we would like to leave the Oxidaze - Oxidizer Utilization Valve [means Oxidizer Flow Valve, on panel 3 of the Main Display Console and part of the Propellant Utilization Gauging System (PUGS)] on - in the Normal position. We'd like it Normal instead of Decrease as we previously told you. [Pause.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: We still have some tools in bag 2, Dave. I'll just leave that bag there and put our last collection bag under my seat.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay. Why don't you tell them when they come back up here.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: Dave and Jim, do you read Houston? (No answer)

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay, going Normal on the PUGS Valve.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Okay, LCRU (power) is on Internal. Blankets are 100 percent open. (Long Pause)

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Roger; and the boys on the surface have the TV tuned up for us now and we're getting some lovely landscape pictures - Hadley Delta, et cetera . Those hills there are just beautiful, round, bare hills, a lot like the ones you see around San Francisco. It's a beautiful sight. They're just about loading up the Rover and getting ready to head off toward the South Com[plex] - first of all, to the rille for a quick visit and then off to the South Complex.

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1634637csm.text: Get new sample collection bags for us, Jim?

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: Jim this...

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Yeah, I (garbled under Joe) Video Clip 2 min 50 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1634637csm.text: . ...is Houston. We prefer bag 2 under your seat shelf and bag 7 on the Hand Tool Carrier, instead. [TV on. Jim is at his seat.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1634637csm.text: Rog, Karl; understand. Did you say they are going to cut it a little bit short today?

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1634637csm.text: Well, bag 7 is Dave's bag. It's on the left side. It's just a question of which one you want on the right side. In other words, which one do you want on me? [Jim has gone to the back of the Rover.]

a15_1634637csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1634637csm.text: Right. a15_1642118csm.text: No problem.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: (Unsure this is wise) Okay. (Pause) There will be a problem when we start working in the bag.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: Negative, Dave. That's an extra bag now, and we'll keep that in mind.

a15_1642118csm.text: Now let's see. Get the treadle off. (Pause) (Try) this (Pause) [Dave hasn't had any success in getting the treadle off and gets the wrench to try to secure the drill string. Before using the wrench, he puts a core cap on the open end of the drill string. Fendell pans left.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [Fendell has panned right to watch Dave. Dave pulls on the drill string to get the treadle away from the Rover and starts to work it off the stem.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: (To Houston) Okay. Delta is the cap on top of the next section. (Long Pause) [Fendell pans left and find Jim taking a pan with Dave's camera.] 164:26:12 Scott: Let's see. (Long Pause) Jim, did you get the vise on right?

a15_1642118csm.text: Can only go on one way, Dave.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Really!? (Pause)

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: It's not working. There it goes. (Grunting) Ohhh! 164:26:56 Irwin: Okay. The pan's complete here, Joe.

a15_1642118csm.text: Super. [Jim's pan (assembled by Dave Byrne) consists of frames AS15-82- 11047 to 11064 . Hadley are much fainter than they were during the second EVA but are still evident.] [Frames 11055 , 11056 and 11057 are good up-Sun views of the Swann Range and the LM with little glare.] [Frames 11060 and 11061 show Dave at the back of the Rover examining the vise. He has the core with him, lying horizontally along the back

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: Sounds good.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: You have a new mag on there today, Jim. It couldn't have been the one that failed yesterday.

a15_1642118csm.text: No, I had the color mag on there, TT. That's the one that was on there yesterday.

a15_1642118csm.text: No it wasn't, either. TT is brand new.

(Long Pause) [The magazine that was on Jim's camera when the camera failed at Station 4 was PP (Papa-Papa) or AS15-90.] [During the preceding discussion, Fendell panned right until he found Dave at the back of the Rover. He pulls the drill string out a little farther to his right and tries the wrench again. There is a vise mounted on the back of the Rover which, in principle, should bite into the third section and hold i

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. I'll throw a little malfunction procedure on it (meaning the Hasselblad) then.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. That a boy. [Jim comes around the back of the Rover to his seat. Dave is still turning the drill string with the wrench, trying to figure out why the vise won't hold the section seated in it.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: I hate to tell you, Jim, but that...Oh boy! This vise is on...I swear it's on backwards. (Pause) Video Clip 3 min 27 sec ( 0.9 Mb RealVideo or 30 Mb MPG )

a15_1642118csm.text: The holes on the Hand Tool Carrier only line up one way. (Pause)

a15_1642118csm.text: (Discouraged) Doesn't work then. [Fendell zooms in on Jim's camera as he performs the malfunction procedures. In the background, Dave slides the drill string to his left.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: (To Houston) How many hours you want to spend on this drill, Joe? (Laughs) Like the vise doesn't bite strong enough to get a grip so I can break the sections.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Dave, if you want, I can get on the other end and hold it steady.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Well, you can try...

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Yeah. [Jim puts his camera down on the LMP seat and goes around Dave to try to hold the stems in the vise.]

a15_1642118csm.text: ...(and) see if it does any good. But the training ones hold good. There's never any problem with them. It would grip the stems and hold them very well, but the one mounted on the pallet provided no torque at all."] [As it turns out, the vise mounted on the back of the Rover was

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. Let me get on the other end. Some caps behind your left boot.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Oh, shoot! I knocked them off again.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Here I'll get them.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: (Dismissively) No, go get the vise! I mean the drill (stem). I think we're about through with this.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. I've got it.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. (Pause) [The fact that Dave snapped at Jim is the clearest possible indication that he is very frustrated. Characteristically for both of them, Dave recovers his composure before his next transmission and Jim graciously ignores the outburst.] [The stems turn freely as Dave uses the wrench. The treadle is still attached to the top section and it's motions give us a good idea of how the stems are turning.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Won't bite. Don't hold it that way. Hold it straight in the vise, if you can, Jim. See how it sits?

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Yeah. [Jim may have been holding the stems at an angle to the vise in order to improve their chances of getting it to grip.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. See, it doesn't grab. There, that's got it there. Okay. Hold it like that. (Pause) [This time, treadle moves in jerks as the stems bite in the vise and Dave starts to get the top section loose. Note that the treadle is pointed down when the vise begins to grip.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Man, oh man! Okay. Hold it right there.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: Dave, the treadle may be jammed against the fender. There it moves away. (Pause)

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: (To Joe) Yeah, I know. No problem. (Pause) (Delighted as the stem breaks free even more noticeably) There!! (Pause) [The treadle has gone through a complete revolution and, once again, is close to the right-rear fender.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Trouble is...Okay. Let go a minute. (I'll) get it out here a little ways. (Pause) [Dave lifts the stems and pulls them out six inches or so to get the treadle clear of the fender.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Hold it again, Jimmy.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay, I got it. (Pause)

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Is in the next section. (Perhaps putting the caps in the SCB) Okay. (To Jim) Now, old buddy, if you think you can have some luck taking that (treadle) off. I'll tell you what, we got to break it again. [Off-camera, Jim is helping Dave get the treadle off section 2. Although we can see Dave's PLSS and upper torso and head, his hands are off-camera and it is impossible to know exactly what he and Jim are doing.] MP3 Audio Clip ( 15 min 54 sec ) by David Shaffer Video Clip 2 min 01 sec ( 0.5 Mb RealVideo or 18 Mb MPG )

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. Oh boy! [Dave completes another half turn with the wrench, puts it down, and goes to his left and stands facing the Rover so that he can grab the treadle and turn it to finish removing the second stem from the string.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Joe, I haven't heard you say yet you really want this that bad. (Pause) Tell me you really want it this bad.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: (With a touch of wistful sympathy in his voice) It's hard for me to say, Dave. [After a three-quarter turn of the treadle, the second section comes free.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1642118csm.text: Beautiful.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: I'll get those caps for you, Dave.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: You need those now?

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Yeah.

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause) [Dave watches while, off-camera to the right, Jim gets the core caps off the ground. Dave reaches forward and down to take them from Jim.]

a15_1642118csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1642118csm.text: Okay. Thank you. (Pause) Okay. Cap number Echo. [Dave has put the cap on the bottom of section 2]

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Dave, how many more sections to come apart?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If you can get the wrench, I'll hold the treadle.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. (To Joe, with clear annoyance) Oh, stand by, Joe. (Counting the remaining sections) We've got 1, 2, 3. 4.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Thank you. [Dave is probably annoyed because Houston should have been able to keep count.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay, I've got it there if you can...

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) (Grunting) Ahhh! (Pause) Nope, wrong way. (Long Pause) That doesn't look right either. Let's go the other way. Man, how did that treadle get like that? (Long Pause) [During the struggle to remove the treadle, Dave edges off-camera to the right.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: It's moving.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: It's broken.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: That's got it. (Pause) It's really jammed.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: See if I can get it out.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Work it out towards you, because of the cap. See what I mean?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Yeah.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Take that...The end of your right hand should come through, while I work on the rest of them, here. (Pause) Okay. Foxtrot on the next section. Video Clip 3 min 07 sec ( 0.8 Mb RealVideo or 27 Mb MPG )

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Dave is back in view and has put a cap on the top of the third section. He pulls the string out until the fourth section is seated in the vise. Dave starts turning the wrench but, without the treadle on the string, it is difficult to tell if he is getting any grip from the vise.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If I had known (about) this, I would have left my cover gloves on, Dave.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Well, don't mess with it then. Don't mess your gloves up. I'll do it. [Evidently, Dave is still wearing his cover gloves.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Oh, they're okay. I'll take it.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: This vise just won't hold. There's something wrong with it. (Long Pause) The vise doesn't work, at all! We're still fiddling with this thing. [Scott, from a 1996 letter - Ah ha! I did use the watch!! And I recall this.] [Dave arrived at the drill site at about 164:03:55 and, consequently, they have been working on the deep core for about 30 minutes.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. The treadle's off.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Beautiful! (I'll) stick this (stem-section 2) in here (SCB-2). (Pause) Now, hold that section for me...

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: ...(Like you) did before. (Pause) It's just not gripping. The...

a15a1643123.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Go ahead.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Roger, troops. What's your best guess?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: (Under Joe) Try to bring that back that way, Dave?

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Do you think you can turn off the bottom-most drill section? [Dave takes the drill string off the back of the Rover and holds it up for Houston to see.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Joe, you can see on the TV. That's what we got. Now, the vise...(correcting himself) My hand wrench works okay. The one on the back of the Hand Tool Carrier doesn't seem to want to work for some reason. It may just be because of the threads on the stems. I just can't get them broken apart! And that's the main problem. The wrenches don't work. (Pause) [Dave puts the string back in the vise and resumes his efforts with the wrench.] 164:35:43 Allen: Dave and Jim, put that section on the ground, if you would, please. [Dave takes the drill string out of the vise without hesitation once he hears Hou

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: We'll pick it up on the way back. And we want you to continue on with the Grand Prix.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Good enough. Do that. [During the Grand Prix, Jim will stand facing northwest and take movie footage with the Data Acquisition Camera (DAC) while Dave drives through a pre-determined set of maneuvers. They had planned to do the Grand Prix at the end of EVA-2 and the relevant cuff checklist page is EVA-2/CDR-20 .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Stick it in there, Dave. We might be able to return it (to Earth) just like that. Video Clip 1 min 00 sec ( 0.3 Mb RealVideo or 9 Mb MPG )

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah, I think probably so. I don't know where we're going to put it in the Command Module. (Jim chuckles) I'll think of something. Let me see. a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: I guess we ought to take it back (to Earth). There's more time invested in that than anything we've done. Okay. (To Jim) Get your (16-mm movie) camera. [Jim comes into view at the back of the Rover and goes to the LMP seat. Dave is at the back of the Rover.]

a15a1643123.text: Okay. Let's see. We don't want the drill on here. What do you want to do with the drill?

a15a1643123.text: Oh. Just leave it right here.

a15a1643123.text: Put it on the surface here?

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Jim lifts the drill and merely turns so that he can put it down far enough out that Dave won't hit it when he starts driving. a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Got a good mag (on the 16-mm)? Why don't you check it out and see if it runs?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I did. I checked it out at 1 foot per second earlier.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I'll give it a short burst here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Good thinking, Jim. (Pause) Dave, while you're climbing on the Rover, we'll take...

a15a1643123.text: High gain antenna is getting...

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: The meter readouts and your heading is 292. [TV off. At this time, Jim is still in view and is holding the DAC in his hands. Joe, I never did any systems reset, but they were all sitting zero when I stopped here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Good enough for me.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: PM1/WB . (Long Pause) Okay. Let's get our little handy...

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. I have the (16-mm) camera set.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay. (Looking at EVA-2 CDR-20) The Sun should be over your right shoulder, so why don't you take a right turn there. In the Command Module view linked here, Schaber Hill and the North Complex are right of center. See the discussion following 146:49:02 .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: You want to do a quick turn there so you don't get dust on my experiments.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Oh, sure. Watch out going backwards, Jim.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Ah, no sweat.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Dave hasn't started driving. Jim is probably walking backwards, which can be a good way to fall down.]

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: If you want, you can do a left turn there, Dave. And I'll move back a little more.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. If I can get my seatbelt on. (Long Pause) Oh, my.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Dave, before you move out, you want to double-check your heading at 292.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay, Joe. (Long Pause) Torquing now. (Pause) Got a long way to go. (Pause) Make this torquing switch a set-and-hold switch, instead of spring loaded, would help! (Pause) Be with you in a minute, Jim. I've got to torque another 90 degrees or so.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: No rush.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Enjoy the scenery, Jimmy. (Pause)

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Yeah. I'm looking to find out where all the big rocks are.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Sounds good. And tell Dave once again that you don't want any dust on your experiments. (Jim laughs)

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Hey, Joe, you never did tell me that drill was that important. Just tell me that it's that important , and then I'll feel a lot better. (Pause)

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: It's that important, Dave.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Good. Because then I don't feel like I wasted so much time.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: No. Quite seriously, Dave and Jim, that's undoubtedly the deepest sample we'll have out of the Moon for perhaps as long as the Moon itself has been there. [Grant Heiken, who took the core apart almost grain by grain, has called it the most valuable sample returned from the Moon. It revealed 58 distinct layers of soil, a detailed record of a very complex sequence of local impact events that covered, overturned, and re-covered this particular section. A summary of results obtained from the deep core can be found in the discussion of samples 15001-006 in the Lunar Sample Compendium .]

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Well, that sounds good. [The following is from an exchange of e-mail in November 2003.] [Jones - "Grant Heiken and I have been discussing your drilling activities at Hadley and we wonder if you have any thoughts about how hazardous an activity it was. If, for example, a drill stem snapped and you fell on the exposed end, would the fall in 1/6th have been enough to compromise the suit? I know you strained your shoulder lifting the core out. Was that stressing the suit? Etc."] [Scott - "Well, falling on the exposed end would not be good, but I believe the suit would have taken it, especially sin

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay, Joe. I'm torqued to 292. And, Jim, I'll take a left turn out of here. (Pause) Making sure I don't get any dust on your experiments. (Pause) Okay. You're in a good spot.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I'm ready for you.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Wait, let me get over here and get set up.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Let me move back a little bit then. 164:42:36 Scott: No, you're okay. Right there. The Sun's over your right shoulder. That's just about right. Okay. Take a little left turn there. I'll start up and go constant, if you are ready.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: I'm ready.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. (Pause) Okay; there's about 7 clicks.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Camera's on. (Pause)

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Seven kilometers an hour. Tell me when to turn.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay; you can turn now.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Better. (Laughs) Okay. Here comes acceleration. Couple of di-do's here. Up to 12 clicks.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Ride 'em Bronco.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Yeah, man. (Pause) Okay. I'm going to make a right turn.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: You kicked up a very nice rooster tail.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Good. Make a right turn here. (Pause) And I'll come back across, and give you a hard stop If I can find us a smooth spot to get going here.

a15a1643123.speaker: Allen
a15a1643123.text: Jim, this is Houston here. How does that camera seem to be working?

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Okay. Here we go.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: It feels like it's working, Joe.

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Here's the hard stop.

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin
a15a1643123.text: Okay. We'll check it. Ah, shoot!

a15a1643123.speaker: Scott
a15a1643123.text: Didn't work?

a15a1643123.speaker: Irwin

a15a1662738.text: Okay, Dave. Copy that. It may also be that it's quite dusty, and the brush might help you out there.

a15a1662738.text: Okay. We'll try that. Didn't try that.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: And to set your minds at ease, we think that even if you can't separate it into two pieces, we can get the whole thing into the LM. So we'll bring it home anyway. We'd like it in two separate pieces, though.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Well, I guarantee you we're not going to leave it here now (laughing) after we got that much invested into it. Oop! (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: We're looking directly east now as we head back to the LM...Did you put your visor down?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Haven't yet, but I think I just might.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Boy, that Sun is really fierce. (Pause) [In this passage, Jim seems to be using 'directly east' to mean up-Sun. The Sun is actually about 20 degrees south of east at this time. Jim could look at the heading indicator and see that the Sun is not 'directly east' but, given the fact that they are following their tracks home to the LM, that level of precision is completely unnecessary.] 166:32:49 Irwin: And I can see, as I look to the east, several places up the slope [of] Big Rock Mountain where there're outcrops exposed.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Roger, Jim. Copy...

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: One about a quarter of the way up directly east from us...That was Big Rock Mountain.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: And the name of the mountain again, please.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: That was Big Rock Mountain.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: You know, Joe. Big Rock-o Candy Mountain.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Roger; we copy. (Pause) And do we have a big smile here in the MOCR.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: (Laughs) [Scott - "I think we decided, at some point, that we would call that 'Big Rock Mountain' , after Rocco Petrone. He picked the landing site. He made the decision."] [Jones - "Were you involved in the site selection process?"] [Scott - "Sure."] [Jones - "Tell me about it."] [Scott - "We had, what, four sites? There was Marius Hills, Davey Rille and a couple of others, right after Apollo 12. Rocco finally had a meeting in Washington and said, 'We're going to make a decision, and nobody leaves the room, even for lunch.' And the contest was between Hadley and Marius Hills. And the two oppo

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: I'm not going in there, Jim.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: I hope not. (Laughs) Haven't picked up our tracks yet...Think we're probably still a little north of them.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. Because we came 3/10ths north.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: We're heading 105. Range (is) 1.4.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Copy, and sounds good. [These readouts put them near BU.0/67.6 or, if we apply the 8-degree bearing correction, near BT.3/67.4. Clearly, they drove around the north side of Scarp Crater.]

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Can't see the LM today. (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Oh, look at the mountains today, Jim, when they're all sunlit; isn't that beautiful?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Really is.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: By golly, that's just super! It's, you know, unreal. (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Dave, I'm reminded of a favorite Biblical passage from Psalms. "I look unto the hills, from whence cometh my help." But of course, we get quite a bit from Houston, too. (Pause) Okay, we're heading 140.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: We've got to go around this...

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: ...crater here, ol' buddy. (Long Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: What's your estimate as to when we'll be able to see the LM?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Who's, mine?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, do you think we'll be able to see it at 1 kilometer?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Nope. I think we're going...

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: ...to be going up and down the valleys here.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: ...No, I think I see the top of it, Dave; at 12 o'clock.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Really?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. Just barely see the top of it.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Okay, well, you look far-range, and I'll look near-range.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. And there are our tracks.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, we got our tracks. How about that?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: And the Rover's (sic, means LM) a little black blob over there at about 12:30. That's exactly where the Nav system says it is.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: I think we'd do better going straight ahead on, don't you?

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. We just got that one depression over that next ridge. Might want to just drive through it, huh?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, let's see how we do it.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Wasn't that the deep one, though, that had the crater in the lower part? [The crater in question is centered at about BS.7/71.5.]

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. It's saying (bearing) 093 and heading 08(0), so coming right's going to help us some. (Pause) No, we're okay.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Good shape.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. This is a better route than we used coming out.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) Wish we could get that 16-millimeter camera to work.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: I'll change mags on it.

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: See if that helps. (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: How about that for maneuvering, huh? (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Slick! (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: This thing would really be great in shirtsleeves up here, you know it? (Pause) [During the early to mid 1960s, the Marshall Spaceflight Center in Huntsville worked with industry on the design of a much larger Rover, one with an enclosed cabin to provide the astronauts with a shirtsleeve environment during long traverses. However, such a rover could have been delivered to the Moon only with a cargo-only version of the LM.]

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Jim, concerning that 16-millimeter camera, if you're changing the mag out, you might try the one-frame- per-second trick at the beginning. It worked before.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, I did that this morning, Joe, on this mag. It...

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Roger. You've got plenty of mags.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: ...didn't work; I'll try it again, though.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Keep trying.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Yeah, we will. (Pause)

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: By the way, do you want us to bring back those jammed mags or shall we chuck 'em?

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Let me check with SPAN. (Pause) 166:38:03 Scott: Boy, look at the few big boulders up there. Yeah, that's pretty neat. [Dave may be refering the the large boulders near the summit of Big Rock Mountain that can be seen in a detail from AS15-89- 12169 .]

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: Up on the slope of...

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yeah.

a15a1662738.speaker: Irwin
a15a1662738.text: It's appropriately named, don't you think?

a15a1662738.speaker: Scott
a15a1662738.text: Yes, it is. (Pause) It's the only one around here.

a15a1662738.speaker: Allen
a15a1662738.text: Dave and Jim, we think it will be just as easy for you to bring them (meaning the 16-mm magazines) back, and we'll troubleshoot them. 166:38:34 Scott: All right, we'll do that. (Long Pause) You know, so far in the past, our Nav system has always been biased pointing us to the right a little bit more than we should, so I'm going to bias it a tad left here. Because I know if we get too far left, we'll pick up our tracks. I've noticed on the other two trips when we got back, it was asking us to head 8 degrees or so to the right. (Pause) MP3 Audio Clip ( 12 min 06 sec ) by David Shaffer

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: See our tracks running to the east there (at the) 12 o'clock position. Just over that next ridge, we should...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah, you're right.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: ...should see the LM.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Oh, we cut a big chunk out.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. (Pause) Range, now, of 0.5. (Long Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Hey, this shade really helps. It's no problem at all driving up-Sun, with the center visor down. (Pause) [Dave is referring to the center visor at the top of the helmet which was first used on Apollo 14. Photo AS12-49- 7278 shows that Al Bean did not have a central visor while photo AS14-68- 9405 shows that Al Shepard did have one. AS14-64- 9059 shows Ed Mitchell with his Central Visor raised. Finally, AS15-92- 12424 shows Jim with his visor partly raised.]

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: In fact, I reckon we're making pretty good time.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Going about 11 clicks there.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: There's the LM, 12:30.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: How about that! By golly, we must have come just about straight back. And the bearing - yeah, it's great.- says 096, and I'm... 166:40:39 Irwin: Hey, let me take a picture right here.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Oh, yeah!

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Slow down a little bit...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yes, let me stop on the rim here and point you.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Okay.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Oh, isn't that pretty! Okay. Oop. Too much, huh? Let me go around. (Pause) There, how's that? (Pause) Little more?

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: You're okay. Swing it.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay. (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Okay.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Still on a (f-stop setting of)5.6? 166:41:17 Irwin: Yeah. [Jim's first LM picture is AS15-82- 11192 .]

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: That's a super picture.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Swing it a little more to the right and let me make sure...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay, there you go. 166:41:26 Irwin: Got it. [After Dave turned slightly to the right, Jim took AS15-82- 11193 and 11194 . Dave Byrne has combined these with 11192 in a mini-pan .]

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay. (Pause) Let's see. We'll go find the ALSEP site; I think we've been there before.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: And Dave and Jim...

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Boy, this ALSEP... (Laughs)

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: ...I want you to notice how we planned the fourth stop...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: No, I don't think it was.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: ...at the ALSEP site for you.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: (Hearing Joe; Laughs) Yeah, it's got to be a new all-time record. It will probably stand forever.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Roger. It'll certainly...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Sure would like to do some more geology up here someday.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: ...scare the competition.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah, we didn't get a chance to get up the Northern Complex and see Pluton, Icarus...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: I know it!

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: ...Eagle Crest. Doggone.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: All the good places.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah, the really big surprise was up there!

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Jim, I'll go around the north here and avoid the dust on our trusty ALSEP. (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Hey, that's...That's a pretty nice picture right there, Jim. Let me point you...

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Swing around there, I'll take some. 166:42:42 Scott: That's really pretty! What kind of mag...Oh, you got black and white. Better change that mag, buddy. (Pause) Okay; there you go, right there. (Pause) Got it?

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah, I'll change it out when we stop. (Pause) [Jim's final approach picture is AS15-82- 11195 . Note that the Rover tracks visible in this picture are not as dark as the ones photographed closer to the LM at the ALSEP site. Silver Spur is at the right.]

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: I'll drive slow in here. There's our trusty drill.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: I thought you left it in the erect position.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: No. No. (Long Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Friendly plains of Hadley.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: We've stopped, Houston! We're at ALSEP. (Pause) 166:43:47 Allen: Roger, troops. We're thinking that when you...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay. We're reading.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: ...arrive back at the drill site: Jim, why don't you hop off and pick up the three important items there: the drill stem, the treadle, and the wrench. And, Dave, you can drive on back and park by the LM. Over.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay, give me your camera, Jim.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Got it, Joe.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: In work.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Okay, I'll just skip the navs (that is, the readouts).

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. (Pause) Here. (Pause) Okay.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Let's see you have all the other stems in the bag.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: You have the wrench in there, too, don't you?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. I think so. If it's not there, I've got it in the bag.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: It's not here by the treadle. So all I'll do is pick up the treadle? (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: I don't know why we need the treadle.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: I don't either...

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Just take it on back. We might use it as a wrench.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: (Responding to Joe) Yeah, I guess you could. Alright.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: And that's Walter Mitty plan number 2. (Long Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Okay, I have the treadle (and) stems, and I'm heading back. (Long Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay, I'm off the Rover (at the LM), Joe. (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: When I get up there, Joe, I'll give you the readings.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Okay, Jimmy. We're standing by. (Long Pause) Dave, are you arriving at the LM, now?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Dave's been here for a couple minutes.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Okay, sorry. I guess I missed it. We're standing by for TV, Dave.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: And the heading is...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Roger, Joe. 166:46:52 Irwin: The heading is 001, (bearing) 032, (distance driven) 5.1; (range) 0.0; (amp-hours remaining) 88, 90; (battery temperatures) 108, 113; and motor temps are still low.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Copy, Jim. Remarkable Nav system.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Sure is. (Pause) [Although we don't know exactly where Dave initialized the Nav system, it was within 100 meters of the LM and, therefore, the fact that the range is now reading zero means that there was virtually no significant range error during this EVA.] [Journal Contributor Jeroen Wackers notes that Dave and Jim have driven a total of about 27.9 km and have used about 47 amp-hours of battery power. The average use rate is 1.69 A-h/km and has been quite consistent across the three EVAs. However, at 167:35:58 after Dave drives out to the final Rover parking place, Joe asks him to tap the am

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: (To Houston) Okay, AGC says you should have it, Joe.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Okay. (Pause) [TV on. Fendell is looking at the battery covers and, once again, the camera is stuck.] Video Clip 2 min 47 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 25 Mb MPG )

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Dave, are you going to use that (Hasselblad) camera?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yes, sir.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Okay, 'cause I want to...We never have taken any dust pictures of the Rover.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: I'll do it right now.

a15a1663922.text: (Reading LMP-36) You need two cross-Sun and one down-Sun.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: At f/11, 1/250th, 11 feet.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: All the way, huh?

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. And, also, I've got to take a photograph of the solar wind (experiment).

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Okay; I'll get it.

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: And we needs some help on our (TV) camera, Dave.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: (Garbled)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: (To Houston) I guess we kind of follow the checklist here for a while, huh? [Dave raises the TV and gives us a view of the side of the LM. Fendell pans right.]

a15a1663922.speaker: Allen
a15a1663922.text: Jim, that's affirm. But we want you to break down the core stem first, please. That is, separate it.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: (Laughing) Of course. The crew'll break down; the stem never will. 166:48:58 Scott: Okay; I got a pan of the Rover. [Dave's Rover pictures start with AS15-82- 11196 , which shows the front of the vehicle from the left side. Note that the TV camera is pointed down. Jim has rested the multiple section of the deep core on his seat. This photo gives us an excellent view o

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: No, all I saw was a (pause) UHT.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Must be in your seat, then.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Is it?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Let's see. (Pause) Ah, shoot; I don't see it. (Pause)

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: I'll whip out there (to the drill site) again. But the only thing I saw was the UHT lying on the surface out there. Did you have a UHT in that area?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Yeah!

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Yeah. That's all that was out there.

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: But, you know, I thought I put the tool in the bag with the stems.

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: Maybe it just...

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: How could it get out and the stems not get out?

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: How many stems did you have?

a15a1663922.speaker: Scott
a15a1663922.text: Two. (Pause) Video Clip 2 min 44 sec ( 0.7 Mb RealVideo or 24 Mb MPG )

a15a1663922.speaker: Irwin
a15a1663922.text: I don't know, Dave. [Fendell has stopped his counter-clockwise pan and is panning up along the high-gain antenna mast. I guess we'll have to use the treadle. (Looking under the CDR seat) It's not in my side, either. Darn. Whew! Man, that's hot! I tell you what. The treadle. [The treadle and drill stems have been out in the Sun at the drill site since the start of the EVA. However, Dave doesn't remember what it was that was hot.]

a15a1665055.speaker: Scott
a15a1665055.text: Yeah, okay. (Pause)
