a15_1680411csm.text: Closed.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay, up she comes. (Sound of repress) There's 1 (psi). (Pause) 1.5. (Pause) 2. (Pause) 2.5. (Pause) 168:08:09 Scott: 3.5. (Long Pause) 4.0. (Pause; sound of repress ends) Okay; " Press Reg A and B to Cabin".

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay. Standby. (Pause) [An EVA is defined as the time when the cabin pressure is below 3.5 psi and, therefore, EVA-3 started at approximately 163:18:11 and ended at approximately 168:08:09. These times give a duration of 4 hours 49 minutes 58 seconds. The Apollo 15 Mission Report gives start and end times of 163:18:14 and 168:08:04, respectively. The differences are too small to be significant and are indicative of the typical errors in the original NASA transcript.]

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1680411csm.text: Dave and Jim, this is Houston.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay; A and B are in Cabin.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Okay; PLSS O2 going off. [Dave is a little annoyed at the thought of another interruption.]

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Joe's trying to call us.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Yeah, I know it.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1680411csm.text: Troops...

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1680411csm.text: Rog, Dave and Jim. Ed's coming on the line down here. Just wanted to say I enjoyed it.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: (Pleased) Oh! Well, thank you, Joe. You did a superfine job. Appreciate you keeping such good track of us.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Allen
a15_1680411csm.text: Wouldn't have missed it for anything.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Thank you, Joe. [Flight Director Gerry Griffin comes on line briefly.]

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Griffin
a15_1680411csm.text: Hadley Base, this is Flight, too. The whole Mission Control team wants to take their hats off to you for a fine job. It was a lot of fun.

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1680411csm.text: Well, thank you, Gerry. We'd like to take our hats off to the whole team. By golly, you guys are really sharp down there, and we sure appreciate it. 'Cause you know as well as we do we sure couldn't do it without you. (Pause) (To Jim) Okay, let's see. "Cabin warning lights off. Cabin pressure's stable at about 4.5." "Use purge valve to depress." We're depressed. I am. Aren't you?

a15_1680411csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1680411csm.text: Yeah. [Journal Contributor Harald Kucharek wonders "if this is really a pure technical exchange or is it also a play on words? They've finished their last EVA and they are going to leave, never to return. They are not really depressed; but, perhaps, feel a little bit sad, particularly after the loss of the North Complex."] Return to the LM Apollo 15 Journal Post-EVA-3 Activities

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: (Reading Surface 11-1) "Verify EVA circuit breaker configuration." If you can move forward, I can get in there and verify mine.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Stand by.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Are you trying to get your O2 off?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Okay; it's off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Good. Okay. (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay, my circuit breakers are okay except Fan 2 to Suit Fan Delta-P, which we'll pick up (in just a few seconds).

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Check mine here. Okay. Mine are okay. Let's see. "CB(16) ECS: Suit Fan 2, close."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay, closed.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: "Suit Fan Delta-P, close."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Closed.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; "doff the gloves and stow on the comm panel."

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Wait. I didn't depress. I'm going to have to use the purge valve.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Oh, you didn't, huh? Oh. Okay. Can you get it, okay?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. Stand by. (Long Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: No, I can't, Dave. I'll turn around.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. Let me get out of your way. (Pause) Okay, come on around.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: It (meaning the suit pressure)'s coming down, but very slowly.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; come on around. (Pause) Okay; put you in high (purge valve) flow, here. There you go.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; let's take off your gloves. When you get down (in pressure). (Long Pause) I'll "verify the safety" (on the forward dump valve ), here. Auto. Safety's on the dump valve. Next thing is to remove purge valves, anyway. "Descent Water valve, Open", when you get to it, Jim.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Okay; in just a moment. Back up a little bit. (Pause) Okay, Descent Water is coming open.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: What's next?

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; "pull the purge valve out". You did it. "Disconnect OPS O2 hose." (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: In work. (Long Pause) Okay; mine's out.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay; and the next thing is "connect the LM O2 hoses; red to red and blue to blue".

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Red to red and blue to blue.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah, we've got to do a dump.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. (Long Pause) [Once they doff the PLSSs and check the OPSs, they will depressurize the cabin, open the hatch, and jettison the PLSSs and a jettison bag .]

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: We better make sure we got them (the LM hoses) under the OPS (hose)...(correcting himself) PLSS (hose). Okay. Okay; I go to Suit Flow. (Garbled) Phew! (Pause)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Doesn't look like my prime water is off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Say again?

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Doesn't feel like the prime water is off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: I've got bare hands, now, when I get back here. (Garbled)

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Getting water in the suit.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: I know it. There, it's off. It was off, and you must have bumped it, maybe. (Pause) It was off, but you are getting water, all right.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: I feel it running down my leg.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah. I can't understand that. It was off. I mean it wasn't off then, but I remember turning it off, and it went off.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: Yeah, it's probably catching up on something, Dave, just like it did yesterday...

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Yeah.

a15a1680952.speaker: Irwin
a15a1680952.text: When I turn around. Okay. My O2 hose is disconnected, and going to Suit Flow.

a15a1680952.speaker: Scott
a15a1680952.text: Okay. Then " Suit Isolation (Valve to) Suit Flow; PLSS Pump, Off".

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1681613csm.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: PLSS Pump, Off.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Fan, Off. (Pause)

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1681613csm.text: Endeavour, go ahead.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Fan, Off.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. "Disconnect PLSS water from PGA and connect LM water to PGA."

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. You ready for me to turn the Data Systems, Off? [Pause.]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: In work. (Long Pause) Okay; water's connected. How about a little (LM) LCG pump action?

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1681613csm.text: Roger, Al. If you've secured the SIM bay experiments, we're ready for the Datum [means Data] System, Off.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay, we're secured now. [Long pause.]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Yes, sir.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Is it called for?

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Not yet. Let's press on down here.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Your (LM oxygen) flow ought to cool you there; it's cooling me pretty good.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Yeah. [They have completed Surface 11-1 and are about to start 11-2.]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. "PLSS Mode, both to O. Audio circuit-breaker, open, and connect to LM comm."

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay; you back on (LM comm)? (No answer; Pause) Back on, Jim? (No answer; Pause) Back on, Jim? (Long Pause)

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay, Al; as you go around the corner, all of your systems are looking in good shape. Have fun with the gegenschein photos.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay, Karl; hope so, and see you around the other side.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Henize
a15_1681613csm.text: Righto.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1681613csm.text: This is Apollo Control at 168 hours, 24 minutes Ground Elapsed Time after a third EVA at 4 hours and 50 minutes and 9 seconds from depress to repress. They started depressurization of the Lunar Module at 163:17:50 Ground Elapsed Time. The crew loaded equipment aboard the Lunar Roving Vehicle at 164:04 at which time they began the trip out to the ALSEP area. And the abbreviated timeline for the third extravehicular activity included recovering the core tube which had been driven yesterday and partially loosened. That had to be recovered from the ALSEP area. From then, they drove over to station

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay?

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Yeah, that's better. Okay, Audio panels for both of us, "VHF A to Receive and B to..."

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1681613csm.text: Back over here.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: "B to Off. Mode, ICS/PTT, and Relay, Off." [Comm Break]

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1681613csm.text: Hadley Base, Houston. Do you read?

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Rog, Houston. Hadley Base. Go.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1681613csm.text: Okay; could we have the Power Amp, On, please.

a15_1681613csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1681613csm.text: Power Amp coming on. [Very Long Comm Break] [Scott - "Ed Mitchell has come on as CapCom because he's the expert in the rendezvous. We would normally have a new CapCom for launch; but the CapCom is specially Ed Mitchell because Ed really understands the rendezvous - just like Joe Allen really understood the geology. Ed did the direct rendezvous on 14, so I wanted Ed Mitchell there. I shouldn't downplay rendezvous. It's not trivial. It's got to be done very carefully. Aviation, like the sea, is not inherently dangerous; but it is terribly unforgiving of any carelessness, incapacity, or neglect.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Endeavour, Houston, Standing by.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Houston, Endeavour's on.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay, Al. Good morning.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Is it morning, Ed?

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Yeah, it's morning down here, Al. Al, we've got a couple of changes for you. We're going to delete the P22 because the LM crew needs a little extra time, and substitute a P24 from the Command Module for it. If you've already got your camera on the sextant, sorry about that. If not, delete it.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. I've already got it on, but that's no problem.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. We'll give you a P24 landmac - landmark track PAD whenever you're ready.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay. Your target's the LM. T-1, 169:34:08; T-2, 38:15; TCA, 40:38; T-3, 41:06; south 3 nautical miles; and your attitude will have to change a little, Al. We're using roll, pitch and yaw of 000, 350/231 and 000. Noun 89, latitude 26.107; longitude over 2, plus 01.828; altitude, minus 013.26; and, at 169:25 in your Flight Plan, change the R2 of Noun 78 to minus 080.00.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Al, I gave you a wrong time [for the R2 change]...

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Roger, Ed; copy...

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: 169:15 is the time where that should be. I don't see it there.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay, Ed. I have - I have that one in the Flight Plan now; at 169:15, R2 is minus 068.00.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: That's affirm; and we're substituting minus 080.00.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Understand; substitute for that, minus 080.00.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: That's affirm, Al.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay; here goes the landmark tracking PAD. P24 on the LM, T-1, 169:34:08; T-2 is 38:15, 40:38, 41:06; that's 3 miles south; roll, pitch, and yaw are 000, 350/231, 000. Noun 89's are plus 26.107, plus 01.828, minus 013.26; and I've changed R2 of the DAP load.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Okay, Al; and we will need marks on them of course.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Roger.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1690607csm.text: Be back with you in a little while.

a15_1690607csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1690607csm.text: Oh, okay.

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay, Falcon. We observe the batteries coming on; and I have a lift-off time when you're ready.

a15a1691556.speaker: Irwin
a15a1691556.text: Stand by. (Pause) Okay, Ed. I'm ready to copy the LM ascent PAD (as per Surface 12-4).

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay; I don't have an ascent PAD for you, but I have the lift-off time. It's 171:37:22.36.

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: I think I heard that. Let me read it back: 171:37:22.36. And I have some star changes for the P57.

a15a1691556.speaker: Irwin
a15a1691556.text: Okay; go ahead. [In Program 57, they re-align the inertial platform using star sightings made with the Alignment Optical Telescope (AOT). The P57 procedures are on Surface 12-2.]

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Rog. For the P57 coming up right now, let's use star 5 (Polaris) and detent 3 and you should find it at a cursor of 182.2 and the spiral of 284.0.

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: And, Falcon, when you get around to it, how about an ED batt, check, please (as per Surface 12-1)?

a15a1691556.speaker: Scott
a15a1691556.text: And, Ed, an E(rasable)-memory dump coming down (as per Surface 12-1).

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay; we're ready. Let her come. (Pause)

a15a1691556.speaker: Mitchell
a15a1691556.text: Okay. Hadley Base, Houston. We got your E-mod. We're ready to give you an uplink (as per Surface 12-2) if we can have P00 (Program Zero-Zero) and Data. (Pause)

a15a1691556.speaker: Scott
a15a1691556.text: All righty, P00 and Data. You got it. [Comm Break. Here, Houston is updating the LM computer's memory.]

a15_1692033csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692033csm.text: Al, it seems like we had a - error on that last PAD I read you. The altitude should be minus 001.33. Understand?

a15_1692033csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692033csm.text: Understand the altitude should be minus 001.33.

a15_1692033csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692033csm.text: Falcon, Houston. Looks like we need to do a Verb 96. You're going through an integration loop.

a15_1692033csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1692033csm.text: Yeah. I thought that P00 and Data might get you in trouble. (Pause) Okay; how's that?

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. On your High Gain [Antenna], go Wide and Manual, please. [Pause.]

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692905csm.text: Roger. Wide and Narrow - Wide and Manual.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692905csm.text: Okay. Any angles you want me to put in?

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Endeavour and Falcon, Houston. We're going to delete the VHF check at this pass, just to give you a little more time. [Long pause.]

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Endeavour and Falcon, Houston. We're going to delete the VHF check at this pass just to give you a little more time.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692905csm.text: Roger. Endeavour's got the VHF set up anyway.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: That's fine. We just won't - bother the LM with it.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: That's fine. We just won't bother the LM with it. [Long Comm Break]

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692905csm.text: Okay. You might tell them though, I've got my - if you want to check out the rendezvous radar, I've got the transponder on.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Al, you're in the mud. You'll have to try me on that one again.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1692905csm.text: Okay. Just wanted to let you know that I've also got the rendezvous transponder on.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. One minute to T-1.

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1692905csm.text: Houston, Falcon. Do you have the torquing angles?

a15_1692905csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1692905csm.text: Okay, you can torque. 169:37:47 Irwin: Roger; torque at 38. [Dave and Jim are performing the platform alignment on Surface 12-2. Houston has looked at the star-sighting measurements they have fed into the computer and has decided that they are consistent with the other available information.] [Very Long Comm Break] [As per Surface 12-3, once Dave and Jim finish the platform alignment, they will stow the film magazines, samples and other EVA-related items. At some point during this interval, Dave takes a color CDR window pan and then Jim takes an LMP window pan (assembly by David Harland). Dave

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1694137csm.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. Through with tracking, but I'm not sure they're very good marks.

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1694137csm.text: Okay, Al; we understand. High Sun angle may have made it difficult. [Pause.]

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1694137csm.text: Yeah, I seemed to have a lot of interference in the sextant from the landmark, by the sight - part of the optics.

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1694137csm.text: Al, do you think you saw him at all?

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1694137csm.text: Yeah. I think the first couple of marks were on him, Ed, but I couldn't hold him.

a15_1694137csm.speaker: Worden
a15_1694137csm.text: I kept - I kept losing him.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. In the blind, give us the best Omni[directional antenna], please. [Long pause.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: En - Endeavour, Houston. Best Omni, please. [No answer.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. In the blind, best Omni, please. [No answer.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. Best Omni. [No answer.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Hello, Endeavour. Best Omni, please. [No answer.] [Long pause.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Endeavour, Houston. Give us best Omni, please.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: I... [Long pause.]

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Falcon, Houston. How do you read?

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1695751csm.text: Go ahead, Houston. 5 by.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Roger. How are you coming with your stowage (as per Surface 12-3)? We have these locations available still, if you're not too well stowed up yet.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Ende...

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Scott
a15_1695751csm.text: Well, we were just mushing along with it by the checklist here, and why don't you go through what you have in mind? I'm sorry. We're pressing on. We'll take a listen to what you got here.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Okay. What we were expecting was bags 4 and 6 in the ISA (Interim Stowage Assembly); bag 3 behind the aft engine; and 2 and 7 in the right- and left-hand stowage compartments with 7 in the left-hand, 2 in the right-hand.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Irwin
a15_1695751csm.text: Ed, let me tell you where we have them.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: Okay.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Irwin

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell

The pre-flight plan was to take the checklist we had on board - and the limitations on the weights - and stow according to that checklist. a15_1695751csm.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1695751csm.text: And be advised we're showing total weight of slightly in excess of 230 pounds, which is a little over what we expected. However, by deleting a plane change, we're going to have plenty of fuel for it.

a15_1695751csm.speaker: Irwin

[Scott - "You were asking about extending the EVA two hours; and here's a comment by Mitchell: 'We have a little bit more weight than we expected, in terms of rocks,' he says, 'however, by deleting a plane change we're going to have plenty of fuel. See, we had a margin built for a plane change (by the LM), which we can now use for rocks. Al Worden has done that plane change (as scheduled with the Command Module), so we're not taking something away that we might need later on."] [Jones - "It's padding that's suddenly become available because everything has gone 'bing, bing'."]

a15_1720108.text: Let's see, what - [garble] I remember, we've got a [garble] to do.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: How you doing over there, Albert?

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Doing just fine, but it's back to end-to-end, and I've got much in motion.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Very good. And reading the procedures and checking...

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Oh, yes! Bad update! What do you know. I've been looking for it and I finally saw it, but it's not very funny.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Yes, you're right down the path.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Yes, so are you. Your light is right through the money.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Is it really? Yours - yours is really dim. About like a - maybe a fourth magnitude star? Okay, let's really hit them.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Especially about this problem. Make it stick.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Okay. Know what you got to do, Jim?

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Yes. I'll take it. I think that's going out there.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: You guys coming up on final comp.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Okay. We got 20 seconds or so.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Why don't you mark final comp. Get you back with us.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: All right, I sure will. 10 seconds. 3, 2, 1...

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Well, it's a 3-second burn, so that makes sense.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: No, I don't need it. We have to go to coffee in a minute.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Okay, Al. We've got a minus 1.1, 0, and a minus 1.1.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Okay, and I got a plus 1.5, and a minus .2, and plus 1.9.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: How about that! That's very nice. Think we'll burn our solution on time. That's - it sort of took an [garble].

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Okay, go ahead and burn your solution.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: All right. We'll burn our solution.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Got the AGS and redo solution.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: All righty. It's reading straight, now.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Yes, I guess they're using it.'

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: One more cycle now. Okay, we got it all in.

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Consider it down there, Jim. It's really 2222s.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Oh, you're shining in the sunlight now! Boy, is that pretty!

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: Yes, I can see in the sunlight now, too.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Okay. We've got our first mark. We should be up with you.

a15_1720108.speaker: Worden
a15_1720108.text: I believe I can even make out the shape.

a15_1720108.speaker: Irwin
a15_1720108.text: Think you can call another one up?

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Hmm! You sure if you got the right thing?

a15_1720108.speaker: Scott
a15_1720108.text: Okay. Can't put too much [garble]. Seems to be squared away though, now.

a15_1720108.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1720108.text: This is Apollo Control at 173 hours. We're just under a minute away from Acquisition Of Signal with both the Command Module and the Lunar Module. We'll be getting a TPI burn report from Falcon soon after acquisition. And Falcon will be starting the rendezvous braking maneuver a few minutes after acquisition. We expect television to begin at about 173 hours, 10 minutes, as scheduled in the Flight Plan and see this rendezvous. We'll stand by live now for the first conversation."

a15_1720108.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1720108.text: We have acquired both vehicles now, we'll stand by."

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Falcon, Houston. Standing by.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Rog, Houston. Falcon had a good TPI. It burned a small midcourse 1, and a small midcourse 2. Presently, we have a visual on the Command Module and all the solutions have been agreeing very well.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. Did you write down your solutions, Dave?

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, we got them all in.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. We'll ask you for them later.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1730041.text: Range is about 2½ [nautical] miles now [4.6 km]. Range-rate, 29 feet per second [8.8 m/s]."

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Houston, Endeavour.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Hello, Endeavour. Standing by.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, TV's up to [garble].

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Say again. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Roger, copy. TV's on. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Endeavour, Houston. We're not tracking your High Gain [Antenna], yet.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1730041.text: We've got a black and white picture now. Be coming in color in just a minute.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: We have your picture, Endeavour. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I've got you visually there, Falcon. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, you're looking good.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: You're very garbled, Dave. Say again.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I got you at 1.28 [nautical] mile [2.37 km].

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we're right with you. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Endeavour, Houston. Give us Auto on the High Gain [Antenna], please.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: On Auto. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, one [nautical] mile and 27 feet per second on the radar.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Rog.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Endeavour, Houston. Do you have the Falcon on your monitor? [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: No, I wasn't watching it, Ed. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Okay, 3,000 feet, braking down to 20 [fps]. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Don't waste any time on it, Al. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Okay, 1,500 feet, braking down to 10.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Okay, 500, braking to 5.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: [Garble].

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: [Garble] Falcon [garble]. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, Houston. We're station-keeping at about 120 feet [37 metres] or so.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: The which sensor?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Roger, Dave. during the Command Module pitch-around, we'd like for you to take a look at the V-over-H sensor in the SIM bay, if you can. Do you know how to spot it?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: V-over-H.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, it's - it's on the Pan Camera gadget.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I guess we're not - Well, Al's talking to us.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay, what we're looking for is to see if anything is in the way of the lens of that sensor. [Pause.] If you're not familiar, I can give you a page number in your LM Data Systems Book to take a look at it. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, stand by one.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: No, it's not - it's not on the lens, Dave. It's right alongside the lens on the body of the camera...

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: We've got a picture of it, Al.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: ...it tells us what speed to take the picture at.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we'll get a picture of it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay. I'll go ahead and do your pitcharound. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: And, give me - give me a call when you start.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Houston, what page is that on in the LM Systems book?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. It's page 43 in the LM's System's Bo - Data Book.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. On the right-hand side, Dave, you see that one little line that says, "Mapping and Pan Cameras N 2 [nitrogen] Press[ure] Systems Assembly."

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: We haven't got it out yet. Stand by.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, I'll go the higher rate, Dave. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, here we go.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, looks good, you're going the right way. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Dave, while he's pitching, I'll tell you - should be about the middle of the SIM bay by the Mapping Camera. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Unknown speaker
a15_1730041.text: [Garble.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Unknown speaker
a15_1730041.text: [Garble.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: A very nice maneuver, Endeavour. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, Houston. We don't see it labeled in here. Where - is it labeled on the picture?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Negative. As soon as you have the picture, I'll tell you where to look.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we got the picture; tell us where to look.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay, way over on the right-hand side, where it says, "Mapping and Pan Cameras N 2 Press System Assembly." [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: It's on the right picture. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: The one with the covers open?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: That's affirm. Between the end of that arrow and the lens, about halfway, is a little dot that represents the V-over-H assembly. Now, the camera lens will be covered - rather it will be folded up so you will not be able to see it; however, that is the item you're looking for, represented by the small circle about halfway in between the end of the arrow and the lens of the camera.

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I see a small circular object there just - just to the right of the handle, and I don't see anything covering it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Are you talking about the diagram, or in the SIM bay?

a15_1730041.speaker: Irwin
a15_1730041.text: No, in the SIM bay.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Okay. That's what we wanted to know.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Yeah, it's a little round black...

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: That's it - that's it.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: ...holder type of affair, right?

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: If you can snap a picture of it, we'd appreciate it. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we'll get one, Ed. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we've got the picture, Houston, and we'll proceed on with the docking.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Thank you, sir. [Pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, I'll pitch back around now, Davy.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: And, Falcon; Houston. Do you have any comments on the SIM bay, anything look out of the ordinary?

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: No, it looks very clean. The doors are all covered, and all the booms are retracted; and it looks neat and tidy.

a15_1730041.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1730041.text: Thank you.

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Okay, where'd you go?

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: We should be right where we were. Have you completed your maneuver?

a15_1730041.speaker: Worden
a15_1730041.text: Rog.

a15_1730041.speaker: Scott
a15_1730041.text: Okay, we're in the same inertial attitude, I'll come back around to you. Just stay there.

a15_1732724.speaker: Scott
a15_1732724.text: Okay, Endeavour. Would you handle station-keeping, we're going to pitch and yaw now.

a15_1732724.speaker: Worden
a15_1732724.text: Okay, Houston. Ready to get [garble, should be "Pyro"] Arm, On.

a15_1732724.speaker: Worden
a15_1732724.text: Roger. I'll [garble] turn on the [Sequential Events Controller] Logic when you're ready.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: I got barberpole.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: [Garble. May be "There, I got you."].

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: [Garble.] [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Okay. You ready to come in?

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: All set. [Long pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Hard dock.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Roger. Copy hard dock. And, Falcon, if you'll give us 105 [degrees pitch] and 67 [degrees yaw, on the steerable S-band antenna], we should have your steerable [antenna].

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: Roger. 105 and 67. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Good show, Endeavour. It's nice to be aboard again.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Welcome home.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: And Falcon, Houston. Now that we have the steerable [antenna] back, when you get a moment, pull the ECS Auto Transfer, Open, and then the Glycol Pump 1, Open.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Roger. ECS Auto Transfer is Open - and I'll open the Glycol Pump 1 now.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. We want to get a little data down here.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Okay, do you want us to select 2, or just let it run?

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Negative. Just wait for 30 seconds.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Okay, we'll stand by for your call.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Thank you.

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: And, Houston; Falcon. Do you have an update for us for the LM weight/CSM weight?

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Stand by. LM weight, 5444 [pounds, 2,469 kg].

a15_1733552.speaker: Irwin
a15_1733552.text: Roger. LM weight 5444.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: And I don't have the CSM weight at the moment. And you can close the Glycol Pump 1 first and then the Auto Transfer.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Closing Glycol Pump 1 now - Auto Transfer now.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger, and I thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1733552.text: Docking time was 173 hours, 36 minutes, 27 seconds.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Go ahead. All right, I got it. [Long pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. A couple of changes to the Command Module - LM/Command Module transfer list on stowage items, when you get a break. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Okaky, Houston. Stand by one. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: And, Falcon, we'll take Data and uplink to you.

a15_1733552.speaker: Scott
a15_1733552.text: You've got it.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. You might as well give me those updates now.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Okeydoke, Endeavour. On page 2 - 283. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Okay, go.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Okay, Al. About the middle of the LM to Command Module transfer list, the second Decom bag and the fourth Decom bag - scratch. [Pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Understand. Scratch second and fourth Decom bags.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: That's affirm. And the - at the bottom, write "Collection bag, 3, in [compartment] A9." [Long pause.]

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Understand. Add "Collection bag, 3, in A9."

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: Roger. And they're going to give you a - a section of core stem, three sections long. You ought to put that on the left-hand tray along A1 and A2, and secure it with - with either your LM tiedown rope or your extra webbing in there.

a15_1733552.speaker: Worden
a15_1733552.text: Roger. Understand. The core tubes go along A1, A2, tied down on the tray.

a15_1733552.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1733552.text: That's affirm. You got it. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Dave, you want to verify that the dump valve's in Auto?

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Roger. Standby one. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Verify.

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Okay, I'll go ahead and start equalizing the pressure.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, good. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: And, Falcon; Flight - or rather, Falcon, Houston. FIDO's on pins and needles for your TPI solution if you can get a moment to read it to us.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Rog, we'll do it right now. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, Houston. I assume that you got the recycle before we went around the corner there.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: That's affirm.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, on the final [rendezvous burn] comp[utation], I'll read PGNS, AGS and CMC, if you are ready to copy them, in that order, in local-vertical coordinates.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Roger. Ready.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay. For the PGNS: plus 70.3, plus 5.9, minus 17.7. For the AGS: plus 70.4, plus 5.9, minus 19.1. The CMC: minus 69.1, minus 6.1, plus 16.1. We burned the PGNS on time, and we had about a 4-foot-per-second overburn on the APS which we trimmed out to 2/10ths.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Copy. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, the residuals were - for the PGNS after the trim - were plus .2, plus .2, and minus .4.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Copy. And assume midcourses were...

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Rog. We'll give you those too. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, and I'll give you the same answers for midcourse 1 if you're ready to copy, Houston.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Okay.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, PGNS was minus 1.1, 0, and minus 1.1. AGS was minus 1.5, 0, and minus 3.0. CS - CSM, plus 1.5, minus .2, plus 1.9. And we burned the PGNS solution to 0, .1 and .2.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Thank you, Dave, that's fine. Appreciate it.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: No, we'll take your PGNS - we'll take all the rest of them; we'll get them later.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, fine. It was pretty smooth all the way, everything looked nice, and the data went in very well, and I thought it was a super rendezvous.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Very good. Getting home's the main thing.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Yeah, but you know, these systems are just magnificent.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Yeah, they sure are, Dave. Okay, we suggest you press right along with your transfer and cleaning up.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Rog. We're in work right now.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: And whenever Jim's ready to do the targeting, we'll read him a PAD on that.

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, stand by, we'll give you a call. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1734227.text: This is Apollo Control at 173 hours, 47 minutes. The docked Falcon and Endeavour are in orbit, 64.1 by 53.8 nautical miles [118.7 by 99.6 km].

a15_1734227.speaker: Irwin
a15_1734227.text: Okay, Ed. I'm ready to copy the impact PAD.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Okay, understand you're ready for the LM impact PAD, Jim; is that correct?

a15_1734227.speaker: Irwin
a15_1734227.text: Yes, if that's what you have to pass.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Okay, it's a P30 PAD. 179:06:22.50; Noun 81s, minus 0121.9, plus 0056.0, plus 0148.8; 0071.1, minus 0037.1, 0200.3; 1:27; 047, 174. The rest is NA. And the LM weight: is 5444. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Irwin
a15_1734227.text: Roger, Readback for P30 PAD. 179:06:22.50; minus 0121.9, plus 0056.0, plus 0148.8; 0071.1, minus 0037.1, 0200.3; 1:27; 47, 174. And LM weight is 5444.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Good readback, Jim. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: And, Falcon; Houston. The computer's yours.

a15_1734227.speaker: Irwin
a15_1734227.text: Rog.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: And we want to leave it in Data, of course. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Scott
a15_1734227.text: Okay, we'll leave it in Data. It's all yours now. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. Before you get LOS and get too busy with the transfer, I need to give you a camera photo PAD for the next pass. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Okay. Go ahead, Houston.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Okay, this is the one at 174:50, Al. T-start - it's for the Map Camera - T-start, 174:50:04; T-stop, 175:49:36. Your Image Motion BP plus 4 at T-start, and BP at 175:30:00. And your Pan Camera photo PAD, to be copied at 175:20. T-start, 175:34:32; T-stop is 36:52. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Roger, Ed. Understand Mapping Camera photo PAD is T-start, 174:50:04; T-stop, 175:49:26. And at T-start, you want Image Motion to go barber pole plus 4.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: That's affirm.

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: And, at 175:30, understand you want Image Motion to go to barber pole.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: That's affirm, Al. And the correct time for the T-stop on that was 175:49:36. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Understand, 49:36. [Long pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: And the Pan Camera photo PAD is T-start, 175:35:42; T-stop, 175:36:52.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: Roger. The T-start, 175:34:32, T-stop is good. [Pause.]

a15_1734227.speaker: Worden
a15_1734227.text: Understand, T-start is 175:34:32.

a15_1734227.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1734227.text: That's a good readback now, Al.

a15_1735512.speaker: Worden
a15_1735512.text: Yeah, it's pressurized, Jim. Can you read me? Okay, tunnel's pressurized and I'm up in it now, checking the latching.

a15_1735512.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1735512.text: The cabin pressures are equalized, now.

a15_1735512.speaker: Scott
a15_1735512.text: Hello, Houston. The Falcon is back on its roost and going to sleep.

a15_1735512.speaker: Scott
a15_1735512.text: She's all yours now, Ed. We're going to go off comm and put her to bed.

a15_1735512.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1735512.text: Okay, one item, Dave. You're not marking these bags before you head them down, are you.

a15_1735512.speaker: Scott
a15_1735512.text: The bags are all numbered. We've got the collection bags in the cover bags with the proper numbers on them, and that was all we're planning to do.

a15_1735512.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1735512.text: Okay, you're not helping him with the stowage when you pass them in, are you? I would change your Flight Plan if you did; otherwise, I'll just give it to him. [Pause.]

a15_1735512.speaker: Scott
a15_1735512.text: Well, I guess the best thing would be to go ahead and give it to him, because we'll just pass them over then.

a15_1735512.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1735512.text: Okay, I've given them to him already. Thank you.

a15_1735512.speaker: Scott
a15_1735512.text: Yeah, that fine. He - he's got a much better handle on the stowage over there anyway than we do.

a15_1735512.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1735512.text: This is Apollo Control at 173 hours, 59 minutes. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin are powering down Falcon now. We'll be off communications for some time. They'll power down the LM and transfer the equipment and the samples into the Command Module.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Endeavour, Houston.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go ahead.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Al, we observed when you were in P79, just before the docking, that you got a POO DOO. Do you have any words on that. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: No, I don't, Ed. [Long pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. We're going to have to update your Flight Plan with a couple of items before you go around the corner, whenever you can get around to it.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, Ed, let's go ahead and do them now.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Roger. And, Al, give us a Verb 74 when I'm talking to you.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Rog. Verb 74.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, the first Flight Plan update is the - at 174:12. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, where it says the "Mapping Camera Laser Experiment Covers, Open," et cetera, et cetera. Delete that.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Rog. Go ahead.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: And the second line after that, the "Map Camera Track," et cetera, et cetera; delete that, we're going to move those to 174:40. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, understand.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, down a little bit in the next group of words where it says "Laser Altimeter, On" at 174:17; we're going to scratch that. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, scratch Laser Altimeter.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: We're going to move that to 174:49. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Roger. Move to 174:49.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, and at 175:49, going to add a - another Laser Altimeter, Off. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Rog, understand. At 175:49, Laser Altimeter, Off.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, the next item is at 1 - Stand by on that a minute. And at 175:54 [means 175:58], delete the Laser Altimeter, Off. [Long pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Understand. At 175:58, delete Laser Altimeter, Off.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: That's affirm.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: And at 176:02, the next page, right after all those words, we want to add in the "Map Camera" - that's about 176:02 - "Map Camera Laser Experiment Covers, Close, Talkback's barberpole slash gray, then Off." [Long pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Looks like that item came down there about 4 minutes later, Al. [Pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Roger that, I see it now.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Yeah, I just now saw it, too. I presume they want it moved up there a few minutes. And at 178:02; Oh, sorry about that - at 177:56, put in a "Logic Power, two, Off." [Long pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, I understand Logic Power, both of them, Off, at 177:56.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Rog. Next page, 178:02, "Laser Altimeter, On." Delete. [Long pause.]

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Delete "Laser Altimeter, On," at 178:02.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay. And at 179:40, following page, delete "Laser Altimeter, Off" - and about 179:41, delete those two lines, "Map Camera Laser Experiment Covers" and "Logic Power, two, Off." Delete those.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay. Delete the three lines at 179:40, "Laser Altimeter," "Mapping Camera Covers," and "Logic Power, Off." Delete those three lines.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay. I think we got them all that time, Al. Thank you.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. If you can holler at Dave and Jim, remind them that - to get their radiation meters out of their pockets. We'd still like those readings we didn't get earlier.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Roger, Houston.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Okay, Endeavour; Houston. Can we have Auto on the High Gain [Antenna]? And request Falcon to go to Aft Omni as he goes over the hill, or after he's over the hill.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay. You want Falcon to go to Aft Omni.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: Yeah, at LOS. And you're about 3 and a half minutes from LOS now.

a15_1740220.speaker: Worden
a15_1740220.text: Okay, I'm in Auto and they're going to go to Aft Omni at LOS.

a15_1740220.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1740220.text: That's affirm. [Pause.] And ask them when they do that to verify Track Mode, Slew.

a15_1741353.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1741353.text: And, Endeavour, we're about 40 seconds from LOS; see you on the other side.

a15_1741353.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1741353.text: This is Apollo Control at 174 hours, 14 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on both spacecraft as they go behind the Moon, and on the 49th revolution for Endeavour. As we acquired Falcon on this pass, Dave Scott reported a good Terminal Phase Initiate burn. He reported he had performed two small midcourse corrections, and at that time could see the Command Module. The braking in the rendezvous went well. Al Worden brought the television up a few minutes early. We lost the picture for a while when the High Gain Antenna went to Wide Beam while Worden was maneuvering Endeavour for its inspection by

a15_1741353.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1741353.text: This is Apollo Control at 174 hours, 58 minutes. We're a little over 30 seconds away from Acquisition Of Signal. There will be a news conference at 8:30 am tomorrow on the lunar surface activities conducted by astronaut Jack Schmitt. This news conference will be in the main auditorium. We'll stand by now for first words on this 50th revolution.

a15_1745845.speaker: Worden
a15_1745845.text: Houston, 15. [We're] still in the midst of doing a little house cleaning.

a15_1745845.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1745845.text: Okay; kind of figured that, Al.

a15_1750637.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1750637.text: Endeavour, Houston. Would you ask Falcon to switch to Forward Omni?

a15_1750637.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1750637.text: And, Al. Do you want to verify - verify that you got your Mapping Camera started at 174:50?

a15_1750637.speaker: Worden
a15_1750637.text: Roger, Ed. Was 1 minute late on that - on the Mapping Camera, but we got it started at 1 - at 174:51.

a15_1750637.speaker: Worden
a15_1750637.text: Roger, Ed. One other thing, I didn't get the P52 in.

a15_1750637.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1750637.text: Al, I'll keep track of your cameras for you and give you a warning on the stops and starts.

a15_1750637.speaker: Worden
a15_1750637.text: Okay; if you would, that would help. [Long pause.]

a15_1750637.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1750637.text: 15, Houston. Give me Reacq and Narrow [on the High Gain Antenna], please.

a15_1751344.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1751344.text: 15, Houston. We're having a lot of trouble with the LM comm. Apparently, we're right at the midst of the Omni. Let's try aft again, please. [Pause.]

a15_1751344.speaker: Worden
a15_1751344.text: Houston, I was talking with Dave. Say again.

a15_1751344.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1751344.text: Roger. Let's try the LM Aft Omni again, please.

a15_1751621.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1751621.text: How about the Gamma-ray Gain switch? Step it three times for us, please, Al.

a15_1752202.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752202.text: Al, we're going to change your Mapping Camera procedures. I'm going to call them to you on time rather than read them to you now. So press on, and I'll give you a warning here in about 5 or 6 minutes.

a15_1752202.speaker: Worden
a15_1752202.text: Yeah, that'd be fine, Ed. Just give me a couple minute warnings, so I can get over to the camera. As you probably know, the LEB [Lower Equipment Bay] Timer's not working.

a15_1752202.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752202.text: Rog. I'll keep you posted on time; press on.

a15_1752456.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752456.text: Al, we observe that your - you've got P00 up instead of P20. Better check your attitude and get her back in P20, and let's see if our camera is pointed at anything.

a15_1752456.speaker: Worden
a15_1752456.text: Rog. That just happened about 15 seconds ago. You must have caught it just as it went to P00. And I don't think we're even out of the deadband.

a15_1752456.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752456.text: Very good. And Al - just stand by. We still got a couple of minutes, yet. What I'm going to do is have you retract the Mapping Camera with it still running and then turn it off. We're running a little test on it. And I'll call that for you in a couple of minutes.

a15_1752456.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1752456.text: P20 is the orbital rate program which we want for the camera operations in the SIM bay.

a15_1752456.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752456.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Stand by to retract the Mapping Camera.

a15_1752456.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1752456.text: [It will] take about 4 minutes, Al, and I'll call you after that.

a15_1753154.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753154.text: Okay. Apollo 15, Houston. Turn your Mapping Camera, Off. [Pause.]

a15_1753154.speaker: Worden
a15_1753154.text: Okay, Ed. Mapping Camera going Off.

a15_1753154.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753154.text: Roger. The Laser Altimeter, Off. And the Map Camera Laser Covers, Closed.

a15_1753154.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753154.text: And I'll have the Pan Camera T-start here in just about 2 minutes. I'll call you and give you 15 or 20 seconds warning.

a15_1753154.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753154.text: 15, Houston. Stand by for T-start on the Pan Camera. [Pause.]

a15_1753640.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753640.text: 15, Houston; stand by for Pan Camera, Off. [Pause.]

a15_1753640.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753640.text: Okay, Al. That completes all that for us. Thank you.

a15_1753640.speaker: Worden
a15_1753640.text: Okay, Ed. Thank you very much.

a15_1753640.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753640.text: Okay, Apollo 15; Houston. We're getting a little itchy for some LM data. We'd like for them to bring up the steerable [antenna] if they can, please, at 146 and 29.

a15_1753640.speaker: Worden
a15_1753640.text: Okay, Ed. [I'll] have them bring up the steerable.

a15_1753640.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1753640.text: And, 15, we verify that your Pan Camera [lens]'s [tucked] in, and you can turn the Power, Off, on it.

a15_1754329.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754329.text: Apollo 15, Houston. You can start your maneuver to jettison attitude at any time. And I have a slight update to the attitude. [Pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Your Gamma-ray Gainstep, Shield, Off, please. [Pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Worden
a15_1754759.text: Okay, Ed. Gamma-ray, Gain, Shield, going Off. [Long pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Worden
a15_1754759.text: Okay, Ed, it looks like the chaos is slowing down a little bit here, if you want to talk about the Flight Plan.

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: Okay, Al. You can start your maneuvering to your LM jettison attitude most anytime. And I'll update the attitude for you. It's Roll, 14; Pitch, 38 and Yaw 344. [Pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Worden
a15_1754759.text: Rog, Ed. Understand the LM jettison attitude is Roll, 014; Pitch, 038 and Yaw, 344.

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: That's right; and the CSM Sep time here is 177:25:33. [Long pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: Rog. And your CSM weight for your DAP is 36370. [Pause.]

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: Rog. And I'll call this Gamma-ray, Gainstep, Shield, back On, Al. We want to let it go for 10 minutes here.

a15_1754759.speaker: Worden
a15_1754759.text: Okay, Gainstep comes back to Shield, On.

a15_1754759.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1754759.text: Negative, negative. I'll call it back On in 10 minutes.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Apollo 15, Houston.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Houston, 15; go ahead.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Rog. Would you ask Dave and Jim to make sure that we go ahead and get steps 4 and 5 on page 14 of their checklist before LOS here? And then, soon as we get into attitude, we can take a look at all this before we go LOS. We got about 16 minutes.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Okay, understand. That's steps 4 and 5 on page 14.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: That's affirm. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: And, Apollo 15; Houston. Also, go ahead and get the P30 and et cetera, et cetera . [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Rog. Understand. Go ahead and get the P30 in the LM.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: And there is no update to the T IG . It's good as given to you earlier. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Rog. Understand. T IG is good. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: And, Al, stand by to turn the Gamma-ray, Gainstep, Shield, On.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Gamma-ray, Shield, On.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Okay, Mark, On and let's take the Map Camera, On switch to Standby and the Map Camera, Image Motion, Off. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Okay. Map Camera, Standby, Image Motion, Off.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: That about cleans us up, Al.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Okay, Ed. Thank you much for your help. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Oh, Ed, I'm back on comm, over in the Falcon.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Okay, Jim. Sounds good. Should be in attitude in just a minute. And your angles, 205 and 70, as in the Flight Plan, should be good. And we're about 13 minutes from LOS.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay. Do you have any updates for me before we have LOS?

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Negative. All we wanted to do was just - the guidance system's state vector's okay and configured before LOS, and I don't believe we have an update. I'll check. [Long pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Falcon, Houston. We'd just like to complete down through step 1 or 2 of configure AGS before LOS. And, Endeavour, if you can give us an Accept, we'll shoot you an uplink before LOS.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Okay, getting Accept.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Falcon copies. [Pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: You got Accept.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Understand.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Ed, can you get for - the P30 load here for me as I go through it.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Okay, stand by one. [Pause.] Okay. Go ahead. Got the first one.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay, how does that look?

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Looks good.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Looks good here, Jim.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay, I'll [press] Pro[ceed] on this one. [Long pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay, I'm going to go to P00, Ed.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Rog, Jim. That one looks okay, too. I don't see much of it.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: That's right. [Pause.] Okay, do we have a Go for closeout?

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Give us a 470 readout on the DEDA [Data Entry and Display Assembly, part of the AGS], please.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay. You have it. [Long pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Okay. And, Jim, can you verify that you've done all of step 2 on the comm?

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Yes, I meant Slew on the Track Mode. [Long pause.]

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: Okay, Jim. You're Go for closeout. The next time we see the LM, you'll all be buttoned up. So suggest you make a very careful check of the items from now on.

a15_1755706.speaker: Irwin
a15_1755706.text: Okay; thank you, Ed.

a15_1755706.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1755706.text: And, Endeavour. It's your computer.

a15_1755706.speaker: Worden
a15_1755706.text: Roger, Ed.

a15_1761123.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1761123.text: Okay, Endeavour, Houston. We're a minute and 20 seconds from LOS. Your ascent CapCom's going off duty, and I'll see you back on Earth. It's been a lot of fun getting you up here.

a15_1761123.speaker: Worden
a15_1761123.text: Okay, Ed. You're - thanks a million, pal. You've been a great help, and it was fun talking to you.

a15_1761123.speaker: Irwin
a15_1761123.text: Hey, Ed; Falcon. Looks like we just about got things cleaned up here.

a15_1761123.speaker: Mitchell
a15_1761123.text: Very good, guys. We'll see you in a few days. Thanks a lot.

a15_1761123.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1761123.text: This is Apollo Control at 176 hours, 12 minutes; and we've had Loss Of Signal on the 50th revolution. Dave Scott and Jim Irwin still in the Lunar Module but preparing to close it out. By the time we reacquire, they will be back in the Endeavour with the Lunar Module set up for jettison and later deorbit burn and impact on the lunar surface. During this pass, they transferred the lunar samples to the Command Module. Al Worden remarked they were doing some house cleaning, obviously a lot of dust and dirt comes up with those samples and they use the vacuum cleaner to clean up the cabin after the

a15_1761123.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1761123.text: This is Apollo Control at 176 hours, 23 minutes. The change of shift briefing scheduled for 5:15 has been canceled. To repeat, the change of shift briefing scheduled for 5:15 has been canceled. And to repeat an earlier announcement, a news conference on lunar surface activities will be held at 8:30 am tomorrow in the main MSC auditorium. Astronaut Jack Schmitt, the backup Lunar Module Pilot for Apollo 15, will be present at that news conference. This is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_1761123.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1761123.text: This is Apollo Control at 176 hours, 56 minutes. We'll be reacquiring the Command Module Endeavour , still docked with the Lunar Module Falcon , in about 2 minutes. At that time we expect that all three crewmen will be buttoned up inside the Command Module, and on this revolution will be preparing to jettison the Lunar Module and perform a small separation maneuver with the Command Module prior to LM impact. Glynn Lunney, the Flight Director for this shift, has completed a review of the status of the mission with each of his flight controllers, and, essentially, that status is as follows: For

a15_1765617.speaker: Parker
a15_1765617.text: Roger. Doing fine down here. Can you fellows confirm LM closed out and ready for jett[ison of LM].?

a15_1765617.speaker: Scott
a15_1765617.text: Rog. LM's closed out, and we're just now running our pressure integrity check, and we'll be all set in a jiffy.

a15_1765617.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1765617.text: Dave Scott reporting that the LM is ready for jettison on time. The Spacecraft Communicator on this shift is astronaut Robert Parker. During the LM impact, Doctor David W. Streinway, Chief of the Geophysics Branch at the Manned Spacecraft Center, will be available in the MSC News Center briefing room to provide background information and answer questions on the LM impact and the seismic data that is received. That will be at 8 pm in the MSC News Center briefing room. Also, in the way of briefings, tomorrow morning at 8:30 am, there will be a lunar surface science briefing with astronaut Jack S

a15_1770401.speaker: Scott
a15_1770401.text: Okay, we're going to be a few minutes here. We got to put some LCG plugs in our suits and it's going to take probably about 10 or 15 minutes to get all that done.

a15_1770401.speaker: Parker
a15_1770401.text: Okay, and we'd like a verification from Al that [the] X-ray [Spectrometer] is in Standby and X-ray/Alpha Covers are Closed before jett and Sep burn. [Pause.]

a15_1770401.speaker: Scott
a15_1770401.text: Okay. We - we'll get that for you when we get squared away here.

a15_1771002.speaker: Slayton
a15_1771002.text: Say, Dave, beautiful job there today all the way around. Hey, one quick question - how come you guys need plugs for those suits?

a15_1771002.speaker: Scott
a15_1771002.text: Well, because, apparently, the LCG connection on the inside won't hold an air seal, so we're getting them taken care of with these special - extra little blue plugs we got that are airtight on the inside. [Long pause.]

a15_1771002.speaker: Scott
a15_1771002.text: At least that's our first guess of - of why we didn't get a good suit integrity check or didn't even get a good buildup in the suit pressure.

a15_1771002.speaker: Slayton
a15_1771002.text: Rog. We - we had a complete misunderstanding on that, so that's the reason I asked the question, because we thought those plugs only were required when the LCG was not on. We're trying to crack that one for you down here, Dave. There's something screwy here. [Pause.]

a15_1771002.speaker: Scott
a15_1771002.text: Okay. Well, we'll put these plugs in and run another pressure integrity check and see how it works.

a15_1771002.speaker: Parker
a15_1771002.text: Roger, Dave. You guys talking about inside plugs or outside plugs?

a15_1771002.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1771002.text: This is Apollo Control. The plugs that are being discussed between Dave Scott and Donald K. Slayton, Director of Flight Crew Operations at the Manned Spacecraft Center, is a Liquid Cooling Garment plug. It plugs the inside of the hole or the feed thru in the suit where the water is normally brought into the suit from the backpack, the Portable Life Support System [PLSS], Of course, in suited operations inside the spacecraft, the backpack is not required and there is a plug on the inside of the suit that should seal this. Apparently Scott and Irwin were having some problems getting their suits

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, Houston, 15. We've got a good suit circuit now.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger. We've been looking at it; copy, agree.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: And, 15, we're still looking for an X-ray/Alpha Cover door, Closed. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay. Stand by one, Houston.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, Houston. The X-ray/Alpha door is Closed.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy.

a15_1771614.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1771614.text: The spacecraft is now in the proper attitude for the separation - jettison and separation. And you heard Dave Scott report that, and we confirmed through telemetry on the ground, that their suits are now holding pressure as they should. Apparently they've gotten problem, whatever it was, with the...

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Go.

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: Okay, we're ready to Arm the Logic.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger. We're looking.

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: Okay. Logic 1. [Pause.] Logic 2. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger. You're Go for Pyro Arm. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1771614.text: We do have a good seal on the plugs for the liquid-cooled garment fittings on Irwin's and Scott's suits. And we're moving toward the LM jettison at 177 hours, 20 minutes, 33 seconds and separation 5 minutes later at 177:25:33. We're counting down to separation - rather to jettison, in 2 minutes, 47 seconds.

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: 15, LM/CM Delta-P is 2.5 - 2.0, excuse me.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy, 2.0.

a15_1771614.speaker: Worden
a15_1771614.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Go. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger, 15. Go.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, the LM/CM Delta-P doesn't look exactly right to us. What do you think?

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to get another pound [per square inch of pressure] out of there. We're showing about 3.5 [psi, 24 kPa] in there.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay. We had a suspicion that possibly the LM overhead dump valve was open, and it might be.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: We don't think so down here.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay. Well, we'll go to Tunnel Vent for a little longer, must just be slow then; we've been in it for probably about 15 minutes.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: 15, what position are you in when you're reading that out, in Vent or in Delta-P?

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Delta-P.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: It's up to about 2.3 now, and I've been holding it in Tunnel Vent. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: 15, we'll take that. It'd take too long to get it down, we believe. So let's press on with Jett at that pressure.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, well, the strange thing about it is that we had it up to about - oh 2.7 or 2.8 at one time and then went back to LM/CM Delta-P, and for some reason it [the pressure] built back up in the tunnel. And, I guess the only conclusion we could come to was - from the LM, 'cause the hatch is pretty simple and secure in here. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Dave, we think that the increase in the cabin pressure during the suit integrity check could have raised it from - from your side.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Well, okay, that's - that's true.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: [Stand] by, Dave; confusion reigns down here.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: [Thinking out loud] Have you seen any ch - Well, I guess it sort of does up here, too. I wonder if you see any difference in the - you can't read the tunnel, though, can you? [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: And, 15; this is Houston. We'd like to verify that you did get a good hatch integrity check back there a ways. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Yes, that's affirm. We got a good hatch integrity check, but - I guess what I'm thinking is there's - you know, there could be something in the seal there. And perhaps the thing to do would be to repressurize the tunnel and pull the hatch down, and take a good close look at the seal and then stick it back in. It shouldn't take too long. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Apollo 15, Houston. That seems to be about the best conclusion we can come to down here, but we're - [we'd] kind of like to go into a hold briefly. Another indication is that we would - we are seeing the LM cabin holding steady and not using any oxygen from the ascent tanks, which seems to say that we're not leaking into the tunnel from the LM.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, understand.

a15_1771614.speaker: Irwin
a15_1771614.text: Do we? [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1771614.text: This is Apollo Control. Recapping our situation at the moment, we're going to hold off on the LM jettison until we've gotten a more fuller, more complete understanding of the pressure rise in the LM tunnel. We've seen a slow pressure rise in that tunnel.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to verify that the pressure equalization valve is closed.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: That's verified; it's closed and on the yellow stripes.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: And, 15, we'd like to back out of your Pyro Arm situation right now. [Pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, Houston; 15. Pyro Arm is Safe, Logic is Off, and the Pyro Arm circuit breakers are pulled.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: 15, can you give us a LM/CM Delta-P reading at this time, please?

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: Okay, right now it's 3.0.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy, 3.0.

a15_1771614.speaker: Scott
a15_1771614.text: And, I've had the valve in Tunnel Vent for the last 5 minutes or so.

a15_1771614.speaker: Parker
a15_1771614.text: Copy.

a15_1773440.speaker: Parker
a15_1773440.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Recommendation right now is to stop the - the LM Tunnel Vent, and then we will sit and monitor the CM/LM Delta-P for a short while to see what happens to it. And, after that, we're still considering opening up the tunnel to check the seal. Over.

a15_1773440.speaker: Scott
a15_1773440.text: Okay, we're in LM/CM Delta-P right now, and it's reading about 3.1.

a15_1773440.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1773440.text: This is Apollo Control. We're going to continue watching the pressure in the tunnel between the LM and the CSM for a pressure rise. The pressure has not dropped as we would expect and this implies that perhaps there is some leakage into the tunnel. Since the LM cabin appears to be stable, we suspect that if there is leakage, it would be coming from the Command Module side. If this is the case, the thing we would suspect is some bit of contamination in the CSM [forward] hatch. We're going to continue to watch the pressure in the tunnel, see what happens, and if necessary, we'll remove the hatch

a15_1773440.speaker: Parker
a15_1773440.text: 15, we'd like to pull the B/D Roll jets.

a15_1773440.speaker: Irwin
a15_1773440.text: Roger. B/D Roll jets coming off. [Long pause.]

a15_1773440.speaker: Parker
a15_1773440.text: And, 15, if one of you has a chance, would you put X-ray to Standby, please? [Pause.]

a15_1774040.speaker: Parker
a15_1774040.text: 15, Houston. [Can] you give us a reading now on that? [Pause.]

a15_1774040.speaker: Scott
a15_1774040.text: It's just a little under 3.1, just a - just a hairline.

a15_1774040.speaker: Parker
