a15_1774040.text: Roger; copy. And we're still looking at the possibility of opening the hatch. We're just trying to - right now, trying to understand the situation before we open the hatch and destroy the configuration we're in.

a15_1774040.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1774040.text: This is Apollo Control. Flight Director Glynn Lunney has just advised the Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] to be prepared to go either way with the LM jettison. We're holding the option open to jettison this revolution if we get the situation with the CSM tunnel cleared up. However, it begins to look more and more likely that we will be jettisoning the next revolution which would be two hours from the Flight Plan time, and would move the subsequent activities with respect to the Lunar Module; the deorbit burn and the impact also two hours later. Again the situation here is that we're holding the

a15_1774638.speaker: Parker
a15_1774638.text: And, 15; Houston. Could we have another reading in 10 minutes? [Pause.]

a15_1774638.speaker: Scott
a15_1774638.text: Well, it's reading right now just about the same that it was when I last called you.

a15_1774638.speaker: Parker
a15_1774638.text: Roger; copy. There's certainly enough uneasiness down here that we think we ought to proceed back through and open both the Command Module hatch and the LM hatch, check the seals on both and the relief valves on both, proceed back through that, doing - doing those checks, because there could be a very slight leak from the LM that the telemeter guys would not see at - for this small volume in the tunnel. Over.

a15_1774638.speaker: Scott
a15_1774638.text: Rog. We sort of think that's a good idea, too. We'll proceed.

a15_1774638.speaker: Parker
a15_1774638.text: Roger. Keep us posted when convenient.

a15_1774638.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1774638.text: Flight Director Glynn Lunney has just made the decision that we will delay the jettison one revolution and consequently the subsequent Flight Plan relating to the Lunar Module will also slip by one revolution.

a15_1774638.speaker: Parker
a15_1774638.text: 15, just in case you haven't got the idea, when I said check the seals, I mean clean them too.

a15_1774638.speaker: Scott
a15_1774638.text: Rog. Understand. We'll make sure they're good and clean.

a15_1774638.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1774638.text: This is Apollo Control. One of the problems in diagnosing the pressure rise in the tunnel is that the tunnel volume is very small with respect to the volumes of the cabin in either the LM or the Command Module, which makes it very difficult to detect the amount of a pressure loss in either of those vehicles that would account for the pressure rises we're seeing in the tunnel. The amount of oxygen lost would be on the order of 1/100th of a pound and this is really below - as they say, below the noise level, almost undetectable. So that's one of the reasons - the principle reason that we are ask

a15_1775536.speaker: Scott
a15_1775536.text: Okay, Houston; 15. Both hatch seals are clean, and both hatches are now closed and locked. Do you want to vent the tunnel again?

a15_1775536.speaker: Parker
a15_1775536.text: Roger. Go ahead, Dave. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1775536.speaker: Parker
a15_1775536.text: And, 15, are you guys all still fully suited?

a15_1775536.speaker: Scott
a15_1775536.text: Rog. We did not break down the suits; we're still locked up.

a15_1775536.speaker: Scott
a15_1775536.text: And the LM overhead dump valve was verified in Auto.

a15_1775536.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1775536.text: And that is the proper position for that vent valve.

a15_1775536.speaker: Scott
a15_1775536.text: Okay, Houston. We're 1.3 [psi] on - Delta-P and coming - coming up.

a15_1780137.speaker: Worden
a15_1780137.text: Okay, Houston; we're about 2.2 [psi]. [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Worden
a15_1780137.text: And, Houston, do you want to go to 3 [psi] and let it stabilize there?

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: I guess we'll do it per the checklist which is 3.5, right? [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Well, not really. Our checklist says before jettison only, LM Tunnel Vent valve, LM Tunnel Vent at least 10 minutes, period. [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Okay. Stand by. [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: 'Course, that's after the hatch integrity check. If we want to go ahead and run through the full hatch integrity check, then we'd run up to 3.5 and then run another 10 minutes, I guess.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Yeah, that's the point, Dave. We want to run a complete hatch integrity check; in fact, we'll proba - we may ask you to run it longer than usual.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Okay.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Obviously, what we're thinking about here is a bad hatch seal, so we're particularly interested in that.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: And, 15, a reminder. When you're on the back side, the LM is still in 5 degree deadband, so play it cool with the Command Module. [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Rog.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: And, 15, what we'd like to see you do is leave that tunnel at 3.5 for the entire back side pass, and we'll see what happens to that leak rate. That gives us a nice, long leak check on the hatch. And, we'll be satisfied with that Delta-P for Jett[ison], if that's the way it works out on the other side. [Pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Okay. And, I guess in that case, we'll probably break the suits down and then run another suit check before we see you around the corner. So...

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Okay, we'll buy that.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: It's about time for dinner.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: I knew there was a reason.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Rog. [Pause.] Okay, we're about 3.2 [psi] now on the Delta-P. We'll leave LM [meaning tunnel] in Vent.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Rog. I understand; 3.2 and still venting.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Dave, stand by on taking your suits off; if you haven't taken them off already.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Oh, we hadn't planned to take our suits off; we were just going to break off the helmets and gloves so we could get something to eat.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Roger. But stand by on breaking the suits down; because it's a debate as to whether we want to do another suit integrity check.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Okay.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: 15, press on. You may - you are permitted to break the suits down, but do not do the suit integrity check until you come back around the other side; we can take another look at that tunnel. Over.

a15_1780137.speaker: Scott
a15_1780137.text: Roger; understand. We'll break them down and hold off until we see you on the other side.

a15_1780137.speaker: Parker
a15_1780137.text: Okay, good luck.

a15_1780137.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1780137.text: This is Apollo Control at 178 hours, 11 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal now with the Command Module, with the LM still in tow. And to resummarize the situation on that last revolution front-side pass: As the spacecraft came into acquisition at the start of this revolution, they were preparing to jettison the Lunar Module on the scheduled time in the Flight Plan. However, one of the checks that we run is a pressure integrity check on the tunnel in the Command Module - the tunnel used by the crewmen to pass from one vehicle to the other - which has hatches at both ends sealing the LM from the

a15_1780137.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1780137.text: In order to assure that on jettisoning the LM, we had a good tight seal on the CSM hatch, the crew was instructed to open the tunnel up and remove the probe and drogue assembly and check the seals on both the LM and the CSM hatches. They did this, and Dave Scott reported, at 177 hours, 56 minutes, that the hatches had been checked; they were clean, resealed and ready to proceed. By this time, we had gone beyond the point which we could jettison the LM as per the Flight Plan. Flight Director Glynn Lunney decided to delay the LM jettison and subsequent activities with the LM for one revolution.

a15_1780137.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1780137.text: The conversation with the crew, just prior to Loss Of Signal, about removing the suits centered around concern here in the Control Center that nothing be done to change the pressure in the Command Module cabin. In removing the suits, there would be nothing that would change the pressure, however, in running a suit integrity check, where the suits are pumped up and then the pressure bleeds off slowly, we do get a change in the cabin pressure. It was decided that there would be no problem in allowing the crew to remove their helmets and gloves so that they could get something to eat on this back

a15_1780137.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1780137.text: This is Apollo Control at 178 hours, 53 minutes and we are about 3 minutes away now from reacquiring Apollo 15 on its 52nd revolution of the Moon. The Command Module and Lunar Module are still docked at present time. We've delayed the jettison for one revolution because of an unexplained rise in the pressure in the tunnel which is used by the crewmen to pass from one vehicle to another, and which at jettison would have hatches both on the LM side and on the CSM side sealing it off. During this backside pass, while we were out of radio contact with the spacecraft, Flight Director Glynn Lunney r

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1785314.text: Our network controller reports that we may have a ground problem, which is why we're not getting a response from the crew to our calls, and he's checking that, at the present time, to see if we do have a problem at one of our ground - ground stations.

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1785314.text: We do have telemetry data from the spacecraft but we' re not getting voice communications, apparently because of a problem on the ground.

a15_1785314.speaker: Comm tech
a15_1785314.text: Goddard Voice, Houston Comm tech. Net 1.

a15_1785314.speaker: Comm tech
a15_1785314.text: Goddard Voice, you're loud and clear.

a15_1785314.speaker: Comm tech
a15_1785314.text: Roger.

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston, Reacq and Narrow. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1785314.text: Our telemetry data shows that the pressure in both the LM and the Command Module cabins is normal.

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Scott
a15_1785314.text: Houston, Apollo 15. Go ahead.

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Roger. Do you - Roger. Do you have any good word for us?

a15_1785314.speaker: Scott
a15_1785314.text: I'd say LM/CM Delta-P is off-scale high. [Pause.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: Roger. And how'd the hatch integrity check go? [Long pause.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Scott
a15_1785314.text: Well, we've just had it in tunnel vent all the - the way around the back side as I think you suggested. [Long pause.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: 15, did you have a look at holding it in Delta-P to see how the - see how it was holding on there?

a15_1785314.speaker: Scott
a15_1785314.text: No, we just left it in Tunnel Vent all the way around the back side. I - That's what we'd thought you'd said to do. We can check it now. [Long pause.]

a15_1785314.speaker: Parker
a15_1785314.text: 15, why don't you bring it up to 3.5, and let us watch it for a while. I think we garbled some - and you watch it. I think we garbled something there.

a15_1785314.speaker: Scott
a15_1785314.text: Okay. Our understanding was to let it go all the way, and then you get a good look out on this side. So we'll bring it up to 3.5.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: 15, Houston. Two items; one, we want to make sure that you're aware that we cannot read the tunnel pressure, and so we're depending upon your readouts of this Delta-P to give us the confidence here in the hatch integrity. One other item that we do know, is that during all that period when the tunnel was vented, our O 2 flow was off-scale low, which does give us some confidence in the integrity of the hatch. And, meanwhile, we're waiting for your call on a 3.5 reading so we can begin a hatch integrity check. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Roger.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Mark. Two minutes and 3.5 plus or minus 0.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Roger. Copy.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: And - and I think we have the same confidence, Bob. We noticed the low O 2 flow also. The only question we had was, why did the Delta-P change? [Pause.]

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: That's the same question that was bothering us.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: But, it's steady at 3.5, and has been now for about 2 and a half minutes.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Copy. [Long pause.]

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Okay, 15. This is Houston. We'd like to run that hatch integrity check to about 5 minutes total, because of what we suspect was the problem before. And, if it passes at that point, we'll press on, per the Flight Plan, for following the normal steps. And you can plan, if we have time for it, we're looking for a jett[ison of the LM] at 179:30, at the present time. Over.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Roger. 179:30, and we'll give you a call at the 5-minute point.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Thank you.

a15_1790358.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1790358.text: At the present time, the crew has vented the tunnel to a pressure differential of 3½ pounds, and then resealed it. And we're going to continue looking at it for a total of about 5 minutes to see if it continues to hold its pressure - to hold the pressure differential. Scott reported after the first 2, 2½ minutes that it was holding well and we'll continue to look at it for another minute or so before deciding with certainty that we have a good hatch seal.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Okay, Houston. There's 5 minutes at 3.5 and it looks solid.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Roger, Dave. Let's press on with a nominal timeline.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: And, Houston. Are you happy with 3.5 or would you like to bleed it down a little more?

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Roger, Dave. We're happy with the hatch integrity, and let's open the tunnel vent and bleed down towards 4.0 at - for the nominal setup. And I guess it's on the decal there.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Rog. No, the decal says go for 10 minutes in LM tunnel vent.

a15_1790358.speaker: Parker
a15_1790358.text: Roger. And I guess that means after hatch integrity, which means beginning now.

a15_1790358.speaker: Scott
a15_1790358.text: Rog. Step 7, and it's in work.

a15_1790358.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1790358.text: With that test, we're satisfied that we do have a good seal on the hatch and we're going to proceed now with jettison and separation. The LM jettison is scheduled to occur at 179 hours, 30 minutes, and the separation maneuver by the Command Module will be at 179:35, or 5 minutes after the jettison.

a15_1791735.speaker: Parker
a15_1791735.text: 15, Houston. Your suit integrity check looks good as far as we can tell down here. [Pause.]

a15_1791735.speaker: Scott
a15_1791735.text: Well, we had it for about 5 seconds there, and then the O 2 flow went back up, so we'll hang on here and see if it comes back down.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Okay, Houston; 15. We got a good pressure integrity check. We're ready to press on.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger, we agree. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: And, 15, we're still aiming for 179:30 for Jett[ison]. And be advised, of course, this means we're going to have to retarget P30 to 179:35. And, other than that, all attitudes will be the same. Although, of course, since you'll be local vertical, your inertial attitudes for the burn will be slightly different than what you've seen. [Pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Okay. Understand. And your Delta-P is off-scale high now.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger. And you're 14 minutes past that time [that they began venting the tunnel for the last time]. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Go. - Go ahead, 15.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Roger. Understand. The retargeting on P30 - you want to target that for 179 plus 30 plus 00, and the same Delta-Vs as before?

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Negative, Al. It's going to be 179 plus 35 plus 00 for the Sep burn.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Sorry about that. I meant 179 plus 35. Three zeros Jett, huh?

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: That's affirm. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Go. [Pause.] 15, go ahead.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Roger. We're ready to turn the sequence arm on [to re-arm the tunnel pyrotechnics].

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger. You're Go for turning them on.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Okay, and Logic 1, On; Logic 2, On. [Pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: And, 15, you're Go for Pyro Arm.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: And, 15, we need Direct RCS, On, please. [Pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Okay. Directs are on. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: And, 15, 3 minutes to Jett[ison], and we're wait - we're watching for Pyro Arm.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Okay. We're proceeding through the pre-Jett checklist at this time, and we'll get right to you.

a15_1792140.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1792140.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about 2½ minutes away from the scheduled time for jettisoning the LM. At the time of jettison, the spacecraft will be in an attitude with the Service Module SPS engine pointed towards the Moon and the LM jettison will occur with the LM jettisoning away from the lunar surface. Following the jettison, the Command Module will perform a small retrograde separation maneuver to assure that there's no chance of recontacting the Lunar Module, and with separation coming at 179:30, the deorbit burn, the burn to impact the Lunar Module into the lunar surface, will

a15_1792140.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1792140.text: Coming up now on 15 seconds to LM jettison.

a15_1792140.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1792140.text: And we confirm jettison.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: And, it's away clean, Houston.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger, copy. Hope you let her go gently. She was a nice one.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Oh, she was at that.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Houston, 15. Question on the separation maneuver. Do you want us to burn the residuals in P41, or just make 1 foot per second burn?

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger, Terry. Burn them in P41, please.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Rog.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: You understand that's burn the residuals, right?

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Just - just making - just making sure. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1792140.text: This separation maneuver will be performed using the attitude control thrusters, the RCS system, and will be 1 foot per second [0.3 m/s] velocity change.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Houston, P41 says 7/10ths forward. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Yes, 7/10ths forward, 7/10ths up.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger, Dave.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: And forward takes us right back to the LM. [Pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Stand by, Dave. We're looking into that, of course.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Okay. We got about a minute and 15 seconds or so.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Average g is On [i.e. the computer is about to begin the burn and has begun measuring acceleration]. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Ah, hold the burn, Dave.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Okay, we'll hold the burn.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to have visual reference relative to your position to the LM. We'd like you behind the LM. And, we'll give you a burn attitude for 5 minutes from now. [Pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Roger. [Pause.] Okay, I guess she's 150 feet [45 metres] dead ahead.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Okay. Copy, Dave. Thanks.

a15_1792140.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1792140.text: Spacecraft Communicator Bob Parker double checked the attitude - or the position of the Lunar Module relative to the Command Module. And while we were getting that double check, we delayed the separation maneuver for 5 minutes. And we're, at this point, waiting for the Flight Dynamics Officer to recompute the burn attitude. And we'll be performing that separation maneuver in about 3 to 4 minutes from now.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: And, Dave. Can you verify, were you behind, in local vertical, or body attitude coordinates?

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Well, give us a little while to figure that one out.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Roger. Are you behind it in the orbit, or are you just - is it just sitting there in front of you as you sit there and look at it?

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: It's sitting in front of us when we sit there and look at it.

a15_1792140.speaker: Worden
a15_1792140.text: Bob, we're almost directly radially inward from the LM right now.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Copy that. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Houston, our attitude is 150 degrees relative to the local horizontal.

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Say that again, please, Dave.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Rog. Our attitude, according to Verb 83 down there, is 150 degrees, relative to the local horizontal. Which means we're, I guess, fairly close to local horizontal, at least within 30 degrees. [Long pause.]

a15_1792140.speaker: Parker
a15_1792140.text: Stand by, guys. Confusion still reigns, I think.

a15_1792140.speaker: Scott
a15_1792140.text: Roger. Understand.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: 15, do you have an ORDEAL ball going at the moment?

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Sure do, and it's on the DSKY; you can see it right down there.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger, Dave. We would like you to do a VFR burn, which means go - maneuver to a trailing position - and fire one foot per second retrograde. Understand?

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: That sounds like a good burn. Rog. We'll do that. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1794322.text: This is Apollo Control. The separation maneuver which...

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Houston, 15. This ought to make for some interesting discussion, but I guess what you want us to do is point at him and burn aft to one foot per second; is that correct?

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger, Dave. That's probably the best way to keep an eye on him.

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Well, we're having a tough time doing that, because he's right in the Sun right now. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: But, Houston, I think at this attitude, a one foot per second aft will give us sufficient clearance. Don't you? [Pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: As long as you're trailing him, Dave. I guess, right now, we can't give you any sound advice down here.

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Okay, well, if we burn one foot per second on the local horizontal, which we are almost on right now, I think that will put us in a orbit which re - remains clear of it. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Okay, Houston. As far as trailing goes, right now as we look over the ground, we're leading him.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger. That's our...

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: We're about on a horizontal in front of him.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger. We need you behind him, Dave. That - we were gradually coming to that conclusion. That was the only way you could have him in the Sun. We need you behind him and then a firing of retrograde. [Pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Yeah, that's going to take an awful lot. Because we're a fair ways out now, and we'll have to maneuver quite a ways to get behind him, and it'll take quite a while and a little bit of gas.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger, Dave. Understand that. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Okay, Dave. How about 2 foot per second posigrade, as long as you're in front of him. Understand? 2 foot per second posigrade. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Okay; so that'll be a minus-X Delta-V for 2 feet per second at out present attitude, right? [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Rog. That affirm, Dave.

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Okay. We're all in the same frequency. We'll do that.

a15_1794322.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1794322.text: We show the separation maneuver in progress at this time.

a15_1794322.speaker: Worden
a15_1794322.text: Okay, Houston. We put in 2 feet per second aft. And that was done just at local horizontal.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: Roger, copy. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_1794322.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1794322.text: The timing of the separation maneuver is not critical and won't affect the events with the Lunar Module; the deorbit burn and the subsequent impact of the Lunar Module. We took some additional time to assure that the crew aboard the Command Module had good visibility of the Lunar Module at the time they performed the separation. And they completed the maneuver using the attitude control thrusters, changing their velocity [by] 2 feet per second to assure they got adequate separation from the Lunar Module.

a15_1794322.speaker: Parker
a15_1794322.text: And, 15; if you can anticipate, why don't you give me a call when you get yourself partially powered down from this. Then we'll read you some Flight Plan updates, which are mostly just the deletion of activities so you can get to bed.

a15_1794322.speaker: Scott
a15_1794322.text: Okay, Houston. Appreciate that. Thank you, and we'll call you back.

a15_1794322.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1794322.text: And CapCom has just advised Dave Scott that we're going to proceed on with the power down as soon as possible to allow the crew to get some much needed rest.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: 15, Houston. You got a moment for this update?

a15_1795532.speaker: Scott
a15_1795532.text: Just a minute, Bob. [Long pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, Bob. What changes do you have for us.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Okay. These will start out in the Flight Plan here. And, after LM Jett, we'd like you to proceed with the activities that run on the original Flight Plan from 177:30 through 178:01. So that last entry that we will be doing will be the line that says "X-ray, On" at the very top of that next page.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, understand. We'll delete that particular line, "Mapping Camera/Laser Experiment, Off," and we'll do all the activities up to - through 178 there, the Mass Spec. X-ray, On.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Roger. And at the - on that same page, beginning at 178:20 to 178:30, we will scratch that particular - that whole block of items. And going along with that, at 178:39, it says "DAC, On;" we'll also scratch that. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Roger. Understand. We'll scratch the activities from 178:20 to 178:30. And, at 178:39, we'll scratch "DAC, On." How about the activity there at 18:31 [means 178:31]? We - guess we'll do that, huh?

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Roger. At 178:31, that "Mass Spec., Multiplier, Low, Discriminator, High: Ion Source, On" will be done 30 minutes - three zero minutes after the Mass Spec. Experiment, On; Ion Source to Standby, which is over there at 178:01. [In] other words, we need a 30-minute delay between the top item on the left-hand column and the top item on the right-hand column.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, we understand.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Okay, we'll delete the Pan Camera activities over on 179 hours. There's one at a hundred [pause] 15, if you read, there's one item at 179:16, and another item at 179:21 that pertain to the Pan Camera. We will delete both of those. [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, understand. Delete the Pan Camera action at 179:18 and 179:21.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Roger. Copy. And when your ready to sleep, I guess you can start with the Systems Checklist - pre-sleep checklist at 179:31, there.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, thank you, Bob.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: And you'll noticed we didn't delete the eat period. [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Thank you.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: And - and, Jim; do you guys want a TEI-58 PAD? [Long pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay. We'll take one.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Okay. If you got - have you got the [writing] pad out?

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: No, stand by.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Give me a call.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Okay, Jim. Understand you have the [writing] pad. SPS/G&N; 36363; plus 0.61, plus 0.93; 192:13:33.30; plus 2799.7, plus 0609.5, minus 0098.0; 181, 112, 015. Rest of the PAD [is] NA. Ullage: 4 jet, 12 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Understand. It's a TEI-84 SPS/G&N; 36363; plus 0.61, plus 0.93; 192:13:33.30; plus 2799.7, plus 0609.5, minus 0098.0; 181, 112, 015; 4 jet for 12 seconds.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Roger, Jim. Except it's TEI-58.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Roger. It's 58. [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Slayton
a15_1795532.text: Okay, Jim. And, while we got you, - this is Deke. I'd like to have you and Dave, at least, take a Seconal here before you go to sleep so you can really power down for the night. You guys need it. It's up to Al whether he wants one or not.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, thank you, Deke.

a15_1795532.speaker: Slayton
a15_1795532.text: Roger.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: 15, Houston. We have a correction to that update, if you'd get the Flight Plan back out please.

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Okay, go ahead.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Roger. That item 178:30, on the Mass Spec., the discriminator value there should be Low. Copy? [Pause.]

a15_1795532.speaker: Irwin
a15_1795532.text: Roger. Understand, Discriminator, Low.

a15_1795532.speaker: Parker
a15_1795532.text: Thank you, Jim.

a15_1800735.speaker: Slayton
a15_1800735.text: Apollo 15, Houston. You're about one minute until LOS. Sleep tight.

a15_1800735.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1800735.text: This is Apollo Control. We've had Loss Of Signal now. Again to go back over and sort out some of the activities on that revolution. We successfully completed the LM jettison and that occurred at 179:30, after reverifying that the tunnel was maintaining the proper delta pressure - pressure differential, and that we had a good tight Command Module hatch seal. We had planned to do the separation maneuver performed in the Command Module using the Reaction Control System thrusters at 179 hours, 35 minutes; and just before the maneuver was to be performed, Dave Scott gave us a call indicating that h

a15_1800735.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1800735.text: The LM impact is scheduled now to occur at 181 hours, 29 minutes, 23 seconds; and this will be about 25 minutes after the deorbit burn which will be performed on command from the ground at 181 hours, 4 minutes, 19 seconds. The one revolution delay in performing the jettison will affect, of course, the LM impact time. This time that we've just given you is approximately one revolution later than the Flight Plan time. However, by the time we've completed the sleep period tonight and back in activities tomorrow, we should - we would expect to see no change to the Flight Plan for such events as Tr

a15_1800735.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1800735.text: This is Apollo Control at 180 hours, 52 minutes. And we're now 2 minutes from reacquiring the spacecraft. We would hope that Jim Irwin and Dave Scott either have begun their rest period, or will shortly after we reacquire the spacecraft. And on this revolution, the major activities will be the Lunar Module deorbit burn and LM impact. The deorbit burn is scheduled to occur at 181 hours, 4 minutes, 19 seconds; with impact on the lunar surface occurring about 25 minutes later at 181 hours, 29 minutes, 23 seconds. The impact coordinates are 26.12 degrees north and 1.06 degrees east. Let's correct

a15_1800735.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1800735.text: The LM, at the present time, is in an orbit 64.3 nautical miles by 52.2 [119.1 by 96.7 km]. And at the time the deorbit burn is performed, we estimate that the Command Module will be 8 [nautical] miles [15 km] behind and about 2¼ miles [4.2 km] above the LM. We should have Acquisition Of Signal from the Command Module in about 1 or 2 seconds. And our network controller, INCO, report that we have Acquisition Of Signal.

a15_1800735.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1800735.text: The INCO reports that the radio contact we have is with the Lunar Module. We're still waiting to get radio lock on with the Command Module in its 53rd revolution of the Moon now. The Guidance Officer [GUIDO], just a minute or so ago, radioed the command to the LM guidance system which starts the proper computer program in process and will end with the deorbit burn, which will occur about 8 minutes, 50 seconds from now - or correction - 6 minutes, 12 seconds from now at 181 hours, 4 minutes and 19 seconds.

a15_1805733.speaker: Parker
a15_1805733.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. Standing by in the blind. [No answer.]

a15_1805733.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1805733.text: INCO says we do have radio signals now from the Command Module.

a15_1805733.speaker: Parker
a15_1805733.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. Standing by in the blind. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1805733.speaker: Parker
a15_1805733.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Calling in the blind and standing by. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1805733.speaker: Parker
a15_1805733.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Calling in the blind. Standing by. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1805733.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1805733.text: We're coming up now on 20 seconds until the beginning of the LM deorbit burn. It will be a 201-foot-per-second [61.3 m/s] burn, using the four Reaction Control System thrusters on the LM ascent stage.

a15_1805733.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1805733.text: Our LM Guidance and Control Officers both report telemetry data indicates the LM is burning. And we should have impact at 181 hours, 29 minutes, 23 seconds. We do have lock on with the Command Module, However, the signal strength is not strong enough at the present time for us to hear any response from the crew. Apparently they're not in the attitude with the High Gain Antenna yet to give us a good - good enough signal strength for voice communications. The Guidance Officer says that the burn is progressing normally with the LM ascent stage. And again those predicted impact coordinates are 26

a15_1805733.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1805733.text: The Guidance Officer says we've had shutdown now. And the LM guidance system appears to have shut the burn off right on time. Guidance says the residual was .08 [fps, 2.4 cm/s], which indicates that the burn was almost precisely as planned. And at the conclusion of that burn, the ascent stage has a weight of 5,315 pounds [2,411 kg]. Currently the altitude is 61.4 nautical miles [113.7 km] and we'll be able to watch that altitude as it drops off to nothing at impact.

a15_1805733.speaker: Parker
a15_1805733.text: Apollo 15, Houston, in the blind. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1811014.speaker: Parker
a15_1811014.text: Apollo 15, Houston, in the blind. Over. [No answer.]

a15_1811014.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811014.text: Falcon's altitude at the present time is 53.1 nautical miles [98.3 km] and at impact the LM ascent stage will have a velocity of 5,560 feet per second [1,695 m/s]. The flight path angle will be minus 3.2 degrees, or 3.2 degrees pitched down from horizontal; very shallow angle of impact. We're now about 17 minutes, 50 seconds away from LM impact.

a15_1811014.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811014.text: INCO reports that signal strength is coming up on the CSM antenna indicating that we're getting the antenna - the High Gain Antenna around into position where we should be able to get voice communications with the crew aboard Endeavour .

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Houston, 15.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay, we're just about getting bedded down here, Bob. I wanted to check and clarify one thing with you before we did.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Please do.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay, the Flight Plan updates that you gave to Jim a little while - earlier included Mass Spec. Experiment, On, and some switching with the discriminator and multiplier. Now, as of yesterday, we had decided not to use the Mass Spec. because of the boom deploy problems. Has somebody decided that we now should deploy the boom?

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Rog. My understanding is that we didn't want to do it before the plane change because we might have to jettison it and it's - now that we've got the plane change accomplished, we'll run it. And, if you have to jettison before TEI, we'll do that. Over.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay, I understand. I guess I didn't understand that yesterday; and, we'll go ahead and deploy it and get the Mass - Mass Spec. going now.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Roger, Al. And one more thing; we'd like to make sure tonight that Jim is on the EKG for the evening.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: That's affirm. Jim will stay on biomed tonight.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Rog. And, one more thing, Al, we would like to verify High Gain Antenna angles as pitch 25, yaw 185.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Right. That's what they're set on now, Bob.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Okay. We had a long while picking you up. I guess we were a little worried, there.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: No, we just got our signals crossed in here. And, we had some different numbers on them before. So I got them. We're fixed up now.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Okay, and we'll be expecting you to be in VHF bistatic later on, right? [Pause.]

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: I guess. Do you want us to go ahead and do that?

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Yes, please, Al.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Okay, and one last little check is Optics Power is On. We'd like it Off eventually. I expect you haven't gotten that far yet, Al.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: That affirm. We'll get it.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Okay, and otherwise you call us; we won't call you.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay, we'll call you. Thank you, Bob. Goodnight.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Goodnight.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: We're coming up now on 10 minutes until LM impact. And we currently show Falcon to be at an altitude of 31.5 nautical miles [58.3 km].

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: 15, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Famous last words; go ahead.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Yeah. How's that for broken promises. Hey, OSO [Orbital Science Officer] just came out of the woodwork and was worried because he doesn't have X-ray and Gamma-rays and all those on yet either. I'd assume you probably have - just haven't done any of that block, right?

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Yeah. Hey, Bob, we're still trying to get cleaned up in here and get suits put away and all that sort of stuff. We'll get with it as soon as we can, but it's awfully cramped quarters and an awful lot of stuff to move around.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: Rog. We were afraid you'd get used to the luxury of all that space.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: I kind of liked it here by myself.

a15_1811549.speaker: Parker
a15_1811549.text: This time I'll keep my promise.

a15_1811549.speaker: Worden
a15_1811549.text: Okay.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: This is Apollo Control. We're nearing 6 minutes away now from LM impact. In the MSC News Center briefing room, Dr. David W. Strangway will be available to provide background information and answer questions on the LM impact and we'll have displays of the seismometer tracings that we're receiving here in Mission Control from the Apollo 15 and Apollo 14 science experiment packages - Passive Seismic Experiments. At the present time we show Falcon to be 17.4 nautical miles [32.2 km] above the lunar surface.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: Falcon is now 3 minutes from LM impact. We show its altitude 9.3 nautical miles [17.2 km].

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: 2 minutes now from LM impact. Falcon's altitude is 6.1 nautical miles [11.3 km].

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: 1 minute prior to impact. Falcon's altitude now is 3 nautical miles [5.6 km].

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: 5 seconds to impact. And we've had LOS LM, Loss Of Signal from the LM.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: Our science room reports we're getting seismic tracings now from the ALSEP at the Apollo 15 site.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: This is Apollo Control. The actual time of LM impact, as computed from the time at which our displays on the LM went static and we lost radio communications from the vehicle, was 181 hours, 29 minutes, 37 seconds.

a15_1811549.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1811549.text: This is Apollo Control at 182 hours, 7 minutes. We said goodnight to the crew aboard Apollo 15 about 45 minutes ago. At the time, Al Worden reported that they had a good bit of cleaning up to do, and getting things shipshape before they'd be able to actually begin their rest periods. However, we do not plan to call the spacecraft again. If there is any communications, the crew will initiate a call to Mission Control. The Flight Dynamics Officer [FIDO] is continuing to refine the impact time for the LM ascent stage. At the present time our best estimate is that impact occurred 181 hours, 29 min

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Cabin reading about 5.7 over there, Dave?

a15_1820700.speaker: Irwin
a15_1820700.text: Okay. I guess we ought to wait until we complete chlorination before we get the...

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Help me put the other end of this guardrail on here.

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Is it in the way? Huh?

a15_1820700.speaker: Irwin
a15_1820700.text: Yes, just as well. Just fiddling around and getting squared away.

a15_1820700.speaker: Scott
a15_1820700.text: That's right. I guess all I'm saying is the Flight Plan really ought to reflect that.

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Yes, they had you learning the [garble] switch.

a15_1820700.speaker: Scott
a15_1820700.text: Oh, Christ. I'm putting it all over your face here.

a15_1820700.speaker: Irwin
a15_1820700.text: Want to use some of your soap?

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Hey, you're supposed to be somehow nonaffected by the CMP.

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Oh, yes, 7 hours left of my 9-hour rest period.

a15_1820700.speaker: Irwin
a15_1820700.text: Not interested in what he's doing. You'd like that more than this.

a15_1820700.speaker: Scott
a15_1820700.text: Your urine bag? Oh, no, I got them all cleaned out so...

a15_1820700.speaker: Worden
a15_1820700.text: Oh! Poor [garble]. I've been - I tell you, I've been rinsing everything out with water every time I pee and every time I go to sleep.

a15_1820700.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1820700.text: This is Apollo Control. We're now about a minute away from reestablishing radio contact with Apollo 15. The spacecraft now in it's 54th revolution of the Moon. We do not expect to have any communications with the crew. We said goodnight to them at 181 hours, 18 minutes; or about an hour and a half ago. And at that time, Al Worden said they still had a fair amount of cleaning up to do and getting sample containers stowed and the Command Module cabin cleaned up and ready for sleep. We told them that we would not call them. If they had anything for us, that they could give us a call and recommend

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Houston, 15. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: 15, go ahead.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Is it time to get up yet, Bob? [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Rog. We've got about 15 updates here for you, if you want to get ready in the SIM bay.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Thought we'd give you a crew status report and the onboard read-outs before we called it a night. I just wanted to check and make sure we got everything turned on for you. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Roger. We'll get the guys looking at that...

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: We got the Mass Spec. out. Okay, Bob, we got the Mass Spec. out, and I think we've cleaned up everything else for you for tonight, and I'll give you the readings here and then we'll call it a night.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Rog. We're listening, and I hope everybody else down here will be getting with me so we can give it to you at the end, if anybody wants anything. Go ahead. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Copy.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: My read-outs: Bat C, 37 [volts]; Bat A, 37.5; Bat B, 37.5. RCS quads are 63, 58, 60, 58.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Copy.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: And, we are configured for the bistatic radar test. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Al, that should be bistatic VHF.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Okay, three verifies for you, Al. Can you verify the Gamma-ray's out? The X-ray is ready? And we need a verify on Jim for his EKG.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: That's correct, Bob. The bistatic VHF radar test. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: And, can you think of anything else that needs to be done?

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Stand by, Al.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay. He's not hooked up yet but he will be shortly. And we'll verify the Gamma-ray, out and On, and the X-ray, On.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: And, Al, we're working a state vector uplink for you. Stand by a minute and we'll get a decision on that.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay, Rob. I guess we didn't have a[n indication of the] Gamma-ray [boom going] out, so it's going out now.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Roger. That's a verify, I guess.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: And the X-ray is On.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay, the X-ray is On. Seems like we had quite a few loose ends tonight. [Long pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: And, Al, how about a verify on X-ray Covers, Open? [Long pause.]

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Roger. That's verified. It's Open.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Thank you. We're still discussing the vector here.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: If you can give us P00 and Accept, we'll have a load in about a minute. Stand by, just Accept...

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: ...sorry.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Do you want P00?

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Negative. Accept only.

a15_1825119.speaker: Worden
a15_1825119.text: Okay. I'll leave it P20.

a15_1825119.speaker: Parker
a15_1825119.text: Swinging.

a15_1830237.speaker: Parker
a15_1830237.text: Okay, and 15, you can have Block back again. Good show. Thanks for the patience this evening, and Karl will wake you when he wakes you and not a moment before. Goodnight.

a15_1830237.speaker: Worden
a15_1830237.text: Okay, that sounds like a winner, Bob. Good night.

a15_1831452.speaker: Parker
a15_1831452.text: Rog. This isn't Karl waking you up; but we don't show the Mass Spec. Experiment to On, and if the out - outgassing has been completed, we need the Ion Source, On. Over.

a15_1831452.speaker: Worden
a15_1831452.text: Okay. We've got it On, and it's been on for about 45 minutes now. And we now have Multiplier, Low, and Discriminator, Low.

a15_1831452.speaker: Worden
a15_1831452.text: Stand by on that, Bob, stand by.

a15_1831452.speaker: Worden
a15_1831452.text: Okay, Bob, we got it now.

a15_1831452.speaker: Parker
a15_1831452.text: Understand you got Experiment, On, now...

a15_1831452.speaker: Worden
a15_1831452.text: Checking [garble], it should be On now.

a15_1831452.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1831452.text: This is Apollo Control. We hadn't expected to hear from the crew aboard Endeavour on this, the 54th revolution. However, we received a call from Al Worden about 30 minutes ago. Worden passed along a crew status report and mentioned that Jim Irwin was still in the process of getting set up for the sleep period, and hadn't, at that time, hooked up the biomedical sensors that we'll be using to monitor his sleep this evening. We had Worden double check some of the switching configurations for the orbital science experiments, particularly the Gamma-ray and X-ray spectrometer, and also, a bit later,

a15_1831452.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1831452.text: This is Apollo Control; 183 hours, 51 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Crew still asleep. 14 minutes remaining until Loss Of Signal with Command Module Endeavour toward the end of the 54th lunar revolution. Handover complete to Gene Kranz's White Team of flight controllers, Black Team headed by Glynn Lunney going off shift. Change of shift press conference with Flight Director Lunney will commence in about five minutes at 12:30 Houston time in the small briefing room in the News Center. We'll leave the line up through the end of this revolution until Loss Of Signal this revolution, in the off chan

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Hello, Houston; Apollo 15.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Good morning, Alfredo. This is Houston.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Good morning, Dr. Joe. How are you?

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Couldn't be better, Al. How's it going?

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Just fine, Joe. You all talked out?

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: No, sir. Just getting ready to start. And, pleased to have a chance to talk to you.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Very...

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: I've got all kinds of things for you, Al, when you...

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Very good, Joe. Glad to be talking to you.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay. I've got all kinds of things for you, which I can start handing it up to you at your convenience, pretty much. We're going to change the Flight Plan around a little bit - primarily, lifting out things because of our getting a somewhat later start than normal, and a couple of other minor modifications. I also have a lot of news to read to you and some other good things you might be interested in. Over.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. Let's - why don't you give me a couple of minutes here to get some pens and the Flight Plan out and - and in about 5 or 10 minutes or so, I'll have the guys put the headsets on and we'll all listen to the news.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Al, out of curiosity, is everybody awake up there?

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Yeah, man.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Good morning, Davy...

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Yes, Joe, sure are. We're just in the middle of breakfast.

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Hello, Joe. How are you?

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Well, I'm fine, D.R.; how are you today?

a15_1924511.speaker: Irwin
a15_1924511.text: Morning, Joe.

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Oh, we're in great shape. Hey, you sure did a fine job for us down there, Joe. Jim and I'd like to really thank you. That was a superfine job of taking care of everything for us.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: I think the superfine job is the two of you; it was just most remarkable. Everybody down here is still floating so high, they're having a hard time getting down to all that data you gave us. And you'll be interested to know that - that we have sitting in front of us, a preliminary report from each EVA of the geology of the area that I would say is more complete than our 90-day preliminary reports which were issued on some of our other landings. It's just most exciting.

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Well, it's because you've got the real professional backroom there. Those - those guys really know how to put - put it together. Especially with the way they were coming up with the new ideas while we were on the surface. That was really neat.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: And, Dave, I do have to ask you one question. Is there a three-unit segment of deep core stems some place in that Command Module?

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Joe, we wouldn't lose sight of that for all the tea in China. That's number 1 priority.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Yes sir. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Oh, as a matter of fact, Joe, we made a good thorough search of the LM before we let it go. We went from top to bottom to make sure we got everything, and I'm sure we got everything we brought up off the surface, and I'm pretty sure we did - did fairly well cleaning up the surface.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Dave. Good news; good news. Al, if you're ready, I'll start hitting you with a few things we're interested in knowing from you right away. And then, when we get those, I'll give you the general plan for the day. And I think, in some cases, we'll want to just talk you through some of the changes while you're making your front-side pass. There's no need to feed up all the data in detail to you at the beginning here. My first question: we need from you a configuration of panel 230 , particularly - in fact, only really the Mass Spec. switches, could you - call out the settings for the Mass S

a15_1924511.speaker: Scott
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe, I'm right there. Experiment is up and On. Ion Source is centered. The Discriminator is Low and the Multiplier is Low.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, thank you. That's - that's what we'd guessed. And, Al, I - I guess the first thing we want - we're going to want you to do today is to start to get ready to go plus-X forward, P20 option 5. We're going to want you to retract the Mass Spec. boom and close the X-ray and Alpha Particle cover.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. We'll do all that. How about putting it on a - on a time basis for me so I can write it in the Flight Plan.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, real fine. You can start that right now at - just put it in at 192:52, I guess. And also, right after that, list fuel cell purge, H 2 O dump and LiOH canister change. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. Understand. You want us to go ahead into plus-X P20 SIM bay attitude, and pull in the Mass Spec. and the Gamma-ray booms, and, I guess, turn off the Mass - turn the Mass Spec. to stand by.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Al, let me hit you with that last statement again. We want you to retract the Mass Spectrometer boom, but not the Gamma-ray, and close the X-ray and Alpha Particle covers. Retract Mass Spec. boom and close two covers. Over.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, understand. You want us to pull in - to retract the Mass Spec. boom and close the X-ray [and] Alpha covers, then do the fuel cell purge, the water dump and a canister change.

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: That's affirm.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay, Joe. I'll get that in work. [Long pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: And one more item. You can start to charge Bat B at your convenience.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_1924511.speaker: Allen
a15_1924511.text: Okay, and looking downstream here, as soon as you get turned around, and these other good things done, we're going to ask you to open the X-ray and Alpha Particle covers. And for rev 60, the [current] agenda calls for an eat period for you. And Gamma-ray, X-ray and Alpha Particle data being taken during that time. Sounds like you've got your eat period pretty well out of the way.

a15_1924511.speaker: Worden
a15_1924511.text: Yeah, that's right, Joe.

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Okay, Joe. While we're maneuvered here to a plus-X forward, how about reading some news to us?

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Okay. Sure will. Let me - let me begin with just a note on that water dump. It'll take about 15 minutes to run, and they're interested in your dumping it to close to 10 per cent onboard reading. Over.

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Roger, understand. Probably the same as we've been doing before. We dump down to 10 per cent, but not below 10 per cent.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: That's correct. And I've got several things to read to you here. I have the official morning Gold Bugle Zeitung report and - that comes from two rows behind me here. And I've also got a telegram for you, Jim. And I have some history - a little bit of history that's been researched for you by the people at Honeysuckle concerning a small problem with a leak on the Endeavour about 200 years ago. And I'll start with whatever you'd like to hear first. [Long pause.]

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Okay, let me just start with the morning's news. The weather report in Houston-Galveston area calls for showers and thunder showers through Wednesday. Today's temperatures will be in the lower 70s and upper 80s.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: The United States will support Communist China's admission to the United Nations this fall, Secretary of State, William Rogers announced. The U.S. will also fight against expelling the Nationalist Chinese Government on Taiwan. U.S. Steel, the industry pace setter, announced a price hike averaging 8 per cent on virtually all its products and several other companies followed suit, as an aftermath of a new 3-year labor contract. Trainmen won pay increases of nearly a dollar and a half an hour, spread over a 42 months, in a nationwide contract settlement, and called off their crippling strike agai

a15_1925634.speaker: Worden
a15_1925634.text: Roger, Joe. Copied all these off.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Roger. Okay. In the National League: Philadelphia 4, Atlanta 0; Cincinnati 4, New York 2; St. Louis 3, San Diego 1; and Los Angeles 5, San Francisco 4. And Lee Trevino added another thousand bills to his bank roll, Monday, by taking first place with the number - with a 7-under-par, 65, in the Colombus Invitational Pro-Am. Jack Nicklaus and Arnie Palmer teamed last weekend to close in on Trevino in professional golf's money-winning race, though. Nicklaus and Palmer won twenty thousand dollars each when they won the National Team Championship at - I guess Ligonier, Pennsylvania. Trevino leads fo

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: And, I'll go over now to - Jim, a special telegram for you which reads, essentially: Mother, Dad, and your brother Charles are proud of you. We were thinking of our trip together on top of Mount Whitney and we are with you in spirit on the Moon. Love, Mother, Dad, and your crew. And I might add, that there - An occasional piece of mail for - for all of you that's starting to - starting to come in to the Manned Spacecraft Center, here. In fact, I think a truck pulled up there yesterday to deliver some of the first.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: I'm going to go on, if you're still listening, to read some history that was sent to us by the Honeysuckle people. And the subject is "A Leak on the Endeavour at 62 hundred GET." Following the above incident and the wonder from the Apollo 15 crew whether Captain Cook's Endeavour had ever sprung a leak, staff at Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station has searched the records and come up with the following incident, which may be of interest. Information has been extracted from an old newspaper article and an entry in Captain Cook's log book. "It was 11 pm on June 11, 1770, a clear moonlit night, whe

a15_1925634.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1925634.text: This is Apollo Control at 193 hours, 4 minutes. We are in conversation with the crew. We had a call from Al Worden at 192 hours, 45 minutes, 22 seconds; shortly after Acquisition Of Signal on the 59th revolution. And the conversation has been fairly consistent since then. We've accumulated a fair amount of tape and we'll play that back for you now.

a15_1925634.speaker: Scott
a15_1925634.text: That's quite an analogy, isn't it.

a15_1925634.speaker: Allen
a15_1925634.text: Quite an analogy, Dave. Certainly is.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Houston, 15. I'm ready to copy the consumables, Joe.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Alfredo. GET 191 plus 25; RCS total, 47 [per cent]; quad A: 50, [B] 47, [C] 46, [D] 47; H 2 tank 1: 56, [2] 53, [3] 42; O 2 tank 1: 64, [2] 67, [3] 54.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Rog, understand, Joe. At 191:25, RCS total, 47; quad A: 50, 47, 46, 47; H 2 is 56, 53, 42; O 2 is 64, 67, 54.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Copy, Al. And I'll be right back.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. [Long pause.]

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Endeavour, this is Houston again.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Al. Let me lay some more words on you concerning your Flight Plan, when you're - you're ready to talk about that.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger, Joe. Go ahead.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay. You'll be in the configuration plus-X forward, and will be taking Gamma-ray, X-ray and Alpha Particle data, data during rev 60. We want you to do, at 193 plus 45, a P52 option 3. And we're going to add a Map and Pan Camera pass sometime during rev 60. And I'll be coming at you with the necessary data for that. Also...

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger, Joe; understand.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Al. Now I guess a - a word about biomed configuration, today. In order to get some very interesting baseline data, medical data on you, Al - and, Jim, for your EVA coming up later - we're requesting that the two of you give us that biomed data today. I think, Dave, you were scheduled for it, but I guess we'd prefer Jim on the line with Al to get baseline data for later. Now, Al, let - let me run through in just some blocks here, [of] the next revs as we see them, and the approximate activities. And then I'll come up with specific data concerning those revs later on, perhaps actually duri

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Roger that.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay. On rev 61 will be UV photography of the lunar mare. We're coming up on, I guess, an hour of light flash experiments, and it's pretty much dealer's choice between Dave and Jim, who - whichever one of you would like to do that. Rev 62 will be a crew exercise period, science photos, and science visuals. And we'll be taking the Mapping Camera and Laser Altimeter data during rev 62. And it will end with terminator photos. On rev 63, more Mapping Camera, Laser Altimeter, and a burst of the Pan Camera. UV photos and terminator photos again. Rev 64 will be eat period, boom photos, LiOH canister

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. Understand in the Flight Plan that the object is going to be to get us back to the - to the printed Flight Plan as much as possible.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: That's exactly right, Al. And you'll be coming on to it kind of as the day progresses. We're just going to pick up a few quick items that we've missed over the past 2 hours and mainly just lift - lift out other sections, as I understand it. But you'll be back on the Flight Plan shortly.

a15_1930736.speaker: Worden
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Joe. Fine. Thank you.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Rog. And...

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: And, Joe, let me request that Jim be...

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Go ahead, Dave.

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: I'd like to say that I'd like to have Jim without his sensors on today. That 3 - 4 days in a row is pretty tough with those things on. I think probably, if we get him tonight, you could probably get your data, don't you think?

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Stand - stand by, Dave, and I'll - let me double check,

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: Say, as a matter of fact, Joe, why don't you give Jim and Al both a break today on the sensors, and I'll stick mine on, because I've had them off since we got back yesterday. And then if you want us to have some particular data-gathering periods, why don't we take a look at that starting tonight, huh?

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, Dave. That sounds good.

a15_1930736.speaker: Scott
a15_1930736.text: Okay. And concerning the light flash things - Jim and I both saw light flashes while we were on the surface, as a matter of fact.

a15_1930736.speaker: Allen
a15_1930736.text: Okay, copy that, Dave. That's remarkable.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Good ship Endeavour, this is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_1932051.speaker: Scott
a15_1932051.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Roger. On our downlink data, we see indications of High Gain Antenna yaw fluctuations. Wonder if you could glance over at your onboard indication and see if you see it there as well. And, also we're standing by for crew status reports, when you're ready to give it.

a15_1932051.speaker: Scott
a15_1932051.text: No, we - we see no oscillations up here, Joe.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, thank you.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Al, this is Houston. With a TEI-62 PAD, when you're ready for that. We also have a question. How did the Mass Spec. boom retraction go? And we've got a switch setting for your Mass Spec. when you're ready.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay. Jim will be ready to copy a TEI PAD here in a minute. And Mass Spec. boom retracted without a hitch this time, Joe. Sorry I didn't get the time on it, but it was very close to the nominal time, and apparently it didn't hung up this time.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, fine, Al. Thank you. We'd like the - I guess the Mass Spec. placed on Standby, please. And that's the Experiment switch.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay. Mass Spec. on Standby. Yeah, that's verified on standby, Joe.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: And, Joe, I'm ready to copy that TEI PAD.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Jim, good morning. We need Accept, and we're going to uplink a new state vector to you.

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Joe. The readback on TEI-62. SPS/G&N; 36310; plus 0.61, plus 0.92; 200:10:34.64; plus 2928.4, plus 0190.3, minus 0043.5; 180, 106, 006; four jets, 12 seconds.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Jim. Readback correct. And how are you doing this morning?

a15_1932051.speaker: Irwin
a15_1932051.text: Fine, Joe. Had a good night's sleep.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Super. [Pause.]

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Joe, I've got a clear status report for you.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Go ahead.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay. Longest 9 hours sleep in one period there, Joe, to begin with. And the PRDs are 25024, 08031 and 23175.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Al, copy that. And assume there was no medication.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: That's affirmative.

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Okay, thanks, babe. [Long pause.]

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Endeavour, you can go back to Block. You have a new state vector and we're standing by to watch your water dump.

a15_1932051.speaker: Worden
a15_1932051.text: Okay, Joe, crank out the water dump. Want to watch one for a change, huh?

a15_1932051.speaker: Allen
a15_1932051.text: Roger, lay it on us.

a15_1933257.speaker: Allen
a15_1933257.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston with a Map Camera photo PAD when you'kre ready.

a15_1933257.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1933257.text: This is Apollo Control at 193 hours, 34 minutes. We're back live on air/ground now. The briefing on the subsatellite, which was scheduled for 10 am today at the News Center briefing room, has been postponed until approximately 10:30 am this morning. That briefing will be carried on the release line while Endeavour is behind the Moon.

a15_1933447.speaker: Worden
a15_1933447.text: Houston, 15. Go ahead with your Mapping and Pan Camera photo patchup.

a15_1933447.speaker: Allen
a15_1933447.text: Okay, Al. And I - I forgot to tell you when you're dumping water, you can also go ahead with the urine dump if you need to do that. I just forgot to mention that. The Map Camera photo PADs for rev...

a15_1933447.speaker: Allen
a15_1933447.text: Yeah. For rev 60. T-start, 194:35:05, T-stop, 195:34:50. Image motion setting at T-start: barber pole plus 4; At 195 plus 20 plus 00: barber pole. And a couple of notes on this. Be sure to retract the Gamma-ray boom prior to the start of the camera pass. And be sure to go to 5 degrees deadband in P20 - I'm sorry, Al; that's 5/10ths of a degree deadband in P20 prior to camera pass. And you want to extend the camera and start the Laser Altimeter per the system's checklist, page S/1-38. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1933447.speaker: Worden
a15_1933447.text: Roger, Joe. Understand. Mapping Camera photo PAD: T-start, 194:35:05; T-stop, 195:34:50. Now for the image motion, you want a T-start barber pole plus 4, and at 195:20:00, you want that increased to barber pole. And notes: Retract the Gamma-ray boom before taking the pictures; go to half-degree deadband; and extend the Mapping Camera; and start the Laser Altimeter as per system's checklist S/1-38.

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: Endeavour, this is Houston with the new O 2 heater configuration for you. [Pause.]

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: Rog, Al. We want O 2 Heater in tank 3 to Auto and tanks 1 and 2, Off. Over.

a15_1934116.speaker: Worden
a15_1934116.text: Understand, Joe. You want O 2 Heater in tank 3, Auto, and the other two, Off.

a15_1934116.speaker: Allen
a15_1934116.text: That's right, Al. And we want you to proceed with your O 2 fuel cell purge listed at 193 plus 58 in the Flightk Plan.

a15_1934116.speaker: Worden
a15_1934116.text: Roger, Joe. We'll get that in work here now.

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Al, this is Houston. You can terminate the dump now. And turn the Alpha Particle experiment Off, please. [Long pause.]

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Endeavour, Houston. Requesting Auto in the High Gain [Antenna]. And, troops, you may have to delay the P52 we've called out to you, and it's coming up shortly, until about 194 plus 20, to make sure most of the water's out of the way. Over. [Pause.]

a15_1934438.speaker: Worden
a15_1934438.text: Roger, Joe. I'll just go take a look here and see if I can pick up the star okay, I'll go ahead and do the P52.

a15_1934438.speaker: Allen
a15_1934438.text: Okay, Al. And you got the call about the Alpha Particle counter, I hope.

a15_1934438.speaker: Worden
a15_1934438.text: Right. Roger. We got it turned off.

a15_1935113.speaker: Worden
a15_1935113.text: Okay, Joe. I got the gyro torquing angles up, and I'll torque them out on the minute.

a15_1935113.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935113.text: I'll get out of your way, Al, so you can get down in here.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Al, we no - noted the termination of your fuel cell 3 purge. At your convenience, open the X-ray and the Alpha Particle experiment covers, please, and turn the Alpha Particle back on. Over.

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Okay, Joe. We'll be about another 2 or 3 minutes finishing up all the dumps, and then we'll do that.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Okay. Fine. We do want you to wait until all the dumps are completed, and then open the doors and turn Alpha Particle on at your convenience, really.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes, Myrtle. I didn't use - I didn't - hadn't used Myrtle this morning. I didn't use Myrtle this morning.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: I think that checklist is [garble] 5 minutes and then closed.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes. Yes. I didn't use that this morning.

a15_1935339.speaker: Allen
a15_1935339.text: Good ship Endeavour, this is Houston. We'll see you on the other side.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: We stow this in that Jum [?] bag down there? When I took that [garble], Al? Okay.

a15_1935339.speaker: Mission Control
a15_1935339.text: This is Apollo Control at 193 hours, 56 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on this revolution. Endeavour and its crew performing orbital science throughout the day. We passed up an update to the Flight Plan for today. Crew reporting 9 hours of sleep last night and no medication. The briefing on the subsatellite will begin momentarily in the MSC News Center briefing room. We'll reacquire Endeavour again at 194 hours, 41 minutes, about 30 seconds on its 60th revolution. At 193 hours, 57 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_1935339.text: Okay. I'll just stay here in the center.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: I know. You [garble] put mine on.

a15_1935339.text: ...Get the vacuum cleaner [garble] off, lay down every bag and [garble] everything before we leave. [Garble] shoes [garble] stow away [garble]. a15_1935339.text: Yes, okay. Okay, Dave. If you hand me the tape. I think this is about as tight as we'll get this.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Dave Scott taught me. Tape everything. Yes, I don't know what we would have done if we hadn't had the tape along. I might have been without comm on the surface.

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Okay, I think your seat's fixed.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: You know what we can also do, Dave, is wet wipe the MAGs. Might be even better then - wet wipe them - get a towel - damp towel here - Just wipe them off.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Procedure says to unstow them, vacuum, and then wet wipe. Yes.

a15_1935339.speaker: Irwin
a15_1935339.text: Yes, I was just going [garble] LM Timeline.

a15_1935339.speaker: Scott
a15_1935339.text: I think I would follow the [garble].

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
a15_1935339.text: Can't we use this little square?

a15_1935339.speaker: Worden
