a15_2205148.text: Not much. It's just, if you put your hand around the nozzle there, why, you can get some water on it.

a15_2205148.speaker: Allen
a15_2205148.text: Okay; we copy that. We think it's probably normal, but we'll look into it real closely. Sounds to me like the Endeavour has a few plumbers aboard as well as experts in other things.

a15_2205148.speaker: Scott
a15_2205148.text: Well, by the time this is over, I guess we will be plumbers.

a15_2205148.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2205148.text: This is Apollo Control at 221 hours, 4 minutes. Endeavour is maneuvering to the burn attitude now. We're 16½ minutes away from ignition.

a15_2211547.speaker: Allen
a15_2211547.text: Endeavour, you're looking good. You are Go for the shaping burn.

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: Okay, Houston. Endeavour with a burn status report.

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: Okay. Burn was on time, and it was a 3-second burn. We had about 1.0 or 1.1 residual, and that was trimmed to 0.1, minus 0.2, minus 0.2. Delta-V C was minus 11.0; fuel, 26.40; oxidizer, 26.25. [Pause.]

a15_2212152.speaker: Scott
a15_2212152.text: And it has us in an orbit, 76.0 by 54.3 [nautical miles, 140.8 by 100.6 km].

a15_2212152.speaker: Allen
a15_2212152.text: Okay, Dave. Great. And you just gained about 240 more days for our subsatellite, something like that.

a15_2212537.speaker: Allen
a15_2212537.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. You're looking good at LOS minus 5. And I have a reminder on your water dump. We'd like you to monitor it down to 10 percent. And we'll see you on the other side. Over.

a15_2212804.speaker: Allen
a15_2212804.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. And we've copied your torquing angles.

a15_2212804.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2212804.text: This is Apollo Control at 221 hours, 30 minutes. We've had Loss of Signal on the 73rd revolution. The shaping burn performed a few minutes ago has achieved the desired results giving the sub - will give the subsatellite at least a year's lifetime in lunar orbit. The onboard orbital reading after that burn: 76 by 54.3 nautical miles [140.8 by 100.6 km]. The next event will occur while we are in acquisition on the 74th revolution. That will be the jettisoning of the subsatellite at 222 hours, 39 minutes, 27 seconds. We'll join the orbital science briefing on this line now.

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: ... it in the SIM bay, huh?

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Okay. Waste water's down to about 20.

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: Okay, we'll purge. Are you going to time her?

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: ... to do that on the front-side pass?

a15_2213147.speaker: Worden
a15_2213147.text: Think we'll be okay once we get out in the...

a15_2213147.speaker: Worden
a15_2213147.text: All you got to do is look after the purge, huh?

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: We got this great big filter floating around. Why is that floating around?

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: I'm sorry, Dave. I'll throw it in the diaper bag.

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Gee, Jim, we got to make another burn.

a15_2213147.speaker: Worden
a15_2213147.text: I didn't realize we were so close to another burn. ... close.

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Where'd you put the second garbage can?

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Al, wait. Stick it up here. No, wait.

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Did you have any tissues down here when you did your thing, Jim?

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: No, I didn't have any, Dave.

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: How'd I get by? I used the...

a15_2213147.speaker: Irwin
a15_2213147.text: ...UCTA. I used the UCTA. So I had to dump it anyway.

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: Yes. Right over there with the camera is, we got to configure the DAC anyway. Open it up. You got to put the DAC together anyway for photographing the subs at.

a15_2213147.speaker: Scott
a15_2213147.text: What? Yes. Didn't think about that.

a15_2213147.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2213147.text: This is Apollo Control at 222 hours, 15 minutes. We're about to acquire Endeavour on the 74th revolution. During this pass the subsatellite jettison is scheduled, and on this 74th revolution, after Endeavour goes behind the Moon, the Trans-Earth Injection burn will be performed. We will not be in contact at that time. The subsatellite will be jettisoned at the time the spacecraft is crossing the lunar equator on its way to apolune. [It] will be jettisoned to the north so that the spin axis will be perpendicular to the Sun's line of sight and allow maximum sunlight on the solar cells. The sprin

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Clear.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Oh, my. Look at this. That's a good picture.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Hello, Endeavour. This is Houston. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Houston, Endeavour. Go.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Roger, Endeavour. We're requesting you verify your systems - Data Systems, On, and the S-band Aux switch to Science, please. [Long pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Yes.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Right here it is.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Huh!

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Yes. That's verified, isn't it?

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: No, Data Systems isn't On.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Well, it wasn't in here then.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: It sure was and I missed it. I'm sorry.

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: Okay; that's verified now, the data systems are on now.

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Shoot!

a15_2221542.speaker: Scott
a15_2221542.text: They're easy to overlook, aren't they?

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Okay, Dave; we copy that. I've got a map update, rev 75, when you're ready to copy. And I have a message for Al from the King [Farouk El-Baz], when he's ready to copy. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Roger, Al. The message to you is to stand by to copy your final exam grade in orbital science and observation. It's an alpha-plus, with a subnote of "Well done." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: Tell the King, thank you very much, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Rog, Al. And I've got the map update...

a15_2221542.speaker: Worden
a15_2221542.text: And I expect to see him back in Houston soon.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Oh! Oh, no - no problem there.

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Go ahead, Joe.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Rog. The map update, rev 75. Copy at 223 plus 20. [Pause.] And it is: LOS, 223 plus 29 plus 45; 180, 223 plus 52 plus 57; AOS with TEI, 224 plus 03 plus 03; AOS without TEI, 224 plus 15 plus 30. Over.

a15_2221542.speaker: Irwin
a15_2221542.text: Okay, the map update readback for rev 75: 223:29:45, 223:52:57, 224:03:03 and 224:15:30.

a15_2221542.speaker: Allen
a15_2221542.text: Readback's correct, Jim; thank you.

a15_2221542.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2221542.text: This is Apollo Control at 222 hours, 23 minutes. That message with the grades and the congratulations for Al Worden was from Farouk El-Baz, one of the crew's instructors in Geology.

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: Endeavour. We verify your SIM pyro bus...

a15_2223128.speaker: Scott
a15_2223128.text: This is Endeavour. Can you verify the...

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: ...arm, and - your rates look good to us down here. Over.

a15_2223128.speaker: Scott
a15_2223128.text: Okay. You had us all figured out. We'll go Free.

a15_2223128.speaker: Allen
a15_2223128.text: And we know one of you will be watching out the window. We're particularly interested if the spin of the satellite is sweeping out a cone or if it seems to be a fairly flat spin as it comes out. Over.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Endeavour, we're requesting you go back to Auto and do another Verb 49, please. We see you've drifted off about a degree.

a15_2223355.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2223355.text: We're 5 minutes away from subsatellite jettison.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Okay, Endeavour. We're recommending that you go back to Free at launch minus one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Irwin
a15_2223355.text: Okay; Free at launch minus one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Endeavour, we've got a new update to the last instructions. Go Free at launch, please. [Pause.]

a15_2223355.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2223355.text: Spacecraft rates look good at one minute.

a15_2223355.speaker: Allen
a15_2223355.text: Okay, Dave; copied that. Sounds great. [Pause.]

a15_2223355.speaker: Scott
a15_2223355.text: Oh, looks like it might be oscillating maybe 10 degrees at the most. [Long pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: And, Endeavour, when you're ready, I've got a coming-home PAD to read to you. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Stand by one, Joe.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. And we would like Accept, please, on the computer. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Stand by one.

a15_2224102.speaker: Scott
a15_2224102.text: A very pretty satellite out there. We get about two flashes per rev off each boom, and it seems to be rotating quite well. Very stable.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Very good, Dave. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: And, Joe, I'm ready to copy that coming-home PAD.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. I'm ready to read it to you. It's TEI-74, SPS/G&N. The weight, 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 223:48:45.05; plus 2945.2, minus 0761.3, minus 0171.4; all zips on roll, pitch and yaw; [Pause.] Noun 44 is NA, and plus 0022.1; 3046.8, 2:21, 3028.5; 37; 224.3, 30.5; 053, down 10.3, right 3.1; plus 26.11, minus 157.97; 1084.1, 36179; and the GET, 294:58:34. GDC Align, Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028. Four jets, 12-second ullage. And, we'd like Accept, please. And I'm standing by for the readback. Over.

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay; you have Accept, and here's the readback, Joe. TEI-74, SPS/G&N; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 223:48:45.05; plus 2945.2, minus 0761.3, minus 0171.4; all zips for roll, pitch and yaw; H P , plus 0022.1; 3046.8, 2:21, 3028.5; 37, 224.3, 30.5; 053, down 10.3, right 3.1; plus 26.11, minus 157.97; 1084.1, 36179; 294:58:34. Vega and Deneb; 102; 178; 028. Four jet for 12 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. The readback is right on. I've got a TEI-75 preliminary PAD and a Flight Plan update PAD, when your ready. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay, I'll take TEI-75.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay. SPS/G&N, TEI-75; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 225:48:44.08; plus 2981.4, minus 0807.2, minus 0145.1; 000, 002, 001; all the rest, NA. Ullage, four jet, 12 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Roger. TEI-75, SPS/G&N; 35768; plus 0.57, plus 0.88; 225:48:44.08; plus 2981.4, minus 0807.2, minus 0145.1; 000, 002, 001. Four jets for 12 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Sounds good, Jim. Thank you. And I'm standing by for your call for the Flight Plan update.

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Go ahead, Joe; I'll take that.

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Jim. And it's your computer [i.e. the upload of a state vector and target have been completed and the crew can take control of the computer again]. The Flight Plan update begins at 223 plus 51. And change the "Verb 49 maneuver" from the numbers listed to the numbers "127, 270, 030." Over. [Pause.]

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Read you. For the Verb 49 that occurs at 223:51, change the numbers to "127, 270 and 030."

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: That's correct. And the next entry is at 224 plus 00. Change the line "Omni Delta" to read "Omni Charlie."

a15_2224102.speaker: Irwin
a15_2224102.text: Okay, Joe. Going back to 224:00, that'll be "Omni Charlie" instead of "Omni Dog." Then, on that Map Camera photo PAD, its 224:03:00 and stop on MSFN cue. Then down to 224:15, on the "Map Camera, Image Motion" will - it'll be "barber pole plus two" instead of "three". At 224:21, we'll delete the "Verb 49 maneuver." At 224:23, we'll delete the "Map Camera track." At 224:27, delete "Map Camera/Laser Experiment Covers, Closed." And at 224:40, do a "Verb 49 maneuver to 127, 295, 030; High Gain, pitch, 23; yaw, 229."

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Right on, Jim. Thank you.

a15_2224102.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2224102.text: This is Apollo Control at 222 hours, 53 minutes. We've passed up the final maneuver PAD for the Trans-Earth Injection burn behind the Moon on this revolution to bring Endeavour and its crew home. Ignition time: 223 hours, 48 minutes, 45.05 seconds. Delta-V, change in velocity of 3,046.8 feet per second [928.7 m/s]; duration of the burn: 2 minutes, 21 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2224102.text: This is Apollo Control. Acquisition time, given a good TEI burn, will be 224 hours, 3 minutes, 3 seconds. Acquisition time if there is not a burn will be 224 hours, 15 minutes, 30 seconds.

a15_2224102.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2224102.text: This is Apollo Control at 222 hours, 56 minutes. The Canary Island tracking station reports it has acquired the satellite that was ejected by the Endeavour .

a15_2224102.speaker: Allen
a15_2224102.text: Good ship, Endeavour, be advised that our tracking stations have acquired the satellite.

a15_2224102.speaker: Scott
a15_2224102.text: Oh, very good.

a15_2230102.speaker: Allen
a15_2230102.text: Roger. Jim, this is a comment for you. When I was reading the Flight Plan update to you, we noticed that you might be coming up on something not too clear in the Flight Plan and it involves the long list of steps between 224 plus 00 and 224 plus about 15. And there are a number of steps in there that have to be accomplished before the T-start time on the Map Camera photo PAD. It may be, you - be you'll want to start on a few of them, I guess, a little early. Over.

a15_2230102.speaker: Allen
a15_2230102.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We'll be requesting Omni Delta when you lose the uplink.

a15_2230102.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2230102.text: And Endeavour is maneuvering to the burn attitude now.

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Roger, Endeavour. I have three requests for you. The first, the Optics is in the CMC Mode, and we've noticed it's drifting off. We'd like you to drive it manually back to a value less than 10 degrees in Trunnion and then zero it. We're also waiting for a DAP load and a P40. And I have a guaranteed last correction to your Flight Plan, when you're ready.

a15_2231653.speaker: Scott
a15_2231653.text: Okay, number 1, we've still got to make the star check. We'll take care of that, and I hope - I hope you've already seen the DAP load and the P40, but we'll take a look at it again for you. [Long pause.]

a15_2231653.speaker: Irwin
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Joe. We - I'm ready to take that last change to the Flight Plan.

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Jim; stand by one. [Long pause.]

a15_2231653.speaker: Allen
a15_2231653.text: Okay, Jimmy, this is an easy one. At 224 plus 14, we want you to delete the line that reads "Map Camera, Image Motion to On, talkback barber pole in three to five seconds, then gray." Delete that line, please. Over.

a15_2231653.speaker: Irwin
a15_2231653.text: Okay, that's an easy one. I'll delete that line that says "Map Camera, Image Motion, On, talkback barber pole in three to five seconds, then gray."

a15_2232305.speaker: Allen
a15_2232305.text: Roger. Dave, Al and Jim, be advised you are Go for Trans-Earth Injection. Set your sails for home. We're predicting good weather, a strong tail wind, and we'll be waiting on the docks. Over.

a15_2232305.speaker: Scott
a15_2232305.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Houston. We'll see you around the corner.

a15_2232305.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2232305.text: This is Apollo Control at 223 hours, 24 minutes. We're 5 minutes away from Loss Of Signal. 23 minutes, 53 seconds from ignition on TEI.

a15_2232305.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2232305.text: This is Apollo Control at 223 hours, 29 minutes. We've had Loss of Signal. Endeavour is 18 minutes, 48 seconds away from Trans-Earth Injection. The entire backup crew is at the CapCom console here in the control center as is the Director of Flight Crew Operations, Donald K. Slayton and his deputy, Colonel Tom Stafford. We'll come back up several minutes prior to acquisition time. At 223 hours, 30 minutes; this is Mission Control, Houston.

a15_2232946.speaker: Worden
a15_2232946.text: You get the other ones. Thrust A and B to Normal after the Pro.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: And there's the average g coming up. Twenty nine seconds.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: Powering down now. Okay, we trim here in about - just short of 100.

a15_2232946.speaker: Worden
a15_2232946.text: Okay. DSKY and EMS look good, at about 50.

a15_2232946.speaker: Worden
a15_2232946.text: DSKY and EMS are running about 35.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: Are we going to decrease on the - flow valve, Al?

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: Okay, EMS and DSKY are about 50. You got &bout a minute to go.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: Tracking 220. EMS and DSKY look good.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: Okay, babe, your trim's to .2. Forget the Y.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: No, you - X and Z, forget the Y.

a15_2232946.speaker: Worden
a15_2232946.text: Okay. We'll let .2 ... again. Okay, Jim.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: Okay. I'm ready, 1, 2, 3, 4 - TVC Servo Power 1 and 2, Off.

a15_2232946.speaker: Scott
a15_2232946.text: Right on 221. Right down the tube.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: ROT Control Poewr, Direct, two, Off.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: CB SPS, Pitch 1 and Yaw 1, open.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: CB SPS Pilot Valves, Main B, open.

a15_2232946.speaker: Worden
a15_2232946.text: Main A and Main B, both open.

a15_2232946.speaker: Irwin
a15_2232946.text: Okay. PCM Bit Rate going Low.

a15_2232946.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2232946.text: This is Apollo Control at 224 hours, 1 minute. We're now about 2 minutes away from reacquiring radio contact with Endeavour, assuming the Trans-Earth Injection burn went as planned. That 2-minute and 21-second burn with the Service Propulsion System engine was targeted to increase the spacecraft's velocity by 3,046.8 feet per second [928.7 m/s] and would give us a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean about 285 [nautical] miles [528 km] north of Hawaii at 295 hours, 11 minutes, 35 seconds. We're about 1 minute now from a scheduled acquisition time.

a15_2232946.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2232946.text: We're about 30 seconds from our expected acquisition time and the spacecraft velocity at this point should be about 7,500 feet per second [2,300 m/s]. We do expect that the communications will be noisy, when we do regain radio contact, the spacecraft will be using the small Omni antennas and it'll be about 30 minutes before we have the High Gain Antenna up, which will give us the stronger signal strength. And we do have Acquisition of Signal.

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Hello, Houston. Endeavour's on the way home with a burn status report for you.

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Roger. Ignition was on time. Burn time was 2 plus 21. No trim. Our residuals were minus 0.2, plus 0.6, and plus 0.2. Delta-V C was minus 16.7; fuel, 2.35; oxidizer, 2.2; the unbalance was about minus 25. And what a smooth burn that one was.

a15_2240105.speaker: Parker
a15_2240105.text: Roger. Sounds very good to us, Dave. [Pause.]

a15_2240105.speaker: Scott
a15_2240105.text: Just can't beat these rocket engines for traveling.

a15_2240105.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2240105.text: That was Dave Scott passing the burn report back to CapCom Bob Parker and Scott reporting the burn almost precisely as planned. Burn time; 2 minutes, 21 seconds and other residuals so low that he did not even have to trim them.

a15_2240105.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2240105.text: This is Apollo Control. As a result of what appeared to be a near perfect Trans-Earth Injection burn, we predict that the impact point and splashdown time will be as predicted. Again, the splashdown location is about 285 [nautical] miles [528 km] north of Hawaii, the targeted coordinates are 157 degrees, 58 minutes west, 26 degrees, 7 minutes north and the predicted splashdown time is 295 hours, 11 minutes, 35 seconds. There will be several opportunities for mid-course corrections en route home. Those will be primarily for corridor control, to put the spacecraft in the proper entry corridor. C

a15_2240105.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2240105.text: This is Apollo Control. Now 27 minutes after performing that trans-Earth burn. Apollo 15 is about 940 nautical miles [1,741 km] above the Moon, And the spacecraft velocity dropping off rapidly, we're down now to 6,500 feet per second [2,000 m/s] from the approximately 8,500 feet per second [2,600 m/s] velocity after the burn was performed. The Flight Activities Officer reported that the crew should have a good view of the Moon out of their spacecraft windows and we recall from the television transmission that we got during this portion of the flight, I believe it was on Apollo 10, they should

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Houston, 15. Go.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Roger. Two questions. One, we notice you have A/C roll jets selected. I guess we aren't sure whether you have B - A/C roll jets selected on DAP, we aren't sure whether you have A/C or B/D selected on the panel. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Okay. Al's checking them over now. [Long pause.] Okay, A/C, you're selected.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Okay, and could we pry out of you guys any comments on the Moon as you leave?

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Well, we're almost speechless looking at this thing. It's amazing. Looks like we're going straight up; and we're leaving, there's no doubt about that. And we're right on the terminator. It shows very distinctly all the topography - all the topographic highs and lows. And we can see some major rilles. And we noticed one large lava filling within a depression, with domes very prominent within the lava fill. [Pause.] Oh, it's just really pretty spectacular. We have one crater almost below us that has a flat floor with radial rilles and circumferential rilles extending from the central peaks. I th

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Roger; copy. Sounds beautiful.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: It's really spectacular. The elevation - the topography on the ridge line is quite clear, and, of course, all the features near the terminator stand out quite well because of the shadows. And we're busily taking pictures so maybe we can bring some of it back for you to see.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Be looking for it in three or four days.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Rog. It's really spectacular though, and there's no question that we're leaving. As a matter of fact, the first glimpse we got, it was quite obvious that we're on the way. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: That's a pretty good view after all those days of going around and around, isn't it Dave?

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Yeah, boy.

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Looks like you're going straight out, Dick.

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: Yep. Reminiscing for me. Thank you.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Although, I'll tell you, we never got to see half of what we passed over, I'm sure. There's just so much up there. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Gordon
a15_2242010.text: Well, I'll tell you, Dave, I'm not so sure you guys didn't get at least your share, or maybe a little more. Spectacular.

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2242010.text: That was Dick Gordon reminiscing with Dave Scott there. Gordon was backup commander for Apollo 15 and also was..."

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Well, I guess our orbital geologist up here just figured out which way we were. I guess we were sort of momentarily disoriented there, because south is up, and we're looking right up and down the terminator. So I guess we're upside down looking at new territory that we haven't seen during the flight. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: Jim just said "Gee, maybe I ought to look out my window." and, by golly, on his window he's looking up - he's looking up to the north. As a matter of fact, out window number 5 now, you can get a full half - half Moon view. [Pause.] And you can see it all in one big gulp, and boy, what a gulp. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2242010.text: Endeavour's 1,300 [nautical] miles [2,400 km] from the Moon now.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: We'll look at Tycho, now, before too long. [Pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Scott
a15_2242010.text: That's a good point; we can't see it yet. [Long pause.]

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_2242010.speaker: Worden
a15_2242010.text: Okay, Bob, I'm looking from Humboldt straight south now, and, in fact, you can draw a line between Humboldt and the - and a great ditch or scarp to the south [Vallis Schrödinger]. And there's quite a change in the - in the light level or the intensity of the albedo in - between those two areas. And it looks like there's some - you know - fairly smooth fresh lava flows throughout that area. And, in fact, we noticed that while we were in orbit also, that in several of those areas around Humboldt there, and to the north of Humboldt, and to the east of Humboldt, that the flows in some of the

a15_2242010.speaker: Parker
a15_2242010.text: Copy Al. Very interesting.

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: And, Houston; 15. As we leave and look back, why, I guess we still have the impression the Moon is mostly gray. However, when you're up-Sun, as we were just prior to TEI - when you're looking up-Sun, it does definitely take on a chocolate brown color. We came around prior to TPI on the day side - or TEI on the day side, looking backwards into the Sun across Schröter's Valley, and that was a pretty spectacular sight. And it did start turning a chocolate brown, but now everything is a variation of gray, very light to a gun-metal gray near the terminator.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Well, is that a unanimous vote in the spacecraft, Dave? [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Rog. I got three ayes on that one.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Rog. We'll add that, and continue to keep the score. [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Hey, Bob, we don't report to you the other kind.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Some day I'll get up there and make my report.

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: We can see a point on the terminator now where we mentioned we saw a lava filling and some domes in a depression which is not the circular crater-like depression; it's a big cavity. And now, I guess, as the Sun angle has changed some, we can see where the lava has apparently spilled over a scarp into a deeper cavity, which is in - in shadow. And it's very clearly a filling of the cavity with two levels.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Roger, Dave. We call that a polye, don't we? [Pause.]

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: Well, I guess if we were in Hawaii.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: You guys don't see any motion of that stuff, do you?

a15_2243047.speaker: Scott
a15_2243047.text: And, Houston; 15. We got another unanimous vote up here. That was really a great trip.

a15_2243047.speaker: Parker
a15_2243047.text: Roger. I think that's unanimous on everyone, isn't it?

a15_2243910.speaker: Parker
a15_2243910.text: And, 15, if you'll give us Accept, we'll uplink a REFSMMAT for desired orientation PTC.

a15_2244111.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2244111.text: This is Apollo Control. Most of that vivid description of the lunar surface came from Dave Scott. Al Worden also interjected some comments about what appeared to be distinct fresh lava flows near the crater Humboldt. During the description, the spacecraft was at an altitude that began at about 1,200 [nautical] miles [2,200 km] from the Moon and when most of the description was finished, they were about 1,700 [nautical] miles [3,150 km] from the Moon. Our change of shift press briefing is ready to begin at this time in the MSC News Center Briefing Room. During the briefing, we'll record any con

a15_2244447.speaker: Parker
a15_2244447.text: And, Apollo 15; Houston. We'd like that Verb 49 maneuver, so we can pick up [the] High Gain [Antenna], please.

a15_2244447.speaker: Worden
a15_2244447.text: Roger. We just did it, Bob.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Scott
a15_2244500-cospb.text: Hey, Houston. Take a look at the DSKY. I think those are the numbers you gave us.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Parker
a15_2244500-cospb.text: Roger, 15. Those are the numbers. Looks good, thank you.

a15_2244500-cospb.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2244500-cospb.text: This is Apollo Control at 224 hours, 53 minutes. Apollo 15 now about 27 hundred [nautical] miles [5,000 km] from the Moon, and during the change of shift press briefing, we had one or two very brief exchanges with Dave Scott aboard the spacecraft. We'll play that for you now.

a15_2245729.speaker: Parker
a15_2245729.text: And, 15; Houston. We'd like Gamma-ray Gain Step, On, up, three clicks. Over.

a15_2245729.speaker: Scott
a15_2245729.text: Okay. Gain Step, On, up, three clicks.

a15_2250407.speaker: Parker
a15_2250407.text: Roger. We'd like to move that "Verb 49 maneuver to lunar surface photo attitude" that you'll find at 225:30 in the Flight Plan. We'd like to move that up to 225:24. Over.

a15_2250407.speaker: Worden
a15_2250407.text: Roger. Understand; move the "Verb 49 maneuver" to 225:24.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Apollo 15, Houston.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Houston, 15. Go.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Ah, Rog. Be advised we'll be monitoring your maneuver here in case you get in your gimbal lock. And the High Gain [Antenna] angles [you should use] in case you lose antenna lock in the new attitude will be pitch of minus 45 and yaw of 024. Over.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Understand pitch minus 45 and yaw 024, if we lose it.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: And thanks for watching it for us, Bobby. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: And, 15, if one of you has time, I have a few more Flight Plan updates for you. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Okay, Houston. Stand by one. [Pause.] Go ahead, Bob.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay. The pitch and yaw angles for the P20 - P52 attitude at 226:00 is: pitch of minus 37; yaw of 322. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Understand at the P52 attitude, it's pitch minus 37, yaw 322.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger. At 226:15, we're changing that Verb 49 maneuver attitude to the following coordinates, 327, 143, 055. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Copy the change to the Verb 49 maneuver that occurs at 226:15 to 327, 143 and 055.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger; and the High Gain angles will be pitch 13, yaw 212. [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Pitch 13, yaw 212.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: And, 15, we're observing yaw of 61 degrees right now. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: 15, Houston. We have 65 degrees yaw.

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Rog, Bob. We're watching.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay, three more Flight Plan updates, Jim, if you're ready. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Worden
a15_2252526.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Okay, at 226:22, on - it'll be a line above the line that says "X-ray, On." The new line that will be added will be "X-ray, Off, for 1 second; then". Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Understand. The new line added above "X-ray, On", and it'll read "X-ray, Off, 1 second; then".

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger, that's good. At 227:32, we'll add a line on top of the "Verb 48" line that says "X-ray, Standby". [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Rog. Understand. At 227:32, "X-ray to Standby."

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: Roger. And at 227:57, on a line with the Mass Spec. on it, we'll have - we'll change that "Discriminator, High" to "Discriminator, Low". [Pause.]

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Understand. "Discriminator, Low" instead of "Discriminator, High".

a15_2252526.speaker: Parker
a15_2252526.text: And that completes the update for now.

a15_2252526.speaker: Irwin
a15_2252526.text: Roger.

a15_2252526.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2252526.text: This is Apollo Control at 225 hours, 38 minutes. Apollo 15 now 4,745 nautical miles [8,788 km] from the Moon; the spacecraft velocity almost matching the altitude - 4,700 feet per second [1,430 m/s]. And at the present time, the crew aboard Endeavour are photographing the lunar surface. At the same time, the instruments in Scientific Instrument Module bay, the Gamma-ray, Alpha Particle, and Mass Spectrometer are gathering background data to be used in calibrating the data gathered in lunar orbit. A little later this evening, the crew will be turning on the X-ray instrument in the SIM bay and t

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Houston, Apollo 15.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Roger, 15. Go.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Rog. Do you have any best guess on MCC-5 yet - whether or not we'll have one?

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Stand by. It's not going to be very large.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Well, the question is whether or not we have to prepare for it. And we have another request. We'd like to reschedule the UV photos presently scheduled for 239:10 to some other time, primarily because of the stowage in here. We've got most of the UV equipment already stowed beneath the rocks in prep for the EVA, and - to go in and go out of the stowage container takes a fair amount of time. And we'd like to reschedule that if it's possible.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Rog. [I] assume you mean after the EVA?

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Rog.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Okay. Stand by.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Okay. This is a - this is a crowded fellow up here.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: You guys shouldn't have brought so many rocks back. [Pause.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Well, I guess every once in a while we wonder. [Long pause.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: But we don't wonder very long. [Long pause.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Okay, Davy. First of all, no problem. We can delay those UV photos until after the EVA. Second, right now midcourse 5 looks like 2 feet per second, and we do want to do it. Over.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Okay, thank you. That's a couple of quick answers; appreciate it. That - that will help us in our planning.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Okay. That is only a preliminary estimate on that midcourse 5 though.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: That's okay. That tells us the difference between SPS and RCS kind of burns.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Oh; Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: 15; Houston. One more thing if it's convenient.

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Go ahead. [No answer.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Go ahead, Bob.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Okay. At your convenience, we'd like to verify or check the Primary Accumulator fill valve, On, until the primary accumulator quantity - that's for the glycol loop - is up to 50 to 55 percent. This is the result of a review of the EVA checklist from tomorrow. It assumes that this has already checked and that we're at the 50 to 55 percent level, so we'd like this check - you could do it tonight when you're getting ready for sleep or something. [Pause.]

a15_2254443.speaker: Scott
a15_2254443.text: Okay, we'll do it right now. That's planning ahead.

a15_2254443.speaker: Parker
a15_2254443.text: Copy.

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: Okay, Houston. Our Prim. Accumulator quantity is now about 51 percent.

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: And we filled it from about 45 [percent].

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: And if you have any other goodies you think we ought to check over, might as well do it this evening.

a15_2255028.speaker: Parker
a15_2255028.text: Rog, Dave. That's the only goodie we came upon - Stan - Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2255028.speaker: Parker
a15_2255028.text: Okay, 15. That's the only goodie we had from the review of the EVA checklist for tomorrow. That - that's the only one we could find. An extra goodie that we'd like this evening sometime; if you fellows intend to use the vacuum cleaner - is for you to give us a cue when you turn it on, so we can check and watch the currents. They saw a funny on an AC bus - or an extra current load on an AC bus when they think you were using the vacuum cleaner then. They'd like to verify that by watching it again when you use the vacuum cleaner.

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: Okay. Well, we've been using it quite often on and off.

a15_2255028.speaker: Parker
a15_2255028.text: Okay. Just sometime when you use it, if you give us a cue as you turn it on, that would help. [Pause.]

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: Okay, I - I guess we don't see any need for it this evening. And we could check it out if you'd like...

a15_2255028.speaker: Scott
a15_2255028.text: ...we cleaned up pretty well. The cabin's nice and clean and I...

a15_2255028.speaker: Parker
a15_2255028.text: Rog, Dave. No, that's just a callout. The next time you happen to get around to feeling dirty and want to use the vacuum cleaner, give us a call if you would please.

a15_2255028.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2255028.text: This is Apollo Control. The UV photography, which Dave Scott requested we reschedule, is the ultraviolet photography of the, in this case of Earth, using the electric Hasselblad camera. This is an experiment being conducted to obtain ultraviolet photographs of both the Earth and the Moon to be used in study of planetary atmospheres among other things. And Scott mentioned that the equipment for that photography is stowed under the rock boxes. They've already gotten the cabin apparently set up for the EVA and requested that we reschedule it to some point after the EVA, when Al Worden will be goi

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Houston, 15. Did you get the P52 numbers?

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Rog. We have all your P52 numbers, Al. [Long pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Al, we know that one of them wasn't five balls. [Pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Say again.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Rog. We noticed one of those didn't have five balls on it.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Rog. Did you get the torquing angles on both the P52's.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Rog. Yeah, we got them.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2261416.text: This is Apollo Control. At the present time Al Worden is completing a platform alignment, the Program 52. He's aligning the platform to a new set of coordinates provided by the ground and these coordinates will be used as an attitude reference by the...

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: And, Endeavour; Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Endeavour, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Go ahead, Houston; Endeavour.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Roger. If one of you guys has time, we have what may or may not be the last iteration on troubleshooting the Pan Camera this afternoon. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay. Have at it.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Okay, step one; we'd like to know - you - you can give us these afterwards, but the first step is to determine the status of the Service Module Sector 1 AC 2, circuit breakers on panel 181. Those are three circuit breakers. Number two is to determine the status of the Pan Camera Mode switch. Number three, after these have been done, Pan Camera Mode, Standby; Power, On, talkback barber pole for 2 seconds, then gray, and then Stereo. Number four, Pan Camera Mode, Operate, talkback barber pole for 2 seconds, then gray. Number five, operate Pan Camera until MSFN cues, or until the beginning of the

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay, Bob. You clipped the first part of number 5. Say again, please.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Roger. Number 5 says operate the Pan Camera until the ground gives you a cue or until the beginning of the sleep period. Then we'll give you a cue.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okeydoke. Stand by a minute. [Long pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay, Houston. SIM Sec AC 2 circuit breakers, three, Closed, verified. And the Pan Camera Mode switch is in Standby. So would you like us to go to step 3?

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Endeavour, Endeavour, this is Houston. Roger. That appears to be the problem. Stand by and I'll see what we want to do. Do we... [Pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, this is Houston. Roger. Press on with step 3 from that point when convenient.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay. Going Power, On, 2 seconds, gray, and then stereo. [Long pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay. Power, On, and we have a continuous barber pole.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Roger. Understand, continuous barber pole.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Why don't you just tell us what next? Do you want to go to Stereo or not?

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, stand by.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Okay.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, press on with Stereo, please.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Roger. It's Stereo now, still barber pole. [Long pause.]

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: And I guess we'll go to step 4 now. Okay?

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Roger.

a15_2261416.speaker: SCott
a15_2261416.text: Okay. Operate, still barber pole.

a15_2261416.speaker: Parker
a15_2261416.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, Houston. Roger. We understand; it's still barber pole, and we'll give you a cue when to turn it off. Okay? Thank you.

a15_2261416.speaker: Scott
a15_2261416.text: Roger. Be standing by.

a15_2262537.speaker: Parker
a15_2262537.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, we've succeeded in using up the last of the film in the Pan Camera. You may now go Pan Camera Mode, Standby; and, after 1 minute, Pan Camera Power, Off, per step 6. Over.

a15_2262537.speaker: Scott
a15_2262537.text: Okay, understand. Pan Camera to Standby, and 1 minute, Off.

a15_2262537.speaker: Parker
a15_2262537.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, Houston. We're going to take down the network line here for 20 seconds. We'll be back up with you after that.

a15_2262537.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2262537.text: This is Apollo Control. Now Apollo 15 is now 8,200 [nautical] miles [15,200 km] from the Moon. And the crew should be in the midst of an eat period, and we plan to put them to bed at 228 hours, or about 1 hour from now. Prior to that, they'll put the spacecraft in a stable attitude and then start it rotating slowly so that it gets equal exposure to sunlight and darkness. This is to maintain the proper temperature equilibrium. Dave Scott inquired a while ago if we were planning to do midcourse correction 5, that's a midcourse opportunity at 238 hours, 46 minutes, and the Flight Dynamics Officer

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Over. [No answer.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Houston, 15. Go ahead.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Roger, 15. We see you maneuvering to PTC, and we're requesting that you not maneuver to PTC until the SIM bay covers are closed. I don't know whether they're closed at the moment or not. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Roger. They're closed up. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Understand. And if you fellows...

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: We're just following down through the Flight Plan.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Good. We weren't sure where you were. If you fellows are through eating, we have two or three calls to send up to you, when it's convenient. [Long pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. We can go to T-stop with the Mapping Camera now. And that would be - to follow the checklist on pages 1-39, steps - section 6, 7 and 8; first one being Mapping Camera, On to Off, 30 seconds, and then Standby. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Worden
a15_2273636.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Go.

a15_2273636.speaker: Worden
a15_2273636.text: Houston, 15. Okay...

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo...

a15_2273636.speaker: Worden
a15_2273636.text: ...Listen, Bob. Is this the T-stop on the Mapping Camera photo PAD at 224:10?

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, that's a Roger. [Long pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Okay, Houston. Go with the rest of the updates to the Flight Plan.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Roger. We - want to remind you, when you go into PC - TC, to follow the block in the Flight Plan for the usage of quads, rather than the section in - in the checklist where it calls out to disable all jets on two adjacent quads. This is to avoid contamination of the Mass Spec. It's just to remind you to follow that little box in the Flight Plan. Over.

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: You mean that little box on page 3-343?

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, that's a Roger.

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Okay. We'll follow that little box just like it's in the Flight Plan. Go ahead with your - the rest of your updates.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Roger. On - one discussion here on the UV photos which we're delaying until after the EVA, it looks like the last chance to get these photos is at 246 dash 15, which is about 3 or 4 hours after the nominal end of the EVA. We'd like to propose that for your consideration. Over.

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: That's just fine. We'll do it, 246:15. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Okay, Bob. Do you have anything else to add to the Flight Plan.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Roger. One more item we just got is a request that now that the covers on the X-ray are closed, we're requesting X-ray, On, for 10 minutes and then Off. Over.

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Okay, X-ray, On, for 10 minutes and then Off. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, the posit - the last [switch] position should be Standby rather than Off. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Roger. Standby. [Long pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Okay, Houston. The X-ray is On, and we'll turn it Off in 10 minutes. Anything else?

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. That's a Standby in 10 minutes. I believe you understand that, Dave, anyway. And I believe that the next...

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Rog.

a15_2273636.speaker: Parker
a15_2273636.text: ...thing we will want from you is a call when you're ready to go to sleep. And we will verify all systems at that time so we can get a solid goodnight, rather than tagging on, again like last night. [Pause.]

a15_2273636.speaker: Scott
a15_2273636.text: Roger that.

a15_2274629.speaker: Parker
a15_2274629.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. We see you cycling through the DAP. We suggest you need a zero in R2 to get B/D roll. Over.

a15_2274629.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2274629.text: This is Apollo Control at 227:55 minutes. The crew is - aboard Apollo 15, is presently getting the spacecraft set up for the Passive Thermal Control where they'll be rotating at about 3 revolutions per hour. This is the standard set up used during the sleep periods to maintain proper thermal equilibrium on the spacecraft. And at the present time, Apollo 15 is 10,488 nautical miles [19,424 km] from the Moon. The spacecraft's velocity is 4,129 feet per second [1,259 m/s]. We're going to replay the videotape from this morning's check of the TV system on the Lunar Roving Vehicle at the Hadley Base

a15_2275510.speaker: Worden
a15_2275510.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Go.

a15_2275510.speaker: Worden
a15_2275510.text: Hey, Bob, you didn't update the [garble] load in the P20 for PTC. Was that meant to be updated to .375 or shall we leave it at .35? [Pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Let's keep it at .375.

a15_2275510.speaker: Worden
a15_2275510.text: Understand you want the Flight Plan updated to .375.

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. That's a Roger.

a15_2275510.speaker: Worden
a15_2275510.text: Roger. Thank you. We got the update. [Long pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Irwin
a15_2275510.text: Houston, Apollo 15.

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Go ahead.

a15_2275510.speaker: Irwin
a15_2275510.text: Yes, Bob. We're trying to retract the Mapping Camera. But the time has been well exceeded and we still have the barber pole indication. [Pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. We'd just as soon you didn't spin up quite yet. We still think the rates are a little high. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Worden
a15_2275510.text: Okay, Houston. We'll wait on your cue then.

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Concerning the Mapping Camera retraction problem, the question is did you get a barber pole during the Alpha/X-ray cover procedure? Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Irwin
a15_2275510.text: You ought to amplify your question there a little bit, Bob. You mean when we are - operating the covers? [Long pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Jim, the question basically is, did the barber pole, did the talkback function properly when you just closed the alpha/X-ray covers? Over. [Pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Irwin
a15_2275510.text: Yes. Dave said it works fine. [Long pause.]

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Jim, stand by on that. We got your last answer, and they're working on it.

a15_2275510.speaker: Irwin
a15_2275510.text: Okay. I think I'll take the - go out of the Retract position on the switch and just wait for your word.

a15_2275510.speaker: Parker
a15_2275510.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15. That sounds good to me, Jim.

a15_2280945.speaker: Parker
a15_2280945.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. We'd like to hold off on PTC a little bit longer until we get this Mapping Camera business straightened out. And, Jim, for some troubleshooting on this, we'd like to have you check on panel 181, the Main A circuit breaker, Closed, and the Deploy/Retract switch in the Retract position. And on panel 278, the Deploy Main A circuit breaker, Closed. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2280945.speaker: Irwin
a15_2280945.text: Those two circuit breakers and the switches are verified, Bob, Closed.

a15_2280945.speaker: Irwin
a15_2280945.text: And the presleep checklist: been no medication today. Onboard readouts are Bat C, 37; pyro Bat A, 37.3; pyro Bat B, 37.3. On the RCS, it's 56, 55, 54, and 55. And I guess, after we get PTC squared away, we'll give you the E-memory dump. [Pause.]

a15_2280945.speaker: Parker
a15_2280945.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Copy the crew status and the onboard readout. And stand by on the E-mod; we may ask you for that before PTC, but we'll be back with you on that in a minute.

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Houston, 15. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Go.

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Rog. Un - unless you got a solution for the camera now, why don't we troubleshoot it in the morning and get on with our evening powerdown. Okay?

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. That's a Roger. We've just come to that conclusion ourselves down here. We're ready for an E-mod dump before the start of PTC, please. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Okay. It's on the way. [Long pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. One last attempt on the Mapping Camera. We suggest you try Mapping Camera doors, Open, then Retract, and then doors, Close, if successful on the retract. And you can do that while - after you start up PTC, if you like.

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Roger. We've already attempted to do that, Bob.

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Roger. You're ahead of Building 45. [Pause.] And, Apollo 15, Apollo 15, we have a good E-mod dump. [Long pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Worden
a15_2281248.text: Houston, 15. How do the rates look now?

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. Your rates look good. You're Go for PTC.

a15_2281248.speaker: Worden
a15_2281248.text: Okay. We'll try. [Long pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. As soon as you configure the Mass Spec - Multiplier, Low; Discriminator, Low; Experiment, On; Ion Source, On; et cetera, you're Go for sleep. Then no more comments from the ground until morning.

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, Houston is out for the evening. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Don't go too far out, though. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, our ever watchful eye will be on you while you sleep.

a15_2281248.speaker: Scott
a15_2281248.text: Very good. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Worden
a15_2281248.text: Houston, 15. [Garbled] initial rates [garbled]. [Long pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2281248.text: This is Apollo Control. The spacecraft now is beginning the Passive Thermal Control rotation. As we rotate from one antenna to another on the Omni antennas, we'll pick up some noise from time to time during the evening.

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15; Houston. You called just as we lost and locked onto the high - onto the Omni. [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Worden
a15_2281248.text: Okay, Bob. Just wanted to know how initial rates of PTC looked? [Pause.]

a15_2281248.speaker: Parker
a15_2281248.text: Apollo 15, Apollo 15, initial rates look good. We'll be keeping an eye on it though for you, Al.

a15_2281248.speaker: Worden
a15_2281248.text: Okay, Bob. It just didn't look like I got quite as much rate when I entered on that as I expected.

a15_2281248.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2281248.text: Our Communications Engineer reports that the crew has configured - have configured the communications circuits on board the spacecraft now for their sleep period and we do not expect to hear from them further during this 8-hour rest period. We've had some questions [from journalists] on the double calls, the repetition of the call Apollo 15, by the CapCom. And the Network Controller reports that this is being done because of a weak or low level we've got on the landlines from Houston to - to Madrid. And normally the tone that is sent out in conjunction with the CapCom's call, the bleep that us

a15_2284149.speaker: Parker
a15_2284149.text: ...we see a certain rise in temperature there which may mean that if it was frozen; it'll improve. And we do not see any - the Mass Spec. configuration yet. And a progress report on your PTC says it's about 60/40, but it'll - it will last the night.

a15_2284149.speaker: Parker
a15_2284149.text: Roger, 15. Would you believe that we have one more call on the Pan Camera. We do not show Pan Camera Power to Off, please, and unfortunately, that means that we might heat up the film too much. So we would like Pan Camera Power to Off. [Pause.] And guys, as long as you're down there, would you mind trying Mapping Camera, Retract once more. [Pause.] 15...

a15_2284817.speaker: Scott
a15_2284817.text: Houston, it doesn't look like the Mapping Camera is going to come back in. What's the problem if it's left out?

a15_2284817.speaker: Parker
a15_2284817.text: 15, Houston. Would you believe we've just determined that it doesn't seem to be a problem if it stays out overnight.

a15_2284817.speaker: Scott
a15_2284817.text: Great. Then I guess we can call it quits for the night. Okay?

a15_2284817.speaker: Parker
a15_2284817.text: 15, we don't have TM on you right now. Is the Mass Spec. taken care of?

a15_2284817.speaker: Scott
a15_2284817.text: Rog. The Mass Spec's taken care of. There's one switch out of position. And the Mapping Camera is going to go to Off. [Pause.]

a15_2284817.speaker: Parker
a15_2284817.text: Roger. Copied, Dave. We'll try again. [Pause.]

a15_2285850.speaker: Parker
a15_2285850.text: Apollo 15, Houston. In the blind, no need to reply. Our Pan Camera data still shows Power, On. This is the middle switch in the bottom row. The Power Boost switch should be in the center, Off position. No need to reply. Over.

a15_2285850.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2285850.text: This is Apollo Control at 229 hours, 30 minutes. The Flight Surgeon reports that the crew appears to be getting to sleep at this time. We have biomedical data on Command Module Pilot Al Worden and his rates indicate that at least he is approaching sleep. Apollo 15, at the present time, is 14,244 nautical miles [26,380 km] from the Moon and the velocity is down now to 3,976 feet per second [1,212 m/s]. During this rest period we plan to come up with hourly status reports and in the - in between status reports we will have lines down with tape recorders running to record any unexpected conversat

a15_2354515.speaker: Allen
a15_2354515.text: Good morning, Endeavour. This is Apollo Control in Houston, Texas, tuning the band [i.e. about to play some "wake-up music" to the crew]. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2354515.speaker: Scott
a15_2354515.text: Good morning, tuning the band. This is Endeavour. Go. [Pause.]

a15_2354515.speaker: Allen
a15_2354515.text: Roger. Good morning, Endeavour. This is Houston with CSM consumables and a few good words about your Flight Plan, when you're ready. [Pause.]

a15_2354515.speaker: Allen
a15_2354515.text: Okay, Dave. And you troops sure start the day early up there, I must say. [Pause.]

a15_2354515.speaker: Scott
a15_2354515.text: Yeah, seems that way, doesn't it?

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay, Houston. We've located the Flight Plan. Go ahead with your updates. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Were you calling? [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Rog, Joe. We've located the Flight Plan. Go ahead with your update.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay, Dave. I guess, let me start with the CSM consumables. At 235 plus 30, RCS total, 41; quad A: 43, 40, 38, 41; H 2 tank 1, 41, 40, 36; O 2 tank 1, 56, 58, 45. And the only immediate other thing I have for you, Dave, is a comment on the maneuver at 236 hours - about the Gamma-ray boom retract. We'd like for you to confirm - I'll be back when...

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read?

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Last I heard was gamma-ray. Go ahead.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. The rest of that mysterious transmission is essentially the following, Dave. We've got a funny in that gamma-ray experiment and - so we're going to - to want to modify the use of it a little bit today. It should be no major imposition, but the Flight Plan calls out for the Gamma-ray boom to be retracted at 236 hours. We'd like to modify that by saying, turn the Gain Step, Shield, Off, at that time and we'll want you to retract it about 10 minutes later. We'll give you a cue for that. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Gain Step, Shield, Off, at 236 and stand by for your cue for retraction.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: That's correct, Dave. I've got a few other good things here, but there's no hurry on any of them. [I would] be willing to stand by, if you wanted to get squared away and give me a call later, or whatever you'd like to do. It's your preference.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Well, let's go ahead, Joe. We're getting squared away up here.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. If you have the Flight Plan then, let me add the following. At 236 plus 45, add the step, "X-ray to On". [Pause.] And then turning over several pages...

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Roger. 236:45; X-ray, On.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. And turning over several pages to 241 plus 25. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Go.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Roger. After the step "O 2 heaters 1, 2 and 3 to Auto", add "O 2 tanks 1 and 2, 50 Watt Heaters, Main B, 2, to Open." And "O 2 tank 3, 50 Watt Heater, Main A, 1, to Open." Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. 241:25; O 2 Heater - or O 2 Tank 1 and 2, 50 Watt Heaters, Main B to Open, and O 2 Tank Heater - They're 50 Watt also? Main A, 1, Open? [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Stand by, Dave. I'm sorry about this one. Stand by.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay, Endeavour. Let me try that again. Had a typographical error down here. It should read "O 2 Tank 1, 50 Watt Heater, Main B, 1, Open"; and "O 2 Tanks 2 and 3, 50 Watt Heaters, Main A, 2, Open". Over. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. O 2 Tank 1, 50 Watt Heater, Main B, 1, Open; and Tanks 2 and 3, 50 Watt Heaters, Main A, 2, Open.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: That's correct, Dave. I apologize for the slow start there. Now I've got some DAP load changes that cover the times from about 247 hours to 252 hours. And - the change is apparently because of a mis - of a mistake in the Flight Plan you have on board that we, in the meantime, have caught down here. And - so there are several deletions and additions during that time. The first one starts at 247 plus 28.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Go ahead, I've got it.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Delete your Verb 48, 11111 and X1111, and add - stand by a second. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: That's twice. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: I'll be very careful from here on. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay, D.R. [i.e. David Randolph Scott] I'm ready to try it again. You've deleted at 247:28 the line with all the funny number ones, and you're supposed to delete, in the DAP load column, also that same entry. It's in the time column, I guess. And then turn the page.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Yeah. Rog.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Go to 248 hours, on the next page, and in the notes column, change the DAP load status to read 11101. And the rest is the same. And this DAP load status continues through the PTC until 251 hours. [Pause.] And the next change is at 251 hours and 4 minutes. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. 251:04, and I got the other three changes. Go ahead.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Delete the Verb 48 line and the DAP load over in the time column there. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: And the next change is at 251:47. Delete the Verb 48 line and the DAP load in its corresponding time column. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. And I guess over in the notes column, we're still carrying 11101. Right?

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: That's affirm, Dave. And starting at 252 hours, your DAP load status should read 111 - Stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Let me try again. Starting... [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Okay, starting at 252 plus 00 hours, in the notes column, the DAP load status should read 11101 times 1111 [means 11101 X1111]. And this should be carried through the rest period until 261 hours. Over.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay, Joe. You were saying something there about 252:30, as we lost comm. I got the entry at 252:00. Was there any change at 252:30?

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Negative, Dave. The change at 252:00 should just be continued through until 261 hours. And that's just the DAP - DAP load status - should be changed correspondingly through until that time. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. I see. And then we're - we're just 11101 all the way.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: That's correct. [Long pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. Go ahead with your next. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Dave, that's all I've got for the time being. And I think I'd be afraid to go ahead much further, if you're really counting those times. Maybe I should start keeping score on you as well.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: [Laughter.] Okay. [Pause.]

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: We're happy for the time being. We're - we're standing by for a crew status report at your convenience. And we'll be watching for the Gain Step Shield to come Off.

a15_2355101.speaker: Scott
a15_2355101.text: Okay. We'll get right back with you in about 5 or 10.

a15_2355101.speaker: Allen
a15_2355101.text: Thank you.

a15_2361801.speaker: Allen
a15_2361801.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. We'd like for you to retract the Gamma-ray boom for us, please, and we'll be watching for your torquing angles. Also, if you'd like some news reporting in the background, I have the morning news here, if you're interested in that at all. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2361801.speaker: Scott
a15_2361801.text: Rog. Gamma-ray going to Retract now, and stand by on the news. [Pause.]

a15_2361801.speaker: Allen
a15_2361801.text: Okay. Roger. You can use that for background for the P52, I guess. President Nixon in effect declared US responsibility for offensive ground combat operations in Vietnam at an end. With the draft still in limbo, Selective Service went ahead today with the lottery to determine the order in which next year's nineteen-year-olds will face military service. Secretary of State William P. Rogers plans to go to the United Nat - Nations to push for a more energetic international relief effort for East Pakistan today. The Senate Armed Services Committee completed action on a 21 billion dollar military b

a15_2361801.speaker: Scott
a15_2361801.text: Boy! It sounds like he's as good as our very own Blinky.

a15_2361801.speaker: Allen
a15_2361801.text: That may well be, Dave. I - That never occurred to me.

a15_2362517.speaker: Allen
a15_2362517.text: Endeavour. We've copied the torquing angles. Thank you. And, Dave, if you can get a volunteer to work on the Mapping Camera for us, we'd like to try to pull that Mapping Camera in and get the covers closed in preparation for the EVA. We're not quite sure the position that the camera's in right now and the procedure I'll - can read up step by step, but it's basically to open the covers, try to extend the camera, we'll confirm the extension, and then we'll have you retract the camera and ultimately retract the covers. And I'll be standing by for your advice on this. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2362517.speaker: Scott
a15_2362517.text: Okay, Joe. We'll see if we have time to work on that. But, it's my understanding we do not have to have it retracted for the EVA. [Long pause.]

a15_2362517.speaker: Allen
a15_2362517.text: Dave. That's my understanding, too. I think - the main reason - for wanting to do this, if time is available and it's, o - and it's only - would be a nicety - would be it - gives us a warm feeling regarding the film. [Long pause.]

a15_2362517.speaker: Allen
a15_2362517.text: Dave, just to complete that last statement, you're correct. We don't have to have that device retracted for the EVA. But, apparently, it - it gives the film people a nice feeling regarding their film not getting too cold or too hot. That's the reason for that.

a15_2362517.speaker: Scott
a15_2362517.text: Okay. Well, let us see if we can get to it.

a15_2362517.speaker: Scott
a15_2362517.text: Okay. And we sort of flip-flopped that P23 and eat period so that we can take advantage of our setup for eating and all. And we'll get on with P23 as soon as we finish breakfast.

a15_2362517.speaker: Allen
a15_2362517.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. All other things being equal, troops, we'd prefer that you do the P23 before you begin the eat period, because it gives us an hour of pointed X-ray data during your eat period. [Pause.]

a15_2362517.speaker: Scott
a15_2362517.text: Okay, Joe; but I guess the inequality is the stowage situation in here and assuring that we can get properly prepared for the EVA. So - we'll start the P23 in probably about - oh - 5 minutes or so, because we're almost through eating. But we sort of have to take advantage of our configuration in here in order to stay with the time line later on.

a15_2362517.speaker: Allen
a15_2362517.text: That's fine, Dave. We understand, thank you.

a15_2364320.speaker: Allen
a15_2364320.text: Roger. I've got some information about your midcourse [correction opportunity] 5, which is scheduled to come up here [at 238:46]. We have a firm decision that there will not be a midcourse 5 maneuver required and the numbers behind that are a Gamma of minus 6.69 [degrees, with respect to the local horizon at Entry Interface]; your vacuum perigee is 18.4 [nautical miles, 34.1 km], and the midcourse 5 correction that we're showing now would be 3/10ths of a foot per second. The corresponding midcourse 7 correction runs at about 1.8 feet per second. And, based on that new information, we're wonder

a15_2364320.speaker: Scott
a15_2364320.text: Okay. That's pretty fantastic guidance, ain't it? Let us - take another look at the Flight Plan here and come right back at you.

a15_2364320.speaker: Allen
a15_2364320.text: Okay, Dave; fine. And no hurry on - on the - on that decision. We would like the Gamma-ray [Gain] Step Shield, On, now, please. [Pause.]

a15_2364320.speaker: Scott
a15_2364320.text: And, Joe, I guess on the corona photography, mag R has been ex - expended. As far as the UV, is not so much a problem of time. It's a problem of stowage. It's stowed way down deep in one of Endeavour's lockers here and to get at it requires quite a bit of manipulation of bags. And that's the reason we wanted to delay that if it was possible.

a15_2364320.speaker: Allen
a15_2364320.text: Okay, Dave. We understand that. And that - that sounds like it's a far more reason - reasonable to delay that. The timing's not critical as far as we're concerned. We just wanted to give you a balanced workday.

a15_2364320.speaker: Scott
a15_2364320.text: Okay; fine. We don't mind loading up a little after the EVA, because it really saves us a lot of work in the long run. And you might wonder why we didn't put - the UV stuff somewhere else, but there's just nowhere else to put it but in it's - in its own proper little spot.

a15_2365746.speaker: Scott
a15_2365746.text: Okay. Have a crew status report for you, and you can have the docs take a look at the LMP bio[medical], see if that's acceptable.

a15_2365746.speaker: Scott
a15_2365746.text: Okay. 7 hours sleep apiece, and PRDs 25028, 23193, 08031.

a15_2365746.speaker: Allen
a15_2365746.text: Okay, Dave. Thank you. And we see that we've got the X-ray going. We'd like for you to change the setting on the Gain Step. Give us a one-click increase, which'll move us from - the position 7 back to position 1. Over.

a15_2365746.speaker: Scott
a15_2365746.text: Okay. You've got a one-click increase.

a15_2365746.speaker: Allen
a15_2365746.text: Okay. We see it, Dave, and Jim's Bio looks clean to us down here. Thank you.

a15_2365746.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2365746.text: This is Apollo Control. The crew reported during the last exchange, that the - each of the three crewmen had a good seven hours sleep during the night. And also the ground advised the crew that the magnitude of midcourse number 5 - midcourse correction burn number 5, as shown by present tracking, is so small that it will be deleted. It's now showing around 3/10 of a foot per second. Meanwhile, the space flight meteorology group of the National Weather Service said this morning, that the end-of-mission weather conditions are expected to be satisfactory in the area north of Hawaii where Apollo 1

a15_2371505.speaker: Allen
a15_2371505.text: Endeavour. Give us six clicks on the Gamma-ray Gain [Step] switch, please.

a15_2373559.speaker: Allen
a15_2373559.text: Rog, Dave. A couple of miscellaneous items I'd like to ask you about. First of all, the trench sends their congratulations to whoever's doing the P23 for us. The errors are less than one sigma - and they're awarding the honorary Vasco da Gama Navigation Award for excellence in this. Secondly, we're puzzling over your remark about magazine Romeo [the high-speed black and white film magazine], which you reported to us was exhausted. And we're wondering if you just read - the frame number from the mag and, if so, what it read. Over. [Long pause.]

a15_2373559.speaker: Worden
a15_2373559.text: Yeah. Joe, this is Al. The last reading of Romeo, I think, was 110. [Pause.]

a15_2373559.speaker: Allen
a15_2373559.text: Okay, Al. Thank you. And were you doing the P23 for us?

a15_2373559.speaker: Allen
a15_2373559.text: Okay. I'll tell you a little something about Vasco da Gama later on. Another easy item here; you're going to come up on a bat[tery] charge - I guess Bat B charge - starting at 239 hours, and we'd like to delay that to 244 hours, please.

a15_2373559.speaker: Scott
a15_2373559.text: Okay. Delay the Bat B charge to 244. And be advised - you've got to know that we've got best navigator in trans-Earth lunar space up here.

a15_2373559.speaker: Allen
a15_2373559.text: At least one of them, I'm sure.

a15_2373559.speaker: Allen
a15_2373559.text: Rog. We copy. And, finally, I'd like to get a volunteer to take a whack at this - configuring the Map Camera properly. And it's going to be a few short steps, and if it works, great; we'll have a lot of good engineering data regarding the thermal properties of that beauty. And if it doesn't work, we're just going to turn it off and leave it. And - when somebody's ready to do that, I'll go through the steps. There are not too many.

a15_2373559.speaker: Scott
a15_2373559.text: Okay, Joe. Somebody'll be ready in just a few minutes.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Okay, Houston; Endeavour. If you want to try your camera techniques again, let's give it a whirl.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Okay, Endeavour. I've got five steps here, and I think it's easiest for me just to read them to you and have you carry them out rather than copying them down. And the first one - first two steps...

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Rog.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: ...on panel 181, verify Logic Power, Main A circuit breaker, Closed. [Pause.]

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Okay, verified.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: And same panel, verify Logic Power switches, two of them, to Deploy/Retract.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Verified.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Step 3 on panel 278, the Experiment Covers Deploy circuit breaker, Main A to Closed. [Pause.]

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Verified. Closed.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Step 4 on panel 230, the Map Camera, verify Standby.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Verified to Standby.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
