a15_2374642.text: Okay, and coming up on step 5 and let me read through this - and - I'll stand by for questions then, if there are some. We want the Map Camera Track to Extend; and, simultaneously, we want the Experiment Cover Map Camera/Laser Altimeter to Open, and we want those two things done simultaneously.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Okay. Understand. Go to Extend and open the Covers, Map Camera/Laser simultaneously.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Roger. And a note on that - I guess - on the Map Camera Track to Extend, we'll be watching that for about between 4 and 5 minutes or until you get a gray talkback on there. And - we think this is going to clear up our problem and if it doesn't, we're just going to turn the whole ball of wax off and go ahead and do the EVA as normally planned. Over.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Okay, Joe. In three seconds, we'll execute.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Rog, Dave. We're watching. [Long pause.]

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Well, I got a gray on the Mapping Camera. How 'bout that.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Okay; stand by. [Pause.]

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Dave, do you have a gray on the door as well?

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: That's affirm, but I did not get a barber pole on the door. It just stayed gray.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Okay; that's good. That just means that it was open already.

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Right.

a15_2374642.speaker: Allen
a15_2374642.text: Okay. Then that - that's worked out fine. Apparently, we were having a temperature problem with that thing before, and we're back in business just like normal. We'd like now the Mapping Camera Track to Retract, and that'll take I guess about 4½ minutes. [Pause.]

a15_2374642.speaker: Scott
a15_2374642.text: Okay. Map Camera Track going to Retract now.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: Endeavour, this is Houston. Be advised that because we're not going to do a midcourse 5, we'll continue the X-ray pointing to about 238 plus 30, and we'll be coming at you with a list of the steps at 238 hours that you can delete because we're not doing the midcourse.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: And, Dave, could - could you have someone check the barber pole on our Map Camera, Track, to see if you have the gray-Retract indication, please.

a15_2375657.speaker: Scott
a15_2375657.text: Rog, Joe. I been watching it. You got about 7 minutes and 20 - 20 seconds now and it's still barber pole.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: Okay. That's what we're showing down here. And stand by. [Long pause.]

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: Okay, Endeavour. We're satisfied with that Mapping Camera exercise. Two more requests on that. Go to Off with the Extend/Retract switch, and to Off with the Mapping Camera/Laser Altimeter Cover switch, please. And we're finished with that.

a15_2375657.speaker: Scott
a15_2375657.text: Okay; Extend/Retract to Off; and a Map Camera/Laser Altimeter's going of Off.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: That's right, Dave. And a note for Al. We think that the magazine Romeo, based on the frame count you gave us, still has enough frames left to take the solar corona pictures. And we'll have some special words for Al on how he's to take those pictures. I guess, we'll delete a few of the solar corona requirements. Also, word about the PRD configuration for the EVA. Apparently, we'll want the CMP to have the PRD whose number reads 25028. And, I guess, that's the one you've been carrying, Dave. And, Jim, will - will use the one that reads 08031, but we would like to have him reconfirm this number

a15_2375657.speaker: Scott
a15_2375657.text: Okay. Let me get that checklist here Joe; standby. The CMP is 250 - say again.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: Roger. We want Al to wear the PRD that's now reading 25028. That will distinguish it from the other two with no ambiguity. And Jim to take the one that begins 080, and we want him to give us the full reading off of that before he starts the EVA, though.

a15_2375657.speaker: Scott
a15_2375657.text: Well, we'll have to give it to you now, because it will be in the suit and we won't be able to get to it.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: That's fine. Any time. Any time. [Long pause.]

a15_2375657.speaker: Scott
a15_2375657.text: Okay. The one Jim will wear will be 08037.

a15_2375657.speaker: Allen
a15_2375657.text: Okay, Dave. Thank you. And if you'll give us P00 and Accept, we'll let you have a new state vector.

a15_2380433.speaker: Scott
a15_2380433.text: And, Houston; Endeavour. [Do] you want to go through the change in the Flight Plan at 238 hours, if you have it?

a15_2380433.speaker: Allen
a15_2380433.text: Okay, Dave. This involves delaying the SIM bay turnoff until 238 hours and 30 minutes. And in detail, at 238 plus 05, delete the P30 external Delta-V, and the Verb 49 maneuver. Lines: at 238 plus 20, delete sextant star check; at 238 plus 28, delete all the steps from there starting with circuit breaker SCS, et cetera , up to 238 plus 55, ending with RHC Power Direct, two, Off, et cetera . Over.

a15_2380433.speaker: Scott
a15_2380433.text: All right. I got all that. Thank you.

a15_2380433.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2380433.text: This is Apollo Control. Coming up in a few seconds, on Apollo 15's exit of the Lunar Sphere of Influence.

a15_2381426.speaker: Allen
a15_2381426.text: Be advised at my mark, you are leaving the sphere of lunar influence; and it's downhill from here on in.

a15_2381426.speaker: Scott
a15_2381426.text: Rog. Thank you, Joe. That's nice to know.

a15_2381426.speaker: Allen
a15_2381426.text: Did you notice anything there, Dave? Discontinuity in velocity or anything like that?

a15_2381426.speaker: Scott
a15_2381426.text: Well, Joe. That's one of the mysteries that we'll probably have keep to ourselves.

a15_2382156.speaker: Allen
a15_2382156.text: Rog, Dave. We're looking down the line here towards the EVA. And the Surgeon's getting good biomed data on Al now, except one of the three EKG sensors is apparently marginal, and there's some noise creeping in. We're just wondering what your standard procedure is regarding sensoring before the EVA exercise. If he's going to resensor, it's probably no problem; if he's not planning to, maybe we ought to talk it over a little. Over.

a15_2382156.speaker: Scott
a15_2382156.text: Okay. We're all three all sensored, ready to go. If they have a problem, let's get it squared away right now.

a15_2382156.speaker: Allen
a15_2382156.text: Okay. Do you have, - Maybe Al could try pressing down on the three EKG leads, one at a time, for us; that may help us out.

a15_2382156.speaker: Scott
a15_2382156.text: Okay. Here we go. The upper right. [Long pause.]

a15_2382156.speaker: Scott
a15_2382156.text: Okay. The upper center is being pressed. [Long pause.]

a15_2382156.speaker: Allen
a15_2382156.text: Dave, it looks to us like it's one of the two top sensors, and we're wondering how difficult it would be to reseat both of them now. [Pause.]

a15_2382156.speaker: Scott
a15_2382156.text: Okay. I'll tell you what we'll do. A little further down the line here, we'll take care of both of those. We'll resync them and reseat them and everything.

a15_2382156.speaker: Scott
a15_2382156.text: And thank you for thinking ahead on that one.

a15_2382156.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2382156.text: This is Apollo Control. With the exiting by [the] Apollo 15 spacecraft [out] of the arbitrary and imaginary lunar sphere of influence, the displays in Mission Control, having to do with velocity and distance, switched over at that time from lunar reference to Earth reference. The crossing occurred at 238 hours, 14 minutes, 51 seconds. At this moment, Apollo 15 is 177,225 nautical miles [328,220 km] out from Earth, approaching at a velocity of 2,855 feet per second [870 m/s]. Landing clock showing 56 hours, 40 minutes until splashdown. Midcourse [Correction] 5 burn, because of its small magnitu

a15_2384321.speaker: Allen
a15_2384321.text: Rog. I've got an update to your corona - window calibration photography and the UV photographs, when you're ready. [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Houston, Endeavour. Can't seem to get the Mass Spec. boom all the way in and I guess Al's had a little trouble with it now and again with the barber pole being half - the talkback being half barber pole. And seems to flutter there, close to the gray position, and doesn't really come all the way in. [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay, Dave. We copy. Let us think about that.

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay. And we're going ahead with the dumps, if that's okay? [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: And if you'd like a visual check of just exactly where that's hanging up, why we can give it to you in a couple of hours. We'll have Al go out and take a look.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: That's not a bad idea. Does he know about this plan yet?

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Well, I don't know. We'll check with him. Yeah, he nods his head like he'd probably be obliged to do that.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. Break it to him gently, though.

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: And, Dave. While I got you here, I do want to comment that the first change in the Flight Plan is to delete the step at 238 plus 23 that says "enable all jets." We think that there is a - a certain chance that that Map Camera may be stuck out, and we particularly don't want RCS jets A4, A2, B1 and B4 to be enabled, because they may give us trouble with that camera. [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay. Understand, Joe. We'll scratch that step and make sure A4, A2, B1 and B4 stay off.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. And I'll - Standing by to read you some more photo PADs, just at your convenience.

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Go ahead. I've got the Flight Plan out. [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. If you'll turn to page 3-352, which is the Corona Window Calibration and UV photos procedures page.

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: I've got it.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. The attitude involved in the corona photographs should read 057, 005, 025. And the time on that, 239 plus 08. And the High Gain [Antenna] numbers, pitch, minus 48; yaw, 238. [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay. 057, 005, 025 at 239:08. Minus 48 and 238 for the High Gain.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: That's correct, and moving down a couple of lines, the shutter speed should be changed from 1/500th to 1/125th. And change the inhibit jets line to read "damp rates for 5 minutes." CMC Mode to Free. [Long pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay. Understand. Scratch inhibit jets, and substitute damp rates for 5 minutes, and then CMC, Free, and the 1/125th replaces the 1/500th on the camera.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: That's correct, Dave. And moving down a little further, delete the line, "cycle 1 frame, change shutter" and delete the line "cycle 1 frame." And finally, change the last line, enable all jets to read, "CMC Mode, Auto." [Pause.]

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Okay, delete line, "cycle 1 frame" and "cycle 1 frame"; and CMC Auto, replaces "Enable all jets."

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: That's correct and assuming you're going to take the UV photographs after the EVA, I have a photo PAD for that, if that assumption is correct.

a15_2384624.speaker: Scott
a15_2384624.text: Looks like that assumption is probably correct, Joe, and we'll take the photo PAD later on. Let us get on with corona [photography], or we won't make it.

a15_2384624.speaker: Allen
a15_2384624.text: Okay. Sounds good.

a15_2385725.speaker: Allen
a15_2385725.text: Rog, Jim. We understand you're going to delete [means postpone] the UV photographs, but after you complete the corona window calibration, you will have to do the first step in the UV photos trans-Earth coast procedures, there. And that first step is Verb 49 maneuver to Earth UV photo attitude, and it lists the attitude there. We need this for thermal reasons.

a15_2390541.speaker: Worden
a15_2390541.text: Hey, Joe. Just a point of clarification on the backing to be used for the corona. I don't know whether you're aware or not, but the backing that fits into window 4, which is the right-hand rendezvous window, has two different mounting pads for the camera, one is 250 and the other is 80. And the 80 is pointing 12 degrees below the X-axis, and I just wanted to check and see if you wanted us - if that's the proper pad or if you wanted us to use the 80 or the 250 pad.

a15_2390541.speaker: Allen
a15_2390541.text: Al, use the 80. The one pointing 12 degrees above the X-axis.

a15_2395045.speaker: Henize
a15_2395045.text: 15, this is Houston, broadcasting in the blind, with a request that, if possible, we bring back Dave's LCG. If it's already stowed in too inaccessible a place in the - in the jettison bag, don't bother. But if you can possibly save it, please bring it back.

a15_2395045.speaker: Scott
a15_2395045.text: Okay. Sorry, Houston, we were getting suited there, and didn't realize we were off comm; but copied your request. Let us think about it for a minute.

a15_2395045.speaker: Scott
a15_2395045.text: Well, Houston, I guess that it's a good reason we're about an hour ahead. So we'll go ahead and dig it out. [Pause.]

a15_2395045.speaker: Scott
a15_2395045.text: Well, we're sort of ahead, expecting little things like that to pop up.

a15_2395045.speaker: Scott
a15_2395045.text: Say, Houston, by the way, the LCG you'll get back is the one I wore on the third EVA only. [Long pause.]

a15_2395045.speaker: Henize
a15_2395045.text: Roger; Dave. That's fine. That's the one we'd like.

a15_2395045.speaker: Henize
a15_2395045.text: And 15, whenever Al has a quiet moment, I have several prebriefing questions to send up to him about what to look for on the V over H sensor.

a15_2395045.speaker: Scott
a15_2395045.text: Okay, give us about an hour for that, then we'll be able to talk to you.

a15_2395045.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2395045.text: This is Apollo Control at 239 hours, 58 minutes. Apollo 15 now 174,778 nautical miles [323,688 km] from Earth. Velocity, 2,909 feet per second [887 m/s]. And the crew is in preparations for the EVA to retrieve the film cassettes from the Panoramic and Mapping Cameras.

a15_2400148.speaker: Henize
a15_2400148.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to have Manual [pointing] on the High Gain whenever one of you has a chance to get there. No need to answer.

a15_2400148.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2400148.text: This is Apollo Control at 240 hours, 06 minutes. Dave Scott reported a short time ago that the crew was about 1 hour ahead on the time line. We do not anticipate however that the EVA will start 1 hour early. We're staying keyed here to the normal Flight Plan time for EVA. If that changes we'll let you know but at the present time, we do not anticipate moving the Flight Plan ahead. The liquid cooled garment that they have asked them to bring back is the one in which Dave Scott replaced a plug when they failed a suit integrity check about LM jettison time in lunar orbit. The experts on the groun

a15_2400148.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2400148.text: This is Apollo Control at 240 hours, 14 minutes. The CapCom Karl Henize, has been joined now by the backup crew Commander and Command Module Pilot, Dick Gordon and Vance Brand and by Donald K. Slayton, the Director of Flight Crew Operations.

a15_2400148.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2400148.text: This is Apollo Control at 240 hours, 37 minutes. The crew is busy with preparations for EVA and Apollo 15 is 173,670 nautical miles [321,636 km] from Earth. Velocity, 2,935 feet per second [895 m/s].

a15_2405959.speaker: Scott
a15_2405959.text: We're all suited up, and down to the comm check portion of the EVA prep, and we're ready to talk to you about whatever you'd like to talk about.

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: I guess the main thing we have to talk about is the inspection of the V over H sensor of the Pan Camera. Are you ready to listen, Al? [Pause.]

a15_2405959.speaker: Scott
a15_2405959.text: Okay. He can read you, but he's got to reconfigure his panel in order to talk to you, so we'll do that.

a15_2405959.speaker: Worden
a15_2405959.text: Okay, Karl, how do you read me now?

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Loud and clear, Al. Hey, on this V over H sensor, I have a set of five steps, or five questions that we'd like to have for you to have in your mind.

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Okay. Number 1 is, inspect the general area - this is sort of a general point of view - inspect the general area around the V over H sensor and comment on any evidence of thermal or mechanical degradation. And 2, 3, 4, and 5 are sort of more specifically. Number 2. Is there any evidence of V over H sensor lens cracking, or debris on the lens? In other words, have a good check of the lens itself. Number 3. Is any large amount of the black paint around the V over H sensor opening missing? Number 4. Is the plume shield in place around the V over H sensor opening? And the plume shield is what I'd

a15_2405959.speaker: Worden
a15_2405959.text: Okay, Karl. We got all those.

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Okey doke. No other special questions at the moment. Stand by. [Pause.]

a15_2405959.speaker: Scott
a15_2405959.text: Okay. We'll proceed on here then.

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Incidentally, I guess we're - we both understand each other on the status of the Mapping Camera? So far as you know, it hasn't retracted. Is that correct?

a15_2405959.speaker: Worden
a15_2405959.text: That is our understanding at this point. I'll let you know when I get out.

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Oh, Al. One more point that I overlooked down here, and that is, the people here would like to have you look at the Mass Spec. boom, Al, if it's at all feasible. If it's not convenient to look down at the base of that boom and look at the coils, forget it; but if you can get a look in there, we would expect to find a coil crossover jamming down in the base there, and we'd like to have your visual confirmation of that.

a15_2405959.speaker: Worden
a15_2405959.text: Roger, Karl. I had intended to do that.

a15_2405959.speaker: Scott
a15_2405959.text: And Houston, Endeavour. I guess the comm's acceptable to you down there on - with Al on VOX. Is that correct?

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: Roger. We're reading him loud and clear.

a15_2405959.speaker: Scott
a15_2405959.text: Flashlight. Flashlight. [Pause.] Yep, got it. It's okay. It's off. Panel 600. Go.

a15_2405959.speaker: Worden
a15_2405959.text: No, I'm negative. [Garble] panel 8, front. [Long pause.]

a15_2405959.speaker: Henize
a15_2405959.text: 15, we'd like to have Omni Charlie. [Pause.]

a15_2412055.speaker: Henize
a15_2412055.text: 15, this is Houston. We'd like to get the High Gain Antenna up, if that's possible. [Pause.]

a15_2412055.speaker: Worden
a15_2412055.text: Okay. Stand by. I'll get the High Gain. [Long pause.]

a15_2412055.speaker: Scott
a15_2412055.text: Don OPS. Connect straps to adapter bracket.

a15_2412055.speaker: Worden
a15_2412055.text: Wait a minute. Let's get the straps up. [Long pause.]

a15_2412055.speaker: Worden
a15_2412055.text: Now, I'm on SCU whenever - Whenever you're ready.

a15_2412055.speaker: Scott
a15_2412055.text: You can leave them off. [Long pause.]

a15_2412055.speaker: Scott
a15_2412055.text: Down in the left-hand LEB, Jim. Bring it up with gloves and helmet, gloves inside. [Long pause.]

a15_2412923.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2412923.text: Distance now 172,176 nautical miles [318,869 km]. Velocity, 2,969 feet per second [905 m/s].

a15_2412923.speaker: Scott
a15_2412923.text: Cabin pressure's approaching 6, and I'll crack the side hatch valve just a bit.

a15_2412923.speaker: Scott
a15_2412923.text: ...valve is on there now. Keep an eye on it.

a15_2412923.speaker: Scott
a15_2412923.text: You guys do your integrity check before I put my helmet and gloves on. [Pause.]

a15_2412923.speaker: Scott
a15_2412923.text: In case I'd have something else closed.

a15_2412923.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2412923.text: Heart rates in the 70's for all three crew men.

a15_2413620.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2413620.text: Heart rates now in the 60's with Dave Scott occasionally dropping down into the 50's.

a15_2413620.speaker: Scott
a15_2413620.text: Side hatch valve coming on full open. [Long pause.]

a15_2413620.speaker: Scott
a15_2413620.text: Rog. That and my SCM. Okay? That'll hold steady.

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Suit pressure's reading about - pound and a half above cabin. [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: I'll pump it down a little bit. [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Jim. Stand by one. Get the cabin pressure down.

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Okay. [garble] valve's, closed. SCS, closed. [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Houston, 15. The suit circuit looks pretty good up here. How's it look to you?

a15_2413953.speaker: Henize
a15_2413953.text: Roger, 15. It looks good to us down here.

a15_2413953.speaker: Irwin
a15_2413953.text: SCU is done. 603 is On. Verified. [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Okay. Let's get the helmet on first. [Pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Pull the OPS down there, would you, Jim? [Pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2413953.text: The back up Lunar Module Pilot, Jack Schmitt, has joined the group at the CapCom console.

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: High. You've got the temp. [Pause.] Can you reach it? Hook that strap in for me, too, would you, please? No.

a15_2413953.speaker: Henize
a15_2413953.text: 15, Houston. We note that your cabin pressure's up to 6. You might consider dumping it down.

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Tell me when my temp [garble] anyone.

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Decay was about .1. It's on. O 2 [garble] is on.

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Okay, Houston; 15. We've got a good integrity check on the CMP, and standing by for a Go for depress from... [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Dave, would you turn my suit diverter valve, please.

a15_2413953.speaker: Henize
a15_2413953.text: We copy, 15. And you have a Go for depress.

a15_2413953.speaker: Scott
a15_2413953.text: Okay. You guys ready? Okay. Houston, 15. The side hatch dump valve is coming open.

a15_2413953.speaker: Worden
a15_2413953.text: Well, okay. Think it's probably easier than I can. [Long pause.]

a15_2413953.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2413953.text: Cabin at 1½ pounds per square inch.

a15_2413953.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2413953.text: Half a pound cabin pressure now.

a15_2413953.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2413953.text: Suit pressure, 4 pounds. Cabin, two tenths.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Yeah. It makes a difference. It's still flowing into the cabin.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: How can you read me? You read me okay? Good. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: You hear my VOX cut in and out? Good.

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Heart rates: Worden and Irwin in the 70's, Scott in the 60's.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Yeah. Okay. You ready? [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: I suspect that SCU is forward enough to keep it there. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: It'll hold. Now. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: It's released. It's in the yellow?

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: No. We've missed it.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Yeah. I can't see it. Jim, can you see the indicator?

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: I can't either, can you?

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Stand by one.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Rog. [Garble.] [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Houston, 15. We're getting ready to open the hatch. How does everything look to you down there?

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Roger, Al. Everything's looking good to us here.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: ...out, Dave.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay? Unlatch. Unlatch. Ready? Rog. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: No.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: 15, Houston. We don't see the TV camera on yet.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: The hatch is open.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Huh. Oh, we haven't got it out yet. We'll have it out there in a minute. It should be on though.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. I got the latch - the handle and latch.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Rog. Rog.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Garble].

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: [Garble] zero. Clips. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Jettison bag is gone. [Pause.] And jettison bag number 2. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: We're getting a picture now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Houston. You should be getting a picture about now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Roger, 15. We're getting a signal. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. Fine. First thing is that the map - the Mapping Camera is all the way out. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: 15, this is Houston. We're getting a clear picture now, but the aiming of the TV camera is poor. Is it possible to open the hatch wider?

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Yeah, that's what - we're - we're looking at that, too. Stand by one, and we'll do that. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Yeah, I can see the TV is pointed right at the Command Module there. Right at the interface.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: That's affirm.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Push it back a little there, Jim.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: No problem.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: That's excellent.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: You should have a picture at a man in space.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Very good. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. You ready, Jim? I'll work my way down. Okay, it's reading 4. Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Distance 171,000 [nautical] miles [316,691 km].

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: We'll have your picture back in a minute, Houston. We're turning on the 16-millimeter.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: We copy.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Yes. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. I'm in the foot restraint.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Yeah, that's good work up there, Al. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay, the Pan Camera cassette is tethered. There's the pip pin. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Worden's heart rate about 130 now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Good.

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Irwin's heart rate 116, Scott's 71.

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: There's the film cassette.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Get it inside there, if you can, Jim. Get it inside. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Rog. Would you like to exchange - would you like to get hold of it? [Laughter.] [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: That's the Pan Camera [cassette], right.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Jim, hold this.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Houston. The Pan Camera is safely inside.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Hold it.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Beautiful job, Al baby. Remember - remember, there is no hurry up there at all.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Rog, Karl. I'm enjoying it. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Going back for the Mapping Camera cassette now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Houston. Rest break. We'll take a look at the V over H sensor.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Very good.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Uh, hum, I see nothing on the V over H sensor. There's no back - black paint missing. There's nothing obscuring the field of view. The glass is not cracked. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: The shield is not obstructing the field of view. There's nothing in the way, Karl.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: We...

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: It's perfectly clear.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: We copy your report, Al. Thank you.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. And as I look around, the Mass Spec. is - oh, it looks like about - not quite in - the cover. It looks like maybe it's the cover that's jammed. Yes, in fact, it is the cover that's jammed. See?

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Roger, Al. We copy. That was most unexpected news.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: No, I can't tell from here. I can't really - I can't really tell from here, Karl, whether it's the cover or not. I thought the cover was jammed. One corner of the cover is overlapping a - side section of insulation which I wasn't expecting it to. But it doesn't seem to be - it doesn't put any force on it - on the Mass Spec. If I could get around and take a look at it. [Pause.] The Mass Spec. is in the guide pins, and the Mass Spec. looks like as it is fully retracted. [Pause.] The Mass Spec. is fully retracted, Karl.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Roger, Al. We're reading you loud and clear.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Any - any diffi - any difficulties with the talkback has to be associated with that cover, because the cover is not closed. How far through the slot should the guide pin come on the - on the reel?

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Stand by, Al.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. 'Cause I can see a guide pin coming through. You do that, and I'll get the map - Mapping Camera.

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Worden's heart rate 97 now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Jim. I'm ready to bring the other one back. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Hey, Al. It looks like you're running a pass up there. That's beautiful. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: And there was the Mapping Camera cassette.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Jim, you look absolutely fantastic against that Moon back there. That is really a most unbelievable, remarkable thing.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Houston. The Mapping Camera cassette is inside.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: We copy. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Houston, is there anything else you want me to check in the SIM bay before we go back in?

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Al, we'd be...

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Is there anything on the Mapping Camera I can check?

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Al, we'd be pleased to have any general comments you had about the SIM bay experiments, otherwise than what we specifically asked you. Did everything look in order?

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. Well, everything looked good, as far as I could tell, except for the cover on the Mass Spec., and the fact that the Mapping Camera is up. Maybe I could take another quick check back here and see if I can see anything on the Mapping Camera.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. You ready guys?

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: All right. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Worden's heart rate 85 now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Oh, just a second. I've got get the mast and get the TV. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. TV coming in. Got it, Dave? Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, take your time.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: I - I'm doing fine. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Hung up - on something. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Ah, yeah, it's about the same place it was when we opened the hatch. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. Hatch is locked.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Neutral. Gear box is in latch. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Can you do it, Dave? Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: 15, Houston. You can turn off the TV anytime you like.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Let us get depr - get pressurized first, Karl.

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Can you get it there?

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Very good. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: Tell me when to close it. [Pause.] That's it. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: [Garbled.] Take it down here before it's too - okay, okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay?

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Cabin pressure coming up now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: I said, I wish I were back outside. It's hell in here. Okay.

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: Closed. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: I can't. No. [Pause.] Yeah. That's okay, Jim. [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: How's that? There we go. Now we should get our positions straight. You see it now, Dave? Okay. Make sure we got a good seal. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: Cool it here for a minute.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, Houston; 15. It looks like we got a good seal. How's it look down there? [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Henize
a15_2420138.text: 15, Houston. Your seal looks good to us.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay, thank you. Okay, 601, Open?

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: It's Open.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Monitor Repress O 2 indicator to zero.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: and it looks zero now, Dave? [Pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay. So, you let your umbilical flow bring every - the cabin up to 3.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott [Worden in onboard transcript]
a15_2420138.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: Cabin pressure 2 pounds.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: That's very nicely done. That's about - 22 minutes. Which is just about what we figured. You went back and looked at all that stuff. So that's just about right.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: It's fun out there, isn't it?

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Mm-hmm. Should have stayed longer.

a15_2420138.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2420138.text: The cabin's at 2.3 now. They'll bring it up to 3 pounds using the spacecraft system. Then they will dump the OPS , the emergency oxygen backpack that Al Worden carried with him. They'll dump that at 3 pounds to bring the cabin pressure on up.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: (Laughter) You done good. You made a lot of people back there very happy.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Roll over and let me take another look again.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Well, I'll tell you what, your - your left arm or something's covering up the light over there.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: The OPS is, I guess.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Really bad lights in here.

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Okay, there. I can see it now.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: We're at 2.4, about. So we'll just let your flow bring it up to 3. Gee, I had a great view on the TV. Did you turn the TV off, Jim?

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: No, I didn't...

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: I'll turn it off.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Can you reach it?

a15_2420138.speaker: Worden
a15_2420138.text: Yes. There. Thought I turned it off.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Can you reach the Scientific TV switch? The S-band TV switch, Jim?

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: No, not yet, Dave.

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: Okay. Maybe I can. No.

a15_2420138.speaker: Irwin
a15_2420138.text: I don't think there's any rush on that, is it?

a15_2420138.speaker: Scott
a15_2420138.text: No.

a15_2423300.speaker: Henize
a15_2423300.text: Fif - 15, Houston. As long as we have the TV camera on, go - go to Average, and we should get a better picture down here.

a15_2423300.speaker: Scott
a15_2423300.text: Well, it's just down in the LEB sort of stowed away, but we'll do that. [Pause.]

a15_2423300.speaker: Scott
a15_2423300.text: We're just not in a position to get the panel 3 switch right now.

a15_2423300.speaker: Henize
a15_2423300.text: We - we copy, and that's fine. [Long pause.]

a15_2423300.speaker: Scott
a15_2423300.text: You may have something on your picture, now.

a15_2423300.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423300.text: That's the hatch window in the background there.

a15_2423618.speaker: Worden
a15_2423618.text: Cabin pressure rate is coming up.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: Cabin pressure is up to 4½ pounds per square inch and the consensus in the control center is that that was reflection of lights in the cabin that you saw in the hatch window.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: Heart rates far Worden and Irwin now in the low 70's, for Dave Scott, high 50's.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: The cabin's up to 5 pounds per square inch.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: Apollo 15's distance from Earth now 170,172 nautical miles [318,158 km]. Velocity, 3,016 feet per second [919 m/s].

a15_2423618.speaker: Scott
a15_2423618.text: Here, give me it first, Al.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: This is Apollo Control. The EVA clock here in the control center recorded 39 minutes, 56 seconds [total EVA time].

a15_2423618.speaker: Scott
a15_2423618.text: Why don't you do it so I don't get my gloves dirty. Get my helmet. Get that stuff off and leave them.

a15_2423618.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2423618.text: And that time is about - from about midway during depressurization to midway in repressurization.

a15_2424559.speaker: Henize
a15_2424559.text: 15, Houston. We see your cabin at 6.1 [psi]. You might want to keep a close eye on that.

a15_2424559.speaker: Scott
a15_2424559.text: Okay; we'll do that. Thank you.

a15_2424559.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2424559.text: This is Apollo Control. We have some unofficial times on some of these EVA events. The Go for depressurization was given at 241 hours, 55 minutes, 33 seconds. Depressurization started at 241:56:12; hatch open, 242:05:33; Worden going out the hatch, 242:07:29; hatch coming closed, 242:25:20; and the pressure - cabin pressure starting to come back up at 242:27:25.

a15_2425238.speaker: Scott
a15_2425238.text: Houston, 15. We're prepared to maneuver to the thermal attitude a little early if you'd like us to go over there.

a15_2425238.speaker: Henize
a15_2425238.text: 15, this is Houston. That would be fine with us.

a15_2425810.speaker: Henize
a15_2425810.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Auto on the High Gain [Antenna] and go from Reacq to Auto quickly.

a15_2425810.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2425810.text: This is Apollo Control at 243 hours, 02 minutes. Apollo 15 now 169,526 nautical miles [313,962 km] from Earth. Velocity, 3,031 feet per second [924 m/s]. Weight, 26,509 pounds [12,024 kg].

a15_2432557.speaker: Henize
a15_2432557.text: After some discussion down here, we'd like to disable your jets A2 - Alpha 2 and Bravo 1, mainly because the Mapping Camera's still out and our concern is that the plume will be deflected down into the SIM bay and possibly damage some of our electrical wiring or some of the - the N 2 plumbing, which may give us other problems.

a15_2432557.speaker: Scott
a15_2432557.text: Rog. Sounds like a good idea. If there's any other particular configuration you want, just let us know.

a15_2432557.speaker: Scott
a15_2432557.text: And A2 and Bravo 1 are disabled.

a15_2432557.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2432557.text: This is Apollo Control at 243 hours, 58 minutes. The crew of Apollo 15 busy stowing equipment, reconfiguring the cabin. Very quiet time as far as communications are concerned. Apollo 15 now 167,882 nautical miles [310,917 km] from Earth. Velocity: 3,070 feet per second [936 m/s]. And the clock showing 51 hours, 12 minutes to landing.

a15_2440139.speaker: Scott
a15_2440139.text: Rog. The OPS pressure is 2,000 [psi] and we'll be off comm for about 5 or 10 minutes here while we reconfigure the suits and everything.

a15_2443413.speaker: Henize
a15_2443413.text: 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_2443413.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2443413.text: This is Apollo Control at 244 hours, 35 minutes. The Apollo 15 crew apparently still off the communications system as they are reconfiguring their cabin. We're showing cabin pressure holding at 5.7 pounds per square inch. Temperature, 68 degrees.

a15_2443413.speaker: Henize
a15_2443413.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_2443413.speaker: Henize
a15_2443413.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [No answer.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Houston, Apollo 15. We'll start to charge on battery B now, if you're ready.

a15_2443941.speaker: Henize
a15_2443941.text: Roger, 15. We're ready for the battery charge; and, while we're about it, the experimenters are getting a little fidgety about the waste water dump because that will impact their Mass Spectrograph work, so we would like to get the dump and the O 2 fuel cell purge started also.

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Rog. We'll get on it right away. [Long pause.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Henize
a15_2443941.text: And, 15, whenever Al has a couple of minutes, we have a few questions about the SIM bay that we'd like to debrief on. [Pause.]

a15_2443941.speaker: Scott
a15_2443941.text: Okay, give - give him another 15 to 20 minutes here.

a15_2443941.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2443941.text: This is Apollo Control at 245 hours. Apollo 15 picking up velocity, getting closer to home each second. Endeavour is now 166,043 nautical miles [307,511 km] from Earth. Velocity: 3,115 feet per second [949 m/s].

a15_2450419.speaker: Henize
a15_2450419.text: We need to make a small change in the Flight Plan, because there's a need now to turn the X-ray experiment on. If you'll go down to that group of steps at 245:30, we'd like to do four of them. We'd like to get the "Data Systems - On - switch to On." We'd like to "Disable the jets." We'd like to get "S-band Aux, TV to Science."

a15_2450419.speaker: Henize
a15_2450419.text: Roger. Four of those steps down to 245:30 we want to do right away, if possible. We want to get the "S-band Aux, TV to Science." We want the "Data System On switch to On." We want to "Disable all jets except -" and we want "X-ray Experiment, On." [Pause.]

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Okay. Understand at 45:30 - 245:30, you want "S-band Aux, TV to Science, Data Systems On to On, disable all jets, and X-ray Experiment, On" immediately.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: We need the repress time on the cabin. [Garble].

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: Ten days and 5 hours we've been gone, Jim.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Long time. We beat your old record.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Sure does. Went farther from home, too.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Didn't go as far, but went farther.

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: And a lot more fun, too.

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: Big Dipper, do you know, on 9, we could have missed any one thing and pressed on.

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: Here, it's a lot different; you can't miss anything and press on.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Well, it looks like we can't miss anything.

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: This is sort of an all-or-nothing kind of operation, you know it?

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Yes, it really is, you know. It's really all your eggs in one basket, boy. I got to thinking about that after you guys left for your descent. Once you start that descent, man, that - that's it...

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: We're there. That's right. It's all hanging out from there on.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: It would be better for [garble] to put pills in all the food drawers.

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: Where will I put them? It's the last time I'm saying it, but you better not lose your pills.

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: You didn't see them in your TSB, did you, Jim?

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: You didn't see the pills in your TSB when you cleaned out, did you?

a15_2450419.speaker: Scott
a15_2450419.text: Ohh, what did I do with it?

a15_2450419.speaker: Worden
a15_2450419.text: It's almost back to normal times.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. We're having some ground problems in communications networks, and we'd like to have a comm check. [Long pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Oh! Did you notice anything loose?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Well, I thought I saw - Well, I saw a...

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Hey, do you guys [garble] get some orange juice? [Garble]. Let's enjoy it - let's enjoy it while we can.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Except for bad stuff, we can always put up with it for 1 more day.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Yes, that's right. Well - Hey, let's - [garble] will be our last meal. We have three meals below and breakfast [garble] 1 day.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: And a long way to go.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Oh, hush.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Apollo 15, this is Houston. How do you read? [Pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Hello, Houston; this is 15. Loud and clear, and I got your first message, Karl. I'm sorry.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Hi, Al. Yeah, we've got some sort of problem on ground circuits here. Just wanted to make sure we were in contact with you.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: No, we're here.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Roger; very good. [Long pause.]

a15_2451649.speaker: SC
a15_2451649.text: [Cough.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Al, we have some questions for you on the SIM bay experiments, whenever you have some time to answer them.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Oh, yes. That's right. That's great.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Okay, Karl. Tell you what, I'll give you a call back in about 10 minutes when I'm ready.

a15_2451649.speaker: Henize
a15_2451649.text: Very good.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: No, he's got some questions on the SIM bay.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: SIM bay looks pretty good.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: What'd [garble].?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: I'm coming. I'm coming, Jim. [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: Yes, I can see through on the handles.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: I didn't even see any scorching or any burning or anything down there.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: The covering on the - on the Service Module, if it hadn't been covered, boy, that would have been burned and scarred and scorched and everything else.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Yes. That's right.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: Yes. Yes. Excuse me one second, will you?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Excuse me, Jim. Let me get out of your way here.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Really?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Well, I guess it doesn't make any difference on this food if we take it back home anyway.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Yes, that's probably true. They can decontaminate it back there.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Sure.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: You can tell them we ran out, though. Do you think this salad's good, Al?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: My what?

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Sandwich spread [garble]. It's a whole half a can.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Sure you can, Jim.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: We have to finish after you.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: Okay, I'll eat it.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: That's right.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: What?

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: If you wouldn't complain so much, we wouldn't leave you so much.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: You guys didn't leave me nothing.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Freak you!

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: I'm thinking.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Laughter.]

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: What kind of desserts we got there, Jim? A lemon pudding, huh?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Mmmm.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Yes, you're right, mouth, and I'm going to catch it [garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: I'm ready, if you can catch it.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: [Cleared throat.] That's the only way a power bowler makes it.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: Huh? Yes, I suppose we ought to think about doing that. We can get to all that stuff now.

a15_2451649.speaker: Irwin
a15_2451649.text: Bright idea. [Garble].

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: I would.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: That's a pretty good sandwich.

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: Mm-hmm.

a15_2451649.speaker: Scott
a15_2451649.text: How much food we got left?

a15_2451649.speaker: Worden
a15_2451649.text: I don't know, at least a couple of days.

a15_2451649.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2451649.text: This is Apollo Control at 245 hours, 30 minutes. Apollo 15's distance now 165,125 nautical miles [305,811 km]. Velocity, 3,137 feet per second [956 m/s].

a15_2453050.speaker: Scott
a15_2453050.text: Six-foot waves in the recovery area, huh?

a15_2453050.speaker: Worden
a15_2453050.text: Yes, if we can dodge and land, that's great.

a15_2453050.speaker: Scott
a15_2453050.text: That's why we had so much trouble on 9. [Garble].

a15_2453050.speaker: Worden
a15_2453050.text: Why can't we just hop on over her pretty good in that fashion, too?

a15_2453323.speaker: Henize
a15_2453323.text: Roger. Just sending up a reminder about the X-ray pointing attitude, which is due very soon now, and the activation of the SIM bay experiments.

a15_2453323.speaker: Worden
a15_2453323.text: Okay, Houston. Boy, oh, boy, I used to think it was a good thing to get on a flight and then they could only talk at you one at a time. Whew, boy! Now, I think it's a good thing to get back so you - you don't have to listen to that goddam radio all the time.

a15_2453323.speaker: Worden
a15_2453323.text: The DAC, yes. But the Hasselblad's above your head.

a15_2453323.speaker: Scott
a15_2453323.text: No, mine's - I don't think so. No, that's Jim's.

a15_2453323.speaker: Worden
a15_2453323.text: It's time for the UV stuff, huh? Let me get out of your way. You couldn't find any more pills, right?

a15_2453323.speaker: Worden
a15_2453323.text: No, I thought I put them in your TSB. I just saw them hanging there just before we started all that stuff, and I don't know.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Apollo 15, we'd like to have Omni Alpha. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Rog; Omni Alpha. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Houston, 15.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Go ahead, 15.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Karl. I'm ready to talk SIM bay; but first, a couple of questions.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Fire away. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. What attitude do you want us to do the UV photo - photography at. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger, Al. The information on - on UV photos is to follow the procedures - Okay - you want the attitude - the procedures are on page 3-352, and the attitude to be used is 210, 242, 322.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Say the attitude again, please.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 210, 242, 322. Also, note use of magazine P, and also the time - the time that we start the maneu - the time that we finish the maneuver is 247 plus 45. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: And let me clarify that magazine. That is the magazine for the UV color photographs. That is magazine P instead of magazine M. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Understand. Use the procedures on page 3-352 , except change the attitude to 210, 242, and 322, and this whole thing is to be done at 247:45.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. That's the time for completing the maneuver. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Well, what time would you like us to maneuver to that attitude then? [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. The time to start the maneuver is 24 - 247 plus 36.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: I understand. 247 plus 36. Rog. Thank you, Karl. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Al. Are you ready for the SIM bay questions? [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Rog, Karl. Sure am.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. First of all, the guys down here would like send up their warmest congratulations on such an ex - successful EVA. You sure made it look easy up there. And the questions. The questions we got are about the Mapping Camera, and they're directed at the general problem of is there - was there anything you could see which might indicate why it jammed? And there are three - three particular items that you might have looked at. First of all, it was the main camera cover at the bottom of the camera. Was it touching or scraping the camera in any way that you noticed?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: The answer to that is negative. In fact. I checked it. I checked the Mapping Camera cover, Laser Altimeter cover quite carefully to make sure, because I do know that there have been some interference problems with that before, particularly with the Pan Camera, so I was looking at that in particular to see that it was maybe adjusted too close or - or interfering along the side of the Pan Camera, and it was not. There was about half an inch clearance between the upper edge of the cover and the body of the Mapping Camera, so that I - I don't see that that was responsible for the thing jamming.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. I think you've very clearly put that suspicion to rest. There are also two covers to the solar camera in the upper left side of the Mapping Camera. And did you notice any - any distortion or any scraping in - in these covers? There's one possibility. The one that stuck out to the left - it - it might have jammed and the screwjack that controls it might have twisted it or distorted it. Was there anything you noticed like that?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Negative, Karl. I noticed nothing out of place with the Mapping Camera, nothing interfering. I checked all the way around it, down into the cavity, nothing interfering. I saw no evidence of anything interfering, and it looked clean underneath, so I don't think there was anything blocking it from underneath. I don't know. My distinct impression after surveying the Mapping Camera and looking around the cavity where the Mapping Camera fits was that there is a problem with the drive.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. You didn't see anything inhibiting its motion, not even the electrical cables up on the top, huh?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Negative, and I guess I can ask a question along that line. Has anyone noticed any high current when we've gone to Retract on the Mapping Camera to indicate that it was hanging up?

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: We didn't see any, Al, although there had been a long controversy down here about the long amount of time required to extend and retract. It was, even though it was about the 4 minutes predicted several months ago, it was somewhat longer than what we'd observed at the Cape. People had been worrying about that for some time.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Yeah, I realize that. And I also, as I re - as I go back to what we saw at the Cape, there was some problems with that thing hanging up in drive itself at the Cape.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. Okay, a couple of questions on the Mass Spectrometer. You gave us some good information there, but when you said the Mass Spectrometer cover wasn't completely closed, could you give us some idea at - as - to - to what degree it had closed, to what angle, and was there any poss - any cocking, any - any twisting in - in that cover.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Well, I couldn't tell whether there was any warpage in the cover or not, particularly because that kind of a cover is a little - looks like its warped anyway. It looked to me, I could - I pulled the cover out of the way enough to look at the Mass Spec. inside, and I could see the guide pin and along the sides of the carriage coming through the holes all the way up, so that they were plainly visible from the outside which - which meant to me that the - the Mass Spec. was either very close to being seated on the carriage or it was seated. I - I guess I don't really know how far those guide pins

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger, Al. We copy that. And would you open the X-ray and Alpha Covers right now, please?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, X-ray/Alpha Covers coming open.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. I guess you've answered most of our questions on the Mass Spec., and you've approached one that we might get a little more out of, and that is those guide rails sticking through the guides. There is a tapered portion, and when it's completely seated, you actually see the - the - the cylindrical portion beyond the tapered portion. Did you actually see the cylindrical portion, or was it all tapered area that you looked at on the guide rail?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay, that's good scoop. All I saw was the tapered area.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. You probably - If it was fully seated, you would have seen about a half inch of - of the cylinder there, and this is a good indication that it was not all the way seated even though it was close. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Here's a couple of other questions. Give me a second to look at them.

a15_2453822.speaker: Scott
a15_2453822.text: Why don't you get the [garble]?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Al. Mostly questions here about the contamination status and things in the SIM bay. First of all, how about the - the - the door eder - the door edges? Did they blow off smoothly and cleanly?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Yes, very cleanly. I saw no rough edges at all. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Stand by a moment, Al.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Don't forget to [garble].

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Ion - Ion Source to Standby.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Al, we're anxious to bring up the High Gain Antenna. I've got a couple of angles here if they'll help.

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Minus 76 and 117. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Minus 76 and 117. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. We copied your comment on the SIM bay door jettison, and further questions go as follows. The white coatings in the SIM bay were - Did you notice that any of them why - were obviously discolored or - or coated from contamination or overheating? [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: I saw no evidence of heating in the SIM bay. I saw no evidence of discoloration of the white surfaces. There were - [cough] - as - as best I could tell, no particulate matter that had come to rest on any of the surfaces in the SIM bay. It looked very, very clean. And - even across the top of the Mapping Camera where there was a - such a heating problem expected, I saw no indications of heating whatsoever, particularly on things like the cover over the Mapping Camera cassette, which was supposedly a very hot spot, and it was just as clean as a whistle. There wasn't - there wasn't any evidence o

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And, on the insulation and foils, I guess there's a question here - Were any of them burned or discolored? You probably already told us that. Were any of them torn or were there any attachment failures? [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: No, I couldn't see any evidence of - of any burning or tearing or anything else back there, Karl. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay, we got one more general question there. And our Flight Dynamics Officer, who is vitally concerned about our reentry weight, would like to know whether or not we jettisoned more or less than a nominal 32 pounds; and, if so, by how much?

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Stand by one.

a15_2453822.speaker: Scott
a15_2453822.text: Say, Houston, we've talked it over, and I guess we'd say it was pretty close to a nominal - as far as weight. We have no idea of - of determining exactly what the weight was, but we're going to try and work our reentry stowage over this afternoon and tomorrow morning, and we hope to give you a - a plan by - somewhere around noon tomorrow, of where all the rocks are stowed and where everything is stowed and what we have on board. So you can start - so Mr. FIDO can work up his entry plan.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And, if somebody has the time to copy it, I've got a small Flight Plan update available now.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, Karl. I'll take that.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Hi, Jim. How're you doing?

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Just fine.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. 246 hours and 20 minutes; we have High Gain [Antenna] angles of pitch, 00; yaw, 240. [Pause.] At...

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And at 246 plus 46, we want to add "Change discriminator to low." [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. Scratch "Discriminator, High," and make it "Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's correct. And, on 247 plus 28, delete that DAP load. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. We already have that change.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Sorry about that. On 247 plus 30, we'd like to have the "Alpha/X-ray Covers, Closed; then Off", and delete the note on the Cover Open/Close. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, understand. At 247:30, you'd like "Alpha/X-ray Doors, Closed," and just delete the note here. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And stand by one second. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 247 plus 30. Also, we would like to add "Mass Spectrometer Multiplier, High; Discriminator, Low." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Worden
a15_2453822.text: Understand. At 247:30, you want to add "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High, and Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Rog. And, at 247 plus 32, we'd like to have "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High; Discriminator, High." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay, 247:32, "Mass Spec. Multiplier, High, and Discriminator, High."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And I guess you need to save room, if there's any left there, because at 34 and at 36, we want to change these two switches again. At 34, we want "Mass Spec. Multiplier, Low; Discriminator, High." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. At 34 you want "Multiplier, Low; and Discriminator, High."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Affirmative and at 36, we want "Multiplier, Low; Discriminator, Low." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. At 247:36, it's "Multiplier, Low; and Discriminator, Low."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Affirmative. Also at 247:36 is "Add the UV photos," and we've already sent up the changes required for that; the changes over and above what's on page 3-352 . And there's one reminder there, and that is to verify that when you use filter 2, that you take one frame for 20 seconds and one frame for 2 seconds.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Roger. We remember that.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. The next step is 247 plus 45, "X-ray to Standby." [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. At 247:45, "X-ray to Standby."

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: And, at 247 plus 50, we want to move the PTC initiation steps from 247:30 to 247:50. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. Understand. The initiation of PTC to be delayed from 247:30 to 247:50.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's affirmative. At 248 hours and 0 minutes, we'd like the following: we'd like the Mass Spectrometer boom retraction sequence. Each retraction step will last 20 minutes, instead of 12. [Pause.] And terminate this test at 249 plus 30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Go back to 248, Karl, on that Mass Spectrometer boom retraction sequence.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. I...

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: I have that in there.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: I - I guess all - all we're doing there is changing - The - the retraction step will be 20 minutes instead of 12 minutes. Down at the end of the writing there, it says "Each sample period will last 12 minutes." We'd like to have that at 20 minutes. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. I'll change the note there then. It occurs about 248:20; this 12 will be 20.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: That's correct. At 249:05, we'd like to move the Mass Spec. boom deploy from 05 to 30 - from 249:05 to 249:30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Understand. Move the Mass Spec. boom deploy from 249:05 to 249:30. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Roger. And one final one at 251:48, which you may already have, is delete the DAP load there.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: I do; we have that one, Karl.

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: Okay. That completes the update. Thank you.

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Henize
a15_2453822.text: 15, Houston. We'd like to have Gamma-ray Gain Step up 4 clicks. [Pause.]

a15_2453822.speaker: Irwin
a15_2453822.text: Okay. That's Gamma-ray Gain Step up 4 clicks.

a15_2453822.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2453822.text: This is Apollo Control at 246 hours, 15 minutes. Apollo 15 now 163,766 nautical miles [303,295 km] from Earth. Velocity: 3,171 feet per second [967 m/s].

a15_2453822.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2453822.text: This is Apollo Control at 246 hours, 20 minutes. Apollo 15 is maneuvering now to the X-ray pointing attitude.

a15_2453822.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2453822.text: This is Apollo Control at 246 hours, 36 minutes. The high voltage has been turned on, on the subsatellite, everything is normal and the vehicle is considered fully operational.

a15_2463658.speaker: Henize
a15_2463658.text: 15, this is Houston. We trust you'll be pleased to hear the news that the high voltage has been turned on to the subsatellite, and that they find that all systems are operational.

a15_2463658.speaker: Scott
a15_2463658.text: Oh, that's very good. Glad to hear it.

a15_2463658.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2463658.text: This is Apollo Control at 246 hours, 59 minutes. Apollo 15, is 162,429 nautical miles [300,819 km] from Earth. Velocity, 3,204 feet per second [977 m/s], and the clock counting down shows 48 hours, 11 minutes to landing. Here in the control center, Flight Director Glynn Lunney and his team preparing to relieve Flight Director Gerry Griffin and his team of flight controllers. The CapCom on the next shift will be astronaut Bob Parker. We estimate the change of shift news conference for 4:15 pm Central Daylight Time in the News Center Briefing Room.

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: 15, Houston. We have a couple of more comments on the UV photo procedures, if somebody can copy.

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: Roger. We overlooked the fact that you are taking these photos in the midst of SIM bay operation, so a couple of little things change. Going back to page 3-352 , you can first of all delete, below the damp rates notation, in - you can delete "Inhibit all jets, except" the jets that are there, and just keep the jet configuration you got right now. [Long pause.]

a15_2470446.speaker: Irwin
a15_2470446.text: Okay. I copy that. Do you have any other comments?

a15_2470446.speaker: Henize
a15_2470446.text: Roger. Under "Remove the CM5 window," put in there "CMC, Free," and likewise, about four lines up from the bottom, just above "note", put in "CMC, Auto". And the final comment, "Enable all jets"; you can delete that. [Pause.] And that's all.

a15_2470446.speaker: Irwin
a15_2470446.text: Okay; understand. Just below "Remove CM5 window cover" put "CMC, Free," and then down at the - the bottom there, just above the note, put "CMC, Auto," and scratch "enable all jets."

a15_2473529.speaker: Worden
a15_2473529.text: Dr. Parker, I presume. Listen, Bob, we got to pull the Gamma-ray [boom] to 15 feet at 50, and wonder if you've got an updated retraction time for us.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: That's affirm, Al. We have a retract time of 247 plus 50, for 72 seconds. Over.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: That's affirm. And, 15, if you got your Flight Plan out, we can update a couple more times in that same general vicinity for you. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Worden
a15_2473529.text: Okay, the Flight Plan is out and the door is open.

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. At 248:02, the Mass Spec. boom retract time - that should be 33 seconds. And that time will apply to the first retraction. The second, third, fourth, and fifth retractions will be 32 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Irwin
a15_2473529.text: Okay, Bob. Understand that the first retraction is 33 seconds and the succeeding retractions will be 32 seconds. Is that 4 or 5?

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Apollo 15, Houston. That will be 32 seconds for all succeeding ones, and we are going to do that up to 249:30. And so all succeeding ones you get will be at 32 seconds. And we will finish that test at 249:30, no matter where we are. And I believe I see that Karl has sent up comment that the sample period would be 20 minutes instead of 12. Is that right?

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. And another change: at 249:36, the Gamma-ray deploy. That time will be 63 seconds. Over. [Pause.]

a15_2473529.speaker: Parker
a15_2473529.text: Okay. That's all we have for right now.

a15_2473529.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2473529.text: This is Apollo Control. Flight Director Glynn Lunney is completing his mission status review with his Flight Controllers at the present time. We're about to begin the change of shift press briefing, and that briefing will be held in the Briefing Room at the MSC News Center. At present time, Apollo 15 is 161,117 nautical miles [298,389 km] from the Earth and the spacecraft velocity is 3,237 feet per second [987 m/s].

a15_2474313-cospb.speaker: Parker
a15_2474313-cospb.text: Apollo 15, Houston. Request Omni Delta, please.

a15_2474313-cospb.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2474313-cospb.text: This is Apollo Control at 247 hours, 59 minutes. During our change of shift briefing, we had no conversations with the crew. It's been quiet in Mission Control. And we're standing by live at this time.

a15_2475913.speaker: Parker
a15_2475913.text: Roger, 15. If you guys will give us a hack when you start the first Mass Spec. retraction, we'll keep an eye on those 20-minute periods for you.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Bob, we just completed one retraction for 33 seconds.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Hey, you woke up just in time to eat again, Dave.

a15_2475913.speaker: Worden
a15_2475913.text: Okay, valve pressure is getting good and [garble] is [garble].

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Sure a relaxed schedule here today.

a15_2475913.speaker: Worden
a15_2475913.text: We're going along all right until we get to [garble].

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: You never do any more UV work, Al?

a15_2475913.speaker: Worden
a15_2475913.text: Yes, we get another one tomorrow.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Hand me the log there, will you? Oh, we don't have the log out, do we?

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: It might be in my TSB. My [garble] TSB.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Let's see. I have a G&C Checklist over here. But I don't have the - I don't have the other good information. I take it back; I have it. I have it.

a15_2475913.speaker: Irwin
a15_2475913.text: Did you take any UV photos in - in orbit?

a15_2480627.speaker: Parker
a15_2480627.text: Roger, 15. We'd like to get a pitch of minus 4.0 and yaw of 90 for the High Gain Antenna. And then, if you'd change your antenna switch to High Gain without hitting the Command Reset switch, we'll maintain comm that way, please.

a15_2480828.speaker: Parker
a15_2480828.text: Negative. You did the right thing without us calling you. Thank you. [Pause.]

a15_2480828.speaker: Irwin
a15_2480828.text: Are we going to press on with the High Gain?

a15_2480828.speaker: Scott
a15_2480828.text: Yes, yes. If you just get your [garble] down here, [garble].

a15_2480828.speaker: Scott
a15_2480828.text: [Garble]. We want to take four breathing samples and do our [garble]. What do we have - we have about 50 left to make, don't we?

a15_2480828.speaker: Mission Control
a15_2480828.text: This is Apollo Control. The crew, at the present time, is setting up their Digital Auto Pilot and this will damp out the rates of the spacecraft, set it up in a stable position just prior to starting it rotating at the rate of about 3 revolutions per hour. And this is the condition that the spacecraft will be in during the sleep period to maintain the proper temperature and the proper - proper thermal equilibrium. Prior to beginning the sleep period, which will be a 9-hour rest period, the crew will also run a Program 52 which is a platform alignment, aligning the stable platform used by their

a15_2481034.speaker: Irwin
a15_2481034.text: You should bring that. I used the scissors to cut mine on the LM, but - Is there a file on the end of those scissors?

a15_2481034.speaker: Worden
a15_2481034.text: I don't think so. That one's [garble].

a15_2481034.speaker: Scott
a15_2481034.text: Not much of a file, huh?

a15_2481417.speaker: Parker
